method: 六个领域（冥想、呼吸、声音与音乐、安全、产品设计、练习结构）分别由研究员检索指南、系统综述、元分析和关键随机对照试验，按统一格式提取结论、数字、样本、局限和对应用的含义；随后每条结论由独立核查员逐条对照原始来源（Crossref / PubMed 元数据、摘要、全文或官方页面）核实作者、年份、DOI、每个数字和结论的措辞，发现夸大、遗漏阴性结果或数字错误时给出修正版。只有「核实无误」或「已修正」的结论进入本库；修正内容和核查记录附在每条结论的 verification 字段里。

grades.high: 高：多项低偏倚随机试验结论一致，或权威指南推荐
grades.moderate: 中：有元分析或大型严格试验支持，但存在异质性或偏倚方面的疑虑
grades.low: 低：小型、探索性或结果不一致的研究
grades.very-low: 很低：几乎没有对照证据，或只有机制推测、观察性资料

claims.topic: IPD meta-analysis: effect size and moderators of mindfulness programmes in community adults
claims.finding: Preregistered systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis (PROSPERO CRD42020200117) of RCTs that passed a quality threshold. Trials compared in-person, group-based, teacher-led MBPs with passive controls in non-clinical settings. Fifteen trials were eligible and 13 shared IPD (2,371 participants; 8 countries: Australia, Canada, Chile, Taiwan, Thailand, the Netherlands, the UK, the US; median age 34; 71% women; moderately distressed on average; 20% missing outcome data, multiply imputed). Versus passive controls, MBPs reduced psychological distress 1–6 months post-intervention (primary outcome): SMD −0.32 (95% CI −0.41 to −0.24; p<0.001; 95% PI −0.41 to −0.24, no heterogeneity; GRADE high). Results were robust to sensitivity analyses, including adding published data from the 2 trials without IPD (SMD −0.31). Post-intervention SMD was −0.28 (GRADE moderate). Beyond 6 months it was −0.29, measured in only 3 trials (GRADE low). Four trials also had active control arms (exercise, health-enhancement programmes, a stress-management course). Versus these there was no evidence of benefit (1–6 months SMD 0.03, 95% CI −0.20 to 0.25; GRADE very low). No prespecified variable (baseline distress, gender, age, education, dispositional mindfulness) modified the effect, so the authors could not build a model predicting who benefits most. The authors state the findings do not extend to automated or self-guided MBPs such as smartphone apps.
claims.finding_zh: 预注册的个体参与者数据（IPD）荟萃分析：纳入符合质量门槛、在非临床环境中比较线下、团体、由老师带领的正念课程与不干预（被动）对照的随机对照试验；15 项符合条件，13 项提供了个体数据（2371 人，来自澳大利亚、加拿大、智利、台湾、泰国、荷兰、英国、美国 8 个国家和地区，中位年龄 34 岁，71% 为女性，平均有中等程度的心理困扰，20% 的结局数据缺失并做了多重插补）。与不干预相比，课程结束后 1–6 个月心理困扰小到中等程度地下降：SMD −0.32（95% CI −0.41 至 −0.24），各试验之间没有异质性，GRADE 可信度为高，多种敏感性分析结果一致。课程刚结束时 SMD −0.28（可信度中等）；6 个月以后为 −0.29（只有 3 项试验测量，可信度低）。其中 4 项试验另设了积极对照（运动、健康促进课程、压力管理课程），与这些相比，正念课程没有显示额外好处（1–6 个月 SMD 0.03，95% CI −0.20 至 0.25，可信度极低）。没有发现基线困扰程度、性别、年龄、教育程度或特质正念会改变效果大小，因此作者无法建立模型预测谁会受益更多。作者明确指出，这些结果不能推广到手机应用等自动化或自助式正念课程。
claims.study_type: individual participant data (IPD) meta-analysis of RCTs (preregistered)
claims.sample: 13 RCTs, 2,371 participants
claims.limitations: The primary comparison is against passive controls. The active-control comparison rests on only 4 trials (very low certainty) and showed no difference. Participants were volunteers who chose a mindfulness course. Programmes were in-person teacher-led groups rather than apps, and the authors explicitly exclude extrapolation to apps. Outcomes were self-reported (high measurement-bias risk in all trials), and passive-control comparisons were at high risk of bias from deviations from intended interventions. 20% missing outcome data (imputed). Only trials passing a quality threshold were included.
claims.app_implication: Headline expectation for teacher-led group courses in non-clinical adults: a small-to-moderate average reduction in distress (about one third of a standard deviation) compared with doing nothing, with no advantage shown over other active programmes such as exercise or stress-management courses. The authors say this does not extend to self-guided apps, so do not present it as the app's own expected effect. It is not yet possible to predict who will benefit, so avoid personalised benefit promises or 'your type will benefit' messaging.

citation.authors: Galante J, Friedrich C, Collaboration of Mindfulness Trials (CoMinT), et al.
citation.title: Systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials assessing mindfulness-based programs for mental health promotion

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; PubMed abstract (PMID 37867573); PMC7615230 author-manuscript full text via Europe PMC (study characteristics, Table 2 by control type and timepoint, GRADE, effect modification, discussion); doi.org resolution
verification.problems: Metadata matches Crossref; PubMed lists the author-manuscript title for the same PMID. The primary numbers are correct (15 eligible, 13 with IPD, 2,371 participants, 8 countries, median age 34, 71% women, 20% missing, SMD −0.32 [−0.41 to −0.24], PI identical, GRADE high, no effect modification). Problems: (1) The limitation 'Passive controls only (no comparison with other active interventions)' is factually wrong. Four trials had active control arms (exercise, health enhancement, stress management), and versus these there was no evidence of benefit (1–6 months SMD 0.03, 95% CI −0.20 to 0.25; post-intervention −0.05; GRADE very low). The finding omits this null result. (2) 'Confidence high' applies only to the 1–6-month passive comparison; post-intervention was moderate (SMD −0.28) and beyond 6 months was low (only 3 trials). (3) app_implication offers the effect as a headline expectation for 'healthy adults'. The authors explicitly state the findings do not extend to self-guided programmes such as smartphone apps, and participants were moderately distressed volunteers.

claims.topic: NICE depression guideline position on mindfulness and meditation
claims.finding: NICE guideline NG222 (published 29 June 2022; later minor amendments, the latest in December 2025, do not affect the mindfulness entries) lists 'group mindfulness and meditation' in Table 1 as one of 11 treatment options for a new episode of less severe depression (defined as subthreshold symptoms and mild depression). Rec 1.5.2 says all Table 1 treatments can be used first line, but to consider the least intrusive and least resource-intensive treatment, guided self-help, first. Table 1 is ordered by the committee's interpretation of clinical and cost effectiveness and implementation factors; group mindfulness is 7th, after guided self-help, group CBT, group BA, individual CBT, individual BA and group exercise. The committee found 'some evidence' for its effectiveness (versus 'good evidence' for group CBT and group BA) and recommended it, with group exercise, IPT and antidepressants, as an alternative for people who do not wish to have CBT or BA. It is described as a group intervention provided preferably by 2 practitioners, at least 1 with therapy-specific training and competence, using a programme such as MBCT specifically designed for depression, usually 8 regular sessions with 8 to 15 participants, with homework that includes mindfulness recordings. Table 1 notes it 'may be difficult for people experiencing intense or highly distressing thoughts, or who find focusing on the body difficult', and that it does not directly help with relationship, employment or other stressors. For relapse prevention, rec 1.8.5 covers people who remitted on antidepressant medication alone and are assessed as at higher risk of relapse: consider continuing the antidepressant, or group CBT or MBCT for those who do not wish to continue it, or both. Rec 1.8.6 says these group CBT or MBCT courses should focus explicitly on relapse-prevention skills and usually consist of 8 sessions over 2 to 3 months, with the option of more sessions in the next 12 months. Group mindfulness is not among the 10 options in Table 2 for more severe depression.
claims.finding_zh: 英国 NICE 抑郁症指南 NG222（2022 年 6 月 29 日发布；之后几次小幅修订，最近一次在 2025 年 12 月，均未涉及正念相关内容）在表 1 中把“团体正念与冥想”列为较轻抑郁（包括阈下症状和轻度抑郁）新发作的 11 种治疗选项之一。建议 1.5.2 指出，表 1 中的治疗都可作为一线选择，但应先考虑最不打扰、资源消耗最少的指导式自助。表 1 按委员会对临床效果、成本效益及实施因素的判断排序，团体正念排第 7，在指导式自助、团体认知行为疗法、团体行为激活、个体认知行为疗法、个体行为激活和团体运动之后。委员会认为其有效性有“一些证据”（团体 CBT 和团体行为激活为“良好证据”），因此把它和团体运动、人际心理治疗、抗抑郁药一起，作为不想接受 CBT 或行为激活者的替代选择。形式是：最好由 2 名从业者带领（至少 1 人受过专门的治疗训练并具备相应能力），采用 MBCT 等专为抑郁设计的方案，通常 8 次，每组 8–15 人，课间要完成作业，包括在家用正念录音练习。指南提示：它对正经历强烈或高度痛苦想法、或难以专注于身体的人可能比较困难，也不能直接帮助解决人际关系、工作等可能导致抑郁的压力。预防复发方面，建议 1.8.5 针对单用抗抑郁药后缓解、且被评估为复发风险较高的人：可考虑继续服药，或者（对不想继续服药的人）参加团体 CBT 或 MBCT 课程，或两者同时进行。建议 1.8.6 指出这类课程应明确聚焦预防复发的技能，通常在 2–3 个月内进行 8 次，之后 12 个月内可视需要追加。较严重抑郁的 10 种治疗选项（表 2）中没有团体正念。
claims.sample: Guideline (committee appraisal of evidence reviews)
claims.limitations: UK health-system guideline. The recommendations concern practitioner-led group programmes (and MBCT for relapse prevention), not self-guided apps. The table order reflects cost-effectiveness and implementation as well as efficacy, and NICE rated the effectiveness evidence for group mindfulness only as 'some evidence'. Checked against the current online version (accessed October 2026), which may be revised.
claims.app_implication: Position the app honestly in NICE's terms. For less severe depression, mindfulness is a recognised option only as a structured group programme (such as MBCT) led by trained practitioners, ranked behind guided self-help and CBT/BA. MBCT is also one relapse-prevention option after remission on antidepressants. The app is a self-practice tool, not treatment, and should point people to such programmes and to professional help. Reuse the NICE caution in onboarding (may be difficult with intense or highly distressing thoughts, or when focusing on the body is hard).

citation.authors: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
citation.title: Depression in adults: treatment and management (NICE guideline NG222)
citation.venue: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence

verification.checked_against: Official NICE NG222 web pages read 23 Oct 2026: Recommendations chapter (Table 1, Table 2, recs 1.5.2, 1.5.3, 1.8.5, 1.8.6, 1.8.8), Rationale and impact chapter, Update information chapter, History page
verification.problems: Relapse-prevention population is overgeneralised. Rec 1.8.5 covers only people who remitted on antidepressant medication alone and are assessed as at higher risk of relapse. For them NICE says to consider continuing the antidepressant, OR group CBT/MBCT for those who do not wish to continue it, OR both. People who remitted with psychological therapy fall under rec 1.8.8 (discuss continuing their therapy). The claim's 'people in remission at higher risk of relapse ... group CBT or MBCT can be considered' drops this restriction. Rec 1.8.6 also requires an explicit relapse-prevention focus and allows more sessions over the next 12 months. Minor: finding_zh drops 'implementation factors' from the ordering criterion. Useful context was also omitted: the committee's rationale rates the effectiveness evidence for group mindfulness as 'some evidence' (vs 'good evidence' for group CBT/BA) and recommends it as an alternative for people who do not want CBT/BA. Everything else matches the current page verbatim: the 29 June 2022 publication date, 11 options, the 7th position and the options ranked above it, the guided-self-help-first advice (rec 1.5.2), the delivery details (preferably 2 practitioners, MBCT-type programme, 8 sessions, 8-15 participants, homework with recordings), the 'may be difficult...' caution, and its absence from Table 2. Minor amendments since publication (Sept 2024, Oct 2025, Dec 2025) do not touch the mindfulness entries.

claims.topic: MBCT for prevention of depressive relapse
claims.finding: Individual patient data meta-analysis of 9 RCTs (1,258 patients with recurrent depression in full or partial remission; mean age 47.1; 75% female) of manualised MBCT vs at least one non-MBCT condition (usual care or active treatment). Within a 60-week follow-up, MBCT reduced the risk of depressive relapse versus all non-MBCT conditions (HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.58–0.82; I² 1.7%). It also reduced risk versus active treatments (maintenance antidepressants or cognitive psychological education; 5 trials; HR 0.79, 0.64–0.97) and versus maintenance antidepressants alone (4 trials; HR 0.77, 0.60–0.98). The protective effect diminished over the course of follow-up (time-varying hazard ratio). The authors describe the moderator analyses as exploratory and not formally powered. In them, age, sex, education, relationship status, age at onset and number of previous episodes showed no statistically significant interaction with treatment, while higher baseline depressive symptoms were associated with a larger MBCT benefit.
claims.finding_zh: 个体患者数据荟萃分析（9 项随机对照试验，1258 名处于完全或部分缓解期的复发性抑郁患者，平均 47.1 岁，75% 为女性）：在 60 周随访期内，与所有未接受正念认知疗法（MBCT）的对照（常规照护或其他积极治疗）相比，MBCT 组抑郁复发风险更低（HR 0.69，95% CI 0.58–0.82）；与积极治疗（维持抗抑郁药或认知心理教育，5 项试验）相比也更低（HR 0.79，0.64–0.97）；单独与维持抗抑郁药相比（4 项试验）为 HR 0.77（0.60–0.98）。这种保护作用在随访期间逐渐减弱。在作者称为探索性、未专门计算统计效力的调节分析中，年龄、性别、教育、婚恋状况、发病年龄和既往发作次数都没有发现与疗效有统计学上显著的交互作用；治疗前抑郁症状较重的人，MBCT 相对其他治疗的获益可能更大。
claims.sample: 9 RCTs, 1,258 patients
claims.limitations: Applies to manualised, group, therapist-led MBCT for people with recurrent depression in remission, not to self-guided apps or to people in a current episode. Most authors were investigators on the included trials, which were largely run by MBCT proponents (possible allegiance bias). The funnel plot was asymmetric, suggesting small negative studies may be missing. Moderator analyses were exploratory. English-language publications only. One eligible trial did not provide IPD. Adverse events were not systematically recorded.
claims.app_implication: This evidence supports therapist-led MBCT courses for preventing relapse in recurrent depression that is in remission; it does not support self-guided app content as a relapse-prevention treatment. The app may include MBCT-derived practices but must not call itself MBCT or claim relapse prevention. Signpost users with a history of recurrent depression to MBCT courses run by trained teachers and to their clinician, and never suggest using the app instead of prescribed antidepressants.

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; PubMed abstract (PMID 27119968); PMC6640038 full text via NCBI efetch (methods, risk of bias, results incl. ADM-only comparison and time-varying effect, moderator analyses, discussion and limitations); doi.org resolution
verification.problems: Metadata and all numbers are correct (9 RCTs, 1,258 patients, mean age 47.1, 75% female, HR 0.69 [0.58–0.82], HR 0.79 [0.64–0.97]). Problems: (1) finding_zh turns non-significant interactions into '都不影响效果' (have no effect), which overstates a null; it also omits relationship status. (2) The severity moderation is stated without the authors' hedge. The abstract says 'some evidence to suggest', and the paper calls the moderator analyses exploratory and not formally powered, with type I error risk. The Chinese '获益越大' presents it as established. (3) Omitted caveats: the protective effect diminished over follow-up (time-varying HR); the funnel plot was asymmetric; trials were largely conducted by MBCT proponents and most authors were trial investigators. Also omitted: versus maintenance antidepressants alone, HR 0.77 (0.60–0.98; 4 trials). (4) app_implication 'The only well-established clinical use of mindfulness in depression' is not something this source assesses; reworded.

claims.topic: Mindfulness apps for depression and anxiety: updated meta-analysis
claims.finding: Preregistered (CRD42023414171) random-effects meta-analysis of 45 RCTs (43 papers) of mindfulness apps. Versus control conditions (waitlist or active non-therapeutic controls), small significant post-test effects for depression (46 comparisons, N=5,852, g=0.24, 95% CI 0.17-0.31, NNT=13.57, I2=32%) and anxiety (48 comparisons, N=6,082, g=0.28, 0.21-0.35, NNT=11.47, I2=44%). Effects were not explained by deterioration in control groups and held under trim-and-fill. They remained similar when restricted to lower-risk-of-bias trials (depression g=0.29) and larger trials (depression g=0.31). Sample type, follow-up length, app, control type and researcher contact did not moderate effects. Trials offering monetary compensation showed larger depression effects, which the authors judged likely spurious given the number of tests. Versus active therapeutic comparisons, effects were small and non-significant (depression: 3 comparisons, N=181, g=-0.15; anxiety: 4 comparisons, N=235, g=0.10).
claims.finding_zh: 对 45 项正念 App 随机对照试验的预注册荟萃分析：与对照组（等待名单或非治疗性对照）相比，练习结束时抑郁症状小幅下降（g = 0.24，95% CI 0.17–0.31，需治疗人数 NNT ≈ 14），焦虑症状小幅下降（g = 0.28，95% CI 0.21–0.35，NNT ≈ 11）；只看偏倚风险较低或样本较大的试验，结果仍相近。与其他积极治疗（如面对面咨询、行为激活 App）相比没有显著差异（抑郁 g = −0.15，焦虑 g = 0.10），但这类试验只有 3–4 项、样本小。给受试者报酬的试验在抑郁上效应更大，但作者认为这很可能是多次检验造成的偶然结果。
claims.sample: 45 RCTs (43 papers); depression 46 comparisons, N=5,852; anxiety 48 comparisons, N=6,082
claims.limitations: Effects measured only at post-test (10 days to 8 weeks), so durability is unknown. Risk of bias was considerable in many trials (only 4 of 45 met all five Cochrane criteria). Samples were mostly non-clinical (students, general adults). About half the trials used waitlist controls. Only 3-4 small trials compared apps with active therapies. The authors flag possible conflicts of interest in Headspace trials. Few trials reported remission, reliable change or deterioration.
claims.app_implication: Canonical in-app statement for depression and anxiety: small short-term improvements of about 0.2-0.3 SD, shown mainly against waitlist or non-therapeutic controls. Put another way, about 11-14 people need to use the app for one extra person to improve. There is no evidence that apps outperform other active treatments, and too few trials to say they are as good. Do not claim long-term effects.

citation.authors: Linardon J, Messer M, Goldberg SB, et al.
citation.title: The efficacy of mindfulness apps on symptoms of depression and anxiety: An updated meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; Europe PMC/PubMed abstract; PMC author-manuscript full text (PMC10872959): Methods, Results, subgroup analyses, Discussion and limitations
verification.problems: Metadata correct (Clin Psychol Rev 2024;107:102370; PMID 38056219; 4th author Fuller-Tyszkiewicz M). All numbers in finding match the abstract and full text. Full text adds I2=32% (depression) and 44% (anxiety); active therapeutic comparisons were 3 comparisons/N=181 (depression) and 4/N=235 (anxiety). evidence_weight 'high' is overstated: the authors say risk of bias was 'considerable in many of the included trials' (only 4/45 met all five Cochrane criteria). Effects were post-test only (10 days to 8 weeks), samples mostly non-clinical, and about half the trials used waitlist controls; 'moderate' fits. The authors judged the monetary-compensation moderator 'likely a spurious finding given the number of tests performed', but finding_zh, the limitations and the app_implication use it without that caveat. The app_implication's 'not better than other active treatments' overstates a non-significant result from 3-4 small trials. That is absence of evidence, not shown equivalence or inferiority.

claims.topic: MBSR vs escitalopram for diagnosed anxiety disorders
claims.finding: Noninferiority RCT (TAME) at 3 US academic medical centres with blinded clinical interviewers: 276 adults with a diagnosed anxiety disorder randomised to 8 weeks of in-person MBSR (weekly 2.5-hour classes, a day-long retreat, 45-minute daily home practice) or escitalopram flexibly dosed 10–20 mg; 208 completed (per-protocol: 102 MBSR, 106 escitalopram). CGI-S fell by 1.35 (SD 1.06) with MBSR and 1.43 (SD 1.17) with escitalopram; difference −0.07 (95% CI −0.38 to 0.23; P=.65), within the prespecified noninferiority margin of −0.495; intent-to-treat analyses also showed noninferiority. At least one study-related adverse event occurred in 78.6% randomised to escitalopram vs 15.4% randomised to MBSR; 10 (8%) dropped out of escitalopram because of adverse events vs none from MBSR.
claims.finding_zh: 非劣效随机对照试验（美国 3 个学术医疗中心，评估者设盲）：276 名确诊焦虑障碍的成人被随机分到 8 周线下 MBSR 课程（每周 2.5 小时课、1 天静修、每天 45 分钟居家练习）或艾司西酞普兰（10–20 mg），208 人完成。临床总体印象-严重度（CGI-S）评分在 MBSR 组下降 1.35，在药物组下降 1.43，组间差 −0.07（95% CI −0.38 至 0.23），落在预设的非劣效界值（−0.495）之内，即 MBSR 不劣于药物。至少出现一次研究相关不良事件的比例：药物组 78.6%，MBSR 组 15.4%。
claims.sample: n=276 randomised; 208 per-protocol
claims.limitations: Single trial; no placebo or waitlist arm; enrolment stopped at 276 because of COVID-19; intensive in-person teacher-led MBSR (2.5 h/week plus 45 min/day), far beyond typical app use; people willing to be randomised to meditation may favour non-drug options.
claims.app_implication: Never imply the app replaces anxiety treatment: the noninferior intervention was a clinician-grade, in-person 8-week course with 45 min/day home practice. The app may cite this trial only to say that structured mindfulness courses are a credible treatment option to discuss with a clinician.

citation.authors: Hoge EA, Bui E, Mete M, et al.
citation.title: Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction vs Escitalopram for the Treatment of Adults With Anxiety Disorders: A Randomized Clinical Trial

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; PubMed abstract (PMID 36350591); PMC9647561 full-text HTML (interventions, sample size and COVID stop, results, adverse events, limitations); doi.org resolution
verification.problems: None found. Metadata is correct (JAMA Psychiatry 2023;80(1):13-21; online 9 Nov 2022). The full text confirms: 3 US academic sites; blinded raters; 276 randomised and 208 per-protocol (102/106); MBSR with weekly 2.5 h classes, a day-long retreat and 45 min daily home practice; escitalopram 10–20 mg; CGI-S −1.35 vs −1.43, difference −0.07 (−0.38 to 0.23; P=.65), margin −0.495; ITT also noninferior; AEs 78.6% vs 15.4%; 10 (8%) escitalopram AE dropouts vs none; enrolment stopped at 276 because of COVID-19. Non-blocking notes the app may want to add: the most common MBSR-related adverse event was increased anxiety (n=13, 11%); there were no serious adverse events; the sample size had been planned on a stricter −0.33 margin (target 368), and the −0.495 margin was confirmed with the DSMB after the COVID stop; arms were not matched for time or attention and participants were unblinded; the authors state that in-person delivery limits extrapolation to apps.

claims.topic: Umbrella review of mindfulness-based interventions by comparator type
claims.finding: Systematic review of 44 meta-analyses of RCTs (k=336 unique RCTs, N=30,483; 160 effect sizes). Versus passive controls (e.g., waitlist), MBIs were superior across most populations, problems, interventions and outcomes (ds 0.10–0.89 at post-treatment). Significant population effects ranged from d=0.10 (children/adolescents) to d=0.55 (adults). Exceptions were older adults, substance use disorders, and objective/physiological measures. Versus active controls, effects were smaller and less often significant. At post-treatment MBIs were superior for mindfulness, stress and psychiatric symptoms (ds 0.16–0.25) but not for sleep, physical-health symptoms, objective measures or physiological measures (ds −0.03 to 0.16). At follow-up only the advantage for psychiatric symptoms was sustained (d=0.29), with no difference for physical health, mindfulness, stress or sleep (ds −0.14 to 0.18). Versus evidence-based treatments (CBT, antidepressants; 11 effect sizes), MBIs did not differ at post-treatment for any category except smoking, where MBIs were superior (d=0.42; other estimates d=−0.18 to 0.02). At follow-up they mostly did not differ, except that MBCT was superior for preventing depressive relapse (d=0.17). Heterogeneity was typically moderate and few consistent moderators were found. Results were generally robust to publication bias, although other important sources of bias were identified. Adverse effects were discussed in only 34% of meta-analyses, and power was limited for active-control comparisons. 52.7% of primary studies were from North America, 28.0% from Europe and 8.1% from Asia.
claims.finding_zh: 对 44 项随机对照试验荟萃分析的伞状综述（共 336 项试验、30,483 人、160 个效应量）。与被动对照（如等待名单）相比，正念干预在大多数人群、问题、干预类型和结局上更好（治疗结束时 d = 0.10–0.89），各人群中有统计学意义的效应从儿童青少年的 0.10 到成人的 0.55；老年人、物质使用障碍以及客观/生理指标未显示显著差异。与积极对照相比，效应更小，也更少达到显著：治疗结束时在正念水平、压力和精神症状上占优（d = 0.16–0.25），在睡眠、躯体症状、客观指标和生理指标上不占优（d = −0.03 至 0.16）；到随访时只剩精神症状上的优势（d = 0.29），压力、正念、睡眠和躯体健康都没有差异（d = −0.14 至 0.18）。与循证治疗（认知行为疗法、抗抑郁药；共 11 个效应量）相比，治疗结束时除戒烟外（正念更好，d = 0.42）都没有差异（d = −0.18 至 0.02）；随访时大多没有差异，但正念认知疗法（MBCT）在预防抑郁复发上优于循证治疗（d = 0.17）。异质性一般为中等，很少找到稳定的调节因素；结果对发表偏倚总体稳健，但存在其他重要偏倚；只有 34% 的荟萃分析讨论了不良反应；与积极对照比较的统计效力可能不足。原始研究 52.7% 来自北美，28.0% 来自欧洲，只有 8.1% 来自亚洲。
claims.study_type: umbrella review (systematic review of meta-analyses of RCTs)
claims.sample: 44 meta-analyses; 336 RCTs; 30,483 participants
claims.limitations: Primary studies overlap heavily across meta-analyses, so no second-order meta-analysis was possible. Meta-analysis quality was not coded and certainty was not formally graded. In no risk-of-bias domain were primary studies consistently rated low risk. Representative effect sizes came from the largest meta-analysis per category, some based on only 4 trials. Statistical power was low for active-control and evidence-based-treatment comparisons. Few Asian samples (8.1%), so applicability to Chinese-speaking users is uncertain.
claims.app_implication: Every benefit statement must name its comparator. Versus doing nothing: typically small-to-moderate. Versus other active approaches: small or none, and by follow-up mainly for psychiatric symptoms. Versus CBT or medication: no evidence of a difference, based on few, underpowered comparisons, so present mindfulness as one reasonable option, not a superior one. Do not promise sleep, physical-health or physiological effects from general mindfulness content. Disclose that the evidence base is mostly Western.

citation.authors: Goldberg SB, Riordan KM, Sun S, et al.
citation.title: The Empirical Status of Mindfulness-Based Interventions: A Systematic Review of 44 Meta-Analyses of Randomized Controlled Trials

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; PubMed abstract (PMID 33593124); PMC8364929 full text via NCBI efetch (method, study characteristics, results by comparator and timepoint, risk of bias, adverse effects, limitations); doi.org resolution
verification.problems: Metadata is correct (online 16 Feb 2021; print 2022;17(1):108-130). Every quoted number was confirmed in the full text: 44 meta-analyses, k=336, N=30,483, 160 ES, passive ds 0.10–0.89, d=0.10 children to 0.55 adults, active ds 0.16–0.25 and −0.03 to 0.16, EBT smoking d=0.42 and others −0.18 to 0.02, 52.7% North America, 8.1% Asia. Problems: (1) The active-control and evidence-based-treatment (EBT) results are post-treatment only, but the claim does not say so. 'Did not differ for any category except smoking' is therefore incomplete: at follow-up MBCT was superior to EBTs for preventing depressive relapse (d=0.17). Versus active controls at follow-up only psychiatric symptoms stayed superior (d=0.29), while stress and mindfulness no longer differed (ds −0.14 to 0.18). (2) evidence_weight 'high' is not supported. The authors did not code meta-analysis quality or grade certainty, no risk-of-bias domain was consistently low risk, power was limited for active comparisons, and the authors conclude only that MBIs 'show promise'. Changed to moderate. (3) app_implication 'versus CBT or medication, no difference' overstates a non-significant result based on 11 effect sizes.

claims.topic: Mindfulness-based programmes and objective cognitive function
claims.finding: Systematic review and meta-analysis of objective cognitive outcomes from randomised MBP studies in adults (search to January 2020; PROSPERO CRD42018100904): 56 studies (n=2,931), of which 45 (n=2,238) were synthesised with robust variance estimation. The overall effect across cognitive domains favoured MBPs but was small (g=0.15, 95% CI 0.05–0.24). By domain, MBPs outperformed comparators only for executive function (g=0.15, 0.02–0.27) and working memory (g=0.23, 0.11–0.36). MBPs outperformed inactive but not active comparators. Within-study risk of bias was mostly unclear.
claims.finding_zh: 对成人正念课程客观认知测验结果的系统综述与荟萃分析：56 项随机研究（2931 人），其中 45 项（2238 人）进入合并分析。总体效应偏向正念，但很小（g = 0.15，95% CI 0.05–0.24）。分领域看，只有执行功能（g = 0.15）和工作记忆（g = 0.23）有显著改善。正念课程优于不干预对照，但不优于积极对照。多数研究的偏倚风险不明确。
claims.study_type: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized studies
claims.sample: 56 studies, 2931 participants (45 studies, 2238 participants pooled)
claims.limitations: Mostly unclear risk of bias; many different cognitive tests pooled; the authors note statistical constraints made some p-values unreliable.
claims.app_implication: Do not market 提升专注力 or 提升记忆力. At most say that some studies find small improvements in working memory and executive function, mainly compared with doing nothing. Keep attention claims modest even when citing small positive RCTs.

citation.authors: Whitfield T, Barnhofer T, Acabchuk R, et al.
citation.title: The Effect of Mindfulness-based Programs on Cognitive Function in Adults: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; PubMed abstract (PMID 34350544); PMC9381612 full text (eligibility criteria, Table 2 domain results, comparator subgroup analyses, risk-of-bias section)
verification.problems: No discrepancies found. The metadata (2022 print issue 32(3):677-702, epub Aug 2021), the search to January 2020, PROSPERO CRD42018100904, 56 studies/2,931, 45 studies/2,238, g 0.15 [0.05, 0.24], executive function g 0.15 [0.02, 0.27], working memory g 0.23 [0.11, 0.36], inactive-but-not-active comparators, and mostly unclear risk of bias all match. Context notes, not errors: eligible MBPs were in-person, facilitator-led group programmes of at least 4 sessions, so app-based practice was not studied. Attention did not improve (g 0.12, -0.02 to 0.26). Working memory is a subdomain of executive function. Versus active comparators g 0.07 [-0.04, 0.19]; versus inactive comparators (mostly waitlist, some usual care or no intervention) g 0.20 [0.06, 0.33]. 'Inactive' is slightly broader than the zh wording 不干预对照.

claims.topic: Mindfulness meditation apps: stress, anxiety, depression and well-being
claims.finding: Meta-analysis of 34 RCTs (N=7,566; search to June 2020) in which a mindfulness meditation app was the main intervention; post-test Hedges' g versus control conditions, random effects. Significant effects: perceived stress g=0.46 (95% CI 0.24-0.68; I2=68%; 15 trials), anxiety 0.28 (0.16-0.40; I2=35%; 15 trials), depression 0.33 (0.24-0.43; I2=0%; 15 trials), psychological well-being 0.29 (0.14-0.45; I2=0%; 5 trials). No significant effects on distress (g=0.10, -0.02 to 0.22; I2=11%; 6 trials) or general well-being (g=0.14, -0.02 to 0.29; I2=14%; 5 trials). The authors call apps promising but say results should be interpreted carefully given the small number of included studies, overall uncertain risk of bias and heterogeneity.
claims.finding_zh: 对 34 项以正念冥想 App 为主要干预的随机对照试验（7566 人，检索至 2020 年 6 月）的荟萃分析。练习结束时与对照组相比：感知压力下降（g = 0.46，95% CI 0.24–0.68，但各试验结果差异大，I² = 68%）；焦虑（g = 0.28）、抑郁（g = 0.33，各试验结果一致）和心理幸福感（g = 0.29）小幅改善；心理困扰（g = 0.10）和一般幸福感（g = 0.14）没有显著变化。作者提醒，纳入研究少、偏倚风险总体不明、结果有异质性，需谨慎解读。
claims.limitations: Effects estimated at post-test only. Only 5-15 trials per outcome. Overall uncertain risk of bias. High heterogeneity for perceived stress (I2=68%). The search ended June 2020; for depression and anxiety it is superseded by Linardon et al. 2024 (45 RCTs). Control-condition types were not verified because the full text was not accessed.
claims.app_implication: Describe app effects on depression (g about 0.33, consistent across trials) and anxiety (g about 0.28) as small. Perceived stress had the largest average effect (g about 0.46) but varied widely between trials, so word it as 'may reduce stress somewhat; results vary between studies', not as the best-established benefit. Do not claim that app use reduces general distress or general well-being, which were non-significant here.

citation.authors: Gál É, Ștefan S, Cristea IA
citation.title: The efficacy of mindfulness meditation apps in enhancing users' well-being and mental health related outcomes: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; Europe PMC/PubMed abstract (PMID 33049431). Full text paywalled (ScienceDirect, Padua and Pavia repositories blocked by Cloudflare), not read
verification.problems: Metadata correct (J Affect Disord 2021;279:131-142; PMID 33049431). Every number in finding and finding_zh matches the abstract exactly. The app_implication overstates: it calls perceived stress 'the outcome with the best app-specific evidence'. Stress had the largest pooled effect but also the highest heterogeneity (I2=68%) and the widest CI (0.24-0.68), while depression (I2=0%) was the most consistent. The larger, newer synthesis (Linardon 2024, 45 RCTs) covers depression and anxiety, not stress. The limitation 'many inactive controls' could not be verified (full text inaccessible); it is replaced with limitations the abstract supports. evidence_weight 'moderate' is acceptable given the authors' own caveats.

claims.topic: Dose-response of mindfulness-based programmes across RCTs
claims.finding: Dose-response meta-regression of RCTs of mindfulness-based programmes (MBPs): 203 studies (N=15,971). Depression was the primary outcome (post-programme and follow-up); mindfulness, anxiety and stress were secondary. Doses examined were session number, duration and length, facilitator contact and practice; programme intensity and actual programme use also appear in the results. Analyses were run separately for inactive and active controls. Initial meta-analyses found significant between-group differences favouring MBPs on all outcomes. However, the majority of dose-response results for psychological outcomes, including depression, were not significant. Significant dose-response relationships were reported for mindfulness with face-to-face contact (d=0.211, 95% CI 0.064-0.358), programme intensity (d=0.895, 0.315-1.474) and actual programme use (d=0.013, 0.001-0.024). These are meta-regression coefficients (change in effect size per unit or category of dose); the abstract does not state the units. The author concluded there was no evidence that larger doses are more helpful than smaller doses for psychological outcomes, while greater contact, intensity and actual use predicted higher mindfulness.
claims.finding_zh: 对正念课程随机对照试验的剂量-反应元回归：203 项研究（15,971 人）。主要结局为抑郁（课程结束时及随访），次要结局为正念、焦虑和压力。考察的“剂量”包括课程次数与时长、与带领者的接触和练习量，结果中还分析了课程强度和实际使用量；对无干预对照和积极对照分别分析。初步元分析显示，课程在所有结局上都优于对照。但在抑郁等心理结局上，大多数剂量-反应结果不显著，作者认为没有证据表明剂量越大对心理结局的帮助越大。摘要中报告的显著剂量-反应关系出现在“正念水平”上：面授接触（d = 0.211，95% CI 0.064–0.358）、课程强度（d = 0.895，0.315–1.474）和实际使用量（d = 0.013，0.001–0.024）。也就是说，接触越多、强度越高、实际使用越多，正念提升越大。这些数字是元回归系数，即剂量每变化一个单位或类别时效应量的变化，摘要未说明单位。
claims.limitations: Dose-response is inferred from between-study comparisons, which are observational and confounded by population, programme and design. Non-significant meta-regression results may reflect low power or poorly reported dose, and are not evidence that dose does not matter. The included trials were mostly multi-week MBPs, so the dose range does not establish a minimum effective dose or speak to 10-min app sessions. It is a single-author review. Only the abstract was available (subscription article), so the coding and units of dose variables, and which control-type analyses produced the significant results, could not be checked.
claims.app_implication: Do not tell users that longer or more sessions bring larger mood benefits: across MBP trials, dose did not reliably predict depression, anxiety or stress outcomes. Do not present this as proof that a 10-min default is as effective as longer practice. The evidence is between-trial and ecological, it covers multi-week programmes rather than brief app sessions, and frequency versus duration was not tested. Frame 10 min as a sustainable starting point.

citation.authors: Strohmaier S
citation.title: The Relationship Between Doses of Mindfulness-Based Programs and Depression, Anxiety, Stress, and Mindfulness: a Dose-Response Meta-Regression of Randomized Controlled Trials

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata (Mindfulness 11(6):1315-1335, single author Sarah Strohmaier, online 2 Mar 2020); PubMed DOI and title searches (no record, so the empty PMID is correct); abstract on the Springer article page read via WebFetch, with targeted quotes of the Methods, Results and Conclusions sentences. Full text is subscription-only and was not read.
verification.problems: Metadata, sample (203 RCTs, N=15,971), outcomes and all three d values with CIs match the abstract. (1) finding_zh says '只有' (only) mindfulness showed dose-response relationships. The abstract says only that the 'majority' of psychological-outcome dose-response results were non-significant, so 'only' overstates it. (2) The d values are meta-regression coefficients (the change in effect size per unit or category of each dose variable), not standalone effect sizes; this is unexplained and could mislead lay readers. (3) Minor: the abstract's Methods list is 'session numbers, duration and length, facilitator contact and practice'; intensity appears only in the Results. Separate analyses for inactive and active controls were omitted. (4) app_implication over-reaches. A null between-trial meta-regression of multi-week MBPs cannot show that 'a modest 10-min default is not expected to sacrifice benefit', and the review did not compare frequency with duration. (5) Only the abstract could be checked.

claims.topic: Mindfulness meditation and sleep quality
claims.finding: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 18 RCTs (1,654 participants; searches to May 2018) in adults with clinically significant sleep disturbance (insomnia diagnosis or above-threshold scores on sleep questionnaires). The interventions were in-person, structured, multi-session mindfulness meditation programmes (MBSR 9/18, MBCT 3/18, mind-body bridging 3/18); internet-delivered interventions were excluded. Only active comparators were included, and the two comparator types were analysed separately. Versus nonspecific active controls matched for time and attention (11 trials, 939 participants), mindfulness meditation improved sleep quality at post-intervention (Hedges' g 0.33, 95% CI 0.17-0.48) and at 5-12-month follow-up (g 0.54, 0.24-0.84; only 3 trials, 341 participants), with moderate strength of evidence. Versus specific active controls, i.e. evidence-based sleep treatments (7 trials, 716 participants), there was low-strength evidence of no difference at post-intervention (g -0.03, -0.49 to 0.43, per the forest plot and results text; the abstract prints 0.03, -0.43 to 0.49) and at follow-up (g -0.14, -0.62 to 0.34; 4 trials). Heterogeneity was high (I2 88% and 84%), driven by a single CBT-I trial. Sleep quality was mostly self-reported (PSQI, ISI and MOS-SS pooled), and only 2 trials used actigraphy. Of the 10 trials reporting adverse events, none showed increased harm.
claims.finding_zh: 系统综述与荟萃分析，纳入 18 项随机对照试验（1654 人，检索至 2018 年 5 月），对象是有明显睡眠障碍的成年人（确诊失眠，或睡眠问卷得分超过临界值）。干预都是线下、结构化、多次课的正念冥想课程（MBSR 9 项、MBCT 3 项、身心桥接 3 项），排除了网络形式的干预。只纳入有积极对照的试验，两类对照分开分析。与时间和关注度匹配的一般性对照相比（11 项试验，939 人），正念冥想改善了睡眠质量：干预后效应量 g = 0.33（95% CI 0.17–0.48），5–12 个月随访时 g = 0.54（0.24–0.84，仅 3 项试验、341 人），证据强度中等。与有循证依据的睡眠治疗等特定积极对照相比（7 项试验，716 人），结果是没有差异，但证据强度低：干预后 g = −0.03（−0.49 至 0.43，依据森林图和正文；摘要误印为 0.03，−0.43 至 0.49），随访时 g = −0.14（−0.62 至 0.34，4 项试验）。这一比较的异质性很高（I² 为 88% 和 84%），主要来自一项失眠认知行为疗法（CBT-I）试验。睡眠质量多为自评（PSQI、ISI、MOS-SS 合并），只有 2 项试验用了活动记录仪。报告了不良事件的 10 项试验中，没有发现伤害风险增加。
claims.study_type: systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs
claims.sample: 18 RCTs, 1654 participants (7 RCTs/716 vs specific active controls; 11 RCTs/939 vs nonspecific active controls)
claims.limitations: Evidence comes from in-person programmes lasting 2-16 weeks in adults with clinically significant sleep disturbance. Internet and app delivery were excluded, so the effect of app audio, or of use by people without sleep problems, is untested here. Outcomes were mostly self-reported and pooled across different scales. Follow-up estimates rest on 3-4 trials. The comparison with evidence-based sleep treatments is imprecise and heterogeneous; one CBT-I trial had 50% attrition in its MBSR arm. Most trials had moderate risk of bias, with allocation concealment and intervention credibility often not addressed. The abstract and forest plot disagree on the sign of one estimate.
claims.app_implication: A bedtime mindfulness track can be offered with cautious copy, e.g. 'structured mindfulness courses have modestly improved self-rated sleep quality in adults with sleep problems'. Do not claim the app's tracks have been shown to improve sleep, and do not suggest they match or replace established insomnia treatment such as CBT-I. Signpost professional insomnia care for persistent insomnia.

citation.authors: Rusch HL, Rosario M, Levison LM, et al.
citation.title: The effect of mindfulness meditation on sleep quality: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
citation.venue: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; PubMed abstract (PMID 30575050); PMC6557693 author-manuscript full text including Table 1 inclusion criteria, results text and the Fig. 3 / Fig. 4 forest plots
verification.problems: (1) Wrong effect size: the post-treatment estimate vs specific active controls is -0.03 (95% CI -0.49 to 0.43) in the Fig. 3 forest plot and the results text. The abstract misprints it as 0.03 (-0.43 to 0.49), and the claim copied the abstract. The null interpretation is unchanged. (2) Population omitted: only adults with clinically significant sleep disturbance (insomnia diagnosis or above-threshold sleep-questionnaire scores) were eligible. (3) Delivery mode omitted: only in-person structured programmes were included (MBSR 9/18, MBCT 3/18, mind-body bridging 3/18), and internet-delivered interventions were explicitly excluded. The app_implication extrapolates to an app bedtime track for general users without flagging this. (4) The follow-up estimate of 0.54 vs nonspecific controls rests on only 3 trials (341 participants); follow-up vs specific controls rests on 4 trials. (5) Heterogeneity in the specific-control comparison was high (I2 88%/84%), driven by one CBT-I trial. Metadata are correct (print June 2019, epub Dec 2018; DOI, PMID, authors). All other numbers are correct (18 RCTs, 1654 participants, 0.33 [0.17-0.48], 0.54 [0.24-0.84], -0.14 [-0.62 to 0.34], strength-of-evidence grades).

claims.topic: Acceptance as an active ingredient of mindfulness training (dismantling RCTs)
claims.finding: Two dismantling RCTs in stressed community adults. Study 1 (n=137; preregistered NCT02502227): 8-week group MBSR teaching monitoring plus acceptance (MA) vs an adapted MBSR teaching monitoring only (MO) vs no treatment. Study 2 (n=153; preregistered NCT02433431): 14 daily 20-minute smartphone audio lessons (about 5 min didactics, 12.5 min guided practice including 7 min silence, 2.5 min home-practice instruction) plus 3–10 min/day unguided practice; MA vs MO vs a structurally matched active coping control. Affect was measured in daily life for 3 days before and after training. End-of-day positive affect rose more after MA than after MO (g=0.40 in Study 1, g=0.46 in Study 2) and than after control (g=0.73 and 0.71); MO did not differ from control on this measure. For momentary positive affect, MA beat MO in Study 2 (g=0.41) but not in Study 1 (g=0.22, p=.263), and in Study 1 MO also increased momentary positive affect compared with no treatment (g=0.68). Negative affect fell over time, but mindfulness showed no specific advantage. In Study 2 it fell with no difference between the three arms, including the coping control. In Study 1, momentary negative affect fell similarly in all groups, including no treatment, and only MA reduced end-of-day negative affect more than no treatment (g=0.66).
claims.finding_zh: 两项“拆解式”随机对照试验，对象为压力较大的社区成人，均已预注册。研究 1（137 人）：8 周团体 MBSR，分为“觉察+接纳”、“仅觉察”和不干预三组。研究 2（153 人）：14 天手机音频课，每天 20 分钟（约 5 分钟讲解、12.5 分钟引导练习（含 7 分钟静默）、2.5 分钟课后练习说明），另加每天 3–10 分钟自主练习，分为“觉察+接纳”、“仅觉察”和结构相同的“应对技巧”对照组。练习前后各 3 天在日常生活中测量情绪。每晚自评的积极情绪：两项研究中，“觉察+接纳”组的提升都显著多于“仅觉察”组（g = 0.40；0.46）和对照组（g = 0.73；0.71），“仅觉察”组与对照组没有差异。白天随时自评的积极情绪：研究 2 结果相同（对“仅觉察” g = 0.41）；研究 1 中两种正念组之间没有显著差异，“仅觉察”组也高于不干预组。负性情绪随时间下降，但正念训练没有特别优势：研究 2 中三组（包括应对技巧对照组）下降程度没有差异。
claims.sample: Study 1 n=137; Study 2 n=153 stressed community adults (Pittsburgh, USA)
claims.limitations: Single research group. Affect outcomes were secondary to the trials' stress outcomes (stated explicitly for Study 2), and were measured over 3 days right after training with no long-term follow-up. Study 1 used a no-treatment control and group classes with instructors not fully blind, so acceptance themes could leak into MO. Participants were paid for adherence. One author (Shinzen Young) has a financial interest in a commercial app based on the Study 2 Monitor+Accept programme. Participants were self-selected, stressed, relatively well-educated US smartphone owners.
claims.app_implication: Guided scripts should teach acceptance explicitly (允许, 不评判, 不需要改变它), not only attention monitoring, if the goal is more positive feeling in daily life. Do not claim that mindfulness reduces negative emotions more than other structured stress-coping practice: in the actively controlled trial it did not. The 14-day smartphone format (20-min lessons with explanation, guided practice and silence) is a tested template for a 2-week starter course.

citation.authors: Lindsay EK, Chin B, Greco CM, et al.
citation.title: How mindfulness training promotes positive emotions: Dismantling acceptance skills training in two randomized controlled trials
citation.venue: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata + PubMed abstract (including the COI statement) + PMC full text (PMC6296247, via NCBI efetch): methods, results and limitations of both studies
verification.problems: Metadata, sample sizes, NCT02433431, the Study 2 lesson structure and every quoted effect size are correct. (1) 'MO did not differ from control' is overgeneralised. It holds for end-of-day positive affect in both studies and momentary positive affect in Study 2. In Study 1, MO increased momentary positive affect more than no treatment (g=0.68, p=.004), and MA vs MO on momentary positive affect was not significant (g=0.22, p=.263). (2) 'All active interventions decreased negative affect' is misleading. These were pre-post decreases with no specific benefit of mindfulness. In Study 2, negative affect fell equally in the coping control (no group × time interaction). In Study 1, momentary negative affect fell similarly in the no-treatment group, and MO did not beat no-treatment on end-of-day negative affect. The Chinese '积极干预' will read to lay users as 'positive interventions'. (3) Left out: Study 1 was also preregistered (NCT02502227); the affect outcomes were secondary outcomes of trials powered for stress (stated for Study 2); and an author (Shinzen Young) declared a stake in a company releasing a commercial app based on the Study 2 Monitor+Accept programme.

claims.topic: AHA statement on meditation and cardiovascular risk
claims.finding: American Heart Association scientific statement reviewing studies of meditation and cardiovascular risk: physiological stress response, smoking cessation, blood pressure, insulin resistance and metabolic syndrome, endothelial function, inducible myocardial ischaemia, and primary and secondary prevention. The authors call it a systematic review, but the searches covered only PubMed plus Google and Google Scholar, and there was no meta-analysis and no formal class or level-of-evidence rating. Studies suggest a possible benefit on cardiovascular risk, although the overall quality and in some cases quantity of data are modest. The statement also flags possible publication bias, investigator allegiance, and reliance on a few research groups. Given low cost and low risk, meditation 'may be considered as an adjunct to guideline-directed cardiovascular risk reduction by those interested in this lifestyle modification, with the understanding that the benefits of such intervention remain to be better established.'
claims.finding_zh: AHA 科学声明，回顾了冥想与心血管风险的研究，涵盖应激生理反应、戒烟、血压、胰岛素抵抗与代谢综合征、内皮功能、诱发性心肌缺血，以及一级和二级预防。作者称之为系统回顾，但检索只用了 PubMed、Google 和 Google Scholar，没有做荟萃分析，也没有给出正式的推荐级别和证据等级。结论：冥想可能对心血管风险有益，但数据质量（有时还有数量）一般。声明还指出可能存在发表偏倚和研究者偏好，而且许多研究出自少数几个团队。鉴于成本和风险都低，有兴趣的人可以考虑把冥想作为指南规范的心血管风险管理的辅助手段，同时要明白这种获益仍有待进一步确认。
claims.study_type: scientific statement (American Heart Association; narrative evidence review described by its authors as systematic; no meta-analysis or formal evidence grading)
claims.sample: review of published studies (no pooled N, no meta-analysis)
claims.limitations: No meta-analytic estimates and no formal grading of the evidence. Searches were limited to PubMed, Google and Google Scholar. Studies were heterogeneous and often small, with high dropout and frequent lack of randomisation or a suitable control. Many studies come from the same research groups, and much of the blood-pressure and hard-outcome evidence comes from Transcendental Meditation trials. Publication bias is possible. The recommendation is limited to an adjunct role. Published 2017; for blood pressure specifically, the 2025 AHA/ACC multisociety guideline gives only a weak COR 2b adjunct recommendation for TM and other stress management.
claims.app_implication: Allowed copy: 美国心脏协会（2017）认为，有兴趣的人可以考虑把冥想作为规范心血管风险管理之外的辅助手段，但其心血管获益仍有待确证。Never suggest meditation replaces antihypertensive or cardiac care.

claims.topic: Home practice amount in MBSR/MBCT and its link with outcomes
claims.finding: Systematic review and meta-analysis of formal home mindfulness practice in MBSR and MBCT (studies to end of 2015). Across 43 studies (N=1,427), participants completed 64% of the assigned home practice (95% CI 60–69%), about 30 minutes per day, six days per week, with substantial heterogeneity. Across 28 studies (N=898), self-reported home practice showed a small but significant association with intervention outcomes (r=0.26, 95% CI 0.19–0.34).
claims.finding_zh: 对 MBSR 和 MBCT 居家练习的系统综述与荟萃分析：43 项研究（1427 人）中，参与者平均完成了布置练习量的 64%（95% CI 60–69%），约为每周 6 天、每天 30 分钟；28 项研究（898 人）中，自报的居家练习量与干预效果呈小幅正相关（r = 0.26，95% CI 0.19–0.34）。
claims.sample: 43 studies (N=1427) for adherence; 28 studies (N=898) for the practice–outcome association
claims.limitations: Correlational (people who improve may practise more); self-reported practice; in-person programmes with weekly teacher contact.
claims.app_implication: Log practice days and minutes automatically and describe the practice–benefit link honestly as small and correlational. About 30 min/day on 6 days a week is what motivated course participants actually achieved: an upper reference, not an app default.

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; PubMed abstract (PMID 28527330); PMC full text (PMC5501725) via Europe PMC, including the results, publication bias and limitations sections
verification.problems: None. Every number matches the abstract and full text: 43 studies, N=1,427, 64% of assigned practice (95% CI 60-69%), about 29-30 min/day on 6 days/week, I²=89%; 28 studies, N=898, r=0.26 (95% CI 0.19-0.34), I²=17%, with the same r in RCTs only (n=15). The search ran to the end of 2015. Authors, year, title, venue, DOI and PMID are verified. Optional context: practice reports came from completers, and trim-and-fill suggested some under-reporting of practice amounts (imputed estimate 61%).

claims.topic: Meditation programs vs active (placebo-type) controls for stress-related outcomes
claims.finding: AHRQ-funded systematic review and meta-analysis of 47 RCTs (3,515 participants; search to November 2012) restricted to trials with active controls for placebo effects, in diverse adult clinical populations (programmes with a meditation teacher physically present and at least 4 hours of training). Versus nonspecific active controls, mindfulness meditation programs had moderate strength of evidence for small improvements in anxiety (effect size 0.38, 95% CI 0.12–0.64 at 8 weeks; 0.22, 0.02–0.43 at 3–6 months), depression (0.30, 0.00–0.59 at 8 weeks; 0.23, 0.05–0.42 at 3–6 months) and pain (0.33, 0.03–0.62), and low strength of evidence for improved stress/distress and mental-health-related quality of life. For positive mood, attention, substance use, eating habits, sleep and weight there was low evidence of no effect or insufficient evidence. In the 20 comparative-effectiveness trials there was no evidence that meditation programs were better than any active treatment (drugs, exercise, other behavioral therapies). These trials were small (average 37 per group) and none was powered to test noninferiority or equivalence. Mantra meditation programs, including Transcendental Meditation analysed separately, did not improve any outcome examined; strength of evidence was low to insufficient and there were very few mantra trials. None of the review's conclusions reached a high strength-of-evidence grade. MBSR programs typically provided 20–27.5 hours of training over 8 weeks; other mindfulness programs provided about half that.
claims.finding_zh: 美国医疗保健研究与质量局（AHRQ）资助的系统综述与荟萃分析：47 项随机对照试验（3515 名成人，检索截至 2012 年 11 月），只纳入设有可控制安慰剂效应的积极对照组的试验，研究对象为各类有临床问题的成人，课程由老师现场指导、训练时长至少 4 小时。与非特异性积极对照相比，正念冥想课程对焦虑（8 周时效应量 0.38，95% CI 0.12–0.64；3–6 个月时 0.22，0.02–0.43）、抑郁（8 周时 0.30，0.00–0.59；3–6 个月时 0.23，0.05–0.42）和疼痛（0.33，0.03–0.62）有小幅改善，证据强度为中等；对压力/心理困扰和心理健康相关生活质量的改善，证据强度低。对积极情绪、注意力、物质使用、饮食、睡眠和体重，要么是低强度证据显示没有效果，要么证据不足。在 20 项与其他积极治疗（药物、运动或其他行为疗法）直接比较的试验中，没有证据表明冥想更好；但这些试验规模小（平均每组 37 人），都不足以证明两者效果相当。以咒语为主的冥想（包括单独分析的超觉静坐 TM）在所有考察指标上都没有显示改善（证据强度低至不足，相关试验很少）。整篇综述没有任何结论达到“高”证据强度。MBSR 课程通常在 8 周内提供 20–27.5 小时训练，其他正念课程约为一半。
claims.study_type: systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs (active-controlled only)
claims.sample: 47 RCTs, 3515 participants
claims.limitations: Search ended in November 2012. No conclusion reached a high strength-of-evidence grade. Included trials commonly lacked blinded outcome assessment, allocation concealment and intention-to-treat analysis, and had high attrition. Very few mantra trials. Comparative-effectiveness trials were small (average 37 per group) and not powered for equivalence or noninferiority. Clinical populations, and programmes with a teacher physically present (remote, video- or audio-only programmes excluded), so generalisation to healthy app users is indirect.
claims.app_implication: Default expectation copy: small reductions in anxiety, depressive symptoms and pain (moderate-strength evidence), and possibly stress/distress (low-strength evidence), after about 8 weeks of structured, teacher-led practice. There is no evidence that meditation works better than therapy, medication or exercise. Do not claim sleep, attention, positive-mood or weight benefits on the basis of this review. Do not present mantra/TM as an evidence-based module.

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; PubMed abstract (PMID 24395196); PMC4142584 full text via NCBI efetch (methods incl. inclusion/exclusion table, results, discussion, funding); doi.org resolution
verification.problems: Metadata, DOI, PMID and every number (47 RCTs, 3515 participants, Nov 2012 search, all ES/CIs, 20–27.5 h MBSR, mantra/TM null, 37 per group) match the abstract and full text. Problems: (1) evidence_weight 'high' contradicts the source. claims.topic: Breath counting task: protocol, scoring, validity and training effect
claims.finding: Four studies (over 400 participants) validating breath counting as a behavioural measure of mindfulness. Protocol (Study 1, 164 usable participants): after a 6-min resting baseline, participants counted breaths from 1 to 9 repeatedly for 18 min. They pressed one button for breaths 1-8 and another on breath 9. If they lost count, they pressed a button reserved for self-caught miscounts and began again at 1 with the next breath. Study 1 also included about 12 experience-sampling probes. Study 2 (n=137) used a 15-min task without probes, with accuracy = 100% - (incorrect ongoing 9-counts + self-caught miscounts)/(ongoing 9-counts + self-caught miscounts). In subsets wearing a respiration belt (n=52 and n=69), mean keypress rate correlated with mean breath rate across participants (r=0.99). Mean error rates were 22% (Study 1) and 16% (Study 2), and 1-week test-retest ICC was 0.60 (n=54). Accuracy correlated with state meta-awareness (r=0.42) and less mind wandering (r=-0.38), weakly with MAAS (r=0.20) and FFMQ (r=0.21), and not with working memory (OSPAN r=0.04). 14 long-term meditators were more accurate than 25 age-matched novices (P=0.03). In a randomised training study (final n=22/20/29), 4 weeks of online breath-counting training (two 25-min sessions each weekday) increased FFMQ scores and decreased mind wandering relative to n-back training and no training. For counting accuracy, the omnibus group-by-time interaction was only a trend (P=0.06), although the planned contrast of breath counting vs both controls was significant (P=0.02).
claims.finding_zh: 四项研究（共 400 余人）验证“数息”可作为正念的行为测量。标准流程（研究 1，有效 164 人）：先静息 6 分钟，再反复从 1 数到 9，共 18 分钟。第 1–8 次呼吸按一个键，第 9 次按另一个键；数乱了就按“自己发现数错”键，从下一次呼吸重新数 1。研究 1 中还穿插了约 12 次思维探测提问。研究 2（137 人，15 分钟，无探测提问）的准确率 = 100% −（数错的 9 次组 + 自己发现的数错）/（全部 9 次组 + 自己发现的数错）。在佩戴呼吸带的部分参与者中，平均按键频率与平均呼吸频率高度相关（r = 0.99）。平均错误率为 16–22%，1 周重测信度 ICC = 0.60。准确率与觉察自身注意的程度正相关（r = 0.42），与走神负相关（r = −0.38），与自评正念量表只弱相关（r ≈ 0.20），与工作记忆无关。长期冥想者比同龄新手更准确。在线随机训练研究中，4 周数息训练（每个工作日 2 次、每次 25 分钟）比工作记忆训练和不训练更能提高自评正念、减少走神。准确率的组×时间交互作用只达到趋势水平（P = 0.06），但数息组与两个对照组的计划比较达到显著（P = 0.02）。
claims.study_type: psychometric validation studies plus a small randomised training study
claims.sample: over 400 participants across 4 studies (Study 1 n=164; Study 2 n=137; Study 3 n=39; Study 4 final n=71)
claims.limitations: Mostly US university and community samples. It is a laboratory keyboard version with respiration checks; a phone tap version has not been validated. Reliability is moderate (ICC 0.60). The training study was small, with 15-33% attrition, and the accuracy effect was only a trend in the omnibus test. The authors note the task is likely not process-pure. Validity was not replicated in all populations: Treves et al. 2025 found weak validity in ruminative adolescents.
claims.app_implication: Implement exactly: one tap target for breaths 1-8, a second for breath 9, and a 数乱了 reset that restarts at 1 with the next breath. Validated durations span 15-30 min (Levinson: 18, 15 and 30 min; Wong 2018: 20 min). The 15-min Study 2 version is the shortest validated and the one with 1-week test-retest data, so use 15 min for the measure mode and treat shorter sessions as practice only. Compute accuracy with the Study 2 formula, report self-caught resets separately, and given ICC 0.60 show trends over several sessions rather than one score.

verification.checked_against: Crossref and PubMed metadata (Front Psychol 5:1202, PMID 25386148, PMC4208398); full text from Europe PMC fullTextXML: Results of Studies 1-4, Materials and Methods for each study, and the accuracy formulas. Treves et al. 2025 was checked via Europe PMC (PMID 40326179, Psychophysiology).

claims.topic: AHA ratings for meditation and other alternative approaches to lowering blood pressure
claims.finding: American Heart Association scientific statement on non-drug, non-diet approaches to lowering blood pressure. It assigns a class of recommendation (COR) and level of evidence (LOE) to each approach for BP lowering. Transcendental Meditation (TM): Class IIb, LOE B ('may be considered'); the writing group judged that TM modestly lowers BP, but it is uncertain whether TM is superior to other techniques because head-to-head studies are few. All other meditation techniques, including MBSR: Class III (no benefit), LOE C, i.e. 'not recommended in clinical practice to lower BP at this time', because of many negative or mixed results and few trials. Yoga: Class III, LOE C. Other relaxation therapies: Class III, LOE B. Biofeedback: Class IIb, LOE B. Device-guided breathing: Class IIa, LOE B. Aerobic exercise: Class I, LOE A. Behavioural therapies generally had modest, mixed or no consistent evidence. The writing group's consensus was that people with BP above 120/80 mm Hg can reasonably consider trials of alternative approaches (exercise first) as adjuvant methods when clinically appropriate. These approaches should be treated as adjuncts to standard treatment (diet and medication). People who need large BP reductions or have a drug indication should use them only as supplements to drug therapy.
claims.finding_zh: 美国心脏协会（AHA）关于非药物、非饮食降压方法的科学声明，对各种方法的降压作用给出推荐级别和证据等级。超觉静坐（TM）：IIb 级（可以考虑）、B 级证据。声明认为 TM 能小幅降低血压，但直接比较的研究很少，无法确定它是否优于其他冥想方法。其他所有冥想技术（包括正念减压 MBSR）：III 级（无获益，目前不推荐用于临床降压）、C 级证据，理由是研究结果多为阴性或不一致、试验数量少。瑜伽：III 级、C 级证据；其他放松疗法：III 级、B 级证据；生物反馈：IIb 级、B 级证据；仪器引导的呼吸：IIa 级、B 级证据；有氧运动：I 级、A 级证据。声明认为行为疗法总体上证据有限、不一致或缺乏。写作组的共识是：血压高于 120/80 mm Hg 的人，在临床合适时可以考虑尝试这些替代方法（首选运动）作为辅助降压手段。它们应被视为饮食和药物等标准治疗的辅助；需要大幅降压或有用药指征的人，只能在药物治疗的基础上作补充。
claims.study_type: scientific statement (American Heart Association; expert-consensus ratings after a structured literature review, not a meta-analysis)
claims.sample: expert review of published trials and meta-analyses (PubMed search Jan 2006 to Oct 2011 plus the most recent meta-analyses)
claims.limitations: Published 2013 and partly superseded. Per the ACC 2025 Guideline-at-a-Glance (Gulati et al., JACC 2025, doi:10.1016/j.jacc.2025.07.010), the 2025 AHA/ACC multisociety high blood pressure guideline (Jones et al., Hypertension 2025;82:e212-e316, PMID 40811516) gives a weak COR 2b to stress reduction through TM and to 'other forms of stress management, such as breathing control techniques or yoga', each as an adjunct to lifestyle or medication (LOE not checked). The 2013 ratings came from the writing group's expert opinion after a structured literature review, not a meta-analysis. Class III for other meditation reflects mixed results and few trials, not proof of no effect. The ratings are BP-specific. The IIa rating for device-guided breathing concerned one commercial device (RESPeRATE) that monitors breathing with a chest belt and paces it with tones, and a meta-analysis cited in the statement raised concerns about bias in manufacturer-sponsored trials. TM is taught by certified teachers in a standard course (Levine et al. 2017), so its rating does not transfer to generic app-delivered mantra practice.
claims.app_implication: Make no blood-pressure or heart-health claims for any meditation track. In 2013 the AHA rated all non-TM meditation, MBSR included, Class III for BP, and even the 2025 guideline gives only a weak 2b, adjunct-only recommendation for TM and other stress management. Do not borrow TM's rating for app-delivered mantra practice, since it concerns the teacher-taught TM course. The IIa rating for device-guided breathing applied to a sensor-based device, so app-paced slow breathing cannot claim it; any BP copy in the breathing module needs its own evidence review.

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; PubMed abstract (PMID 23608661); full text via archived Hypertension HTML (web.archive.org snapshot of hyper.ahajournals.org/content/61/6/1360.full, 2018; the publisher site returned 403); for the update: the ACC '2025 High Blood Pressure Guideline-at-a-Glance' PDF (Gulati et al., JACC 2025, doi:10.1016/j.jacc.2025.07.010) and the PubMed record of the 2025 AHA/ACC guideline (PMID 40811516)
verification.problems: (1) finding_zh misstates scope. '只建议…把它们作为辅助手段' makes the 120/80 consensus apply to behavioural therapies. In the source it covers alternative approaches as a whole, with exercise first, while non-TM meditation (explicitly including MBSR), yoga and relaxation are 'not recommended in clinical practice to lower BP at this time' (Class III, no benefit). (2) finding_zh drops biofeedback (IIb, B) and the LOEs for yoga (C) and relaxation (B). (3) evidence_weight 'high' overstates the source. The statement says it 'does not represent a meta-analysis', ratings were assigned 'based on the expert opinion of the writing group', and the meditation ratings rest on LOE B (TM) and C (other meditation). Set to moderate. (4) The limitations omit that the 2013 ratings are partly superseded: the 2025 AHA/ACC multisociety high BP guideline gives COR 2b to TM and to 'other forms of stress management, such as breathing control techniques or yoga', as adjuncts (per the ACC Guideline-at-a-Glance; LOE not checked). They also omit that Class III reflected mixed results and few trials, and that the IIa for device-guided breathing concerned one sensor-based commercial device (RESPeRATE) with concerns about bias in manufacturer-sponsored trials. (5) The finding omits the statement's caveat that it is uncertain whether TM is superior to other techniques because head-to-head studies are few, which weakens the app_implication's reasoning for treating TM differently from other meditation. All citation metadata and every class and level of evidence in the English finding are verified.

claims.topic: Frequency and emotional cost of everyday mind wandering
claims.finding: Experience-sampling study using an iPhone web app: samples from 2,250 adults (58.8% male, 73.9% in the US, mean age 34) asked about happiness, current activity and mind wandering at random moments. Minds wandered in 46.9% of samples, and in at least 30% of samples during every activity except making love. People were less happy when mind wandering (multilevel b=−8.79, P<0.001), during all activities. Minds wandered more to pleasant (42.5%) than unpleasant (26.5%) or neutral (31%) topics; pleasant mind wandering was no happier than staying on task (b=−0.52, ns), whereas neutral (b=−7.2) and unpleasant (b=−23.9) topics were associated with lower happiness. Mind wandering explained 10.8% of within-person and 17.7% of between-person variance in happiness, versus 4.6% and 3.2% for activity. Time-lag analyses suggested mind wandering was generally a cause, not merely a consequence, of unhappiness.
claims.finding_zh: 经验取样研究：2250 名成人（58.8% 为男性，73.9% 在美国，平均 34 岁）在随机时刻通过 iPhone 回答当下的心情、在做什么、是否走神。46.9% 的时刻人们在走神；除性行为外，任何活动中走神比例都不低于 30%。走神时人们更不快乐（b = −8.79）；走神到愉快的话题时并不比专注当下更快乐，走神到中性或不愉快的话题时更不快乐。走神解释了个体内幸福感差异的 10.8%，而正在做的活动只解释 4.6%。时间滞后分析提示走神通常是不快乐的原因而不仅是结果，但这仍属于相关性数据。
claims.sample: n=2250 adults
claims.limitations: Observational; self-selected iPhone users in 2010, mostly in the US; causal inference rests on time-lag analyses only; brief report.
claims.app_implication: Supports the app's premise (回神: noticing and returning) and in-the-moment check-ins. Copy should say mind wandering is normal (about half of waking moments) and is associated with lower mood, without claiming that meditation will make users happier.

citation.authors: Killingsworth MA, Gilbert DT
citation.title: A Wandering Mind Is an Unhappy Mind

verification.checked_against: Crossref and PubMed metadata (Science 330(6006):932, PMID 21071660); full text of the one-page Science Brevia (publisher PDF hosted by the University of Zurich), extracted and read in full.

claims.topic: Yoga nidra for stress, anxiety and depression
claims.finding: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 73 studies (5,201 participants) of Yoga Nidra (searched 7 databases and 1 trial registry). Between-group Hedges' g: stress −0.80 versus active comparators and −1.70 versus no comparator; anxiety −1.35 (active) and −1.43 (no comparator); depression −0.69 (active) and −0.92 (no comparator); within-group analyses agreed. The authors state that, given low methodological quality and variability in intervention delivery, these moderate-to-large effects should be interpreted cautiously as they likely reflect inflated estimates.
claims.finding_zh: 对 73 项瑜伽休息术（Yoga Nidra）研究（5201 人）的系统综述与荟萃分析。组间效应量 g：压力，对积极对照 −0.80、对无对照 −1.70；焦虑 −1.35、−1.43；抑郁 −0.69、−0.92。但作者指出研究方法学质量低、练习方式差异大，这些中到大的效应很可能被高估，需要谨慎解读。
claims.sample: 73 studies, 5201 participants
claims.limitations: Low methodological quality; likely inflated effects; heterogeneous protocols and designs; branded 'NSDR' protocols are not specifically evaluated.
claims.app_implication: If a guided yoga-nidra or lying relaxation track is offered for winding down, label the evidence as limited (C) and do not quote these large effect sizes as expected benefits. Avoid marketing claims attached to 'NSDR', which this review does not test.

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; PubMed abstract (PMID 41327816); PMC full text (PMC12917937) via Europe PMC, including the search methods, risk-of-bias section, Table 4 (between-group results) and the limitations
verification.problems: None. Metadata are verified (PubMed: Ann N Y Acad Sci 2026 Feb;1556(1):e70149; epub 2025-12-01, so 2026 is the issue year). The search covered 7 databases plus Cochrane CENTRAL. The 73 studies, 5,201 participants, all six between-group Hedges' g values, the within-group agreement and the authors' caveat that effects are likely inflated all match. The review never mentions NSDR, so that limitation is accurate. Context, not errors: only 22 of the 73 studies (30%) were RCTs; 17 were at high risk of bias, 5 had some concerns and none were low risk. 41 of 50 non-randomised studies were rated poor quality. Each between-group pooled estimate rests on 6-17 studies mixing randomised and non-randomised controlled designs, with I² of 37-78%. Most participants were healthy adults.

claims.topic: Prospective dose-response of self-directed meditation practice
claims.finding: Prospective longitudinal observational study of self-directed meditators recruited online: 1,052 analysed per the full text (the abstract says 1,053); 69% female, mean age about 47, median lifetime practice about 305 h. Participants provided data across nine surveys (baseline plus weekly) over 2 months of prospectively monitored practice, and 578 also responded at a 2-4-year follow-up. Controlling for lifetime practice, practice dose was significantly associated with better life satisfaction, positive affect, negative affect and psychological distress, with small standardized coefficients (|beta| = 0.05-0.08). When dose was split into components, practice frequency predicted all four outcomes and was a stronger predictor than session length for three of the four; the two were about equal for negative affect. Session length was significant only for life satisfaction and negative affect. Using an SMD of 0.24 within one month as 'meaningful' change (Phase 1 data), the authors estimated about 18-33 h/month (about 35-65 min/day) for mental-health outcomes: negative affect 17.8 h and distress 32.8 h. For well-being outcomes they estimated about 25-41 h/month (about 50-80 min/day): life satisfaction 24.6 h and positive affect 41.0 h. Confidence intervals were wide (e.g., positive affect 19.1-667.3 h/month). The paper's abstract swaps these two labels; the results and discussion support the mapping given here. Dose-response slopes were steeper for less-experienced practitioners, with lifetime practice moderating all four outcomes. Higher negative emotionality strengthened dose-response for negative affect and distress. Valuing mental health as a practice goal moderated life satisfaction, positive affect and negative affect, but not distress. The authors report the dose-response association was maintained when 2-4-year follow-up data were included.
claims.finding_zh: 前瞻性纵向观察研究：通过网络招募、自主练习的冥想者，正文分析 1052 人（摘要写 1053 人；69% 为女性，平均约 47 岁，既往练习中位数约 305 小时）。他们在 2 个月内共 9 次问卷（基线加每周一次）中报告练习量和心理状态，其中 578 人在 2–4 年后回应了随访。控制既往练习经验后，练习量与生活满意度、积极情绪、消极情绪和心理困扰的改善相关，但标准化效应很小（|β| = 0.05–0.08）。把练习量拆成频率和每次时长后，在 4 个结局中的 3 个上，“练得频繁”比“每次练得久”更能预测获益；消极情绪上两者相近。作者以 1 个月内达到 SMD 0.24 作为“有意义的改善”，并据此估算：心理健康结局（消极情绪、心理困扰）约需每月 18–33 小时，约合每天 35–65 分钟；幸福感结局（生活满意度、积极情绪）约需每月 25–41 小时，约合每天 50–80 分钟。置信区间很宽，例如积极情绪为每月 19–667 小时。注意：论文摘要把这两组数字与结局的对应关系写反了，此处以正文结果为准。既往练习越少的人，同等练习量带来的改善越大。纳入 2–4 年随访数据后，剂量-反应关系依然存在。这些都是观察性相关，不能证明因果。
claims.sample: n=1,052 self-selected meditators analysed (abstract states 1,053); 578 provided 2-4-year follow-up data
claims.limitations: Not randomised: self-selection and reverse causation are possible (people who feel better may practise more), as the authors acknowledge. Practice was self-reported, with session length recorded in bands (0-15, 15-30, 30-60, >60 min) and scored at band midpoints. This coarse measure may understate the role of duration relative to frequency. Opt-in participants differed from opt-outs (older, more experienced, better baseline mental health), and only 578 of 1,052 gave follow-up data. The sample was about 93% from English-speaking or EU countries, largely secular and motivated. The minutes-per-day figures are extrapolations from small linear slopes: most participants practised about 29 min/day, 5.2 days/week, and the CIs are very wide. The 'meaningful change' threshold (SMD 0.24) was adopted by the authors from Cuijpers et al. 2014. The abstract mislabels which minute range applies to which outcome. The authors acknowledge their estimates conflict with app RCTs reporting similar effects at about 10 min/day.
claims.app_implication: Make frequency (most days) the behavioural target in reminders and progress UI rather than long sessions. Say this rests on observational data, and that the authors call for controlled experiments. Do not promise mood benefits from 10 min/day. If dose figures are shown, use the corrected mapping: about 35-65 min/day for a meaningful one-month change in negative affect or distress, and about 50-80 min/day for well-being. Label them as uncertain observational estimates that conflict with brief-practice app RCTs, and show both.

citation.authors: Bowles NI, Van Dam NT
citation.title: Dose-response effects of reported meditation practice on mental-health and wellbeing: A prospective longitudinal study

verification.checked_against: Crossref and PubMed metadata (PMID 40785526, PMC12336962); full text from Europe PMC fullTextXML, including the abstract, Methods, Table 1 (n=1,052), Table 2 (578 completers), Table 3, the meaningful-change estimates (24.6/41.0/17.8/32.8 h per month), the frequency-versus-length analysis, the moderation results, the Discussion and the limitations.
verification.problems: (1) Material: the claim reproduces an error in the paper's abstract, which swaps the outcome labels. The Results give 24.6 h/month for life satisfaction, 41.0 for positive affect, 17.8 for negative affect and 32.8 for distress. The Discussion explicitly states about 35-60/65 min/day for mental-health outcomes (negative affect, distress) and about 50-80 min/day for well-being (life satisfaction, positive affect). The claim and finding_zh say the reverse. (2) The full text reports n=1,052 throughout (Tables 1-2, Discussion, Strengths); 1,053 appears only in the abstract. (3) Only 578 of 1,052 provided 2-4-year follow-up data, which is not mentioned. (4) 'Frequency stronger than duration' held for 3 of 4 outcomes; for negative affect they were about equal. (5) Valuing mental health as a goal moderated life satisfaction, positive affect and negative affect, but not distress (p=.097); the claim follows the abstract's looser wording. (6) 'Required' overstates observational, linearly extrapolated estimates: effects were small (|beta| 0.05-0.08), CIs were very wide (positive affect 19.1-667.3 h/month), and the average participant practised about 29 min/day. (7) finding_zh '在 2 个月内完成 9 次调查' implies everyone completed all 9 surveys; inclusion required at least one follow-up survey. (8) Not mentioned: session length was recorded in coarse bands, which may disadvantage duration against frequency.

claims.topic: Contradicting evidence: limited validity of breath counting in ruminative adolescents
claims.finding: Preregistered (OSF), cross-sectional psychometric study of a 20-minute breath-counting task (BCT) with novel objective respiration (breath-belt) measures. Convenience sample: 78 adolescents aged 13-18 with elevated rumination, recruited from an ongoing app-based mindfulness trial. Mean accuracy was 56.7%. Split-half reliability was fair (ICC 0.61 correct cycles, 0.57 resets, 0.40 miscounts), and distributions resembled adult studies. BCT performance showed none of the expected positive associations with self-reported mindfulness (FFMQ-SF trait or EMA); Bayes factors favoured the null for total FFMQ. FDR-significant associations ran the other way: physiologically verified accuracy correlated negatively with FFMQ Observing (r=-0.33; button-press accuracy r=-0.27, trend-level after FDR); miscounts correlated positively with Non-reactivity (r=0.30); performance decrements were larger with higher Observing, Non-reactivity and total FFMQ scores (r=0.28-0.33). SART no-go accuracy correlated weakly with fewer resets (rho=-0.26, p=0.038; trend-level after FDR). After FDR correction, BCT was unrelated to depression, anxiety, stress, rumination, Big Five personality and self-reported executive function. The authors conclude that, at least in ruminative adolescents, breath counting may measure a narrow, contextual form of sustained attention, may not capture other qualities of mindfulness, and may lack predictive validity.
claims.finding_zh: 预注册的横断面心理测量研究：78 名反刍思维较多的 13–18 岁青少年（来自一项正念 App 试验）完成 20 分钟数息任务，同时用呼吸带客观记录呼吸。平均正确率约 57%；分半信度尚可（ICC 0.40–0.61），成绩分布与成人研究相似。但数息成绩与自评正念（特质问卷和日常即时评估）没有预期的正相关，部分关系甚至方向相反：经呼吸记录核实的正确率与“观察”分量表呈负相关（r = −0.33）；“不反应”得分越高的人数错越多（r = 0.30）；自评正念越高的人，任务后段成绩下滑越多。数息与另一项持续注意任务（SART）只有很弱的关联（多重比较校正后不显著）；校正后与抑郁、焦虑、压力、反刍、人格和执行功能也都无关。作者认为，至少在这类青少年中，数息可能只反映很窄的、依情境而定的持续注意，未必代表正念的其他方面，也未必能预测其他结果。
claims.sample: n=78 adolescents aged 13-18 with elevated rumination (76% female)
claims.limitations: Small convenience sample of ruminative adolescents drawn from an app-based mindfulness trial; 54% had a current DSM-5 diagnosis, mostly anxiety disorders. Cross-sectional. BCT was run without attention probes. The study may be underpowered for the small correlations reported in adults, though Bayes factors favoured the null for total self-reported mindfulness. Several correlations were only trend-level after FDR correction. Results may not generalise to adults or to non-ruminative youth.
claims.app_implication: Never label breath-counting accuracy a 正念分数 or a mental-health indicator; present it only as attention-practice data, and show this contradicting study in the citation panel. Limiting the measure mode to adults (18+) is a cautious product choice, but do not imply the task is validated there: the authors note that in adults its links with self-reported mindfulness are small or absent.

citation.authors: Treves IN, Tierney AO, Goldberg SB, et al.
citation.title: Limited Validity of Breath-Counting as a Measure of Mindfulness in Ruminative Adolescents

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; Europe PMC/PubMed record and abstract; PMC full text (PMC12053031): Methods, Tables 1-6, Results 3.1-3.5, Discussion
verification.problems: Metadata correct (Psychophysiology 2025;62(5):e70071; PMID 40326179; PMCID PMC12053031). The finding copies the abstract's loose wording that accuracy correlated negatively 'with nonreactivity'. The full text (Tables 3 and 6) shows Non-reactivity correlated positively with MISCOUNTS (r=0.30, FDR p=0.045); accuracy vs Non-reactivity was r=-0.08 (ns). Button-press accuracy vs Observing (r=-0.27, p=0.018) was only trend-level after FDR (p=0.109); only physiologically verified accuracy survived FDR (r=-0.33, FDR p=0.04). finding_zh repeats the same imprecision.
