The SART-resets correlation (rho=-0.26, p=0.038) became trend-level after FDR (p=0.076). Nominal personality correlations (extraversion, agreeableness) did not survive FDR, so 'not related' holds. Missing design context: cross-sectional; sample drawn from an ongoing app-based mindfulness trial (NCT04697966); aged 13-18; 76% female; 54% had a current DSM-5 diagnosis. The app_implication's adults-only restriction could imply the task is valid in adults, but the paper notes adult associations with self-reported mindfulness are small (beta=-0.26 in a 430-person IPD meta-analysis) or null (n=96). evidence_weight 'low' is appropriate.

claims.topic: Body scan meditation practised on its own
claims.finding: Systematic review and meta-analysis (robust variance estimation) of RCTs of body scan meditation as a sole intervention, with no population restriction: 14 independent articles, outcomes divided into 7 categories. Body scan only had a small effect on mindfulness compared with passive control (Hedges' g=0.268, 95% CI 0.032–0.504); no other outcome category showed a significant effect. Attrition in longer interventions was low, study quality low and heterogeneity high. The authors conclude that a sole body scan meditation is not effective enough to improve health-related outcomes.
claims.finding_zh: 对单独练习身体扫描的随机对照试验所做的系统综述与荟萃分析（14 篇独立文献，结局分为 7 类）：与不干预相比，单独的身体扫描只对正念水平有小幅提升（g = 0.268，95% CI 0.032–0.504），其他结局都没有显著效果；研究质量低、异质性高。作者结论：单独做身体扫描不足以改善健康相关结局。
claims.study_type: systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs
claims.sample: 14 independent articles (RCTs)
claims.limitations: Few, small, low-quality trials; heterogeneous populations and outcomes; does not evaluate body scan as a component of a full programme such as MBSR.
claims.app_implication: Keep body scan as a course component and a bedtime option, but do not sell a standalone body-scan pack with health claims (缓解焦虑, 改善睡眠). Grade standalone body scan D for health outcomes.

citation.authors: Gan R, Zhang L, Chen S
citation.title: The effects of body scan meditation: A systematic review and meta-analysis

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata + PubMed abstract (PMID 35538557). The Wiley full text is closed access (403 on every route). Per-category results were cross-checked against how citing papers describe the review (Europe PMC citations, e.g. PMC13630349).
verification.problems: Nothing in the abstract disagrees with the claim. Metadata, 14 independent articles, 7 outcome categories, robust variance estimation, g=0.268 (0.032–0.504), low attrition in long-term interventions, low quality, high heterogeneity and the conclusion all match. Caveat: 'no other outcome category showed a significant effect' is implied by the abstract ('Body scan only had small effect on mindfulness when compared with passive control'; 'not effective enough to improve health-related outcomes'). A citing paper describes it the same way ('small effects on mindfulness, but not on other outcomes compared to a passive control'). It could not be checked category by category because the full text is paywalled.

claims.topic: Mindfulness-based programmes for mental-health promotion in non-clinical adults
claims.finding: Preregistered systematic review and meta-analysis (PROSPERO CRD42018105213) of 136 RCTs (11,605 participants; 29 countries; 77% women; ages 18–73). It covered in-person, group-based, teacher-led MBPs in non-clinical settings that met an expert consensus definition (at least four 1-hour sessions). Primary outcomes were measured 1–6 months after the programme, with Bonferroni-corrected significance at p<0.0125. Versus no intervention: anxiety SMD −0.56 (95% CI −0.80 to −0.33; 8 trials; 95% PI −1.19 to 0.06), depression −0.53 (−0.72 to −0.34; 14 trials; PI −1.14 to 0.07), distress −0.45 (−0.58 to −0.31; 27 trials; PI −1.04 to 0.14), well-being +0.33 (0.11 to 0.54; 9 trials; PI −0.29 to 0.94); all prediction intervals include zero. Versus non-specific active controls only depression improved (SMD −0.46, −0.81 to −0.10; 6 trials; PI −1.57 to 0.66). There was no statistically significant evidence for anxiety or distress, and no reliable well-being data. Versus specific active controls (e.g., exercise programmes) there was no statistically significant evidence that MBPs were superior on any primary outcome. All included trials were at high overall risk of bias (RoB2). When trials at high risk from 3 or more bias sources were excluded, only the distress effect remained (SMD −0.30, −0.48 to −0.11). The effects on anxiety (−0.22, −0.57 to 0.13), depression (−0.24, −0.49 to 0.00) and well-being were no longer significant. USA-based trials reported smaller effects, and MBPs targeted at higher-risk groups had larger effects than universal MBPs. GRADE confidence was low or very low for most outcome domains; only anxiety versus passive controls was moderate. 89% of trials did not mention measuring adverse events.
claims.finding_zh: 预注册的系统综述与荟萃分析：136 项随机对照试验（11,605 人，29 个国家，77% 为女性，18–73 岁），考察非临床环境中线下、团体、由老师带领、符合专家共识定义（至少 4 次、每次 1 小时）的正念课程，主要结局在课程结束后 1–6 个月测量。与不干预相比：焦虑 SMD −0.56（95% CI −0.80 至 −0.33，8 项试验），抑郁 −0.53（−0.72 至 −0.34，14 项），心理困扰 −0.45（−0.58 至 −0.31，27 项），幸福感 +0.33（0.11 至 0.54，9 项）；但各项的 95% 预测区间都包含 0，说明在某些场景可能没有效果。与非特异性积极对照相比只有抑郁改善（−0.46）；与其他特定的积极干预（如运动课程）相比，没有统计学上的优势。按 RoB2 工具，所有纳入试验的总体偏倚风险都为高；排除偏倚问题最多的试验后，只剩心理困扰的效果（SMD −0.30，−0.48 至 −0.11），焦虑、抑郁和幸福感的效果都不再显著。美国的试验效应更小；面向高风险人群的课程效应大于面向所有人的课程。GRADE 证据确定性对大多数结局为低或极低，只有“与不干预相比的焦虑”为中等。89% 的试验没有提到记录不良反应。
claims.study_type: systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs (preregistered)
claims.sample: 136 RCTs, 11,605 participants
claims.limitations: All included trials were at high overall risk of bias (RoB2), mainly from self-reported outcomes and missing data. GRADE confidence was low or very low for most outcomes. Substantial heterogeneity (all prediction intervals cross zero). Few trials with active controls. In-person programmes only (online MBPs excluded), so app delivery is an extrapolation. Predominantly women. Adverse events rarely monitored.
claims.app_implication: Frame benefits as average and variable (平均而言有帮助，但并非对每个人都有效). Present mindfulness as one of several reasonable well-being options, not the best one: the authors note that other preventive interventions, such as physical exercise, may be equally effective. This review covered only in-person teacher-led courses and certainty is mostly low, so do not cite it as direct evidence that the app's own content works.

citation.authors: Galante J, Friedrich C, Dawson AF, et al.
citation.title: Mindfulness-based programmes for mental health promotion in adults in nonclinical settings: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; PubMed abstract (PMID 33428616); PMC7799763 full text via Europe PMC (eligibility, outcomes, risk of bias and GRADE section, sensitivity analyses, adverse events); doi.org resolution
verification.problems: Metadata and all abstract numbers are correct (136 RCTs, 11,605 participants, 29 countries, 77% women, ages 18–73, all SMDs/CIs/PIs, non-specific active depression −0.46). Problems: (1) The limitations say 'high risk of bias in many trials', but the paper states that ALL included trials were at high overall risk of bias by RoB2. (2) evidence_weight 'moderate' overstates. The authors report that 'confidence in the cumulative evidence is low or very low for most outcome domains', with only anxiety vs passive controls rated moderate. In sensitivity analysis the anxiety, depression and well-being effects were no longer significant. Changed to low. (3) finding_zh translates 'expert-defined MBPs' as '由专业人士设计' (designed by professionals). It means programmes meeting an expert consensus definition (Crane et al.: group-based, teacher-led, at least four 1-hour sessions). (4) Omitted: the sensitivity-analysis numbers, and that 89% of trials did not mention measuring adverse events.

claims.topic: Self-guided multicomponent meditation app (Healthy Minds Program): efficacy and real usage
claims.finding: Three-arm, fully remote RCT (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04139005; hypotheses preregistered on OSF). It compared 8 weeks of the self-guided Healthy Minds Program app (Awareness+Connection or Awareness+Insight) with waitlist in adults without extensive meditation experience. 343 were randomised; 186 (54.2%) completed at least one follow-up assessment; 166/228 (72.8%) assigned to the app downloaded and used it. Guided practices were selectable at 5-30 min. The two app versions did not differ on any outcome. Combined versus waitlist, they showed larger improvements in distress (primary outcome), social connectedness, mindfulness and insight-related measures (d=-0.28 to 0.41; Ps≤.02). This was despite modest exposure to connection and insight content: only 32% and 23% of participants engaged with it. Usage, with non-users counted as zero: mean 10.52 days (median 4) and 102.16 total minutes of practice (median 26); median time to last use 12 days. In exploratory analyses, above-median days of use was associated with larger improvements in distress, insight, defusion and mindfulness.
claims.finding_zh: 完全远程的三臂随机对照试验：自助式 Healthy Minds Program App（8 周，“觉察+连结”或“觉察+洞察”）对比等待名单，受试者为没有丰富冥想经验的成年人。343 人随机，54.2% 完成至少一次后续评估；分到 App 组的人中 72.8% 下载并用过 App。每次引导练习可选 5–30 分钟。两个 App 版本之间没有差异；合并后与等待组相比，心理困扰（主要结局）、社会联结感、正念和与洞察相关的指标有小幅改善（d = −0.28 至 0.41）。实际使用很少：平均 10.5 天（中位数 4 天），总练习时长中位数只有 26 分钟，最后一次使用的中位时间为第 12 天。探索性分析显示，使用天数在中位数以上的人困扰改善更明显，但这只是相关，不能证明因果。
claims.sample: n=343 randomised adults (mean age 41.7)
claims.limitations: Waitlist control only. High and differential attrition: 47.8% of app vs 67.0% of waitlist participants provided follow-up data. Effects were robust only if missing outcomes were no more than 0.25 SD worse than average, and absent under worst-case assumptions. Sample was predominantly White (81.6%), female (84.5%) and highly educated (55.4% graduate-level), recruited mainly through a US university; participants were paid US$25 for assessments. Several authors are affiliated with the app's nonprofit developer (Healthy Minds Innovations). Usage-outcome associations are exploratory and correlational.
claims.app_implication: Expect most users to practise on only a few days (median 4 days; median last use at day 12), not for 8 weeks. Tracking days practised is reasonable, but this trial did not show that days matter more than minutes (only days of use was analysed), and the usage-benefit links were correlational. Offer short options (the trial allowed 5-30 min). Do not claim that kindness/connection practices drive benefits: the Connection and Insight versions produced the same results, and most users never reached that content.

citation.authors: Goldberg SB, Imhoff-Smith T, Bolt DM, et al.
citation.title: Testing the Efficacy of a Multicomponent, Self-Guided, Smartphone-Based Meditation App: Three-Armed Randomized Controlled Trial

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; Europe PMC/PubMed abstract; PMC full text (PMC7732708): Methods, Table 1, utilisation, attrition analysis, Tables 3-4, Discussion, conflict-of-interest statement
verification.problems: Metadata correct (JMIR Ment Health 2020;7(11):e23825; PMID 33245288). All usage and outcome numbers in the finding match the full text. The limitation 'high-income' is wrong: Table 1 shows income ≤$50k 25.9%, $50-100k 35.0%, $100-150k 22.2%, >$150k 16.6%. The paper describes the sample as predominantly White (81.6%), female (84.5%) and graduate-educated (55.4%), with 'more variable' income. Limitations also omit: differential attrition (47.8% app vs 67.0% waitlist provided follow-up data); effects hold only if missing outcomes are ≤0.25 SD worse than average and disappear under worst-case assumptions; developer-affiliated authors (Healthy Minds Innovations); participants were paid US$25. The app_implication is unsupported in two places. (1) Days of use was the only usage metric analysed (chosen because it was least skewed), so the trial cannot show days matter more than minutes; usage-outcome links are exploratory and correlational. (2) 'Kindness/connection practices showed benefits with modest exposure': the Connection and Insight arms did not differ on any outcome, and only 32.2% of Connection participants engaged with the connection content. finding_zh's '使用天数越多，困扰改善越明显' implies a dose-response gradient from a median-split, correlational analysis.

claims.topic: Self-compassion interventions and psychosocial outcomes
claims.finding: Meta-analysis of 27 RCTs (1,480 adults; mean age 35.8; 76.7% female) of self-compassion-based interventions using validated psychosocial measures. Compared with control groups (wait-list or active), interventions improved all 11 outcomes analysed. Moderate effects: self-compassion (g=0.75, 95% CI 0.53–0.97; 27 trials; I²=84%), stress (0.67, 0.37–0.96; 5 trials), depression (0.66, 0.45–0.87; 15 trials), mindfulness (0.62, 0.44–0.80; 12 trials), anxiety (0.57, 0.33–0.82; 14 trials) and self-criticism (0.56, 0.30–0.82; 8 trials). Smaller effects: positive affect (0.48), life satisfaction (0.40) and negative affect (0.33). The 'large' effects for eating behaviour (g=1.76, 0.53–2.99) and rumination (g=1.37, 0.09–2.64) came from only 4 trials each, with very high heterogeneity (I² about 91–93%). Against active controls, effects were smaller: self-compassion g=0.42 (vs 0.87 against wait-lists) and mindfulness 0.30. Anxiety (0.28, −0.03 to 0.59) and self-criticism (0.37, −0.09 to 0.82) were not significant, while depression held up (0.79, 0.07–1.50; 5 trials). Group delivery produced a larger gain in self-compassion than individual delivery (g=0.81, 18 trials vs 0.37, 9 trials; p=.001). Effects on self-compassion varied numerically by population (community 0.83, clinical 0.82, clinical-health 0.56, university 0.47), but the between-population difference was not significant (p=.191). Follow-up data (1–3 months) came from only 4–5 trials; the authors read them as a slight further improvement in depression (g=0.33) and maintained self-compassion gains (g=0.19).
claims.finding_zh: 对 27 项自我关怀干预随机对照试验（1480 名成人，平均 35.8 岁，76.7% 为女性）的荟萃分析：与对照组（等待名单或其他积极活动）相比，11 项心理社会结局都有改善。中等效应：自我关怀（g = 0.75）、压力（0.67，5 项试验）、抑郁（0.66，15 项）、正念（0.62）、焦虑（0.57，14 项）、自我批评（0.56）；积极情绪、生活满意度和负性情绪的效应较小。饮食行为（g = 1.76）和反刍思维（g = 1.37）虽然效应大，但各只来自 4 项试验，研究间差异极大，置信区间很宽。与其他积极活动对照相比，效应变小：自我关怀 g = 0.42，焦虑和自我批评的改善不再显著，抑郁仍显著（0.79，5 项试验）。团体形式对自我关怀的提升（g = 0.81）大于个人形式（g = 0.37）。不同人群之间的差异没有统计学意义。1–3 个月的随访只有 4–5 项试验，作者认为抑郁略有继续改善，自我关怀的提升得以保持。
claims.sample: 27 RCTs, 1,480 adults
claims.limitations: Small trials (about 55 participants each). Only 1 of 27 trials was preregistered, and randomisation or allocation concealment was often unreported. Heterogeneity was substantial (I²=84% for self-compassion, over 90% for eating behaviour and rumination). The large eating and rumination effects rest on 4 trials each. Anxiety and self-criticism effects were not significant against active controls. Follow-up came from only 4–5 trials over 1–3 months. Intervention types were too diverse to analyse by category, and no children or adolescents were included. The authors judged publication-bias risk small (fail-safe N 1,589; trim-and-fill found no missing studies). Group programmes may not transfer to solo app use.
claims.app_implication: Brief self-compassion practices can be an optional track (grade C), framed modestly as helping people treat themselves more kindly. Avoid claims about eating behaviour or rumination (4 highly inconsistent trials each) and about reducing anxiety or self-criticism, which did not beat active controls. Individual formats, the closest to solo app use, gave only a small gain in self-compassion (g=0.37).

citation.authors: Ferrari M, Hunt C, Harrysunker A, et al.
citation.title: Self-Compassion Interventions and Psychosocial Outcomes: a Meta-Analysis of RCTs

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata + ACBS abstract reproduction + full published article PDF (Mindfulness 10:1455–1473, copy hosted at self-compassion.org), including Table 4 and the moderator analyses. Confirmed not indexed in PubMed or Europe PMC, so the empty PMID is correct.
verification.problems: Metadata and every abstract number are correct. (1) The abstract's 'results differed across population type' is contradicted by the paper's own test: between-population Q=4.76, df=3, p=.191, not significant. The claim repeats the abstract. (2) 'Stronger for group than individual delivery' was tested only for the self-compassion outcome (g=0.81, k=18 vs 0.37, k=9), not across outcomes. (3) The headline 'large' effects lack caveats: eating behaviour (1.76, CI 0.53–2.99) and rumination (1.37, CI 0.09–2.64) each come from 4 trials, with I²≈91–93%. (4) Omitted nulls: against active controls, anxiety (0.28, −0.03 to 0.59) and self-criticism (0.37, −0.09 to 0.82) were not significant, and self-compassion (0.42) and mindfulness (0.30) effects were small. (5) The follow-up statements rest on only 4–5 trials over 1–3 months. (6) Total N is reported (1,480) and CIs are available, so the sample and limitations text are outdated. (7) Evidence weight 'moderate' is too high: small, mostly unregistered trials (1 of 27 preregistered), often unreported randomisation and allocation concealment, I²=84% for the primary outcome, and smaller or null effects against active controls.

claims.topic: 10 min/day for 10 days with popular mindfulness apps: effects and drop-off
claims.finding: Pre-registered three-arm RCT: 208 university students (aged 18-49) were randomly assigned to Headspace, Smiling Mind or Evernote (control app). They were instructed to use the app 10 min each day for 10 days, then given 30 days of access to use at their discretion. Depressive symptoms, anxiety, stress, college adjustment, flourishing, resilience and mindfulness were measured at baseline, after the 10 days and after the 30-day period; app usage was self-reported. Mindfulness-app use was high during the 10-day period (used on 8 of 10 days) but low during the 30-day period (fewer than 20% used the app 2+ times per week). Relative to control, mindfulness-app users improved from baseline to day 10 in depressive symptoms and college adjustment, plus resilience (Smiling Mind only) and mindfulness (Headspace only). Participants who kept using the app frequently were more likely to maintain improvements (e.g., depressive symptoms and resilience, Headspace only) to the end of the 30-day period. Anxiety, stress and flourishing were measured but are not among the improvements reported.
claims.finding_zh: 预注册随机对照试验：208 名大学生（18–49 岁）被随机分到 Headspace、Smiling Mind 或 Evernote（对照 App），要求每天用 10 分钟、连续 10 天，之后 30 天可自由使用。使用情况为自我报告。前 10 天使用率高（10 天中有 8 天在用），之后 30 天的自由使用期使用率很低（不到 20% 的人每周用 2 次以上）。与对照相比，10 天后抑郁症状和大学适应有改善（韧性只在 Smiling Mind 组改善，正念只在 Headspace 组改善）；之后继续频繁使用的人更可能保持改善，但这是相关性结果。焦虑、压力和心理繁荣也测量了，但不在报告改善的结局之列。
claims.sample: n=208 university students aged 18-49
claims.limitations: Very short intervention (10 days) and 30-day follow-up. Small arms (~70 each). Self-reported usage. Student sample. Many outcomes, with effects differing between the two apps. The maintenance finding rests on self-selected frequent users, so it is correlational. The drop in use after day 10 is a before/after observation, not a randomised test of structured vs open-ended use. Full text not read.
claims.app_implication: Expect a sharp drop-off once a structured period ends: in this trial use was high while students were asked to practise daily for 10 days and low once use became optional. A fixed daily starter sequence is a reasonable design choice, but this study did not test structured against open-ended plans, so do not claim that structure causes adherence.

citation.authors: Flett JAM, Hayne H, Riordan BC, et al.
citation.title: Mobile Mindfulness Meditation: a Randomised Controlled Trial of the Effect of Two Popular Apps on Mental Health

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; full abstract from the Springer article page, cross-checked against a verbatim copy on NYU Information for Practice; PubMed and Europe PMC (not indexed); full text paywalled, not read
verification.problems: Metadata correct (Flett JAM, Hayne H, Riordan BC, Thompson LM, Conner TS; Mindfulness 2019;10(5):863-876; online first 31 Oct 2018). Not indexed in PubMed, so the empty PMID is correct. The finding matches the abstract. finding_zh adds '平均' (the abstract gives 'used on 8 of 10 days' without saying mean or median) and '迅速下降' (the abstract only says use was low in the 30-day period). The app_implication makes a causal claim the design cannot support. Structured vs open-ended access was not randomised; the 10-day vs 30-day adherence contrast is a before/after observation confounded by time, novelty and study instructions, and usage was self-reported. The maintenance result concerns self-selected frequent users, so it is correlational. evidence_weight 'moderate' is too high: this is a single small three-arm trial (~70 per arm) with a 10-day intervention, self-reported usage, many outcomes with inconsistent app-specific effects, and 30-day follow-up. 'low' fits, consistent with the larger Goldberg 2020 RCT also rated low.

claims.topic: Critical evaluation of mindfulness research and communication
claims.finding: Critical review and prescriptive agenda by 15 contemplative-science researchers. It discusses the difficulty of defining mindfulness, delineates the proper scope of research into mindfulness practices, explicates methodological issues for interpreting results, and sets out an agenda focused on assessment, mindfulness training, possible adverse effects and the intersection with brain imaging. It warns that misinformation and poor methodology in past studies may lead public consumers to be harmed, misled and disappointed.
claims.finding_zh: 15 位冥想科学研究者撰写的批判性综述与研究议程（题为“警惕炒作”）。文章讨论了“正念”难以统一定义的问题，界定了正念研究的合理范围，说明了解读研究结果时的关键方法学问题，并就测量、训练方式、可能的不良反应以及与脑成像研究的结合提出改进建议。作者警告：既往研究中的错误信息和薄弱方法可能使公众受到伤害、被误导或感到失望。
claims.sample: not applicable (narrative review by 15 authors)
claims.limitations: Narrative rather than systematic; no pooled estimates; reflects the authors' judgement.
claims.app_implication: Editorial policy: name the specific technique rather than generic 正念; no brain-change or imaging-based claims in consumer copy; always state comparator and certainty; disclose possible adverse effects; keep self-report and behavioural measures visibly distinct.

citation.authors: Van Dam NT, van Vugt MK, Vago DR, et al.
citation.title: Mind the Hype: A Critical Evaluation and Prescriptive Agenda for Research on Mindfulness and Meditation

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; PubMed abstract (PMID 29016274); PMC5758421 author-manuscript full text; PubMed, Europe PMC and Semantic Scholar records of the linked 2020 letter (PMID 32750262)
verification.problems: No discrepancies found. 15 authors, the title, venue, 2018 print issue 13(1):36-61 (epub Oct 2017), the DOI and PMID are correct, and the finding paraphrases the abstract accurately, including the 'harmed, misled, and disappointed' warning. Notes, not errors: the acknowledgments say the paper 'should be read as a majority consensus', i.e. not every author endorses every statement, which supports the 'consensus statement' label only in that informal sense. PubMed links a 2020 letter by the same authors ('Miscommunicating Mindfulness', Perspect Psychol Sci 15(5):1289-1290) to this article as an erratum. Its indexed excerpt concerns the passage quoting Rick Hanson on amygdala activity, not the conclusions summarised here. The full letter text was paywalled and not read.

claims.topic: Brief and single-session mindfulness training
claims.finding: Meta-analysis of 65 RCTs (5,489 participants, mostly without meditation experience; 64.6% female; mean age 24.6; 46 of the 65 trials in student samples) of brief mindfulness training, from single-session inductions to multisession interventions lasting up to 2 weeks. Brief training produced a small reduction in negative affectivity versus control programmes (g=0.21, 95% CI 0.12–0.29, p<.001), with significant heterogeneity (I²≈53%). Community samples showed larger effects (g=0.41) than student samples (g=0.14); clinical and non-clinical samples did not differ significantly. Effects tended to fade: g=0.29 immediately after practice, 0.18 later the same day, and 0.08 (not significant, 5 comparisons) one day or more later, although timing was not a significant moderator. After trim-and-fill adjustment for publication bias (an estimated 18 missing null or negative studies), the overall effect fell to g=0.04 (95% CI −0.01 to 0.09), not significantly different from zero. Trial quality was low (mean Delphi score 3.23 out of 9).
claims.finding_zh: 对 65 项随机对照试验（5489 人，多数无冥想经验，平均 24.6 岁；其中 46 项以大学生为对象）的荟萃分析，考察短程正念训练（从单次到最长 2 周）。与对照相比，负性情绪小幅下降（g = 0.21，95% CI 0.12–0.29），研究间差异较大。社区样本效应较大（g = 0.41），学生样本较小（g = 0.14）。效果随时间减弱：练习后立即测 g = 0.29，一天或更久之后只有 0.08（不显著）。校正发表偏倚后，效应降到 g = 0.04（95% CI −0.01 至 0.09），与零没有显著差异。纳入试验的方法学质量偏低。
claims.sample: 65 RCTs, 5,489 participants
claims.limitations: Strong evidence of publication bias (the bias-adjusted effect is not different from zero). Trial quality was low (mean Delphi 3.23/9) and heterogeneity significant. Samples were mostly students (46 of 65 trials). Diverse negative-affect outcomes were pooled, mostly state measures taken immediately after practice, with very few assessments beyond one day. Unpublished studies were not sought.
claims.app_implication: Short 回神 sessions (1–5 min) are fine as in-the-moment and habit tools, but copy must not claim lasting mood benefit from single or very short sessions: the average effect is small, fades within a day and largely disappears after correction for publication bias. Position them as an entry point to the 8-week programme.

citation.authors: Schumer MC, Lindsay EK, Creswell JD
citation.title: Brief mindfulness training for negative affectivity: A systematic review and meta-analysis
citation.venue: Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata + PubMed abstract + PMC full text (PMC6441958, via NCBI efetch), including Tables 1–1d and the publication-bias and limitations sections
verification.problems: Metadata, design and every quoted number match the abstract and full text. (1) Evidence weight 'moderate' is too high. The paper rates trial quality as relatively low (mean Delphi 3.23/9), heterogeneity was significant (I²≈53%), and the bias-adjusted effect (g=0.04, 95% CI −0.01 to 0.09) is not different from zero. (2) The limitations leave out the low trial quality and that the adjusted CI includes zero. (3) Added that effects faded over time (one day or more later g=0.08, not significant), which matters for app copy. Minor: the community-sample effect is 0.41 in the abstract and 0.40 in the results text.

claims.topic: Breath counting task replication in an Asian sample; meaning of resets vs miscounts
claims.finding: Replication and extension of the breath-counting task (BCT) in Asian undergraduates at a university in Singapore. 127 were recruited (mean age 23.4); after excluding 2 incomplete datasets, 7 non-compliant participants with near-zero accuracy and 3 reset outliers (one overlapping), 116 were analysed. Each BCT lasted 20 min using Levinson's verbatim instructions plus an instruction not to count on fingers. Participants pressed the left arrow for breaths 1-8, the right arrow for breath 9 and the space bar when they forgot the count, then restarted at 1. They were asked to sit upright and relaxed with eyes at least partly open. Total button presses correlated with respiration-belt breath counts (r=.96). Mean accuracy was 72%, and performance was worse in the second half of the task. Accuracy correlated with PVT sustained attention (response speed r=.28; lapses r=-.33) and everyday cognitive failures (CFQ r=-.21). Its correlation with self-reported mindfulness was weak and non-significant (MAAS r=.16, p=.08). Miscounts (uncaught errors) correlated with PVT lapses (r=.32), whereas resets (self-caught errors) correlated with self-reported mind wandering (MWQ r=.22, p=.02) and not with PVT. Miscount and reset rates were uncorrelated. Test-retest was measured in recalled top- and bottom-tertile performers (21 and 17; mean interval 54 days): ICC 0.48 for accuracy, 0.47 for miscounts and 0.72 for resets. Split-half reliability was 0.57, 0.55 and 0.33.
claims.finding_zh: 在新加坡一所大学的 127 名亚洲学生中重复并扩展了数息任务；剔除数据不全、未按要求作答和极端值后，116 人纳入分析。每次 20 分钟，沿用原始指导语，并要求不用手指计数：第 1–8 次呼吸按左箭头，第 9 次按右箭头，忘了数到几就按空格，从 1 重新开始；建议坐姿放松挺直，眼睛至少部分睁开。平均准确率 72%，后半程表现比前半程差。准确率与持续注意力和日常认知失误相关，与自评正念只有弱且不显著的相关（r = 0.16，p = 0.08）。两类错误与不同指标相关：没有察觉到的数错与注意力短暂失灵相关（r = 0.32），自己发现后重置的次数与自评走神相关（r = 0.22），两者彼此不相关。重测信度只在表现最好和最差的两组人中测量（共 38 人，平均间隔 54 天）：准确率 ICC 0.48，数错 0.47，重置 0.72。
claims.study_type: psychometric replication study (cross-sectional, with retest subsample)
claims.sample: 127 recruited Asian undergraduates in Singapore; 116 analysed; 38 retested (21 top-tertile, 17 bottom-tertile)
claims.limitations: Student sample from a single university in Singapore. The analysed n was 116, not 127. Retest was done only in extreme-performance tertiles; the authors note this may underestimate reliability. Associations are cross-sectional and mostly small (r about 0.2-0.3), with some at trend level and no correction for multiple comparisons. The miscount/reset dissociation is a first, unreplicated finding. There was no training component. Treves et al. 2025 found weak validity of the BCT in ruminative adolescents.
claims.app_implication: Supports feasibility of the task in an Asian (Singaporean student) sample. Record self-caught resets separately from uncaught miscounts and frame resets neutrally ('noticed and restarted'), since they track self-reported mind wandering rather than attentional lapses. Do not present a high reset count as a skill score. Use accuracy or uncaught miscounts as the error metric, and drop double breath-9 presses as mechanical slips, as Wong did. Translate the verbatim instructions into Chinese for the measure mode, noting that the translation itself is unvalidated.

citation.authors: Wong KF, Massar SAA, Chee MWL, et al.
citation.title: Towards an Objective Measure of Mindfulness: Replicating and Extending the Features of the Breath-Counting Task

verification.checked_against: Crossref and PubMed metadata (Mindfulness 9(5):1402-1410, PMID 30294387, PMC6153891); full text from Europe PMC fullTextXML: Participants, verbatim BCT instructions, Data Analyses (exclusions), Results, Tables 1-2, reliability section and Discussion.
verification.problems: Metadata, protocol and reliability numbers match the full text: 127 recruited; mean age 23.4; 20-min task; verbatim instructions; ICC .48/.47/.72; split-half .57/.55/.33; 21+17 retested; 54-day interval. (1) The analysed sample was 116, not 125: from 127, 2 incomplete datasets, 7 non-compliant participants (0-7% accuracy) and 3 reset outliers were excluded, with one overlap. The claim mentions only the 2 incomplete datasets. (2) The accuracy-MAAS correlation was non-significant (r=.164, p=.08); 'only weakly' is fair, but its non-significance should be stated. (3) finding_zh '两类错误含义不同' overstates a correlational dissociation, and '眼睛至少半睁' mistranslates 'at least partly open'. (4) app_implication: calling resets 'non-negative' is not supported by the data. Reset rate correlated with more self-reported mind wandering (r=.22) and marginally with more cognitive failures (CFQ r=.18, p=.05), and the meta-awareness reading is the authors' speculation. 'East-Asian' also over-generalises a Singapore student sample. (5) Evidence weight lowered to low: this is a single cross-sectional sample, the key dissociation rests on small (r about .2-.3), uncorrected correlations, and retest data come from 38 extreme-group participants.

claims.topic: Loving-kindness meditation and positive emotions
claims.finding: Meta-analytic review of 24 articles (25 independent studies, N=1,759) on loving-kindness meditation (LKM) and self-reported positive emotions, including RCTs and non-randomised studies (search to June 2015). In the 8 RCTs comparing LKM with wait-list controls, LKM increased daily positive emotions: pooled Hedges' g=0.395 (95% CI 0.258–0.533) or 0.392 (0.254–0.530). The two estimates differ only in whether one trial's (Koopmann-Holm et al. 2013) high- or low-arousal measure was entered; they are not separate effects for high- and low-arousal emotions. Heterogeneity was not significant. The authors call this a medium effect; by Cohen's benchmarks it lies between small and medium. Against active controls the evidence was weak: 3 studies found no difference between LKM and 4 active conditions (mindfulness meditation, theatre therapy, memory training, positive-emotion regulation), and only 1 study found LKM better than concentration meditation. Within the wait-list RCTs, interventions focused on loving-kindness had g=0.424 (0.269–0.578) and compassion-focused ones g=0.286 (−0.018 to 0.589), but the difference was not significant (p>0.374). Low-powered meta-regressions found that neither total intervention length nor total intervention time predicted effect size (p>0.349). Among non-randomised pre-post studies, the 2 interventions without weekly courses (the authors' 'didactic components') had a smaller effect (g=0.116) than the other 5 (g≈0.30–0.45); this difference was not significant (p>0.083). The authors describe their conclusions as rather exploratory and warn that expectancy effects and self-selection may inflate the results.
claims.finding_zh: 对 24 篇文献（25 项独立研究，1759 人）的荟萃分析，考察慈心冥想与自评积极情绪，纳入随机和非随机研究（检索至 2015 年 6 月）。在 8 项以等待名单为对照的随机试验中，慈心练习使日常积极情绪增加，合并 g = 0.395（95% CI 0.258–0.533）或 0.392（0.254–0.530）。两个数值的差别只在于其中一项试验采用“高唤醒”还是“低唤醒”积极情绪指标，并不是分别针对两类情绪的效应。作者称之为中等效应，按常用标准介于小与中等之间。与其他积极活动（正念冥想、戏剧练习、记忆训练、积极情绪调节）相比，3 项研究都没有发现差异，只有 1 项研究发现慈心优于专注冥想。以“慈爱”为重点的练习 g = 0.424（0.269–0.578），以“悲悯”为重点的练习 g = 0.286（−0.018 至 0.589），但两者差异不显著。干预总时长和总练习时间都未能预测效应大小（这类分析的统计效力低）。在非随机研究中，2 项没有每周课程（讲解环节）的干预效应较小（g = 0.116），但与其他研究的差异不显著。作者认为结论仍属探索性，期望效应和自我选择可能使结果偏高。
claims.sample: 24 articles (25 independent studies), N=1,759; main pooled RCT estimate from 8 wait-list-controlled trials
claims.limitations: Main RCT estimate rests on 8 small wait-list-controlled trials, which cannot rule out expectancy effects. The few active-control comparisons were mostly null, and 38.9% of risk-of-bias ratings were high risk. Outcomes were self-reported only, and only English-language peer-reviewed studies were included. Subgroup and meta-regression analyses had low power and none was significant. The didactic-component result rests on 2 non-randomised studies. The authors call the conclusions exploratory.
claims.app_implication: Offer loving-kindness as an optional track that may modestly lift everyday positive feelings (grade C for that outcome). Do not present it as better than other meditation, do not promise reduced depression from LKM alone, and do not lengthen sessions expecting larger effects. A short explanation before practice is a reasonable low-cost choice, but the evidence for it is weak (2 non-randomised studies, non-significant difference).

citation.authors: Zeng X, Chiu CPK, Wang R, et al.
citation.title: The effect of loving-kindness meditation on positive emotions: a meta-analytic review

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata + PubMed abstract + Europe PMC full text (PMC4630307), including the results, figure legends, discussion and limitations
verification.problems: (1) Numbers misread: g=0.395 (0.258–0.533) and 0.392 (0.254–0.530) are not separate effects for high- and low-arousal positive emotions. They are two versions of the same pooled wait-list estimate, depending on whether one trial's (Koopmann-Holm 2013) high- or low-arousal measure was entered. (2) The claim leaves out that the loving-kindness vs compassion subgroup difference was not significant (p>0.374), so the contrast is overstated. (3) Omitted nulls: against active controls, 3 studies found no difference from 4 active conditions, and only 1 study found LKM better (than concentration meditation). (4) The 'no didactic components' finding rests on 2 non-randomised studies, with a non-significant subgroup difference (p>0.083). The length meta-regressions were low-powered (p>0.349). (5) 'Medium' is the authors' label; g≈0.39 falls between small and medium by Cohen's benchmarks. (6) Evidence weight 'moderate' is too high. The RCT estimate comes from 8 small wait-list trials, active-control comparisons were mostly null, 38.9% of risk-of-bias ratings were high, and the authors call their conclusions 'rather exploratory'. Metadata is correct.

claims.topic: Kindness-based meditation (loving-kindness, compassion) and health
claims.finding: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 22 RCTs of kindness-based meditation (KBM: loving-kindness, compassion; search to March 2013) in adults from the general population (10 trials), undergraduates (9) and patients (3). Trials were small (median n=65), and each pooled estimate combined only 2–3 trials. Against passive controls (wait-list, usual care, rest), KBM decreased self-reported depression (Hedges' g=−0.61, 95% CI −1.08 to −0.14; 2 trials) and increased mindfulness (0.63, 0.22–1.05; 2 trials), compassion (0.61, 0.24–0.99; 2 trials) and self-compassion (0.45, 0.15–0.75; 3 trials). Also against passive controls, life satisfaction and negative emotions did not differ. A gain in positive emotions in one trial was not confirmed in intention-to-treat analysis or in another trial, and a stress reduction (g=−0.46; 3 trials) lost significance in sensitivity analysis. Against progressive relaxation, positive emotions increased (0.42, 0.10–0.75; 2 trials). Against other active controls, such as mindfulness or concentration meditation, most outcomes did not differ. Methodological quality was low to moderate, and estimates were imprecise. The authors note that exposure to KBM may initially be challenging for some people.
claims.finding_zh: 对 22 项善意类冥想（慈心、悲悯冥想）随机对照试验的系统综述与荟萃分析（检索至 2013 年 3 月），对象包括一般成人（10 项）、大学生（9 项）和患者（3 项）。试验规模小（中位数 65 人），每个合并结果只来自 2–3 项试验。与被动对照（等待、常规照护、休息）相比：自评抑郁下降（g = −0.61，95% CI −1.08 至 −0.14；2 项试验），正念（0.63）、对他人的悲悯（0.61）和自我关怀（0.45）上升。同样与被动对照相比，生活满意度和负性情绪没有差异；积极情绪的提升在意向治疗分析和另一项试验中都没有得到证实；压力下降在敏感性分析中不再显著。与渐进式放松相比，积极情绪增加（0.42；2 项试验）。与正念、专注冥想等其他积极对照相比，多数结局没有差异。研究质量低到中等，置信区间宽。作者提醒：对一些人来说，刚接触这类练习可能有困难。
claims.study_type: systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs
claims.sample: 22 RCTs (median n=65 per trial); each pooled estimate from 2–3 trials
claims.limitations: Each pooled estimate rests on only 2–3 small trials, so confidence intervals are wide. Methodological quality was low to moderate (no trial at low risk of bias in every domain). 14 trials used active comparators, but they were of 7 different kinds and mostly could not be pooled. Follow-up was rarely measured, all but two trials were in the USA, and the search ended in 2013.
claims.app_implication: Introduce loving-kindness after basic breath practice, warn that it can feel awkward or stir up difficult feelings at first, and offer simpler targets. Avoid depression-treatment claims: the depression estimate comes from 2 small trials, and kindness practices were not shown to outperform other meditation.

citation.authors: Galante J, Galante I, Bekkers MJ, et al.
citation.title: Effect of kindness-based meditation on health and well-being: A systematic review and meta-analysis
citation.venue: Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata + PubMed abstract + accepted author manuscript full text (green OA copy via Cambridge Apollo / Cardiff ORCA), including characteristics, risk of bias and all comparison results
verification.problems: Metadata and every quoted number are correct. (1) Overstatement by omission: each pooled estimate combined only 2–3 small trials. Depression, mindfulness and compassion used 2 trials each (df=1), self-compassion 3, and positive emotions vs progressive relaxation 2. Framing these as results of a '22 RCT' review hides that. (2) Omitted nulls against passive controls: no difference in life satisfaction or negative emotions. A positive-emotion gain in one trial was not confirmed in intention-to-treat analysis or in another trial. A stress reduction (g=−0.46) lost significance in sensitivity analysis. (3) The limitation 'few active-control comparisons' is inaccurate. 14 of 22 trials used active comparators, but they were of 7 different kinds, mostly could not be pooled, and mostly showed no difference.

claims.topic: Mindfulness training, mind wandering and cognitive performance
claims.finding: RCT: 48 undergraduates (14 male, 34 female; mean age 20.8) were randomised to a 2-week mindfulness course (n=26) or a nutrition class (n=22; active control). Both met 45 min, four times a week for 2 weeks. The mindfulness group also did 10 min of daily meditation at home; the nutrition group logged daily food intake. Relative to nutrition, mindfulness training improved accuracy on a modified GRE verbal (reading-comprehension) section (condition x session F(1,46)=5.61, p=.02). It also improved working memory capacity on the OSPAN (F(1,46)=3.95, p=.05). It reduced probe-caught (p=.006), self-caught (p=.05) and retrospectively reported (p=.03) mind wandering during testing. The GRE gain was described as analogous to 16 percentile points. A moderated-mediation analysis found that reduced mind wandering mediated the performance gain only among participants with high baseline mind wandering (indirect effect significant at +1 SD, p=.035; not at the mean or -1 SD). The nutrition group showed no significant pre-post changes.
claims.finding_zh: 随机对照试验：48 名本科生被随机分到 2 周正念课（26 人）或营养课（22 人，积极对照）。两种课都是每周 4 次、每次 45 分钟；正念组每天另做 10 分钟冥想，营养组每天记录饮食。与营养课相比，正念组在改编版 GRE 阅读理解测验上的正确率提高（p = 0.02），工作记忆容量也提高（p = 0.05，处于显著性边缘），两项测验中的走神都减少。GRE 的提升约相当于 16 个百分位。统计上的调节中介分析显示，只有在前测时本来就容易走神的人中，成绩提升可以由走神减少来解释。营养课组没有显著变化。
claims.sample: n=48 undergraduates (26 mindfulness, 22 nutrition)
claims.limitations: Small single-site sample of undergraduates at UC Santa Barbara. Outcomes were measured only within a week after training, with no longer follow-up. Several interactions were borderline (WMC p=.05; self-caught mind wandering p=.05). The mediation held only at +1 SD of baseline mind wandering (p=.035). Participants could not be blinded to condition. Whitfield et al. 2022 (Neuropsychology Review; 56 RCTs) found only small cognitive effects of MBPs (overall g=0.15; working memory g=0.23), with no advantage over active comparators.
claims.app_implication: Can be cited for 'in one small RCT, a 2-week mindfulness course reduced mind wandering during demanding tests'. Never extrapolate to exam-score or productivity promises.

citation.authors: Mrazek MD, Franklin MS, Phillips DT, et al.
citation.title: Mindfulness Training Improves Working Memory Capacity and GRE Performance While Reducing Mind Wandering

verification.checked_against: Crossref and PubMed metadata (Psychol Sci 24(5):776-781, PMID 23538911); full-text PDF of the article (hosted by the UCSB Center for Mindfulness & Human Potential), read in full: Method, Results, Tables 1-2, Discussion. Whitfield et al. 2022 was checked via its Europe PMC abstract (PMID 34350544).
verification.problems: Metadata and all study details match the full text: 48 undergraduates randomised 26 vs 22; 2 weeks of 45-min classes four times a week; 10 min daily home meditation; nutrition active control; GRE and WMC gains; reduced mind wandering; moderated mediation; no changes in the nutrition group. (1) finding_zh '成绩提升是通过走神减少来实现的' turns a statistical moderated mediation into a causal mechanism. The indirect effect was significant only at +1 SD of baseline mind wandering (p=.035), and the mediator-outcome path was not randomised. (2) Limitations say 'short follow-up', but there was no follow-up beyond a post-test within one week. (3) Limitations say details came only from a press release; the full text has now been checked and confirms them. (4) Borderline results were omitted: the WMC interaction was p=.05 and self-caught mind wandering p=.05. The Whitfield 2022 reference was verified (Neuropsychol Rev; overall g=0.15; MBPs did not outperform active comparators).

claims.topic: The mind-wandering / awareness / shifting / focus cycle in breath meditation
claims.finding: fMRI study in which 14 meditation practitioners performed breath-focused meditation and pressed a button whenever they realised their mind had wandered, then returned focus to the breath. Around these presses the authors modelled a four-phase cycle: mind wandering, awareness of mind wandering, shifting of attention, and sustained attention. Mind-wandering periods engaged default-mode regions, awareness of mind wandering engaged salience-network regions, and shifting and sustained attention engaged elements of the executive network; activations were modulated by lifetime meditation experience.
claims.finding_zh: 功能磁共振研究：14 名冥想练习者做呼吸专注冥想，每当意识到自己走神就按一下按钮，然后回到呼吸。研究者据此划分出一个四阶段循环：走神、觉察到走神、转移注意、保持专注。走神时默认模式网络活跃，觉察到走神时突显网络活跃，转回并保持注意时执行控制网络活跃；这些激活程度与终生练习时长有关。
claims.sample: n=14 meditation practitioners
claims.limitations: Very small sample of experienced practitioners; no control group; brain-activity correlates do not demonstrate clinical benefit.
claims.app_implication: Script the core loop as 走神 → 发现 → 放下 → 回到呼吸 and treat noticing as success, not failure. An optional 我走神了 tap can mirror the button-press paradigm; show it as neutral practice data, never a performance score, and keep brain-network language out of consumer copy.

citation.authors: Hasenkamp W, Wilson-Mendenhall CD, Duncan E, et al.
citation.title: Mind wandering and attention during focused meditation: A fine-grained temporal analysis of fluctuating cognitive states

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; PubMed abstract (PMID 21782031). The NeuroImage full text is not openly accessible. Sample and experience-effect details were corroborated in the open-access companion paper on the same 14 participants (Hasenkamp & Barsalou 2012, Front Hum Neurosci, PMC3290768).
verification.problems: No discrepancies found. The metadata (NeuroImage 59(1):750-760, Jan 2012, epub July 2011; 4 authors, last Barsalou LW), n=14, the breath-focus task with button presses, the four-phase model, the DMN/salience/executive findings and the modulation by lifetime meditation experience all match the abstract. Notes from the companion paper: participants were aged 28-66 (3 male) with at least 1 year of regular practice; lifetime practice was bimodal (5 with more than 2000 h, 9 with less than 1200 h). The main experience effect was lower medial PFC/ACC activity during the shift phase in more-practised participants. The phases are model-defined time windows around self-reported button presses.

claims.topic: Focused attention vs open monitoring meditation styles
claims.finding: Influential theoretical review that conceptualises meditation as a family of complex emotional and attentional regulatory training regimes. Using Buddhist contemplative techniques and their secular clinical derivatives as its framework, it distinguishes two commonly studied styles, which are often combined within a session or over a practitioner's training. Focused attention (FA) meditation is the voluntary focusing of attention on a chosen object (e.g., breath sensations); the typical instruction is to notice when attention has wandered, release the distraction and return to the object. Open monitoring (OM) meditation is non-reactive, moment-to-moment monitoring of the content of experience without an explicit object of focus. The authors describe OM practices as typically starting with FA training to calm the mind, with the monitoring skill developed in FA becoming the point of transition into OM. They propose that these practices could have long-term effects on brain and behaviour.
claims.finding_zh: 一篇影响很大的理论综述，把冥想看作一类训练情绪与注意调节的方法。它以佛教禅修及其世俗化临床形式为框架，区分了两种最常被研究的方式，两者在实践中常在同一次练习或长期训练中结合使用。专注型（FA）是自主地把注意力放在一个选定对象上（如呼吸的感觉），通常的指导是发现走神后放下干扰、回到对象。开放觉察型（OM）不设特定对象，不加反应地觉察每一刻经验的内容。作者指出，开放觉察练习通常先用专注练习让心安定下来，专注中培养的觉察能力再成为过渡到开放觉察的起点。作者认为这些练习可能对大脑和行为产生长期影响，但这属于理论推测。
claims.sample: not applicable (narrative review)
claims.limitations: Conceptual framework drawing on traditional descriptions and early, small neuroscience studies (mostly long-term practitioners compared with novices); it is not outcome evidence. Real-world practices often mix FA and OM. The clinical efficacy of each style alone, and of the FA-then-OM order, is largely untested.
claims.app_implication: Use FA/OM as the app's practice taxonomy (专注呼吸, 开放觉察) and label each session by style. Introducing FA before OM follows the progression the review describes from contemplative traditions (FA first to steady attention, then OM). It is a traditional sequence, not an experimentally tested one, so do not claim that one style or order is more effective.

citation.authors: Lutz A, Slagter HA, Dunne JD, et al.
citation.title: Attention regulation and monitoring in meditation

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; PubMed abstract (PMID 18329323); full-text PDF of the TICS article (Center for Healthy Minds copy), including the introduction, Box 1, Box 2 and Table 1
verification.problems: The finding, finding_zh and citation metadata are accurate. The 'e.g., the breath' example is in Box 1 and Table 1, and the 'long-term impact on the brain and behavior' wording is in the abstract. The problem is the app_implication, which says teaching FA before OM is 'a design convention borrowed from MBSR/MBCT'. This source itself documents the progression. Box 2 says OM practices share 'the initial use of FA training to calm the mind and reduce distractions', and that FA's monitoring skill 'becomes the main point of transition into OM practice'. The paper describes this from contemplative traditions (Zen, Vipassana, Tibetan Buddhism), which MBSR draws on. The order is still experimentally untested, so the advice not to claim superiority stands. I fixed the app_implication and added the Box 1/Box 2 details to the finding.

claims.topic: Brief daily meditation (13 min/day): when effects appear
claims.finding: RCT in healthy, meditation-naive adults aged 18-45 in New York City. Of 76 recruited, 14 dropped out and 20 were excluded (44.7% attrition), leaving 42 analysed (about 21 per group). Participants were randomised to a 13-minute guided meditation recording (Journey Meditation: breathing exercises and body scan) or a 13-minute science-podcast segment daily for 8 weeks. Meditators averaged 5.5 sessions a week (78.6% adherence); controls averaged 6.4 (91.4%). No measure differed at 4 weeks. At 8 weeks, group x time interactions favoured meditation for total mood disturbance (POMS, p=0.034, adjusted for change in sleep quality), Beck Anxiety Inventory (p=0.038), fatigue (p=0.012), Stroop congruent-trial accuracy (p=0.025), N-back accuracy (p=0.032) and recognition memory (p=0.046). Meditators also showed a smaller rise in state anxiety during the Trier Social Stress Test (p=0.050). There were no effects on baseline or stress-induced cortisol, the other mood questionnaires (including the Beck Depression Inventory and Perceived Stress Scale), Reading Span, Wisconsin Card Sorting, Flanker or pattern separation. Unexpectedly, sleep quality (PSQI) was worse in the meditation group than in controls at 8 weeks (time x group p=0.005): controls improved, meditators did not, and meditators' sleep efficiency fell. Meditators did more sessions between 8 pm and 3 am (48.8% vs 42.4%). Changes in emotional regulation were more strongly linked to improved affective state than to improved cognition.
claims.finding_zh: 随机对照试验：纽约 18–45 岁、没有冥想经验的健康成人。招募 76 人，14 人退出、20 人被排除（流失率 44.7%），最终分析 42 人（每组约 21 人）。参与者每天听 13 分钟引导冥想录音（Journey Meditation，含呼吸练习和身体扫描）或 13 分钟科普播客片段（对照），持续 8 周。冥想组平均每周听 5.5 次（依从率 78.6%），对照组 6.4 次（91.4%）。第 4 周时两组没有任何指标出现差异。第 8 周时，与对照相比，冥想组的情绪困扰总分（POMS，p = 0.034，已校正睡眠质量变化）、贝克焦虑量表得分（p = 0.038）和疲劳（p = 0.012）改善，Stroop 一致条件正确率（p = 0.025）、N-back 正确率（p = 0.032）和再认记忆（p = 0.046）提高，社会应激测试中状态焦虑的上升幅度较小（p = 0.050）。皮质醇（基线和应激反应）、其他情绪问卷（包括贝克抑郁量表和知觉压力量表）及另外几项认知测试均无显著差异。出乎意料的是，第 8 周时冥想组的睡眠质量（PSQI）比对照组差（p = 0.005）：对照组睡眠改善，冥想组没有改善，睡眠效率反而下降；冥想组在晚上 8 点到凌晨 3 点之间练习的比例更高（48.8% 对 42.4%）。
claims.sample: 76 recruited; n=42 analysed (about 21 per group), healthy meditation-naive adults aged 18-45
claims.limitations: Small single-site trial with 44.7% attrition and a completer-only analysis: participants who listened fewer than 5 times a week for two consecutive weeks were disqualified. Many outcomes were tested without multiplicity correction, and the significant effects had p=0.025-0.050. Several analyses were adjusted for the unexpected change in sleep quality. Mood outcomes were self-reported, and adherence was logged only by website log-ins. The study was partly funded by the founder and CEO of Journey Meditation, whose recording was tested. Healthy young adults only, with no follow-up beyond 8 weeks.
claims.app_implication: Can inform, but not establish, a default of roughly 10-15 min/day; only a 13-minute dose was tested. Do not promise a timeline. At most say that in one small trial, differences from a podcast control appeared after 8 weeks of 13-minute sessions (about 5-6 a week) but not at 4 weeks. Do not cite this study for sleep or wind-down benefits: sleep quality was worse in its meditation group, possibly linked to late-evening sessions.

citation.authors: Basso JC, McHale A, Ende V, et al.
citation.title: Brief, daily meditation enhances attention, memory, mood, and emotional regulation in non-experienced meditators

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; PubMed abstract (PMID 30153464); full published article PDF (Behavioural Brain Research version, archived University of Rochester copy via web.archive.org), including methods, results, discussion, limitations and acknowledgements
verification.problems: (1) Sample: the full text reports N, so it is not unknown: 76 recruited, 14 dropped out and 20 excluded (44.7% attrition), 42 analysed (about 21 per group). (2) The claim omits an adverse result: at 8 weeks sleep quality (PSQI) was worse in the meditation group than in controls (time x group p=0.005; controls improved, meditators did not, and meditators' sleep efficiency fell), and meditators did more sessions between 8 pm and 3 am. Several mood and TSST analyses were then adjusted for the change in sleep quality. (3) It omits nulls: no effect on baseline or TSST cortisol, on the other mood questionnaires (including BDI depression and perceived stress), or on Reading Span, Wisconsin Card Sorting, Flanker or pattern separation. The significant effects sit at p=0.025-0.050 with no multiplicity correction, and the TSST result (p=0.050) is a smaller stress-induced rise in state anxiety. (4) It was a completer analysis: participants listening fewer than 5 times a week for two consecutive weeks were disqualified, and meditators averaged 5.5 sessions a week, not daily. (5) The study was partly funded by the founder and CEO of Journey Meditation, whose recording was the intervention. (6) The app_implication generalises one small trial to 'in trials' and treats a single 13-minute dose as support for a 10-15 minute range. (7) evidence_weight 'low' should be very-low given 45% attrition, completer analysis, multiple outcomes and borderline p-values. Citation metadata and the abstract-level statements are verified.

claims.topic: Walking meditation (Buddhist walking meditation) in older adults with depressive symptoms
claims.finding: Randomised exercise intervention study in 45 adults aged 60–90 with mild-to-moderate depressive symptoms, allocated to sedentary control, traditional walking exercise, or Buddhism-based walking meditation (aerobic walking incorporating Buddhist meditation), 3 times per week for 12 weeks. Muscle strength, flexibility, agility, balance, cardiorespiratory endurance and flow-mediated dilation improved in both walking groups; depression score decreased (p<0.05) only in the walking-meditation group; LDL cholesterol, cortisol and interleukin-6 decreased only in the walking-meditation group.
claims.finding_zh: 随机干预研究：45 名 60–90 岁、有轻中度抑郁症状的老人分为久坐对照、普通步行锻炼和佛教行禅（结合冥想的有氧步行）三组，每周 3 次，共 12 周。两个步行组的体能和血管功能都有改善；只有行禅组的抑郁评分显著下降（p<0.05，组内比较）。
claims.sample: n=45 older adults (three arms)
claims.limitations: Very small; the abstract reports within-group changes rather than a between-group test of depression; single research group in Thailand; no systematic review of walking meditation was located.
claims.app_implication: Walking meditation can be offered as an optional variant for people who find sitting difficult, labelled D (insufficient evidence), with no mood or cardiometabolic claims.

citation.authors: Prakhinkit S, Suppapitiporn S, Tanaka H, et al.
citation.title: Effects of Buddhism Walking Meditation on Depression, Functional Fitness, and Endothelium-Dependent Vasodilation in Depressed Elderly
citation.venue: The Journal of Alternative and Complementary Medicine

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; PubMed abstract (PMID 24372522); PEDro record 45288; PubMed and Europe PMC searches for systematic reviews of walking meditation. Full text is paywalled and was not read.
verification.problems: None against the abstract: design (randomised, three arms, n=45, ages 60-90, mild-to-moderate depressive symptoms, 3 times a week for 12 weeks), the fitness and FMD results in both walking groups, the depression decrease (p<0.05) only in the walking-meditation group, and LDL, cortisol and IL-6 falling only in that group all match. The '组内比较' annotation in finding_zh is an inference from the abstract's wording ('decreased (p<0.05) only in the BWM group'), consistent with the claim's own limitation. Context: PEDro scores the trial 5/10 (no concealed allocation, no assessor blinding, no intention-to-treat analysis). The limitation that no systematic review of walking meditation was located holds: PubMed returned only a 2021 review protocol and a 2024 narrative review by two of this trial's own authors.

claims.topic: NICE hypertension guideline position on relaxation therapies
claims.finding: NICE guideline NG136 (published 28 August 2019; last updated 26 February 2026) deleted the 2011 recommendation on relaxation therapies. The evidence 'was limited to a single small study', which suggested some benefit in reducing angina and myocardial infarction but also suggested an increase in stroke; the committee judged the study 'not adequate to assess the effectiveness of these therapies or to make a recommendation'. The 2011 guideline had said relaxation therapies could reduce blood pressure (without recommending routine use), but that rested on blood-pressure evidence only, with no evidence of a direct benefit such as improved quality of life or fewer cardiovascular events. The committee therefore found 'insufficient evidence of benefit to recommend that people pursue this option themselves'. It is 'not the intention of the committee to stop people from trying relaxation therapies if they wish to', but to make people aware there is less evidence of benefit than for other lifestyle interventions or drug treatment. The clinical focus for non-drug treatment should be lifestyle change such as regular exercise and maintaining a healthy weight, and NICE made a research recommendation on whether relaxation therapies reduce cardiovascular events or improve quality of life.
claims.finding_zh: 英国NICE高血压指南NG136（2019年8月28日发布，2026年2月26日最近更新）删除了2011版关于放松疗法的推荐。相关证据“仅限于一项小型研究”：该研究提示心绞痛和心肌梗死可能减少，但也提示卒中可能增加；委员会认为这项研究不足以评估放松疗法的效果。2011版曾表示放松疗法可以降低血压（但不建议常规提供），不过那只基于降压数据，缺乏改善生活质量或减少心血管事件等直接获益的证据，因此委员会认为“没有足够的获益证据推荐人们自行采用”。委员会并不打算阻止愿意尝试的人尝试放松疗法，只是提醒其获益证据少于其他生活方式干预或药物治疗；非药物治疗应以规律运动、保持健康体重等生活方式改变为重点，并建议进一步研究放松疗法能否减少心血管事件或改善生活质量。
claims.sample: Guideline evidence review H (relaxation therapies): a single small study
claims.limitations: Covers 'relaxation therapies' broadly rather than slow paced breathing specifically. NICE's concern was the lack of evidence on direct benefits (quality of life, cardiovascular events); it did not conclude that relaxation fails to lower blood pressure. This is one national (UK) guideline and other bodies differ in detail: the 2013 AHA scientific statement rated other relaxation therapies Class III but device-guided breathing Class IIa (Level of Evidence B) for BP lowering.
claims.app_implication: NICE does not recommend relaxation therapies for managing hypertension (insufficient evidence of benefit). The app must never position breathing as a blood-pressure treatment and should point users with hypertension to standard care. Attribute this to NICE rather than to 'all major guidance', because other bodies differ in detail (e.g., AHA 2013 on device-guided breathing).

citation.authors: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
citation.title: Hypertension in adults: diagnosis and management (NICE guideline NG136)
citation.venue: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)

verification.checked_against: NICE NG136 official pages (overview, Recommendations, Rationale and impact > Relaxation therapies, Recommendations for research, Update information), fetched and read in full
verification.problems: Metadata, dates (published 28 Aug 2019; last updated 26 Feb 2026) and every quoted phrase match the NICE 'Rationale and impact' page. Problems: (1) app_implication overgeneralizes from one UK guideline to 'Major hypertension guidance'. The 2013 AHA scientific statement (Brook et al., Hypertension 2013;61:1360-83, PMID 23608661, abstract checked) rated other relaxation therapies Class III but device-guided breathing Class IIa (LOE B) for BP lowering, so the generalization does not hold for breathing specifically. (2) The finding omits that the deleted 2011 recommendation rested on BP-lowering evidence only. NICE removed it for lack of evidence on direct outcomes (QoL, CV events), not because relaxation was shown not to lower BP. (3) finding_zh uses '显示' where the source says 'suggested' ('提示'), and the source also says the study was 'not adequate to assess the effectiveness'. (4) The 'not the intention' quote is truncated before 'if they wish to, but to make people aware that there is less evidence for benefit...'.

claims.topic: Breathwork for stress, anxiety and depressive symptoms
claims.finding: Meta-analysis of RCTs comparing breathwork with non-breathwork controls (searches to February 2022). Primary outcome, self-reported stress: k = 12, 785 adults, g = −0.35 (95% CI −0.55 to −0.14), p = 0.0009, I² = 42%; most studies at moderate risk of bias; Egger's test p = 0.947. Secondary outcomes: anxiety k = 20, g = −0.32 (−0.48 to −0.16), I² = 51%; depressive symptoms k = 18, g = −0.40 (−0.58 to −0.22), I² = 58%. No adverse events attributed to breathwork were reported in the studies that monitored them (4; 6 including secondary-outcome studies), but participants in one fast-paced breathwork study reported hot flushes, shortness of breath and/or sweating. The authors urge caution to avoid 'a miscalibration between hype and evidence'.
claims.finding_zh: 随机对照试验元分析（检索至2022年2月）：与非呼吸练习对照相比，呼吸练习使自评压力小到中等程度下降，k = 12，785名成人，g = −0.35（95%置信区间−0.55至−0.14），p = 0.0009，I² = 42%；多数研究为中等偏倚风险。焦虑：k = 20，g = −0.32（−0.48至−0.16）；抑郁症状：k = 18，g = −0.40（−0.58至−0.22），异质性中等。有不良事件监测的研究未发现由呼吸练习引起的不良事件，但一项快速呼吸研究中有参与者出现潮热、气短或出汗。作者提醒不要让宣传超过证据。
claims.sample: 12 RCTs, 785 adults (stress); 20 RCTs (anxiety); 18 RCTs (depressive symptoms)
claims.limitations: Pools heterogeneous techniques (slow, fast, yogic, biofeedback-assisted); participants could not be blinded; many inactive or waitlist controls; moderate risk of bias; few trials monitored adverse events.
claims.app_implication: This is the headline number for 'breathing practice and stress' in the evidence panel: small-to-moderate (g ≈ −0.35), always shown next to the null placebo-controlled RCT (Fincham 2023 RCT).

citation.authors: Fincham GW, Strauss C, Montero-Marin J, et al.
citation.title: Effect of breathwork on stress and mental health: A meta-analysis of randomised-controlled trials

verification.checked_against: Crossref + PubMed metadata; open-access PMC full text (PMC9828383), including Results, Table 1 subgroup analyses and Discussion
verification.problems: No discrepancies. Metadata and every number match the PMC full text: k = 12, 785 adults, g = −0.35 [−0.55, −0.14], p = 0.0009, I² = 42%, Egger p = 0.947; anxiety k = 20, g = −0.32 [−0.48, −0.16], I² = 51%; depression k = 18, g = −0.40 [−0.58, −0.22], I² = 58%. The adverse-event statements (4 studies; 6 including secondary outcomes; Ravindran fast-paced study side effects) and the 'miscalibration between hype and evidence' quote also match. Optional context, not errors: the effects are post-intervention only, as follow-up could not be meta-analysed. Of the 12 stress trials, 9 had 'some concerns' and 3 were at high risk of bias. The stress effect was significant in nonclinical samples but not in the physical- or mental-health subgroups (the subgroup difference was non-significant), and the authors say it may be premature to recommend breathwork in clinical populations. Removing one outlier gave g = −0.27.

claims.topic: Coherent breathing at ~5.5/min vs a 12/min breathing placebo
claims.finding: Pre-registered (NCT05676658), participant-blinded, parallel RCT run online via Prolific. 400 UK adults were randomized (blocks of 2) to coherent breathing at ~5.5 breaths/min (equal ~5.5-s inhale and exhale) or a matched attention-placebo paced at 12 breaths/min (2.5-s inhale and exhale). Both were audio-guided, ~10 min/day for 4 weeks, and both arms were told to breathe softly through the nose and abdominally. Credibility and expectancy did not differ between arms. Primary outcome, DASS-21 stress at post-intervention: no group × time interaction (F(1,377) = 0.089, p = 0.765, ηp² < 0.001) and no main effect of group (p = 0.961), but a significant main effect of time (F = 72.1, p < 0.001, ηp² = 0.161). Results were similar at 1-month follow-up and for anxiety, depression and wellbeing: scores improved over time in both arms, with no significant difference between arms. Sleep disturbance did not change in either arm. Per-protocol and multiple-imputation analyses gave the same conclusions. The authors found no measurable effect of coherent breathing over and above a well-designed breathwork placebo.
claims.finding_zh: 预注册、参与者设盲的线上平行随机对照试验（NCT05676658）：400名英国成人被随机分配到约每分钟5.5次的“相干呼吸”（吸、呼各约5.5秒）或每分钟12次的安慰剂节律呼吸（吸、呼各2.5秒），均由音频引导，每天约10分钟，持续4周，两组都被要求用鼻子轻柔地腹式呼吸。两组对练习的可信度和预期无显著差异。主要结局DASS-21压力在干预后无组别×时间交互作用（F(1,377) = 0.089，p = 0.765，ηp² < 0.001），也无组别主效应（p = 0.961），但时间效应显著（F = 72.1，p < 0.001，ηp² = 0.161）。1个月随访以及焦虑、抑郁、幸福感的结果类似：两组得分都随时间改善，但两组之间无显著差异。睡眠困扰在两组中都没有变化。按方案分析和多重插补分析结论相同。作者结论：相干呼吸没有表现出超过精心设计的呼吸安慰剂的可测量效果。
claims.sample: n = 400 adults (UK, recruited online via Prolific); ~95% completed post-intervention measures
claims.limitations: Single trial in a non-clinical online (Prolific) sample, and ~10 min/day for 4 weeks may be a low dose. Adherence was self-reported (mean ~20 of 28 sessions), and actual breathing rate and technique could not be verified because no physiological measures were collected. The research team was not blinded to allocation for analysis. The 12/min 'placebo' was itself a guided, nasal, diaphragmatic paced-breathing practice, so the trial tests rate specificity rather than breathing practice versus nothing. There was no no-practice control, so the improvement seen in both arms cannot be attributed to practice; the authors consider expectation, attention, time and regression to the mean equally plausible.
claims.app_implication: Do not claim that 5.5–6/min is better for stress, anxiety, mood or sleep than other calm, guided breathing. Let users pick a comfortable pace and show this null result openly. Do not attribute the improvement seen in both arms to the practice itself: the trial had no no-practice control, and the authors consider expectation, attention, time and regression to the mean equally plausible explanations.

citation.authors: Fincham GW, Strauss C, Cavanagh K
citation.title: Effect of coherent breathing on mental health and wellbeing: a randomised placebo-controlled trial

verification.checked_against: Crossref + PubMed metadata; open-access PMC full text (PMC10719279), including Methods, Results (primary, secondary, sleep, adherence, credibility) and Discussion
verification.problems: Metadata, registration (NCT05676658, registered 9 Jan 2023), design and all statistics match the PMC full text. Problems: (1) 'both arms improved by the same amount' and the zh '两组改善幅度一样' / '可信度和预期相同' turn non-significant differences into claims of equality; the source says the improvement was 'not different between groups' and found no significant differences. (2) An omitted null: sleep disturbance did not change over time in either arm. (3) The limitations understate the gaps. No physiological measures were collected at all (not merely missing from the abstract), so actual breathing rate could not be verified, and the research team was not blinded to allocation during analysis. (4) evidence_weight 'high' is too high for a single trial with unblinded analysis, self-reported adherence, unverified breathing and a low ~10 min/day dose; corrected to 'moderate'. (5) app_implication 'benefit may come from regular guided practice itself' goes beyond the design: there was no no-practice arm, and the authors call expectation, attention, history, maturation or regression to the mean equally plausible explanations.

claims.topic: Extended exhale vs equal ratio over 12 weeks
claims.finding: Randomized, single-blinded trial (NCT02870868) in healthy adults aged 30-60 (mean age 41; 79% women). Entry required a PROMIS Anxiety T-score >=45 at screening (i.e., not unusually relaxed); baseline mean was about 56. 99 were enrolled and randomized (the abstract says 100); 97 were in the intention-to-treat analysis and 94 had complete data. Everyone did 2 weeks of basic yoga-based slow breathing. Participants were then assigned to 10 weeks of exhale longer than inhale (E>I) or exhale equal to inhale (E=I), with breathing progressively slowed to about 2.7-2.8 breaths/min by week 12. Practice comprised 12 weekly 45-min private classes (mean attendance 10.7 ± 1.5) plus home practice 4.8 ± 1.2 times/week. Smart-shirt (HEXOSKIN) checks during two one-week home periods showed good adherence to the assigned ratios. PROMIS Anxiety T-scores fell from baseline to 12 weeks in both arms (pooled -4.85 ± 5.53; E>I -5.37 ± 6.46, 95% CI -7.24 to -3.49; E=I -4.30 ± 4.32, 95% CI -5.60 to -3.00). The CI the abstract places next to the pooled value is the E=I arm's CI. Lab-measured high-frequency HRV did not change significantly in either arm, and RMSSD changes were also non-significant. Between-arm differences favoured E>I but were small and non-significant: anxiety difference 1.07 points (95% CI -1.19 to 3.32; p = 0.35; d = 0.2); HF-HRV p = 0.56, d = 0.12. Thirty adverse events were recorded (24 mild, 6 moderate). All 12 that occurred during classes were mild, most often lightheadedness (n = 9).
claims.finding_zh: 单盲随机试验（NCT02870868），对象是30–60岁的健康成人（平均41岁，79%为女性），筛查时PROMIS焦虑T分需≥45（即不比一般人群明显更放松），基线平均约56分。共入组并随机分配99人（摘要写作100人），意向治疗分析97人，94人数据完整。所有人先用2周学习基础的瑜伽式慢呼吸，之后10周分别练习“呼气长于吸气”或“吸呼等长”，呼吸被逐步放慢，到第12周约每分钟2.7–2.8次。12次每周一次、每次45分钟的一对一课程平均出席10.7 ± 1.5次，居家练习每周4.8 ± 1.2次；在两段各一周的居家练习中用智能服装（HEXOSKIN）核查，参与者基本按指定吸呼比练习。12周后两组的PROMIS焦虑分数都下降（合计−4.85 ± 5.53；“呼气更长”组−5.37 ± 6.46，95%CI −7.24至−3.49；“等长”组−4.30 ± 4.32，95%CI −5.60至−3.00；摘要中与合计值并列的置信区间其实是“等长”组的数值）。由于没有不做呼吸练习的对照组，这一下降不能完全归功于呼吸练习。在实验室测得的高频心率变异性（HF-HRV）两组均无显著变化，RMSSD的变化也不显著。组间比较略偏向“呼气更长”，但差异很小且无统计学意义：焦虑相差1.07分（95%CI −1.19至3.32，p = 0.35，d = 0.2）；HF-HRV p = 0.56，d = 0.12。研究期间共记录30起不良事件（24起轻度、6起中度）；课堂上发生的12起均为轻度，最常见的是头晕（9起）。
claims.study_type: RCT (single-blinded, two active arms, no inactive control)
claims.sample: n = 99 healthy adults aged 30-60 randomized (abstract states 100); 97 in ITT analysis; 94 with complete data
claims.limitations: No non-breathing control, so the within-group anxiety drop is not a causal estimate. Regression to the mean is possible because entry required PROMIS Anxiety >=45. Teacher-led, very slow yoga breathing (about 3 breaths/min after progressive training) differs from typical app pacing of about 6/min. Sample mostly women and highly educated, with anxiety and depressive disorders excluded. Participants knew their own ratio. Powered for medium effects (d = 0.5), so it is underpowered to detect d of about 0.2. The abstract's sample size and CI do not match the full text.
claims.app_implication: Breath ratio looks like a matter of preference, not a potency setting. A mild exhale emphasis is a fine default, but present an equal ratio as equally valid. Do not promise HRV changes from regular practice. Very slow breathing can cause lightheadedness, so tell users to ease off if they feel dizzy.

citation.authors: Birdee G, Nelson K, Wallston K, et al.
citation.title: Slow breathing for reducing stress: The effect of extending exhale

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; PubMed abstract (PMID 36871835); PMC full text PMC10395759 via Europe PMC, including Methods, Results, Table 1, Table 3, Table 4 and Table 5
verification.problems: (1) Sample: the abstract says 100 participants, but the results report 99 enrolled and randomized (Table 3: 50 E=I, 49 E>I), 97 in the ITT analysis and 94 with complete data. (2) The CI [-5.60, -3.00] that the abstract (and the claim) attach to the pooled change of -4.85 ± 5.53 is the equal-ratio arm's within-group CI in Table 5, not a pooled CI. Arm values: E>I -5.37 ± 6.46 [-7.24, -3.49]; E=I -4.30 ± 4.32 [-5.60, -3.00]. (3) d = 0.2 applies only to the PROMIS Anxiety between-arm comparison (difference 1.07, 95% CI -1.19 to 3.32, p = 0.350). For HF-HRV, d = 0.12 (p = 0.563). (4) 'Regular slow breathing reduced psychological stress' is causal wording for an uncontrolled pre-post change. Entry required PROMIS Anxiety >=45 (baseline mean about 56), so regression to the mean is possible. finding_zh '没有改变HRV' overstates a non-significant change. (5) Missing context that matters for the app. The ratio phase lasted 10 weeks after a 2-week run-in of basic slow breathing, and breathing was progressively slowed to about 2.7-2.8 breaths/min. Practice included teacher-led 45-min classes. The sample was aged 30-60 and 79% women. There were 30 adverse events, mostly mild; lightheadedness was the most common class-related event (n = 9). Citation metadata (authors, year, title, venue, DOI, PMID) is correct.

claims.topic: Voluntary slow breathing and vagally mediated HRV: during practice, right after one session, after multi-session training
claims.finding: Pre-registered systematic review and meta-analysis (PROSPERO CRD42020173255; searches to June 2020) of voluntary slow breathing (<10 breaths/min, most often ~6/min) versus control conditions breathing at >10/min, on vagally mediated HRV. Of 1,842 full-text articles assessed, 223 studies were included (172 during-session, 16 immediately after one session, 49 after multi-session interventions). After outlier exclusion: during practice, RMSSD Hedges' g = 0.53 (95% CI 0.43 to 0.62; k = 71; I² = 81%) and absolute LF power g = 1.49 (1.28 to 1.69; k = 57; I² = 93%); immediately after a single session, RMSSD g = 0.14 (0.03 to 0.24; k = 8; I² = 0%); after multi-session interventions, resting RMSSD g = 0.32 (0.08 to 0.56; k = 22; I² = 79%). Egger's test was non-significant for RMSSD during practice (p = .673) and after interventions (p = .620) but showed funnel-plot asymmetry for LF power during practice (p < .001; trim-and-fill imputed no missing studies). Overall risk of bias was rated high in 215 studies, 'some concerns' in 5 and low in 1 (4 unpublished studies could not be rated). Many studies did not report vagal HRV indices (e.g., 58% did not report RMSSD during practice). The authors state that the high risk of bias calls for careful interpretation.
claims.finding_zh: 预注册的系统综述与元分析（PROSPERO CRD42020173255；检索至2020年6月）：比较自主慢呼吸（每分钟少于10次，多数约6次）与每分钟超过10次的对照条件对迷走神经相关心率变异性（HRV）的影响。在1842篇经全文评估的文献中纳入223项研究（练习中172项、单次练习后即刻16项、多次干预后49项）。剔除离群值后：练习过程中RMSSD效应量g = 0.53（95%置信区间0.43–0.62；k = 71；I² = 81%），绝对低频功率g = 1.49（1.28–1.69；k = 57；I² = 93%）；单次练习结束后即刻RMSSD g = 0.14（0.03–0.24；k = 8；I² = 0%）；多次练习干预后静息RMSSD g = 0.32（0.08–0.56；k = 22；I² = 79%）。Egger检验未发现RMSSD存在小样本偏倚迹象（练习中p = .673，干预后p = .620），但练习中低频功率的漏斗图不对称（p < .001；剪补法未补入缺失研究）。整体偏倚风险：215项研究为高风险，5项“有一定担忧”，仅1项为低风险（4项未发表研究无法评估）。许多研究没有报告迷走相关指标（例如58%未报告练习中的RMSSD）。作者强调，由于偏倚风险高，结果需谨慎解读。
claims.sample: 223 studies (172 during-session, n = 7,491; 16 single-session post, n = 835; 49 multi-session, n = 2,706); k = 8 to 71 per vagal-HRV analysis
claims.limitations: Nearly all included studies (215 of 221 rated) were at high risk of bias, and selective reporting of HRV parameters is possible. Heterogeneity was large (I² 79–93%) for most estimates. Many during-session comparisons were not randomized (the control condition often preceded the breathing condition), and many were from studies not designed to test HRV. The LF-power estimate shows funnel-plot asymmetry. The outcome is a physiological marker, not a health or mood outcome, and the after-intervention effect is small and low certainty. The source is internally inconsistent: the text gives k = 71 (RMSSD) and k = 57 (LF) during practice, whereas Table 3 and the authors' OSF data contain 70 and 66 studies after outlier exclusion (the reported g, CI, τ² and I² reproduce exactly with 70 and 66). Numbers were checked against the authors' accepted manuscript (Bournemouth University eprint 38169) and the OSF data (osf.io/jzf2c); the typeset version was not accessible.
claims.app_implication: Justifies slow paced breathing (~5.5–6/min) as the default mode on physiological grounds, because vagal HRV rises during practice. Honest copy: the effect is moderate during practice, small right afterwards and small (low certainty) after weeks of practice. HRV is a physiological marker, not proof of better mood or health. Never imply large lasting HRV changes, and never show HRV gains without a validated sensor.

citation.authors: Laborde S, Allen MS, Borges U, et al.
citation.title: Effects of voluntary slow breathing on heart rate and heart rate variability: A systematic review and a meta-analysis

verification.checked_against: Crossref + PubMed metadata/abstract; authors' accepted manuscript (Bournemouth University Research Online eprint 38169, 'Revised Manuscript (Clean Version)') read page by page incl. Results, Discussion, Table 3 and PRISMA chart; authors' OSF data and R script (osf.io/jzf2c) used to recompute the pooled RMSSD/LF estimates and Egger tests
verification.problems: Metadata, DOI and PMID correct; every g, 95% CI and I² in the claim matches the manuscript and reproduces from the authors' OSF data (e.g. RMSSD during g = 0.527 [0.435, 0.619], I² 81.3%; single-session g = 0.136 [0.031, 0.241]; after-intervention g = 0.318 [0.076, 0.559], τ² 0.219). Problems: (1) Selective bias reporting: the claim cites only the non-significant Egger tests for RMSSD and omits that Egger's test showed significant funnel-plot asymmetry for the LF-power estimate it also reports (P < .001; trim-and-fill imputed no studies). Recomputed from the OSF data: intercept 4.08, p < .001. (2) Risk of bias understated: 'the majority' is in fact 215 studies at high risk, 5 with 'some concerns' and 1 at low risk (4 unpublished studies could not be rated), i.e. about 97% high.
