(3) '1,842 abstracts' copies the authors' abstract wording, but the PRISMA chart shows 1,842 = full-text articles assessed for eligibility (19,667 records screened). (4) The source is internally inconsistent, which is worth flagging: the text gives k = 71 (RMSSD) and k = 57 (LF) during practice, but Table 3 and the OSF data contain 70 and 66 studies after outlier exclusion, and the reported g/CI/τ²/I² reproduce exactly with 70 and 66. Recomputed Egger p for RMSSD after interventions is about .37 vs .620 reported; both are non-significant. (5) evidence_weight 'moderate' is defensible only for the during-practice effect; the after-intervention estimate is low certainty.

claims.topic: HRV biofeedback across emotional, physical and performance outcomes
claims.finding: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled studies of heart rate variability biofeedback (HRVB: slow paced breathing guided by real-time heart-rate feedback, often at an individually assessed resonance frequency). The authors analyzed all problems addressed by HRVB and all outcome measures in all studies, whether or not relevant to the studied population. Of 1,868 papers, 58 met inclusion criteria. A significant small-to-moderate overall effect favoured HRVB and did not differ from that of other effective treatments. Each outcome had only a few studies; the largest effect sizes were for anxiety, depression, anger and athletic/artistic performance, and the smallest for PTSD, sleep and quality of life. No significant differences were found by number of sessions, weeks between pre- and post-test, whether the outcome was targeted to the population, or publication year. Effects were larger versus inactive than versus active control conditions, though significant for both. The authors conclude that HRVB appears useful as a complementary treatment and that further research is needed to confirm its efficacy for particular applications.
claims.finding_zh: 对HRV生物反馈（在实时心率反馈引导下慢节奏呼吸，常采用个体测定的共振频率）随机对照研究的系统综述与元分析，纳入了各研究涉及的所有问题和所有结局指标（不论是否与该研究人群相关）。从1868篇文献中纳入58项。总体为小到中等的显著效应，与其他有效疗法的效应无显著差异。各结局的研究数量都不多：对焦虑、抑郁、愤怒和运动/艺术表现的效应最大，对创伤后应激障碍、睡眠和生活质量的效应最小。训练次数、前后测间隔周数、结局是否针对该人群以及发表年份，均未发现与效应大小有显著关联。与非活性对照（未接受积极干预）相比效应更大，与积极对照相比效应较小，但两者均显著。作者认为HRV生物反馈可作为辅助疗法，具体用途仍需更多研究确认。
claims.study_type: systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs
claims.sample: 58 randomized controlled studies (from 1,868 papers)
claims.limitations: Only the abstract could be read. The full text is paywalled; the paper was checked via PubMed, Crossref and the 2021 correction, which only adds an omitted author. Pooled effect sizes, confidence intervals and risk-of-bias ratings were therefore not verified. The meta-analysis pools all outcomes in all studies regardless of relevance to the population, and there are few studies per outcome. HRVB uses physiological feedback equipment (often with clinician contact) that a sensor-free app cannot provide. Shaffer & Meehan (2020) report that this meta-analysis found non-significant effects on systolic and diastolic blood pressure.
claims.app_implication: Supports describing HRV biofeedback (with a heart-rate sensor) as a complementary tool with small-to-moderate average benefit, largest for anxiety, depression and anger. The app's sensor-free paced breathing is not HRVB, so do not transfer this estimate to it; quote breathwork RCT evidence (Fincham 2023) instead. Make no claims for sleep, PTSD, quality of life or blood pressure. A sensor-based HRVB mode is a candidate for a later version.

citation.authors: Lehrer P, Kaur K, Sharma A, et al.
citation.title: Heart Rate Variability Biofeedback Improves Emotional and Physical Health and Performance: A Systematic Review and Meta Analysis

verification.checked_against: Crossref + PubMed metadata and abstract; Springer correction notice 10.1007/s10484-021-09526-y; Shaffer & Meehan 2020 PMC full text (PMC7578229) for the blood-pressure statement. Full text is paywalled (Unpaywall, Semantic Scholar and Europe PMC all report it closed)
verification.problems: Metadata, DOI, PMID and every statement in the English finding match the abstract (1,868 papers, 58 studies, small-to-moderate effect, outcome ranking, moderators, inactive vs active controls). The 2021 correction only adds an omitted seventh author (P. Sgobba); no data changed. The blood-pressure statement attributed to Shaffer & Meehan (2020) is confirmed in their full text ('found non-significant effects on diastolic or systolic blood pressure'). Problems: (1) The gloss defining HRVB as 'resonance-frequency slow breathing' is not from the source and is over-specific; Shaffer & Meehan note that some HRVB protocols use fixed slower-than-normal rates. (2) finding_zh turns null tests into equivalence or no-effect claims ('与其他有效疗法相当', '训练次数、周数和发表年份不影响效果') and drops the 'outcome targeted to the population' moderator. (3) app_implication transfers an equipment-based biofeedback result to sensor-free slow breathing, and names 'stress', which the abstract does not list among the outcomes. Because the full text is paywalled, pooled effect sizes, CIs and risk-of-bias ratings could not be checked.

claims.topic: Breathing exercises (incl. Buteyko, Papworth, yoga) for adults with asthma
claims.finding: Cochrane review of 22 RCTs with 2,880 adult outpatients with mild-to-moderate asthma. Interventions: 14 yoga, 4 breathing retraining, 1 Buteyko, 1 Buteyko plus pranayama, 1 Papworth, 1 deep diaphragmatic breathing; 20 trials used an inactive control and 2 asthma education. Results versus inactive control: Asthma quality of life (AQLQ) improved at up to 3 months (MD 0.42, 95% CI 0.17 to 0.68; 4 studies, 974 participants; moderate certainty; I2 = 76%), slightly below the 0.5-point minimal clinically important difference. At 6 months the odds of at least a 0.5-point improvement were not clearly higher (OR 1.34, 0.97 to 1.86; 1 study, 655). Asthma symptoms (ACQ) were inconclusive up to 3 months (MD -0.15, -2.32 to 2.02; 1 study, 115; low certainty) and beyond 6 months (MD -0.08, -0.22 to 0.07; 1 study, 449). Hyperventilation symptoms (Nijmegen) were lower at 4-6 months (MD -3.22, -6.31 to -0.13; 2 studies, 118; moderate certainty) but not beyond 6 months (MD 0.63, -0.90 to 2.17; 2 studies, 521). FEV1 in litres at up to 3 months was inconclusive (MD -0.10 L, -0.32 to 0.12; 4 studies, 252; very low certainty), whereas FEV1 % predicted favoured breathing exercises (MD 6.88%, 5.03 to 8.73; 5 studies, 618; not GRADE-rated); neither differed beyond 6 months. Exacerbation data could not be pooled. Adverse effects were not assessed.
claims.finding_zh: Cochrane系统综述：22项随机对照试验、2880名轻中度哮喘门诊成人（14项瑜伽、4项呼吸再训练、1项布泰科、1项布泰科加调息、1项Papworth法、1项腹式深呼吸）。与无干预相比：3个月内哮喘生活质量提高（均数差0.42，95%置信区间0.17–0.68；4项研究974人；中等确定性），但略低于0.5分的最小临床意义差值，且6个月时达到明显改善的比例无确切差异；哮喘症状在3个月内和6个月以上均无明确差异（低确定性）；过度通气症状在4–6个月时减少（均数差−3.22，−6.31至−0.13；中等确定性），6个月以上无差异；第1秒用力呼气量（升）结果不确定（极低确定性），但占预计值百分比提高6.88%，6个月以上两者均无差异。综述未评估不良反应。
claims.sample: 22 RCTs, 2,880 adults with mild-to-moderate asthma
claims.limitations: Mostly yoga trials; only 1-2 Buteyko trials. Interventions and methods were heterogeneous, and risk of bias was poorly reported. The quality-of-life gain is below the MCID, with substantial heterogeneity, and most benefits were not sustained beyond 6 months. Adverse effects were not assessed; the search ran to April 2019. Applies to asthma, not general stress.
claims.app_implication: Buteyko-specific evidence is too thin to offer it as a branded mode. For users with asthma, breathing practice is a complement to, never a replacement for, medication; no respiratory-disease marketing.

citation.authors: Santino TA, Chaves GS, Freitas DA, et al.
citation.title: Breathing exercises for adults with asthma

verification.checked_against: Crossref + PubMed metadata; PubMed abstract; PMC7096190 full-text HTML (summary-of-findings table, results, discussion, plain-language summary); Crossref check that no newer version (pub5) exists
verification.problems: Metadata is correct (CDSR 2020, issue 3, CD001277.pub4; PMID 32212422), and no newer version exists. These match: 22 RCTs, 2,880 participants, the technique counts, AQLQ at 3 months, ACQ up to 3 months, Nijmegen at 4-6 months, FEV1 in litres, and 'adverse effects not assessed'. Problems: (1) Lung function is reported selectively. FEV1 in litres was inconclusive (very low certainty), but FEV1 % predicted favoured breathing exercises (MD 6.88%, 95% CI 5.03 to 8.73; 5 studies, 618; not GRADE-rated); neither differed beyond 6 months. finding_zh's '肺功能结果不确定' is therefore inaccurate. (2) The Nijmegen null is 'over 6 months' (Analysis 1.7), not 'at 6 months'. (3) Omitted context: the AQLQ gain of 0.42 is below the 0.5-point MCID, with I2 = 76%, and the 6-month AQLQ responder OR of 1.34 (0.97 to 1.86; 1 study, 655) is not significant. ACQ beyond 6 months was also null (MD -0.08, -0.22 to 0.07; 1 study, 449), and the plain-language summary says breathing exercises 'probably did not help to improve asthma symptoms'.

claims.topic: Self-guided digital breathing retraining vs face-to-face teaching
claims.finding: Pragmatic, observer-blinded RCT (ISRCTN88318003) in 655 people aged 16-70 (median 57) with asthma and impaired asthma-related quality of life (AQLQ <5.5), recruited from 34 UK general practices. Participants were randomized 2:1:2 to a self-guided DVD-plus-booklet breathing-retraining programme (diaphragmatic, nasal and slow breathing, controlled breath holds, simple relaxation), three face-to-face physiotherapist sessions, or usual care, and followed for 12 months. Primary outcome, AQLQ at 12 months (intention to treat): DVD-booklet 5.40 vs usual care 5.12 (adjusted mean difference 0.28, 95% CI 0.11 to 0.44); face-to-face (5.33) vs usual care 0.24 (0.04 to 0.44); DVD-booklet vs face-to-face 0.04 (-0.16 to 0.24), inside the pre-specified ±0.3 equivalence margin. A clinically important improvement (≥0.5) occurred in 62% (DVD-booklet), 64% (face-to-face) and 56% (usual care), giving NNT 8 for DVD-booklet and 7 for face-to-face vs usual care. No significant differences in FEV1, exhaled nitric oxide or Asthma Control Questionnaire scores. Serious adverse events: 4% DVD-booklet, 3% face-to-face, 8% usual care.
claims.finding_zh: 实用型、结局评估者设盲的随机对照试验（ISRCTN88318003）：英国34家全科诊所的655名16–70岁（中位57岁）哮喘患者，哮喘相关生活质量受损（AQLQ<5.5）。按2:1:2随机分到自助式DVD加手册的呼吸再训练（腹式呼吸、鼻呼吸、慢呼吸、受控屏息、简单放松）、3次面对面理疗师指导或常规护理，随访12个月。主要结局为12个月时的哮喘生活质量评分：自助组5.40，常规组5.12（校正均数差0.28，95%置信区间0.11–0.44）；面对面组5.33，比常规组高0.24（0.04–0.44）；自助组与面对面组相差0.04（−0.16至0.24），落在预设的±0.3等效界值内。达到临床重要改善（≥0.5分）的比例：自助组62%，面对面组64%，常规组56%（相对常规组的需治疗人数：自助组8，面对面组7）。肺功能（FEV1）、呼出气一氧化氮和哮喘控制问卷评分无显著差异。严重不良事件：自助组4%，面对面组3%，常规组8%。
claims.sample: n = 655 people aged 16-70 with asthma (261 DVD-booklet, 132 face-to-face, 262 usual care)
claims.limitations: Asthma population (median age 57). Only 655 of 15,203 invited patients enrolled, so participants may be unusually open to breathing retraining. Participants could not be masked and the primary outcome is self-reported; assessors and analysts were masked. The usual-care control had no attention control, and that group also improved (mean +0.8 vs +1.1 in the active groups). Between-group mean differences (0.24-0.28) are below the 0.5-point individual clinically important difference. DVD-era delivery. The 12-month AQLQ was returned by 85% of participants.
claims.app_implication: The largest breathing-retraining trial in asthma (as of 2018) found a self-guided audiovisual programme equivalent to three physiotherapist sessions for asthma-related quality of life. This supports structured, self-guided in-app breathing lessons. The evidence comes from people with asthma and effects were modest, so claims must stay modest. Never imply better lung function or a replacement for asthma medication; the authors describe it as an adjunct.

citation.authors: Bruton A, Lee A, Yardley L, et al.
citation.title: Physiotherapy breathing retraining for asthma: a randomised controlled trial

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata + PubMed abstract (PMID 29248433) + Europe PMC open-access full text (PMC5757422)
verification.problems: Metadata and every number match: AQLQ 5.40 vs 5.12; adjusted differences 0.28 (0.11-0.44), 0.24 (0.04-0.44), 0.04 (-0.16 to 0.24); 62/64/56%; NNT 8; serious adverse events 4/3/8%. (1) The limitation 'unblinded self-reported outcomes' is imprecise. The paper calls the design observer-blinded: the 12-month assessors and the analysts were masked, but participants could not be masked and the primary outcome (AQLQ) is self-reported. (2) evidence_weight 'high' is generous for a single trial with an unmasked, self-reported primary outcome, a usual-care control with no attention control, only 655 of 15,203 invited patients enrolled, and between-group effects below the 0.5 MCID, so 'moderate'. (3) Participants were aged 16-70 (median 57), not strictly adults. (4) 'Strongest evidence' in app_implication is an unverifiable superlative; the paper says only 'largest trial of breathing retraining in asthma to date'. Equivalence was shown against a pre-specified ±0.3 AQLQ margin. Added the face-to-face mean (5.33) and its NNT of 7.

claims.topic: AHA scientific statement: device-guided breathing and blood pressure
claims.finding: American Heart Association scientific statement summarising BP-lowering evidence for non-drug, non-diet ('alternative') approaches and assigning classes of recommendation and levels of evidence (LOE). Behavioural therapies 'generally had modest, mixed, or no consistent evidence demonstrating their efficacy': Transcendental Meditation Class IIB, LOE B; other meditation techniques Class III, LOE C; yoga Class III, LOE C; other relaxation therapies Class III, LOE B; biofeedback approaches Class IIB, LOE B. Among non-invasive procedures and devices, device-guided breathing (Class IIA, LOE B) had greater support than acupuncture (Class III, LOE B). Exercise-based regimens had relatively stronger support (aerobic Class I, LOE A; dynamic resistance Class IIA, LOE B; isometric handgrip Class IIB, LOE C). Writing-group consensus: it is reasonable for all individuals with BP >120/80 mm Hg to consider trials of alternative approaches as adjuvant methods to help lower BP when clinically appropriate.
claims.finding_zh: 美国心脏协会（AHA）科学声明总结了非药物、非饮食类降压方法的证据，并给出推荐等级和证据水平。行为疗法证明疗效的证据总体较弱、结果不一或缺乏一致证据：超觉冥想IIb级、证据水平B；其他冥想III级、C；瑜伽III级、C；其他放松疗法III级、B；生物反馈IIb级、B。在无创操作和设备中，设备引导呼吸（IIa级、B）获得的证据支持强于针灸（III级、B）。运动类方法证据相对更强：有氧运动I级、A；动态抗阻训练IIa级、B；等长握力训练IIb级、C。写作组共识：血压高于120/80 mmHg者，在临床合适时可以考虑尝试这些替代方法，作为辅助降压手段。
claims.sample: Expert writing-group review of published evidence (methods and number of studies not stated in the abstract)
claims.limitations: Published 2013; a scientific statement, not a practice guideline. The Class IIA rating for device-guided breathing rested on LOE B evidence: small, short trials of one device (RESPeRATE). In a contemporaneous meta-analysis, five of eight trials were manufacturer-sponsored or manufacturer-involved, and the BP effect disappeared when they were excluded (Mahtani 2012). A later independent double-blind, sham-controlled trial found no BP effect (Landman 2013). NICE NG136 (2019) deleted its earlier relaxation-therapy recommendation, citing insufficient evidence of direct benefit such as fewer cardiovascular events or better quality of life. The classes here were checked against the abstract only, because the publisher full text was not accessible.
claims.app_implication: Gives limited and dated support only. The Class IIA rating covers device-guided breathing (the trials then available were of the RESPeRATE device), not unguided or app-paced slow breathing, and the same statement rated yoga, non-TM meditation and other relaxation therapies Class III. At most, it allows wording such as 'guided slow breathing may modestly lower BP as an add-on, but evidence is mixed'. Never use treatment language, and any BP-related content must advise continuing prescribed care.

citation.authors: Brook RD, Appel LJ, Rubenfire M, et al.
citation.title: Beyond Medications and Diet: Alternative Approaches to Lowering Blood Pressure: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata + PubMed abstract (PMID 23608661); publisher full text blocked (HTTP 403, not read); NICE NG136 recommendations and rationale pages for the NICE limitation
verification.problems: Metadata, every class and level of evidence, and the >120/80 mm Hg consensus sentence match the abstract. The NICE NG136 deletion of its relaxation-therapy recommendation is confirmed on the NICE site. (1) The app_implication extends the Class IIA rating to 'slow breathing' in general. The rating is for device-guided breathing, and the same statement rated yoga, non-TM meditation and other relaxation therapies Class III. (2) The limitation cites Landman 2013 for evidence being 'small and largely manufacturer-linked'. Landman was published after the statement and is an independent null trial; the manufacturer-involvement point comes from Mahtani 2012 (5 of 8 trials). (3) In finding_zh, '优于针灸' can be read as 'works better than acupuncture'; the source says only that device-guided breathing 'had greater support than' acupuncture. (4) The 'Narrative evidence review' label is unconfirmed because the methods are not in the abstract; reworded.

claims.topic: Sham-controlled trial of device-guided slow breathing for hypertension
claims.finding: Single-centre, double-blind, sham-controlled RCT in 48 patients with type 2 diabetes and hypertension: 15-min sessions for 8 weeks with a device guiding breathing through musical tones to <10 breaths/min vs a sham device (music without breathing guidance). No significant BP effect: SBP difference 2.35 mm Hg (95% CI −6.50 to 11.20) in favour of the control group; DBP difference 2.25 mm Hg (−2.16 to 6.67) in favour of the intervention. 21 of 24 (88%) intervention and 24 of 24 control patients completed; 3 intervention patients had adverse events. The authors conclude that device-guided lowering of breathing frequency does not appear to be a viable nonpharmacologic option for hypertension treatment.
claims.finding_zh: 单中心、双盲、假装置对照随机试验，48名2型糖尿病合并高血压患者：8周内每次15分钟，用音乐音调把呼吸引导到每分钟10次以下，对照组只听音乐不引导呼吸。血压没有显著变化：收缩压差值2.35 mmHg（95%置信区间−6.50至11.20），反而偏向对照组；舒张压差值2.25 mmHg（−2.16至6.67）偏向干预组。干预组3人出现不良事件。作者结论：设备引导降低呼吸频率似乎不是可行的非药物降压手段。
claims.sample: n = 48 adults with type 2 diabetes and hypertension
claims.limitations: Small; single centre; diabetic population; office BP only; wide confidence intervals.
claims.app_implication: The best-blinded trial was null, so the app must not present breathing as a hypertension treatment.

claims.topic: Over-breathing (hyperventilation): adverse events and contraindications
claims.finding: ANS/BSCN guideline for voluntary hyperventilation during EEG (3–5 min at ~20–30 breaths/min; patient may stop at will). Informed by a 2012 prospective national audit of 3,475 patients: fewer than 3% had reported events, two-thirds of them seizures; among 3,170 with suspected epilepsy, hyperventilation provoked seizures in 69 (2.2%; 56 absences, 1 generalized tonic–clonic). Other potential adverse events: dizziness, distress, confusion, paraesthesias, tetany and prolonged over-breathing; no significant cardiac, respiratory or cerebrovascular complications were reported. Absolute contraindications: stroke (intracranial or subarachnoid haemorrhage) or myocardial infarction within 12 months, significant cardiac disease (poorly controlled or unstable angina), pulmonary disease (COPD with breathlessness at rest), sickle cell disease or trait, and moyamoya disease. Relative contraindications: stable cerebrovascular disease, ischaemic heart disease and asthma.
claims.finding_zh: 英国神经生理科学家协会与英国临床神经生理学会（ANS/BSCN）关于脑电图检查中“过度通气诱发试验”的指南（每分钟约20–30次，持续3–5分钟，患者可随时停止）。依据2012年对3475名患者的前瞻性全国审计：报告不良事件的不到3%，其中三分之二为癫痫发作；在3170名疑似癫痫者中，过度通气诱发发作69例（2.2%，其中56例失神发作、1例全面强直阵挛发作）。其他可能的不良反应：头晕、不适、意识混乱、肢体麻刺感、手足抽搐和持续过度呼吸；未报告严重心脏、呼吸或脑血管并发症。绝对禁忌：12个月内的卒中（颅内或蛛网膜下腔出血）或心肌梗死、控制不佳或不稳定心绞痛、静息时气促的慢阻肺、镰状细胞病或镰状细胞特征、烟雾病；相对禁忌：稳定的脑血管病、缺血性心脏病、哮喘。
claims.study_type: professional-society clinical guideline (v1.3, 2013) informed by a national audit
claims.sample: Audit of 3,475 patients (3,170 with suspected epilepsy)
claims.limitations: Supervised clinical EEG setting with ECG monitoring; brief hyperventilation; population under investigation for seizures; short web guideline (v1.3/2013); the underlying audit is published as Kane et al., Seizure 2014.
claims.app_implication: Fast/over-breathing protocols are excluded. Safety copy should name dizziness, tingling and muscle cramping as over-breathing signs, and people with epilepsy, recent stroke or MI, unstable angina, severe COPD or sickle cell disease should be steered away from any fast-breathing content.

citation.title: ANS/BSCN Guidelines for Hyperventilation During EEG Recordings (v1.3)

verification.checked_against: Full text of the guideline PDF at bscn.org.uk (one page, 'NMK/RK v1.3/2013'); PubMed abstract of the underlying audit, Kane et al., Seizure 2014;23:129-134 (PMID 24252807)

claims.topic: Device-guided breathing and BP: industry-sponsorship caveat
claims.finding: Systematic review and meta-analysis of device-guided breathing: 8 trials, all of the RESPeRATE device, 494 adults. SBP fell by 3.67 mmHg (95% CI −5.99 to −1.39; p = 0.002) and DBP by 2.51 mmHg (−4.15 to −0.87; p = 0.003). Five of the eight trials were sponsored by or involved the manufacturer; with those excluded, there was no overall effect on BP. Maximum trial duration was 9 weeks; there was no overall effect on heart rate or quality of life.
claims.finding_zh: 系统综述与元分析：8项设备引导呼吸试验（均为RESPeRATE设备），494名成人，收缩压下降3.67 mmHg（95%置信区间−5.99至−1.39），舒张压下降2.51 mmHg（−4.15至−0.87）。但8项中有5项由厂商资助或有厂商参与；排除这些试验后，对血压没有总体效果。最长试验仅9周，对心率和生活质量无影响。
claims.sample: 8 trials, 494 adults
claims.limitations: Small, short trials of a single device; manufacturer involvement in most trials.
claims.app_implication: A key reason to make no BP claims: the apparent benefit disappears when manufacturer-linked trials are excluded. Show this caveat in the evidence panel.

citation.title: Device-guided breathing exercises in the control of human blood pressure: systematic review and meta-analysis

claims.topic: One-minute cyclic sighing or box breathing in real-life acute anxiety
claims.finding: Pre-registered pilot just-in-time ecological momentary intervention with a within-person design in 47 university students (43 female, mean age 21). Participants first had a group instruction session and six practice trials. Then, whenever they felt tense or anxious in daily life, they opened a smartphone app and rated state anxiety (5-item STAI-SKD, 10-point items). The app then gave, in randomized order across episodes, a video-guided one-minute exercise (cyclic sighing, 70 s, or box breathing, 69 s) or a passive control. Each person received each condition about six times (782 episodes analysed). Five minutes after the first rating, both cyclic sighing (b = -0.73, SE 0.10) and box breathing (b = -0.80, SE 0.09) were associated with greater reductions in state anxiety than control; partially standardized effects were about -1 SD of the change score. The techniques did not differ (p = .19), and trait anxiety did not moderate the effect. On a smartphone attention test (633 tests, 44 participants), box breathing was followed by fewer commission (inhibition) errors (b = -0.29, SE 0.17, one-tailed p = .04), more so in people with higher trait anxiety (one-tailed p = .03); cyclic sighing was not. Both exercises were followed by lower performance efficiency, which exploratory analyses traced to slower reaction times.
claims.finding_zh: 预注册的试点研究，采用个体内设计的“即时生态瞬时干预”：47名大学生（43名女性，平均21岁）先参加集体指导并练习6次；之后在日常生活中感到紧张或焦虑时，打开手机应用评定状态焦虑，再按随机顺序做视频引导的1分钟循环叹息（70秒）、1分钟方块呼吸（69秒）或不做练习（每人每种条件约6次，共分析782次）。5分钟后，与不做练习相比，循环叹息和方块呼吸都伴随更大的状态焦虑下降（10分制条目上分别多降约0.7和0.8分），两种方法之间无差异，特质焦虑高低也不影响效果。手机注意力测试中，方块呼吸后抑制错误更少（单侧检验p=0.04），高特质焦虑者更明显，循环叹息则无此效果；但两种练习后反应都更慢，注意效率降低（反应时为探索性分析）。
claims.study_type: pre-registered pilot within-person randomized just-in-time ecological momentary intervention (field experiment)
claims.sample: n = 47 university students (782 anxiety episodes; attention data from 44)
claims.limitations: Pilot with a small, predominantly female (43/47) young student sample. The passive control was not attention-matched, so expectancy may contribute. Anxiety was self-reported only about 5 min after the first rating; compliance was not objectively verified, and T1 compliance was 84%. The attention findings are significant only on one-tailed tests, and the reaction-time analysis was exploratory. No physiological measures.
claims.app_implication: Supports a one-minute SOS option (box breathing or cyclic sighing) framed as in-the-moment relief, not training. Teach the technique first, since participants were instructed and practised before use. Box breathing was rated easier and less annoying than cyclic sighing. Note that reactions may be slightly slower right afterwards.

citation.authors: Riedl EM, Bracklo T, Wimmer K, et al.
citation.title: Simply breathing anxiety away? A pilot, just-in-time ecological momentary intervention study of one-minute cyclic sighing versus box breathing as tools for acute anxiety reduction and attention promotion in real life

verification.checked_against: Crossref + PubMed metadata; PubMed abstract; full published text (CC-BY publisher PDF from KU Eichstätt-Ingolstadt repository, edoc.ku.de eprint 36573)
verification.problems: Metadata is correct (Anxiety Stress Coping 39(5):608-622, epub 19 Apr 2026; PMID 42002307; seven authors, first three as cited). All abstract-level statements are accurate. The problems are minor precision issues: (1) The design is within-person. Each participant received each condition about 6 times, in randomized order across self-initiated anxiety episodes (782 episodes analysed), so 'were assigned to' reads as a between-subjects design. (2) The box-breathing inhibition-error effect (b = -0.29, SE 0.17) and its trait-anxiety moderation (b = -0.64, SE 0.34) were significant only on preregistered one-tailed tests (p = .04 and .03). (3) The slower-reaction-time result comes from an exploratory, non-preregistered analysis; the preregistered outcome was lower performance efficiency. (4) Omitted nulls: the two techniques did not differ in anxiety reduction (p = .19), and trait anxiety did not moderate it. (5) Effect sizes are available in the full text: cyclic sighing b = -0.73 and box breathing b = -0.80 on a 10-point item scale, partially standardized beta -0.98 and -1.07. (6) The sample was 43/47 female, and participants had group instruction and 6 practice trials before data collection.

claims.topic: Voluntary slow breathing in hypertension: 2026 meta-analysis
claims.finding: Systematic review and meta-analysis (PROSPERO CRD420251026840) of RCTs of voluntary (non-device-guided) slow breathing exercise: 13 RCTs, 1,097 participants described as hypertensive (some trials enrolled prehypertension or high-normal BP). Pooled vs control: SBP mean difference -7.68 mmHg (95% CI -9.87 to -5.49; 13 trials; random effects, I² = 82%); DBP -4.02 mmHg (-5.44 to -2.60; 11 trials; I² = 73%); heart rate -1.15 beats/min (-1.73 to -0.56; 10 trials; fixed effect, I² = 40%); LF/HF -1.09 (-1.94 to -0.23), from only 3 trials and unstable in leave-one-out sensitivity analysis. Interventions varied widely: slow breathing at 4-6 breaths/min, slow-loaded breathing training, pursed-lip breathing, pranayama, bee-humming breathing, yoga breathing, mindfulness meditation, and relaxation with meditation. Durations ranged from single sessions lasting minutes to hours up to 6 months. Only 4 of 13 trials blinded participants or personnel, 8 did not report allocation concealment, and 3 had high risk of attrition bias. No certainty-of-evidence (GRADE) rating was reported.
claims.finding_zh: 2026年系统综述与元分析（PROSPERO注册）：13项随机对照试验、1097名受试者（以高血压患者为主，部分试验纳入高血压前期或血压偏高者），评估自主（非设备引导）的慢呼吸练习。与对照组相比的合并估计：收缩压平均低7.68 mmHg（95%置信区间−9.87至−5.49；13项试验，随机效应，I² = 82%），舒张压低4.02 mmHg（−5.44至−2.60；11项，I² = 73%），心率低1.15次/分（−1.73至−0.56；10项，固定效应，I² = 40%）。LF/HF比值降低1.09（−1.94至−0.23），但只有3项试验，且逐一剔除分析显示结果不稳定。纳入的干预差异很大，包括每分钟4–6次慢呼吸、负荷式慢呼吸训练、缩唇呼吸、调息、蜂鸣调息、瑜伽呼吸、正念冥想、放松加冥想等；时长从单次几分钟到几小时不等，最长6个月。13项中仅4项对受试者或实施者设盲，8项未报告分配隐藏，3项失访偏倚风险高；未进行GRADE证据确定性分级。
claims.study_type: systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs
claims.sample: 13 RCTs, 1,097 participants (mostly hypertensive; some trials prehypertension or high-normal BP)
claims.limitations: High heterogeneity (I² 73-82% for BP). Interventions were mixed and partly not breathing-specific (meditation, relaxation), and single-session acute trials were pooled with multi-week programmes. Many small trials had unclear or high risk of bias. English-language only, and no certainty grading. BP and heart rate are surrogate outcomes, and there are no cardiovascular-event data. The heart-rate effect (about 1 beat/min) is trivial and the LF/HF result is unstable. Device-guided breathing was excluded, so the review does not address the null double-blind sham-controlled device trial (Landman 2013). NICE NG136 (2019) removed its relaxation-therapy recommendation for lack of evidence on cardiovascular events or quality of life.
claims.app_implication: Describe only as: 'pooled estimates from small, varied and often unblinded trials (some single-session) suggest slow breathing may lower BP, but certainty is low'. No BP marketing or treatment claims. Any hypertension programme would need clinical co-design and must advise continuing prescribed care.

citation.authors: Cheng S, Chen Y, Yu M, et al.
citation.title: Voluntary Slow Breathing Exercise on Cardiovascular Parameters in Patients With Hypertension: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata + Europe PMC open-access full text (PMC13093598); PubMed search (no PMID assigned yet); NICE NG136 rationale page
verification.problems: Metadata and all pooled numbers match the full text: 13 RCTs; 1,097 participants; SBP -7.68 (-9.87 to -5.49), I² 82%; DBP -4.02 (-5.44 to -2.60); HR -1.15 (-1.73 to -0.56), fixed effect, I² 40%; LF/HF -1.09 (-1.94 to -0.23); 4 of 13 trials blinded; 8 without reported allocation concealment; no GRADE rating; English-only. The empty PMID is correct. (1) The limitation says the review 'conflicts with' Landman 2013, but this review explicitly excluded device-guided breathing, so Landman tests a different intervention. NICE NG136 dropped relaxation therapy for lack of cardiovascular-event and quality-of-life evidence, which does not directly contradict BP findings. (2) The population is described as hypertensive, but several included trials enrolled prehypertension or high-normal BP. (3) Omissions: durations ranged from single sessions (minutes to 3 h, including a hypertensive-emergency trial) to 6 months; 3 trials had high attrition bias; the LF/HF result rests on 3 trials and was unstable in leave-one-out analysis (the authors flag this). (4) In finding_zh, '使收缩压平均下降' is causal wording for a low-certainty pooled estimate; reworded.

claims.topic: Does a 1:2 inhale:exhale ratio increase HRV at 6/min?
claims.finding: Two small within-subject experiments (original N = 26; replication N = 16) in undergraduates who had already completed 1-2 semesters of slow-breathing training. Participants followed a 6 breaths/min pacer for 5 min at a 1:1 and 5 min at a 1:2 inhalation:exhalation ratio (order randomized, 3-min buffer); achieved rates were about 6.0/min in both. In both studies, the ratio did not change heart rate, SDNN, RMSSD, pNN50, LF power or sample entropy (all p >= .14). The authors' review of nine earlier studies was split: three found no ratio effect, one favoured equal ratios, four favoured longer exhalations and one favoured longer inhalations. The authors rated these earlier studies as high risk of bias or not assessable, often because adherence to the target rate or ratio was not verified.
claims.finding_zh: 两项小型受试者内实验（原始研究26人，重复研究16人），参与者是已接受1–2学期慢呼吸训练的本科生。他们跟随每分钟6次的节拍器，分别以吸呼比1:1和1:2各呼吸5分钟（顺序随机，中间间隔3分钟），两种条件下实际频率都约为每分钟6.0次。两项研究中，吸呼比都没有改变心率、SDNN、RMSSD、pNN50、低频功率或样本熵（所有p ≥ 0.14）。作者回顾的9项既往研究结论不一：3项无差异，1项支持吸呼等长，4项支持呼气更长，1项支持吸气更长；作者评定这些研究偏倚风险高或无法评估，常见问题是没有核实参与者是否按目标频率和比例呼吸。
claims.study_type: two randomized-order within-subject experiments (original + replication) with a narrative review and risk-of-bias ratings
claims.sample: N = 26 (original; 10 women, 16 men) + N = 16 (replication; 8 women, 8 men); undergraduates aged 18-22 with 1-2 semesters of slow-breathing training
claims.limitations: Small samples powered only for large effects (d about 1), so small or moderate ratio effects cannot be ruled out; trained breathers who had practised mainly at 1:1 for 5-6 weeks (may favour 1:1 and may not apply to untrained users); fixed 6/min rather than individual resonance frequency; only two ratios tested; achieved inhale:exhale ratio checked only visually; single session with 5-min conditions; HR/HRV outcomes only, no felt relaxation; reporting errors in the paper (e.g., Study 2's heart-rate statistics duplicate Study 1's).
claims.app_implication: Evidence on inhale:exhale ratio is mixed. In the best-controlled test so far (trained breathers at exactly 6/min), 1:2 did not raise HRV over 1:1. Do not claim that longer exhales 'activate the vagus nerve more'; offer the ratio (1:1 to 1:2) as a comfort setting.

citation.authors: Meehan ZM, Shaffer F
citation.title: Do Longer Exhalations Increase HRV During Slow-Paced Breathing?

verification.checked_against: Crossref + PubMed metadata; Europe PMC abstract; PMC full text (PMC11310264) including Methods, Results, Tables 1-3, Limitations
verification.problems: Metadata is correct (online March 2024, 49(3):407-417). The finding matches the abstract and full text. Omissions that matter for an app population: participants were undergraduates with 1-2 semesters of slow-breathing training who had practised at 1:1 for 5-6 weeks before testing. This could bias results toward 1:1 and may not apply to untrained users. The power analysis targeted only large effects (d about 1; n about 10), so the null result cannot exclude small or moderate ratio effects. Achieved inhale:exhale ratio was checked only visually. The original study also measured sample entropy (null), not only the replication. The paper has reporting errors: Study 2's heart-rate statistics duplicate Study 1's, and pNN50/lnLF units are inconsistent between tables. Useful context: the authors rated all nine earlier studies as high risk of bias or not assessable.

claims.topic: Cyclic sighing vs box breathing vs cyclic hyperventilation vs mindfulness: protocols and main result
claims.finding: Remote randomized controlled study (retrospectively registered, NCT05304000), June-September 2020: 5 min/day for 28 days. Of 108 enrolled adults, 24 were randomized to mindfulness meditation, 30 to cyclic sighing, 21 to box breathing and 33 to cyclic hyperventilation with retention. Some households were allocated together, which explains the unequal arms. Mindfulness control: 5 min with eyes closed, attention on the forehead region between the eyes, returning via the breath when the mind wandered. Cyclic sighing: inhale slowly; once the lungs are expanded, inhale again to fill them maximally (the second inhale may be shorter and smaller); then exhale slowly and fully. Both inhales ideally go through the nose and the exhale through the mouth, though nose-only breathing was allowed; repeat self-paced for 5 min. Box breathing: equal inhale, hold, exhale and hold (e.g., 4-4-4-4 s). Phase length was set by a 'CO2 tolerance test', timing one maximally slow full exhale after a deep breath: 0-20 s gives 3-4 s phases, 25-45 s gives 5-6 s, 50-75+ s gives 8-10 s. Breathe through the nose where possible and shorten the phases if straining. Cyclic hyperventilation with retention: 30 deep inhales (ideally nasal) with passive mouth exhales, then exhale fully and hold with empty lungs for 15 s; 3 rounds. Participants completed on average 19.6 ± 7.7 (breathwork) and 17.7 ± 9.3 (mindfulness) of the 28 days. In mixed-effects models, breathwork overall increased daily pre-to-post-session positive affect more than mindfulness, with a larger advantage the more days on protocol. Compared one by one with mindfulness, only cyclic sighing differed significantly. Raw mean daily positive-affect gains were similar across breathwork arms (PANAS +1.84 to +1.97) vs +1.22 for mindfulness (within-group p = 0.06). The 28-day decline in wearable-measured daily respiratory rate was greater for breathwork overall than for mindfulness (p < 0.05). The cyclic-sighing arm's decline also differed significantly from mindfulness (p < 0.05). The paper does not show cyclic sighing to be significantly better than the other breathing methods.
claims.finding_zh: 远程随机对照研究（事后注册，NCT05304000），2020年6–9月进行，每天练习5分钟，共28天。入组108名成人：正念冥想24人、循环叹息30人、方块呼吸21人、循环过度通气加屏息33人（部分同住家庭整体分到同一组，因此各组人数不均）。正念对照组：闭眼5分钟，把注意力放在两眼之间的额头区域，走神时先回到呼吸、再回到额头。循环叹息：慢慢吸气，肺部扩张后再补吸一口，尽量吸满（第二口可以更短更小），然后缓慢、完全地呼出；两次吸气最好用鼻、呼气最好用嘴，也可全程用鼻；按自己的节奏重复5分钟。方块呼吸：吸、屏、呼、屏四段等长（如各4秒）。每段时长由“CO2耐受测试”决定：深吸一口后尽量慢地呼出，记录呼空所需时间，0–20秒对应每段3–4秒，25–45秒对应5–6秒，50–75秒以上对应8–10秒。尽量用鼻呼吸，吃力就缩短。循环过度通气加屏息：深吸（最好用鼻）、用嘴被动呼出，连续30次，然后呼空并屏息15秒，共3轮。28天中，呼吸组平均完成19.6天，正念组17.7天。混合效应模型显示，呼吸练习整体比正念更能提升每次练习前后的积极情绪，且练习天数越多差距越大；逐一与正念比较时，只有循环叹息达到显著。不过，各呼吸组积极情绪的原始平均日增幅相近（PANAS +1.84至+1.97），正念组为+1.22（组内p = 0.06）。可穿戴设备记录的日常呼吸频率在28天中的下降，呼吸练习整体显著大于正念（p < 0.05）；分组比较中，循环叹息组的下降也显著大于正念组（p < 0.05）。论文并未显示循环叹息显著优于另外两种呼吸法。
claims.sample: n = 108 adults (mostly from a Stanford undergraduate psychology class)
claims.limitations: Exploratory and retrospectively registered, not pre-registered. Small, unequal arms (21-33) with household-level allocation for some participants. Remote delivery with limited monitoring of how the exercises were done. Mainly university students, recruited during the COVID-19 pandemic. Atypical 5-min forehead-focus 'mindfulness' comparator. Many outcomes; standardized effect sizes not reported. WHOOP donated the devices (stated not involved in design or analysis), and the senior author became a WHOOP adviser in 2022.
claims.app_implication: Defines the exact cyclic-sighing instruction to reproduce (two inhales, then a long, slow exhale; self-paced; 5 min) and the box default (4-4-4-4, shorten if straining). Rate cyclic sighing as promising (C), not proven superior to meditation or to other breathing methods.

citation.authors: Balban MY, Neri E, Kogon MM, et al.
citation.title: Brief structured respiration practices enhance mood and reduce physiological arousal

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; PubMed abstract (PMID 36630953); PMC full text PMC9873947 via Europe PMC, including Results, Limitations and STAR Methods protocol descriptions
verification.problems: Metadata, retrospective registration (NCT05304000), arm sizes (24/30/21/33 of 108), the 28-day 5-min/day design and the wording of all three breathwork protocols match the STAR Methods. Corrections: (1) 'cyclic sighing showed the largest reduction in respiratory rate (p < 0.05)' reads as superiority over the other breathwork arms. The p < 0.05 is versus mindfulness only, and the outcome is the 28-day slope of the wearable's (WHOOP) daily respiratory-rate summary, not breathing during practice. (2) Omitted context. The 'mindfulness' comparator was an atypical 5-min, eyes-closed focus on the forehead between the eyes. Raw daily positive-affect gains were similar in all three breathwork arms (PANAS +1.84 to +1.97) vs +1.22 for mindfulness (within-group p = 0.06), so cyclic sighing's unique significance comes from the mixed model with a days-on-protocol term. Adherence was 19.6 vs 17.7 of 28 days. (3) finding_zh drops 'ideally' for nasal inhalation and omits the CO2-test phase durations. Its '下降最多（p<0.05）' implies a significant win over all arms. (4) Limitations should add household-level allocation, a COVID-era mainly student sample, the atypical comparator, and WHOOP ties (device donation; senior author later a WHOOP adviser).

claims.topic: Cyclic sighing trial: null results for anxiety, HRV, heart rate and sleep
claims.finding: In the same trial, every group showed immediate pre-to-post-session reductions in state anxiety, averaged over the days practised (STAI: mindfulness -3.95 ± 4.16; all breathwork -3.03 ± 3.83; cyclic sighing -3.85 ± 4.88; box breathing -3.75 ± 2.83; cyclic hyperventilation -1.81 ± 2.97). Every group also showed reductions in negative affect. Breathwork and mindfulness did not differ in state-anxiety or negative-affect change, even though anxiety and physiological arousal (heart rate, HRV, respiratory rate) were stated primary endpoints. Mindfulness's own pre-to-post gain in positive affect was not significant (+1.22 ± 2.34, p = 0.06). Trait anxiety did not change in any group and did not differ between groups. HRV (RMSSD) and resting heart rate came from a wrist wearable (WHOOP) during deep sleep. Neither changed significantly over 28 days in the mindfulness group or the combined breathwork group, and no breathwork arm differed from mindfulness (data not shown). Sleep hours, sleep efficiency, sleep score and PROMIS sleep-related impairment showed no significant change in either group and no between-group difference. In an optional end-of-study debrief, 90% reported positive and 10% reported negative experiences related to the exercises.
claims.finding_zh: 同一试验中，按练习天数平均，各组每次练习前后的状态焦虑（STAI）都即时下降（正念−3.95 ± 4.16；呼吸练习合计−3.03 ± 3.83；循环叹息−3.85 ± 4.88；方块呼吸−3.75 ± 2.83；循环过度通气−1.81 ± 2.97），负面情绪也下降。但呼吸练习与正念在焦虑和负面情绪的改善上没有差异，尽管焦虑和生理唤醒（心率、HRV、呼吸频率）都是研究预设的主要终点。正念组自身练习前后积极情绪的提升未达显著（+1.22 ± 2.34，p = 0.06）。特质焦虑各组都没有变化，组间也无差异。腕戴设备（WHOOP）在深睡期间测得的HRV（RMSSD）和静息心率，在28天里正念组和呼吸练习合计组都没有显著变化，各呼吸组与正念组之间也无差异（论文未展示具体数据）。睡眠时长、睡眠效率、睡眠评分和PROMIS睡眠相关日间损害，两组均无显著变化，组间也无差异。在自愿填写的结束问卷中，90%的参与者报告练习体验正面，10%报告有与练习相关的负面体验。
claims.study_type: RCT (remote, exploratory): null primary and secondary endpoints
claims.sample: n = 108 adults (physiological slopes analysed in 100: 22 mindfulness, 78 breathwork)
claims.limitations: Same design limits as the main trial: exploratory, retrospectively registered, small arms, mostly students, atypical mindfulness comparator. Nightly wrist-PPG averages may be insensitive. HRV and resting HR were measured during sleep, not during or right after practice. Arm-level HRV/HR comparisons were not shown. 28 days with no follow-up may be too short for trait or sleep effects. Null results from a small trial do not establish equivalence.
claims.app_implication: Do not claim cyclic sighing lowers anxiety more than meditation, improves sleep or raises HRV. Accurate copy: 'In one small trial, daily cyclic sighing lifted mood slightly more than a short meditation; the drop in anxiety was similar.'

citation.authors: Balban MY, Neri E, Kogon MM, et al.
citation.title: Brief structured respiration practices enhance mood and reduce physiological arousal

verification.checked_against: PubMed abstract (PMID 36630953); PMC full text PMC9873947 via Europe PMC, including the Results sections on anxiety, affect, physiology and sleep, the Figure 4 legend and STAR Methods
verification.problems: All numbers (STAI daily changes and SDs per arm, physiological n = 22/78, 10% negative debrief) match the full text. Corrections: (1) study_type labels these as secondary outcomes, but the abstract lists anxiety, heart rate and HRV as primary endpoints, so the nulls fall on primary endpoints. (2) The HRV/RHR and sleep nulls were reported for 'either of the groups' (mindfulness vs combined breathwork). Individual breathwork arms were only compared with mindfulness (no differences, data not shown), so 'did not change in any group' slightly overstates what was tested. (3) WHOOP HRV and resting HR were computed during deep sleep, not during or after practice; this context is missing. (4) An omitted null: mindfulness's own pre-post positive-affect gain was not significant (+1.22 ± 2.34, p = 0.06). (5) The 'daily reductions' are immediate within-session changes averaged over the days practised. The finding should say so.

claims.topic: Implementation features of effective breathing interventions for stress/anxiety
claims.finding: Systematic review (PRISMA; no registered protocol) of clinical studies of isolated voluntary breathing practices with psychometric stress/anxiety outcomes. Sources: PubMed, ScienceDirect and reference lists, English only, to March 2023; biofeedback-device and combined yoga/meditation interventions were excluded. Of 2,904 unique articles, 58 studies met criteria (41 RCTs, 17 non-randomized; 5,407 participants), and 54 of their 72 interventions significantly reduced stress/anxiety. Effective and ineffective interventions were compared with Fisher's exact tests. Effective practices avoided fast-only breath paces and sessions shorter than 5 min. They included human-guided training (live or pre-recorded human audio/video guidance in at least the first session), multiple sessions and long-term practice (at least 6 sessions over at least 1 week). The fast-only component rests on just two fast-only interventions (fast-only vs any other pace p = 0.06), and the authors urge caution; all 12 fast-plus-slow interventions were effective. Population, other breath paces, session duration beyond 5 min, and group vs individual or at-home practice were not associated with effectiveness. A qualitative look at six outlier interventions suggested that some factors may render otherwise promising interventions ineffective: extensive standing, repeated interruptions, involuntarily restricted diaphragm movement (e.g., diaphragmatic breathing while lying face-down during a biopsy) and inadequate training for highly technical practices such as alternate-nostril breathing.
claims.finding_zh: 系统综述（遵循PRISMA，但未预先注册方案）：检索PubMed、ScienceDirect及参考文献（英文，截至2023年3月），纳入58项研究（41项随机对照、17项非随机，共5407人）中的72种单纯呼吸干预（排除生物反馈设备及与瑜伽、冥想等结合的干预），其中54种显著降低了压力或焦虑。对比有效与无效干预发现：有效的练习避免“只做快速呼吸”和“单次少于5分钟”，并包含真人指导（现场或预先录制的真人语音/视频，至少用于第一次练习）、多次练习和长期坚持（至少1周内6次以上）。但“只做快速呼吸”这一条仅基于2种干预（与其他呼吸速度相比p=0.06），作者提醒谨慎解读；快慢结合的12种干预全部有效。人群类型、其他呼吸速度、5分钟以上的具体时长、集体还是个人练习、是否居家练习都与效果无关。对6个例外干预的定性分析提示：长时间站立、练习中反复被打断、膈肌活动被动受限（如俯卧在检查台上做腹式呼吸）以及高难度技法（如交替鼻孔呼吸）训练不足，可能让原本有希望的干预失效。
claims.study_type: systematic review with conceptual framework (vote counting of effective vs ineffective interventions with Fisher's exact tests; no meta-analysis)
claims.sample: 58 studies (41 RCTs, 17 non-randomized), 72 interventions, 5,407 participants
claims.limitations: Vote counting based on statistical significance, not effect sizes; no meta-analysis and no registered protocol; English only, two databases; 22 of 58 studies rated poor quality, and no non-RCT rated good. Components are confounded: all long-term interventions also had human guidance, and most single-session interventions were laboratory simulated-stress studies. The fast-only and under-5-min findings rest on very few interventions: 2 fast-only, and 9 under 5 min, of which 6 were ineffective, 4 of those also lacking any core component. The framework and its caveats were derived post hoc, the caveats from six outlier interventions.
claims.app_implication: Default sessions of at least 5 min. Do not offer fast-only breathing as a default stress tool: the evidence against it is thin, but nothing supports it either. Give human voice or video guidance at least for the first session, and offer a multi-week programme (at least 6 sessions over at least 1 week). Suggest practising seated or lying on the back, and avoid in-session interruptions such as mid-session prompts or questionnaires.

citation.authors: Bentley TGK, D'Andrea-Penna G, Rakic M, et al.
citation.title: Breathing Practices for Stress and Anxiety Reduction: Conceptual Framework of Implementation Guidelines Based on a Systematic Review of the Published Literature

verification.checked_against: Crossref + PubMed metadata; PubMed abstract; full text PMC10741869 (Europe PMC XML: methods, synthesis, outlier analysis, discussion)
verification.problems: Metadata (authors, 2023, title, Brain Sci 13(12):1612, DOI, PMID 38137060) and all abstract numbers (2,904 articles, 58 studies, 54/72 effective) are correct. Problems from the full text: (1) The 'avoid fast-only paces' component rests on only 2 fast-only interventions. Breath pace was no longer significant when fast-only was compared with any other pace (p = 0.06), and the authors say to interpret it 'with caution'. All 12 fast-plus-slow interventions were effective. The claim and app_implication present it as firm. (2) The caveats (standing, interruptions, diaphragm obstruction, inadequate training) come from a qualitative look at 6 outlier interventions; standing and interruptions both come from one study (Meier 2020). The source says they 'may render' interventions ineffective; the claim's 'were linked to' is firmer. (3) Context is omitted: 17 of 58 studies were non-randomized, 22 were rated poor quality (no non-RCT rated good), and there was no registered protocol. 'Effective' meant statistical significance only. 'Human-guided training' includes pre-recorded human audio/video, and 'long-term' means at least 6 sessions over at least 1 week. (4) finding_zh: '腹部受压' loosely glosses 'involuntary diaphragmatic obstruction'; the example was diaphragmatic breathing while lying face-down on a biopsy table. '集体或居家练习' drops the group-vs-individual comparison.

claims.topic: Slow paced breathing with vs without HRV biofeedback
claims.finding: Within-subject experiment (single lab visit, condition order counterbalanced) in 112 healthy young adults untrained in slow breathing. Participants breathed for 5 min at 6 cycles/min following a visual pacer, once while watching a live heart-rate display on a smartphone ('HRV biofeedback') and once without it, with 5 min of rest before and after each. Achieved breathing rate was about 6.45/min in both conditions. During the breathing, compared with the rest before it, both conditions showed higher RMSSD (d = 1.97), lower emotional arousal (d = 0.77), higher emotional control (d = 0.45), lower perceived stress (d = 0.46) and less pleasant emotional valence (d = 0.37). These changes did not last: in the 5-min rest afterwards, RMSSD, arousal, control and valence did not differ from the rest before, and only perceived stress stayed lower (d = 0.25). There was no time x condition interaction for any outcome. The only main effect of condition was valence, which was slightly more positive overall with the heart-rate display (partial eta squared = 0.06, d = 0.25).
claims.finding_zh: 受试者内实验（一次实验室访问，两种条件顺序平衡），112名未受过慢呼吸训练的健康年轻人：跟随视觉节拍器以每分钟6次呼吸5分钟，一次同时看手机上的实时心率曲线（“HRV生物反馈”），一次不看；每次前后各静息5分钟。两种条件下实际呼吸频率都约为每分钟6.45次。与呼吸前静息相比，慢呼吸进行期间两种条件都出现RMSSD升高（d = 1.97）、情绪唤醒降低（d = 0.77）、控制感升高（d = 0.45）、主观压力降低（d = 0.46），但情绪效价变得略不愉快（d = 0.37）。这些变化没有延续：呼吸结束后的5分钟静息中，RMSSD、唤醒、控制感和效价都与呼吸前无差异，只有主观压力仍较低（d = 0.25）。所有指标都没有时间×条件交互作用；唯一的条件主效应是效价——看心率曲线时整体略更正面（偏η² = 0.06，d = 0.25）。
claims.study_type: within-subject experiment with counterbalanced condition order (single session)
claims.sample: n = 112 analysed (120 recruited); healthy adults untrained in slow-paced breathing, recruited on a university campus; 52 men, 60 women; mean age 21.6 (range 18-31)
claims.limitations: Single lab visit with 5-min breathing periods; acute effects only (they had faded within 5 min after breathing); healthy, untrained young adults; 'biofeedback' was only a live heart-rate display at a fixed 6/min (not resonance-frequency biofeedback), and everyone saw the display during familiarization; no non-breathing control condition; unblinded self-reports and possible expectancy effects; respiration estimated from the ECG; a non-significant difference between conditions is not proof of equivalence.
claims.app_implication: In one 5-min session, following a 6/min visual pacer without a heart-rate display gave the same acute RMSSD, arousal, control and stress changes as following it with the display. This supports a sensor-free pacer for v1, but only a heart-rate display (not resonance-frequency biofeedback) was tested, and long-term use was not. Effects were present while breathing and had mostly faded 5 min later, so do not promise lasting calm from one session. Slow breathing felt slightly less pleasant while doing it (overall valence was slightly better with the display), so do not promise that every session will feel pleasant. After a gradual familiarization (2-min steps at 10, 8, then 6/min), untrained participants breathed at about 6.45/min.

citation.authors: Laborde S, Allen MS, Borges U, et al.
citation.title: Psychophysiological effects of slow-paced breathing at six cycles per minute with or without heart rate variability biofeedback

verification.checked_against: Crossref + PubMed metadata; Europe PMC abstract; full published article (Wiley CC BY-NC-ND version, PDF from Bournemouth University repository): Methods, Results, Table 1, Discussion/limitations
verification.problems: Metadata is correct (online Oct 2021, issue Jan 2022, 59(1):e13952). MATERIAL ERROR: the finding says the effects happened 'from pre to post', but the Results show the changes appeared DURING the 5-min breathing compared with the rest before it: RMSSD d = 1.97, arousal d = 0.77, control d = 0.45, valence more negative d = 0.37. PRE vs POST was not significant for RMSSD (p = .20), arousal (p = .38), control (p = 1.0) or valence (p = 1.0). The effects ended once breathing stopped (the authors call it a 'switch-on/switch-off' effect). The abstract's ambiguous wording ('for PRE and POST comparisons...') was misread. OMITTED OUTCOME: perceived stress (VAS) was lower during breathing (d = 0.46) and was the only measure still lower than before afterwards (d = 0.25). Design details the full text supplies: within-subject; one visit; counterbalanced order; 5-min conditions with 5-min washout; untrained healthy adults; achieved rate about 6.45/min. The 'biofeedback' was only a live heart-rate display on a smartphone, and all participants saw it during familiarization. Evidence weight 'moderate' overstates a single 5-min-session acute experiment whose app-relevant result is a null between-condition difference (not an equivalence test), so it is downgraded to low. The app_implication 'can reproduce the main acute effects of HRV biofeedback' should be limited to the measured outcomes and to this heart-rate-display form of biofeedback.

claims.topic: Can untrained people follow a 6/min pacer?
claims.finding: Randomized experiment (n = 96 undergraduates; groups of 31-33). After a resting baseline, participants did 10 min of breathing with a 6 breaths/min pacer, compassion-focused soothing rhythm breathing (audio-guided) or watching a nature video, followed by 5 min of self-critical writing, 5 min of self-compassionate writing and 10 min of recovery. The novices in the pacer group 'were unable to consistently breathe at that rate', averaging 12.2 breaths/min (SD 4.3; baseline 17.8). The soothing-rhythm group averaged 13.1/min and the video group 16.9/min. Both breathing conditions increased SDNN during practice while the video did not. The pacer group showed the largest increases in LF HRV and LF/HF ratio (pacer > soothing > video). HF HRV did not change with any condition. Groups did not differ during the writing (stress) or recovery periods, and blood pressure and heart rate showed no condition differences.
claims.finding_zh: 随机实验（96名本科生，每组31–33人）：静息基线后，分别进行10分钟跟随每分钟6次节拍器的呼吸、慈悲聚焦的“安抚节律呼吸”（音频引导）或观看自然视频，随后进行5分钟自我批评写作、5分钟自我关怀写作和10分钟恢复。节拍器组都是新手，“无法持续保持该频率”，练习期间平均每分钟12.2次（标准差4.3；基线17.8次）；安抚节律组平均13.1次，视频组16.9次。练习期间两种呼吸条件的SDNN都升高，视频组没有变化；节拍器组的低频HRV和LF/HF升幅最大（节拍器＞安抚节律＞视频）；高频HRV在任何条件下都没有变化；在写作（压力）和恢复阶段各组没有差异，血压和心率也没有组间差异。
claims.study_type: randomized controlled experiment, three parallel groups (single session)
claims.sample: n = 96 undergraduates (mean age about 21; about 70% female; about 90% white), randomized to three groups of 31-33
claims.limitations: Single 10-min session with no practice or familiarization reported; young undergraduates recruited through psychology courses; how breathing rate was derived from the respiration belt is not described, and its large SD (4.3) means the group average hides people who did slow down; small groups (about 32 each); internal inconsistencies in the paper (baseline 5 vs 10 min; group sizes reported differently in text and table).
claims.app_implication: Many untrained users may not manage 6/min in a first session (novices here averaged about 12/min against a 6/min pacer). Consider starting near the user's comfortable rate and slowing gradually, let users slow less if it feels uncomfortable, and show the actual target rate. This study did not test a gradual approach. In Laborde et al. (2022), untrained adults breathed at about 6.45/min after 2-min familiarization steps at 10, 8, then 6/min.

citation.authors: Steffen PR, Bartlett D, Channell RM, et al.
citation.title: Integrating Breathing Techniques Into Psychotherapy to Improve HRV: Which Approach Is Best?

verification.checked_against: Crossref + PubMed metadata; Europe PMC abstract; PMC full text (PMC7917055) including Methods, Results and Tables 1-2
verification.problems: Metadata is correct. The finding matches the abstract and full text, so the problems are minor precision issues: (1) The limitation 'breathing rate reported as an approximate average' is inaccurate. Table 2 reports the pacer group at 12.2 (SD 4.3)/min during practice vs 17.8 at baseline (soothing-rhythm group 13.1, video 16.9). The large SD shows wide individual variation, and the method for deriving rate from the respiration belt is not described. (2) The sample was young undergraduates (mean age about 21, about 70% female, about 90% white). (3) The paper has internal inconsistencies: baseline is 5 min in the abstract vs 10 min in the Methods, and group sizes are 33/32/31 in the text vs 31/32/33 in Table 1. (4) The app_implication's '~8/min' starting rate and gradual step-down are design choices this study did not test.

claims.topic: Inhale:exhale ratio and respiratory pauses at 6/min
claims.finding: Within-subject experiment in 64 athletes (27 female; mean age 22, range 18-30; 66 recruited, 2 excluded for technical problems). In one lab session, participants did a 5-min spontaneous-breathing baseline, then six 5-min slow-paced breathing conditions in randomized order, separated by 5-min washouts. All conditions ran at 6 breaths/min (10-s cycles, 30 cycles each), inhaling through the nose and exhaling through pursed lips to a visual pacer. Inhalation/exhalation ratios were 0.8, 1.0 or 1.2 (e.g., 4.5 s/5.5 s, 5 s/5 s, 5.5 s/4.5 s), each with or without 0.4-s pauses after inhalation and after exhalation. Every condition raised log RMSSD above baseline (d = 1.05-1.36; mean raw RMSSD about 82-90 ms vs 57 ms at baseline). Ratio had a significant main effect (F = 8.78, p < 0.001, partial eta-squared = 0.12). RMSSD was higher with the longer exhale (ratio 0.8) than with equal phases (d = 0.37, p = 0.012) or the longer inhale (d = 0.51, p < 0.001); equal phases did not differ from the longer inhale (d = 0.14). The brief pauses had no significant effect (p = 0.119) and did not interact with ratio (p = 0.83).
claims.finding_zh: 受试者内实验：64名运动员（27名女性，平均22岁，18–30岁；招募66人，2人因技术问题排除）。在一次实验中，先静息呼吸5分钟作为基线，然后按随机顺序完成6种各5分钟的慢呼吸，每种之间休息5分钟。全部按每分钟6次（每次10秒，共30次）进行，跟随画面节拍用鼻吸气、噘唇呼气。吸呼比分别为0.8、1.0、1.2（如吸4.5秒/呼5.5秒、5秒/5秒、5.5秒/4.5秒），且分别有或无吸气后、呼气后0.4秒的短暂停顿。所有呼吸方式都让RMSSD比基线明显升高（d = 1.05–1.36；原始均值约82–90毫秒，基线为57毫秒）。吸呼比有显著主效应（F = 8.78，p < 0.001，偏η² = 0.12）：呼气较长（吸呼比0.8）时RMSSD高于吸呼等长（d = 0.37，p = 0.012）和吸气较长（d = 0.51，p < 0.001）；吸呼等长与吸气较长之间无差异（d = 0.14）。0.4秒的短暂停顿没有显著影响（p = 0.119），与吸呼比也无交互作用。
claims.sample: n = 64 athletes (27 female, aged 18-30)
claims.limitations: Athletes only (higher resting HRV, possible ceiling effect). Single session; acute HRV marker measured during breathing, with no psychological outcomes. Narrow ratio range (0.8-1.2) and only 0.4-s pauses tested. Actual phase durations not verified with a respiratory belt. 5-min washouts may allow carryover. Ratio differences in RMSSD were small next to the rise every pattern produced over baseline. Contrasts with the null ratio effect in Meehan & Shaffer 2024 (1:2 vs 1:1 at 6/min). Published in a non-specialist MDPI journal.
claims.app_implication: Brief (0.4-s) pauses between phases added nothing here, so the slow-breathing default need not include them; longer breath holds were not tested. A slightly longer exhale at 6 breaths/min (e.g., about 4.5 s in / 5.5 s out, ratio about 0.8, the most exhale-weighted ratio tested) is a reasonable default. The acute gain is small and not consistently replicated, so present an equal ratio as a valid alternative.

citation.authors: Laborde S, Iskra M, Zammit N, et al.
citation.title: Slow-Paced Breathing: Influence of Inhalation/Exhalation Ratio and of Respiratory Pauses on Cardiac Vagal Activity

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata and abstract; full-text publisher PDF (MDPI, Sustainability 13:7775, retrieved via mdpi-res.com), including Methods, Results, Table 1 and Discussion; Europe PMC/PubMed record for Meehan & Shaffer 2024 (PMID 38507210)
verification.problems: The citation metadata, the design details in finding/finding_zh (64 athletes, 27 female, 18-30; six 5-min conditions at 6/min with 30 x 10-s cycles; ratios 0.8/1.0/1.2 with or without 0.4-s pauses; 5-min washouts) and the direction of results all match the publisher PDF. Corrections: (1) app_implication suggests an inhale:exhale ratio of about 0.7, outside the tested range of 0.8-1.2 (the authors stress the narrow range). 'No pauses are needed' generalizes from 0.4-s pauses only; longer holds were untested. (2) Omitted magnitudes. Every pattern raised RMSSD strongly over baseline (d = 1.05-1.36; raw means about 82-90 ms vs 57 ms). Ratio effects were modest: 0.8 vs 1.0, d = 0.37, p = 0.012; 0.8 vs 1.2, d = 0.51, p < 0.001; 1.0 vs 1.2, d = 0.14, n.s. Pause main effect p = 0.119; interaction p = 0.832. (3) Added the authors' own limitations: possible ceiling effect in athletes, possible washout carryover, phase durations not verified, and a 0.4-s pause much shorter than in prior work. The cited Meehan & Shaffer 2024 null result is confirmed: 1:2 vs 1:1 at 6/min, n = 26 plus a replication with n = 16, with no IE-ratio effect on HRV.

claims.topic: Combat tactical (box-style) breathing vs prolonged exhalation under stress
claims.finding: Counterbalanced repeated-measures laboratory study in 30 healthy participants. They performed a Stroop interference task under time pressure (350 ms inter-trial intervals, 1,500 ms trials) with white noise rising from 77 to 89 dB SPL. During the task they used either combat tactical breathing (the technique used by military and law-enforcement personnel) or prolonged exhalation to reduce the induced arousal. Subjective stress reactions (Multidimensional Mood Questionnaire) did not differ significantly between techniques. Physiological arousal was lower in the tactical-breathing condition; it was assessed via heart rate, HRV and electrodermal activity, and the abstract does not specify which measures differed. Task performance was better with prolonged exhalation. The authors suggest tactical breathing may suit passive coping, and prolonged exhalation situations that require active coping.
claims.finding_zh: 实验室研究，30名健康参与者在时间压力和逐渐增强的白噪声（77→89 dB）下完成Stroop任务，并在任务进行中分别使用“战术呼吸”（军警使用的呼吸法，后来的综述描述为吸气、屏息、呼气、屏息各4拍的方块式呼吸）或“延长呼气”。两种方法的主观压力反应无显著差异；战术呼吸时整体生理唤醒更低，而延长呼气时任务表现更好。作者认为：只需被动应对时战术呼吸可能更合适，需要主动完成任务时延长呼气更有效。
claims.study_type: within-subject (counterbalanced repeated-measures) laboratory experiment comparing two techniques; the abstract describes no no-breathing control
claims.sample: n = 30 healthy adults
claims.limitations: Small, single laboratory stressor. Only two techniques are compared, so it cannot show either beats no breathing; effect sizes are not in the abstract; breathing was done during the task, not before it. The full text is paywalled and was not read. Later OA reviews (PMC12341363, PMC12372116) describe tactical breathing as 4-4-4-4 with breath holds and prolonged exhalation as 2 s in / 8 s out. They report the arousal difference in heart rate and skin conductance or respiratory rate, with no HRV difference. These details are not confirmed against the primary text.
claims.app_implication: Box breathing is a reasonable 'downshift' option when the user can pause. If the user must keep breathing deliberately while doing a demanding task, suggest the exhale-emphasis slow mode instead. This is a single small lab study; do not claim performance gains.

citation.authors: Röttger S, Theobald DA, Abendroth J, et al.
citation.title: The Effectiveness of Combat Tactical Breathing as Compared with Prolonged Exhalation

verification.checked_against: Crossref + PubMed metadata; PubMed abstract; full text paywalled and not read (Springer behind a JS challenge; Unpaywall, OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar list no OA copy; the openHSU repository was down). Secondary descriptions in OA reviews PMC12341363 (Little 2025, Stress and Health), PMC12372116 and PMC11310253, and in Riedl et al. 2026
verification.problems: Metadata is correct: Appl Psychophysiol Biofeedback 46(1):19-28, March 2021 issue (online 5 Aug 2020); PMID 32757097; four authors, Röttger S, Theobald DA, Abendroth J, Jacobsen T. The abstract numbers are correct: n = 30, Stroop task, 350 ms inter-trial intervals, 1,500 ms trials, white noise 77-89 dB SPL, counterbalanced repeated measures. Problems: (1) Overstatement. The finding says physiological arousal '(heart rate, HRV, electrodermal activity) was lower' with tactical breathing. The abstract only names these as the measures and says 'physiological arousal' was lower in the TB condition. OA reviews summarising the paper report lower heart rate and skin conductance (or respiratory rate) under TB, and one states there was no significant HRV change for either technique. HRV should not be listed as lower. (2) Breathing was used during the stress task (abstract: participants used TB or ProlEx 'to reduce the induced ... arousal'; reviews: 'during stress task'). The app_implication's 'before tasks' extrapolates beyond the design. (3) finding_zh's '方块式呼吸' is not in the abstract. It is supported only by secondary sources (TB 4:4:4:4 with holds; prolonged exhalation 2 s in / 8 s out). Effect sizes and exact protocol were not verifiable.

claims.topic: Resonance-frequency assessment protocol and coaching cues
claims.finding: Practical guide to Lehrer and colleagues' resonance-frequency (RF) assessment. Adult RF lies between 4.5 and 6.5 breaths/min (children 6.5–9.5). Clients first practise relaxed breathing at 5.5–6/min, then breathe for 2-min trials at 6.5, 6.0, 5.5, 5.0 and 4.5 breaths/min (0.5-step decreases) separated by 2-min rests; a trial is repeated if the actual rate is off by 0.25/min. Six weighted criteria (weights not validated): heart rate–respiration phase synchrony (~0°, highest weight), peak–trough HR amplitude (HR Max − HR Min), LF power, maximum LF peak amplitude, smoothness of the HR curve envelope and fewest LF peaks; ties are broken by comfort, preference and goals, and fine-tuning compares RF ± 0.5/min. The protocol recommends longer exhalation, though two cited studies found no HRV difference between 1:1 and 1:2 ratios. Clients who feel faint or whose heart is beating too hard should take shallower and smoother breaths. Test–retest evidence is limited (r = 0.73 in 21 undergraduates), and whether RF training outperforms 6/min breathing is an open question.
claims.finding_zh: 实践指南，详述 Lehrer 等人的“共振频率”测定流程：成人共振频率在每分钟4.5–6.5次之间（儿童6.5–9.5次）。先练习每分钟5.5–6次的放松呼吸，再依次以每分钟6.5、6.0、5.5、5.0、4.5次各呼吸2分钟，每档之间休息2分钟；实际频率偏差达0.25次/分就重做。选择依据6项加权指标（权重未经验证）：心率与呼吸的相位同步（约0°，权重最高）、心率峰谷差、低频功率、低频峰值、心率曲线平滑度、低频峰个数；并列时按舒适度和目标决定，再用±0.5次/分微调。流程建议呼气更长，但所引两项研究发现1:1与1:2的HRV无差异。若练习者感到要晕倒或心跳过重，应改为更浅、更平顺的呼吸。重测信度证据有限（21名大学生，r = 0.73）；共振频率训练是否优于固定每分钟6次仍未解决。
claims.sample: Not applicable (protocol description; cites test–retest data from 21 undergraduates)
claims.limitations: Expert protocol; criterion weights unvalidated; requires ECG/PPG and respiration sensors; superiority over a fixed 6/min unproven; contraindication notes (pacemaker-driven rhythm; over-breathing that compensates metabolic acidosis such as in kidney disease) are expert opinion.
claims.app_implication: Sets the recommended slow-pace range (4.5–6.5/min) and 0.5/min steps. Without a validated HR sensor the app cannot perform true RF assessment, so offer at most a comfort-based pace picker labelled as such. Use 'shallower, smoother breaths' in over-breathing guidance.

citation.authors: Shaffer F, Meehan ZM
citation.title: A Practical Guide to Resonance Frequency Assessment for Heart Rate Variability Biofeedback

verification.checked_against: Crossref + PubMed metadata; open-access PMC full text (PMC7578229); corrigendum full text (PMC7793964)
verification.problems: No discrepancies. Every protocol detail matches the PMC full text: the 4.5–6.5 (adult) and 6.5–9.5 (child) bpm ranges, 5.5–6 bpm practice, 2-min trials with 2-min rests in 0.5-bpm steps from 6.5 to 4.5, and the 0.25-bpm repeat rule. The six weighted criteria (weights explicitly unvalidated), tie-breaking by comfort, preference and goals, and RF ± 0.5 bpm confirmation also match. So do the two studies finding no 1:1 vs 1:2 difference, the faint or pounding-heart guidance, Fuller et al. (r = 0.73 in 21 undergraduates, 2 weeks apart), the open question versus 6 bpm and the contraindications. The article type is Review. A corrigendum (10.3389/fnins.2020.627512, PMID 33424548) fixes only the HF band upper limit (0.40 Hz) and does not affect the claim.

claims.topic: An anti-over-breathing instruction during 6/min paced breathing
claims.finding: RCT in 46 participants performing 10 min of paced breathing at 0.1 Hz (6 breaths/min). Without instruction, end-tidal CO2 (PetCO2) fell by 5.21 mmHg; a brief anti-hyperventilation instruction asking participants to avoid excessively deep breathing and to breathe shallowly and naturally reduced the drop to 2.7 mmHg and lowered hyperventilation symptoms. Air hunger and task difficulty were not affected by the instruction, and there were no significant effects on affective state.
claims.finding_zh: 随机对照研究，46名参与者以每分钟6次的节律呼吸10分钟：没有提示时，呼气末二氧化碳下降5.21 mmHg；加入一句简短提示（避免吸得过深，自然、轻浅地呼吸）后，下降幅度减至2.7 mmHg，过度通气症状也更少；“吸不够气”的感觉和任务难度没有因此增加，情绪状态无显著差异。
claims.limitations: Single session; healthy volunteers; small; physiological marker outcome; a published correction fixed the sample size in the abstract (46, not 36).
claims.app_implication: Every slow-breathing session should include an anti-over-breathing cue ('轻、柔、自然，不必吸得很深'); never instruct 'take a big deep breath' in slow-paced mode.

claims.topic: HRV biofeedback for stress and anxiety
claims.finding: Random-effects meta-analysis of 24 studies (484 participants) of HRV biofeedback training for self-reported stress and anxiety. Pre–post within-group Hedges' g = 0.81 (95% CI 0.55 to 1.06). Thirteen studies had a comparison condition (6 waitlist, 2 treatment as usual, 1 standard care, 1 daily thought record, 1 progressive muscle relaxation, 2 sham biofeedback); the between-groups effect versus these was g = 0.83 (95% CI 0.34 to 1.33). Egger's tests were non-significant, and trim-and-fill did not lower either estimate. In moderator analyses of the within-group effects, efficacy was not significantly moderated by study year, risk of bias, percentage of females, number of sessions or presence of an anxiety disorder. Only one study was rated low risk of bias, all outcomes were self-reported, and long-term efficacy could not be assessed. The authors note that more well-controlled studies are needed and that the true effect size can only be determined by more rigorous trials.
claims.finding_zh: 对24项研究（共484人）的随机效应元分析：HRV生物反馈训练后，自评压力与焦虑的组内前后效应量g = 0.81（95%置信区间0.55–1.06）。其中13项研究设有对照（6项为等待名单，其余为常规治疗、标准护理、每日思维记录、渐进式肌肉放松或假生物反馈），与对照比较的组间效应量g = 0.83（95%置信区间0.34–1.33）。Egger检验均不显著。针对组内效应的调节分析中，研究年份、偏倚风险、女性比例、训练次数和是否患焦虑障碍均未显示显著调节作用（这并不等于证明它们没有影响）。仅1项研究为低偏倚风险，所有结局均为自评，缺乏长期随访数据。作者指出，真实效应大小仍需更严谨的对照试验来确定。
claims.sample: 24 studies, 484 participants (13 studies with a comparison condition)
claims.limitations: The headline 0.81 is an uncontrolled pre–post change, and 11 of 24 studies had no comparison group. The between-group estimate rests on 13 small studies, about half waitlist-controlled, with a wide CI (0.34–1.33). Only 1 study was at low risk of bias; randomization and allocation concealment were often not reported. All outcomes were self-reported and there was no follow-up. Non-specific factors (expectancy, therapist contact) may contribute, biofeedback protocols varied, and interventions used biofeedback equipment and often clinician contact. CIs and study-level details come from the authors' submitted manuscript (OpenBU), which may differ slightly from the published version; the abstract numbers are identical.
claims.app_implication: The large effect applies to equipment-based, often clinician-supported HRVB and is probably inflated by uncontrolled and waitlist-controlled designs. For its own sensor-free practice the app should quote the more conservative breathwork estimate (stress g = −0.35, Fincham 2023 meta-analysis) and reserve HRVB claims for a future sensor feature.

verification.checked_against: Crossref + PubMed metadata and abstract; authors' submitted manuscript full text from Boston University's OpenBU repository (hdl.handle.net/2144/26911)
verification.problems: Metadata, DOI, PMID and all abstract numbers are correct (24 studies, 484 participants, within-group g = 0.81, between-group g = 0.83, null moderators). Problems: (1) Important context is omitted. The CIs are 0.55–1.06 (within) and 0.34–1.33 (between). Only 13 of 24 studies had any comparison group (6 waitlist, 2 TAU, 1 standard care, 1 daily thought record, 1 PMR, 2 sham biofeedback), so 'several without control groups' understates it: 11 of 24 had none. Only 1 study was at low risk of bias, all outcomes were self-reported, there was no follow-up, and the moderator tests were run on the uncontrolled within-group effects. (2) finding_zh '效果不受……影响' presents non-significant moderator tests as proof of no influence, which the authors explicitly caution against. (3) evidence_weight 'moderate' is too high for an uncontrolled pre–post headline effect plus a small, mostly waitlist-controlled subset with a wide CI; corrected to 'low'. CIs and study-level details come from the authors' submitted manuscript on OpenBU; its abstract numbers are identical to the published abstract.

claims.topic: Nasal breathing, limbic oscillations and cognition
claims.finding: Intracranial EEG in 7 patients with medically refractory temporal lobe epilepsy showed that natural nasal breathing entrains oscillatory activity in piriform cortex, amygdala and hippocampus, with power peaking during inspiration. In the 3 patients also recorded while mouth breathing (only one with piriform coverage), these respiration-locked oscillations diminished when breathing was diverted from nose to mouth. Behavioural experiments involved 107 healthy subjects aged 18-30 in total. Fearful faces were identified faster when presented during nasal inhalation than exhalation (n = 21; t(20) = -2.64, p = 0.016; about 28 ms). There was no such effect for surprised faces or in a mouth-breathing group (n = 17), and fear-detection accuracy did not differ by phase. Recognition-memory accuracy was higher for pictures retrieved during nasal inspiration than expiration (n = 11; t(10) = 2.85, p = 0.017), with no phase effect during oral breathing (n = 11). The authors describe the behavioural effect sizes as relatively modest.
claims.finding_zh: 对7名药物难治性颞叶癫痫患者的颅内脑电记录显示：自然经鼻呼吸时，梨状（嗅）皮层、杏仁核和海马的振荡活动随呼吸节律同步，吸气时最强。其中3名患者另做了用嘴呼吸的记录，改用嘴呼吸后这种与呼吸同步的振荡减弱。行为实验共107名18–30岁健康人：经鼻吸气时识别恐惧面孔比呼气时快约28毫秒（21人；p = 0.016），惊讶面孔没有这种差异，用嘴呼吸的一组（17人）也没有；恐惧面孔的识别准确率不随呼吸时相变化。在经鼻吸气时进行的图片再认更准确（11人；p = 0.017），用嘴呼吸组（11人）没有这一效应。作者称这些行为效应“相对较小”。
claims.study_type: mechanistic study (intracranial EEG plus behavioural experiments)
claims.sample: 7 iEEG patients with epilepsy (3 with nose-vs-mouth recordings) plus 1 additional patient for an emotion task; 107 healthy subjects aged 18-30 across behavioural tasks (n = 11-24 per group)
claims.limitations: Mechanistic. The nose-vs-mouth neural comparison involved only 3 patients, and the intracranial data come from people with epilepsy. Behavioural groups were small and the tasks were specific laboratory tasks; effects were reaction-time differences of tens of milliseconds. No stress, anxiety or well-being outcomes, and nasal breathing was not tested as a practice.
claims.app_implication: Offers a mechanistic, not clinical, rationale for nasal breathing as a low-cost default cue (mouth breathing allowed when congested). Do not claim that nasal breathing boosts memory, calms the amygdala or reduces anxiety.

citation.authors: Zelano C, Jiang H, Zhou G, et al.

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata + PubMed abstract (PMID 27927961) + PMC full text (PMC5148230, pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov)
verification.problems: Metadata and all statistics match the full text: 7 iEEG patients plus 1 extra patient (P8); 107 healthy subjects aged 18-30; n = 21, t(20) = -2.64, p = 0.016; 28 ms; oral group n = 17; memory n = 11; the authors call the behavioural effect sizes 'relatively modest'. (1) The finding implies the nose-to-mouth reduction in oscillations was shown in all 7 patients. Per the full text, only 3 patients (P5, P6, P7) were recorded during mouth breathing, and only P7 had piriform coverage. (2) 'Supports nasal breathing as the default instruction' overstates a mechanistic study that tested no breathing practice and no stress or well-being outcome; softened. Added details: no phase effect for surprised faces; fear-detection accuracy did not vary with phase; memory p = 0.017.

claims.topic: Hyperventilation before breath-holding in water: fatal blackout
claims.finding: CDC MMWR case series of New York State drownings in 1988–2011 linked to 'dangerous underwater breath-holding behaviors' (intentional hyperventilation, static apnea, hypoxic training): 16 cases (15 incidents) and 4 fatalities. All four decedents were aged 17–22, advanced-to-expert swimmers, and had engaged in intentional hyperventilation. Mechanism described: hyperventilation or breath-holding before submersion lowers CO2 stores and PCO2, delaying the urge to surface and breathe, so falling arterial oxygen causes loss of consciousness underwater.
claims.finding_zh: 美国CDC《发病率与死亡率周报》病例系列：1988–2011年纽约州16例与“危险水下屏气行为”（刻意过度通气、静态屏气、缺氧训练）相关的溺水，共15起事件、4人死亡。4名死者均为17–22岁、游泳水平高，且都做过刻意过度通气。机制：入水前过度通气或屏气会降低体内二氧化碳，推迟“需要换气”的信号，结果在水下因缺氧突然失去意识。
claims.sample: 16 cases (4 fatal), New York State, 1988–2011
claims.limitations: Small retrospective case series; not specific to any named breathing method; cannot estimate risk per practitioner.
claims.app_implication: Any technique combining over-breathing with breath-holding is excluded, and all breathing content carries a 'never in or near water, in the bath or while driving' warning.
