claims.topic: 5.5 vs 6 breaths/min and 5:5 vs 4:6 inhale:exhale
claims.finding: Crossover experiment with Latin-square counterbalancing in random sequences, in 47 healthy college students, comparing four paced patterns: 6 or 5.5 breaths/min, each with an inhalation:exhalation ratio of 5:5 or 4:6. According to the abstract, breathing at 5.5/min with a 5:5 ratio produced higher SDNN and higher LF power than the other three patterns, and all four patterns increased self-rated relaxation compared with the spontaneous-breathing baseline. Anxiety was also measured, but its result is not reported in the abstract.
claims.finding_zh: 拉丁方交叉设计（随机顺序平衡），47名健康大学生比较4种节律：每分钟6次或5.5次，吸呼比5:5或4:6。摘要报告：每分钟5.5次且吸呼等长（5:5）时，SDNN和低频功率高于其他3种节律；4种节律都比自然呼吸基线更让人感到放松。研究也测量了焦虑，但摘要没有报告结果。
claims.study_type: randomized-order crossover experiment (Latin square), single session
claims.sample: n = 47 healthy college students
claims.limitations: Single session; small sample of healthy students; full text not read, so effect sizes and pairwise comparisons are unverified. A later full-text critique (Meehan & Shaffer 2024) reports that each pattern lasted only about 2 min, achieved breathing rate and ratio were not verified, and some post hoc comparisons confounded rate with ratio; it rated the study high risk of bias. SDNN and LF power at slow rates mainly reflect the size of breathing-linked heart-rate swings, not lasting benefit. A better-controlled study at 6/min found no ratio effect, and other studies favour a longer exhale.
claims.app_implication: Weak support for including 5.5/min with equal inhale and exhale (about 5.45 s each) as one preset. One small, short study cannot establish 5.5/min or a 1:1 ratio as better than 6/min or a longer exhale (a better-controlled study found no ratio effect at 6/min), so treat rate (about 5.5-6/min) and ratio as comfort settings.

citation.authors: Lin IM, Tai LY, Fan SY
citation.title: Breathing at a rate of 5.5 breaths per minute with equal inhalation-to-exhalation ratio increases heart rate variability

verification.checked_against: Crossref + PubMed metadata; Europe PMC abstract and MeSH terms; full text paywalled (Elsevier) and not read; full-text-based critique of this study in Meehan & Shaffer 2024 (PMC11310264), used as a secondary source
verification.problems: Metadata is correct. The finding and finding_zh match the abstract. The full text could not be accessed, so effect sizes and the pairwise comparisons behind 'higher than the other three patterns' could not be checked. Anxiety was also measured (MeSH: Anxiety, Visual Analog Scale), but the abstract does not report its result (possible omitted null). Meehan & Shaffer (2024) reviewed the full text and report that each pattern lasted only about 2 min, achieved rate and ratio were not verified, and Fisher's LSD post hoc tests partly confounded rate with ratio; they rated the study high risk of bias. The app_implication overstates: one small, short study does not justify 5.5/min as 'the default target'. '5.5 s in / 5.5 s out' gives 5.45/min, not 5.5/min (5.5/min needs about 5.45 s each). 'The 5.5 vs 6/min difference is small' is not supported by the abstract.

claims.topic: Longer exhalation vs slower rate: HRV and felt relaxation
claims.finding: Within-subject experiment: 30 undergraduates recruited (28 women, aged 18-22), 23 analysed after exclusions. Each did four 5-min paced patterns in counterbalanced order: 6 or 12 breaths/min, each with an inhalation/exhalation ratio of 0.42 (e.g., 3 s in / 7 s out) or 2.33 (7 s in / 3 s out). Achieved values differed from the targets: the '6/min' patterns averaged 7.3-7.7/min, and the inhale-dominant ratio reached only about 1.4. Compared with the inhale-dominant ratio, the exhale-dominant ratio produced higher self-reported basic relaxation, mindfulness and positive energy and less stress (partial eta squared .21-.38), plus higher pleasantness and sense of control. On the relaxation inventory, slower breathing (6 vs 12/min) raised only positive energy, but on the Self-Assessment Manikin it also lowered arousal and raised pleasantness. The exhale-dominant ratio was associated with more HF-HRV power and RSA only during slow breathing. Unexpectedly, it also produced a slightly higher heart rate, and LF power did not differ by ratio.
claims.finding_zh: 受试者内实验：招募30名本科生（28名女性，18–22岁），排除7人后23人进入分析。每人按平衡顺序完成4种各5分钟的引导呼吸：每分钟6次或12次，吸呼时间比0.42（如吸3秒、呼7秒）或2.33（吸7秒、呼3秒）。实际呼吸偏离目标：“每分钟6次”时实际约7.3–7.7次，“吸长呼短”的实际吸呼比只有约1.4。与吸长呼短相比，吸短呼长时自评的基本放松、正念、积极能量更高，压力更低（偏η² 0.21–0.38），愉悦感和控制感也更高。在放松量表上，放慢频率（6次对12次）只提高了“积极能量”；但在自我评估小人量表上，放慢频率也带来更低的唤醒和更高的愉悦感。吸短呼长只在慢呼吸时伴随更高的高频HRV和RSA；出乎意料的是，它让心率略高，低频功率不受吸呼比影响。
claims.study_type: within-subject 2x2 repeated-measures experiment (single session, counterbalanced order)
claims.sample: 30 undergraduates recruited (28 women, 2 men; aged 18-22); 23 analysed after excluding 5 who met exclusion criteria and 2 who did not follow the breathing instructions
claims.limitations: Single session; small sample (23 analysed), almost all women; participants missed the targets (about 7.5/min instead of 6, and an inhale-dominant ratio of about 1.4 instead of 2.33); the comparison pattern (inhale longer than exhale) is artificial and may simply have been unpleasant, and equal 1:1 breathing was not tested; the authors note possible over-breathing; HF power at 6/min partly reflects harmonics of the 0.1 Hz rhythm; unblinded self-reports; the brief practice phase was in fixed order.
claims.app_implication: Avoid inhale-dominant patterns (inhale longer than exhale) in calming modes. An exhale-dominant ratio (around 1:2) is a reasonable default for perceived relaxation. This study did not test equal (1:1) breathing, so it does not show that a long exhale beats an equal ratio; offer the ratio as a comfort setting.

citation.authors: Van Diest I, Verstappen K, Aubert AE, et al.
citation.title: Inhalation/Exhalation ratio modulates the effect of slow breathing on heart rate variability and relaxation

verification.checked_against: Crossref + PubMed metadata; Europe PMC abstract; authors' accepted manuscript (KU Leuven Lirias post-print) including Methods, Results and Tables 1-2; cross-checked against the description in Meehan & Shaffer 2024
verification.problems: Metadata is correct. SAMPLE IS WRONG: 30 were recruited, but 5 met exclusion criteria and 2 did not follow instructions, so N = 23 was analysed (post-print; also reported by Meehan & Shaffer 2024). 28 of the 30 were women. FRAMING: the ratio effects are relative to an artificial inhale-dominant pattern, not to baseline or to equal breathing. Descriptively, mindfulness and pleasantness were below baseline in all four patterns, and stress was roughly at baseline with the long exhale but higher with the long inhale. OMITTED RESULTS: 'a lower rate increased only positive energy' holds only for the relaxation inventory (SRSI-3). On the Self-Assessment Manikin, 6/min also lowered arousal (partial eta squared .27) and raised pleasantness (.17). Participants missed the targets: the 6/min patterns averaged 7.3-7.7/min, and the 2.33 ratio was achieved as about 1.4. The low ratio unexpectedly raised heart rate. LIMITATIONS: 'extreme ratios (0.42 and 2.33) unlike typical app settings' is inaccurate, because 0.42 (3 s in / 7 s out; achieved about 0.49) is close to the common 1:2; only the inhale-dominant ratio is unusual. APP IMPLICATION: 'never use inhale-dominant patterns' is stronger than one small study supports, and 1:1 was not tested.

claims.topic: Cyclic hyperventilation with retention (Wim Hof-type training): physiology
claims.finding: Parallel randomized controlled trial in healthy, non-smoking young men. Thirty were randomized (18 to training, 12 to no training); after training, 12 of the 18 were randomly selected, giving 12 vs 12 in the endotoxin experiment. Training lasted 10 days, was led by Wim Hof and three instructors, and combined meditation, breathing techniques (including cyclic hyperventilation followed by breath retention) and cold exposure (including ice-cold water immersion). All participants then underwent experimental endotoxemia (2 ng/kg E. coli endotoxin i.v.), and the trained group practised the breathing techniques during the experiment. Practising the techniques produced intermittent respiratory alkalosis (pH up to 7.75 in individual subjects) and hypoxia (oxygen saturation typically dipping to about 50% for ~10 s at the end of each breath hold) with profoundly increased plasma epinephrine. In the trained group, anti-inflammatory IL-10 rose more rapidly and was higher (194% higher), TNF-α, IL-6 and IL-8 were lower (by 53%, 57% and 51%), and peak flu-like symptoms were 56% lower.
claims.finding_zh: 随机对照试验，对象为健康、不吸烟的年轻男性：30人随机分为训练组（18人）或不训练组（12人），训练结束后再从训练组随机抽取12人，与对照组12人一起接受内毒素实验。训练为期10天，由Wim Hof及3名教练带领，内容包括冥想、呼吸技术（含循环过度通气后屏息）和冷暴露（含冰水浸泡）。所有人随后静脉注射内毒素（每公斤体重2纳克大肠杆菌内毒素），训练组在实验过程中练习呼吸技术。练习时出现间歇性呼吸性碱中毒（个别受试者血液pH高达7.75）和低氧（每次屏息末血氧饱和度通常短暂降到约50%，持续约10秒），血浆肾上腺素显著升高。训练组的抗炎因子IL-10升得更快、更高（高194%），促炎因子TNF-α、IL-6、IL-8分别低53%、57%、51%，流感样症状峰值低56%。
claims.sample: 30 healthy young men randomized (18 training vs 12 control); 24 underwent endotoxemia and were analysed (12 vs 12)
claims.limitations: Very small, all-male sample (median age 22-24). Unblinded, no-training control. Multi-component training (breathing, cold, meditation): the authors state the design cannot isolate which component raised epinephrine, though they attribute it mainly to the breathing. Three control participants with atypically low responses were excluded after the fact (presumed dosing error) and replaced. Acute laboratory endotoxin model under ICU monitoring, with the method's originator coaching. No mental-health outcomes.
claims.app_implication: In this trial, cyclic hyperventilation with breath retention, practised under ICU monitoring, produced marked respiratory alkalosis, brief deep oxygen desaturation and an adrenaline surge. It is a physiologically activating practice rather than a calming one, and unsuitable for unsupervised app delivery. Exclude.

citation.title: Voluntary activation of the sympathetic nervous system and attenuation of the innate immune response in humans
citation.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; PubMed abstract (PMID 24799686); PMC full text (PMC4034215) incl. Methods, Results, Table 1, Discussion
verification.problems: Citation metadata and all abstract-level statements are correct. The full text shows omissions. (1) Participants were all healthy, non-smoking young Dutch men (median age 22-24), not unspecified 'healthy volunteers'; this matters for generalizing to women. (2) Randomization was 30 men allocated 18:12, with 12 of the 18 trained men later randomly selected for endotoxemia; it was not a 12 vs 12 randomization. (3) Three control participants with atypically low cytokine responses were excluded after the fact (presumed endotoxin dosing error) and replaced, a bias risk missing from limitations. (4) The authors state the design cannot isolate which component raised epinephrine, though they attribute it mainly to the breathing. (5) Training was led by Wim Hof, who also coached participants during the experiment. Verified magnitudes have been added (pH up to 7.75; SpO2 ~50% for ~10 s; TNF-α/IL-6/IL-8 lower by 53/57/51%; IL-10 194% higher; peak symptoms 56% lower).

claims.topic: Sigh as a resetter of breathing variability
claims.finding: Laboratory study of spontaneous breathing in 42 healthy undergraduate psychology students (34 women, 8 men; aged 18-20). Breathing was recorded with the LifeShirt system (respiratory inductive plethysmography) during 20 min of quiet sitting, presented as 'equipment calibration' so that sighs would be spontaneous. Sighs were breaths with at least 2.5 times the median inspiratory volume. 12 participants did not sigh, and 8 sighed too often for no-sigh comparison epochs to be built. Minute-ventilation variability was compared in 10-breath blocks before and after sighs versus comparable no-sigh epochs. Toward a sigh, total variability (coefficient of variation) gradually increased while correlated (structured) variability (autocorrelation) did not change. The authors read this as suggesting rising randomness, while cautioning that this interpretation needs care. Right after a sigh, total and correlated variability both rose, then returned toward baseline within roughly 10-20 breaths. Comparable epochs without a sigh showed no such changes, and end-tidal CO2 did not change around sighs. The authors conclude that a sigh resets structured respiratory variability, calling this a first step toward testing the 'resetter' hypothesis.
claims.finding_zh: 实验室研究：42名健康的心理学本科生（女34人、男8人，18–20岁），在被告知为“设备校准”的20分钟安静静坐中，用LifeShirt背心（呼吸感应体积描记）记录自然呼吸。吸气量达到中位数2.5倍以上的呼吸算作叹气；12人整段时间没有叹气，8人叹气过于频繁、无法构成“无叹气”对照段。研究按每10次呼吸为一段，比较叹气前后与无叹气时段的分钟通气量变异。叹气前，总变异（变异系数）逐渐增加，而有结构的变异（自相关）不变，作者认为这提示随机性增加，但也提醒这一解释需谨慎；叹气后，总变异和有结构的变异都上升，约10–20次呼吸后回到原来水平。无叹气的对照时段没有这些变化；叹气前后呼气末二氧化碳也没有变化。作者据此提出叹气会“重置”呼吸的结构化变异性，并称这只是检验该假说的第一步。
claims.sample: n = 42 healthy undergraduates aged 18-20 (34 women); 12 produced no sighs
claims.limitations: Correlational. Spontaneous rather than deliberate sighs. Small, young, mostly female student sample, with at most 30 people contributing sigh epochs. No subjective, emotional or HRV measures. Short breath strings limited analysis to simple variability indices. The reset model remains a hypothesis.
claims.app_implication: Mechanistic background only, not proof of benefit, for a sigh-based mode. Use only modest copy such as 'sighs seem to help reset breathing patterns'. This study supports no claims about stress relief or the nervous system.

citation.authors: Vlemincx E, Van Diest I, Lehrer PM, et al.
citation.title: Respiratory variability preceding and following sighs: a resetter hypothesis

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; PubMed abstract (PMID 19744538); full text, the author's personal copy of the published version (KU Leuven Lirias), including Method, Data analysis, Results and Discussion
verification.problems: Metadata (authors, 2010, title, Biological Psychology 84:82-87, DOI, PMID) is correct, and the abstract-level results are reproduced accurately. Corrections from the full text: (1) Population: participants were 42 undergraduate psychology students aged 18-20 (34 women, 8 men), not a general adult sample. 12 produced no sighs and 8 sighed too often for no-sigh comparison epochs, so at most 30 people contributed sigh epochs. (2) 'Meaning randomness increased' overstates the source. The abstract says 'suggesting', and the Discussion warns that the rise in total variation could reflect structured components not captured by autocorrelation. (3) The post-sigh increases (total and correlated variability) were transient, returning to baseline within roughly 10-20 breaths; this was omitted. (4) The zh '重置呼吸调节' is broader than the authors' 'resets structured respiratory variability'.

claims.topic: Capnometry-assisted 'slow and shallow' breathing therapy for panic disorder
claims.finding: RCT in 37 patients with panic disorder (31 with, 6 without agoraphobia) randomized to brief capnometry-assisted breathing therapy (n = 20) or delayed treatment (waitlist, n = 17). Therapy: 5 weekly 1-h sessions over 4 weeks plus twice-daily 17-min home exercises with a portable capnometer (2 min quiet sitting, 10 min breathing with pacing tones set to 13, 11, 9 and then 6 breaths/min in successive weeks, 5 min unpaced transfer). The aim was to raise end-tidal pCO2 into the normocapnic range (>35 mmHg) through 'regular slow and shallow breathing'. 26 of 37 patients were hypocapnic (<35 mmHg) at baseline. Post-treatment effect sizes vs waitlist: panic severity (PDSS) d = 2.21; psychological measures d = 0.97-2.21; respiratory measures d = 0.59-1.23 (e.g., pCO2 during recovery from a hyperventilation task rose from 30.29 to 36.18 mmHg), although the group difference in resting (quiet-sitting) pCO2 was only marginal (p < .10, d = 0.59). In week 1, paced breathing lowered pCO2 slightly below the pre-exercise level (34.7 vs 36.7 mmHg); in week 4 the mean paced rate was 7.76/min (target 6). Improvement was not greater in patients who were hypocapnic at baseline or had a 'respiratory' symptom subtype. At 12 months (uncontrolled follow-up) 68% were panic-free; homework completion was 91.3% with no dropouts during treatment.
claims.finding_zh: 随机对照试验，37名惊恐障碍患者（31人伴广场恐惧、6人不伴），随机接受“二氧化碳监测辅助呼吸治疗”（20人）或延迟治疗（候补组，17人）。治疗为4周内5次、每次1小时的会谈，加每天2次、每次17分钟、配合便携式二氧化碳监测仪的居家练习：2分钟静坐，10分钟跟随音调呼吸（第1–4周依次为每分钟13、11、9、6次），5分钟不跟音调、保持同样节律；目标是通过“规律、缓慢且较浅的呼吸”把呼气末二氧化碳分压提高到35 mmHg以上。基线时37人中26人二氧化碳偏低。治疗后与候补组相比：惊恐严重度效应量d = 2.21，心理指标d = 0.97–2.21，呼吸指标d = 0.59–1.23（例如过度通气任务后恢复期的二氧化碳分压由30.29升至36.18 mmHg），但安静静坐时的二氧化碳分压组间差异只是接近显著（p < .10，d = 0.59）。第1周跟随音调呼吸时，二氧化碳分压反而略低于练习前（34.7对36.7 mmHg）；第4周实际平均呼吸频率为每分钟7.76次（目标6次）。基线二氧化碳偏低或以呼吸症状为主的患者，疗效并不更好。12个月时（无对照的随访）68%的人不再有惊恐发作；居家练习完成率91.3%，治疗期间无人退出。
claims.sample: n = 37 adults with panic disorder (20 treated, 17 waitlist)
claims.limitations: Small. Waitlist rather than an active or attention control, so the authors cannot rule out non-specific therapy effects. Participants and therapists unblinded; PDSS rated by independent raters, blinding not reported. 12-month follow-up uncontrolled (12.1% attrition). Benefit unrelated to baseline hypocapnia, so the CO2-raising mechanism is unproven. Mostly female, white, well-educated US community sample. Relies on a capnometer the app cannot provide.
claims.app_implication: For anxiety-prone users, the coaching principle is 'slow and light', not 'deep breaths' (the trial taught 'regular slow and shallow breathing'). Shape pace gradually over weeks rather than demanding 6/min on day one: even after 4 weeks of shaping, patients averaged 7.76/min. This is a design choice drawn from the protocol; the trial did not compare gradual with immediate pacing. The app cannot measure CO2, so panic disorder is a 'see a professional' context, not a treatment claim.

citation.authors: Meuret AE, Wilhelm FH, Ritz T, et al.
citation.title: Feedback of end-tidal pCO2 as a therapeutic approach for panic disorder

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; PubMed abstract (PMID 17681544); PMC author-manuscript full text (PMC2890048) incl. Methods, Tables 1-2, Results 3.1-3.5 and Limitations
verification.problems: Metadata and every reported number match the full text (37 = 20 + 17; 31 with / 6 without agoraphobia; 26 hypocapnic; PDSS d = 2.21; psychological d = 0.97-2.21; respiratory d = 0.59-1.23; VH/pCO2 30.29 to 36.18 mmHg; week-4 paced rate 7.76/min; 68% panic-free at 12 months; 91.3% homework; no treatment dropouts). Corrections address omitted nulls and context. (1) The resting (quiet-sitting) pCO2 group difference was only marginal (F = 3.72, p < .10, d = 0.59). (2) Benefit was not greater in hypocapnic or 'respiratory-subtype' patients, so the CO2 mechanism is unproven, and the authors cannot exclude non-specific therapy effects. (3) 'Unblinded' is accurate for participants and therapists, but PDSS was rated by independent raters whose blinding is not reported. (4) The 68% panic-free figure comes from uncontrolled follow-up with 12.1% attrition. (5) The app implication's 'gradual shaping' advice is drawn from the protocol, not tested against immediate 6/min pacing.

claims.topic: Individual differences in resonance frequency
claims.finding: Mechanistic paper drawing on the authors' earlier biofeedback studies, reporting data from 32 adults with asthma and 24 healthy adults: resonant frequency was negatively related to height and was lower in men than in women, with no relationship to age, weight or presence of asthma. Resonant frequency remained constant across 10 sessions of biofeedback training. The authors suggest it appears to be related to blood volume (a hypothesis, not a measured result).
claims.finding_zh: 机制性论文，使用作者既往生物反馈研究的数据（32名哮喘成人和24名健康成人）：共振频率与身高呈负相关，男性低于女性，与年龄、体重、是否患哮喘无关；共振频率在10次生物反馈训练中保持不变。作者推测它与血容量有关（这是推测，并未直接测量）。
claims.study_type: mechanistic review with secondary correlational analysis of data from earlier biofeedback studies
claims.sample: n = 56 (32 adults with asthma, 24 healthy adults)
claims.limitations: Small, older dataset pooled from earlier studies, mostly asthma patients; correlational; effect sizes and how many participants contributed the 10-session stability data are not given in the abstract (full text paywalled, not read); the blood-volume explanation is a hypothesis; resonance frequency was determined with HRV-biofeedback equipment, which a sensor-free app cannot reproduce.
claims.app_implication: Resonance frequency differs between people (lower in taller people and in men) and stayed stable over 10 sessions, which supports offering an adjustable pace instead of fixing 6.0/min for everyone. The 4.5-6.5/min range comes from standard HRV-biofeedback protocols (e.g., Lehrer & Gevirtz 2014), not from this paper. Without an HRV sensor the app cannot find a user's resonance frequency, so present a saved pace as a comfort preference, not as 'your resonance frequency'. Do not tell users that taller people or men 'prefer' slower paces, because preference was not studied.

citation.authors: Vaschillo EG, Vaschillo B, Lehrer PM
citation.title: Characteristics of Resonance in Heart Rate Variability Stimulated by Biofeedback

verification.checked_against: Crossref + PubMed esummary metadata; Europe PMC/PubMed abstract (PMID 16838124); secondary description in Lehrer & Gevirtz 2014 review (PMC4104929). Full text is paywalled (Springer) and was not read.
verification.problems: Metadata (authors, 2006, title, Appl Psychophysiol Biofeedback 31(2):129-142, DOI, PMID) is correct. The finding and finding_zh match the abstract. Full text not accessible, so effect sizes and the number of participants behind the 10-session stability result could not be checked. The problems are in interpretation: (1) the app_implication says taller users and men 'may prefer slower paces', but the study measured resonance frequency, not preference; (2) the 4.5-6.5/min range comes from standard HRV-biofeedback protocols (e.g., Lehrer & Gevirtz 2014), not from this paper; (3) a self-chosen pace remembered by a sensor-free app is not a measured resonance frequency. study_type: the paper is mainly a mechanistic review with secondary analysis of the authors' earlier data. The blood-volume link is a hypothesis ('appears to be related').

claims.topic: 4-7-8 breathing: early single-session physiological study
claims.finding: Single-session study in 43 healthy adults aged 19-25 (36 female). 22 habitually slept under 7 h a night (mean 6.1 h; labelled 'sleep deprivation') and 21 slept over 7 h (mean 7.4 h). After instruction, participants lay supine with eyes closed and did 4-7-8 breathing: silent nasal inhale counting to 4, 7-s breath hold, 'whooshing' mouth exhale counting to 8, about 3 breaths/min. They did 3 sets of 6 cycles, with 1 min of normal breathing between sets, and were then measured during a further 10 min supine. Compared with pre-exercise values (there was no time-matched control), heart rate and systolic BP fell in both groups, and SDNN, total power and VLF power also fell in both groups. In the adequate-sleep group, LF power, normalized LF and LF/HF fell and normalized HF rose; absolute HF power did not change significantly. In the short-sleep group, RMSSD fell. None of these changes differed significantly between groups.
claims.finding_zh: 单次练习研究，43名19–25岁健康成人（36名女性）：22人长期每晚睡眠不足7小时（平均6.1小时，文中称“睡眠剥夺”），21人睡眠超过7小时（平均7.4小时）。受试者经指导后平躺闭眼做4-7-8呼吸（鼻子安静吸气数到4，屏息7秒，用嘴“呼”地呼气数到8，约每分钟3次），每组6个循环，共3组，组间自然呼吸1分钟，随后继续平躺10分钟进行测量。与练习前相比（没有不做呼吸练习的对照），两组心率和收缩压均下降，SDNN、总功率和极低频功率也都下降；睡眠充足组低频功率、标准化低频和低频/高频比下降，标准化高频上升（高频绝对功率无显著变化）；睡眠不足组RMSSD下降。两组之间的变化无显著差异。
claims.study_type: two-group cross-sectional comparison with a single-session pre-post 4-7-8 test (no non-breathing control)
claims.sample: n = 43 healthy young adults (36 female)
claims.limitations: No control condition, so changes may partly reflect continued supine rest. Single session; small, 84% female sample; groups differed in age. 'Sleep deprivation' meant habitual short sleep with similar sleep quality. HRV changes were mixed (SDNN, total and VLF power fell), and there were no sleep, anxiety or mood outcomes. The authors' conclusion that 4-7-8 'can help participants improve their HRV and BP' goes beyond the data. A later within-subject study of 84 students (Marchant et al. 2025, PMID 39864026) found 6 breaths/min raised HRV more than 4-7-8 or square breathing, with no meaningful BP or mood change.
claims.app_implication: 4-7-8 has minimal, mixed evidence and long breath holds. Do not make it a default, and make no insomnia or blood-pressure claims. If offered, keep it library-only, labelled as a traditional technique with low evidence. Prefer about 6 breaths/min paced breathing for HRV-oriented modes.

citation.authors: Vierra J, Boonla O, Prasertsri P
citation.title: Effects of sleep deprivation and 4-7-8 breathing control on heart rate variability, blood pressure, blood glucose, and endothelial function in healthy young adults

verification.checked_against: Crossref + PubMed metadata; PubMed abstract; full text PMC9277512 (Europe PMC XML: population, protocol, results, discussion, limitations); Europe PMC search for other 4-7-8 studies, with abstracts of Marchant 2025 (PMID 39864026) and Avcık 2026 (PMID 42771122)
verification.problems: Metadata is correct (Physiol Rep 10(13):e15389, 2022; PMID 35822447). Confirmed from the full text: the protocol (supine, eyes closed, silent nasal inhale counting 4, 7-s hold, whooshing mouth exhale counting 8, 6 cycles x 3 sets, 1 min between sets) and the sample (36/43 female). Problems: (1) 'HF power increased' in the adequate-sleep group was normalized HF (HF n.u.). Absolute HF power did not rise significantly (mean change -2.5%). (2) SDNN, total power and VLF power fell in both groups, not only in the sleep-deprived group. The 'whereas' contrast, and '反而' in finding_zh, imply a group difference the paper says was absent; only the RMSSD fall was specific to the short-sleep group. (3) 'Sleep-deprived' means habitually sleeping under 7 h/night (mean 6.06 vs 7.43 h) for at least 3 months with similar sleep quality, not acute deprivation. (4) Post-measures were taken during a further 10 min lying supine, with no time-matched control. (5) The topic 'only physiological study found' is wrong. Europe PMC lists Marchant et al. 2025 (Appl Psychophysiol Biofeedback, PMID 39864026). In that within-subject study of 84 students, 6 breaths/min raised HRV more than 4-7-8 or square breathing, and no condition meaningfully changed BP or mood. It also lists Avcık et al. 2026 (randomized crossover, n = 34; no condition effect on HRV) and several clinical RCTs. (6) '(grade D)' in app_implication is an internal label, not from the source.

claims.topic: Brainstem breathing-rhythm neurons and arousal (mouse)
claims.finding: In mice, conditional bilateral genetic ablation of the ~175 Cdh9/Dbx1 double-positive neurons in the preBötzinger complex (the primary breathing rhythm generator) left breathing intact but increased calm behaviours and decreased time spent in aroused states. These neurons project to, synapse on and positively regulate noradrenergic neurons in the locus coeruleus, a centre implicated in attention, arousal and panic.
claims.finding_zh: 小鼠研究：在呼吸节律发生器（前包钦格复合体）中选择性去除约175个Cdh9/Dbx1双阳性神经元后，呼吸基本不受影响，但小鼠的平静行为增多、处于唤醒状态的时间减少。这些神经元投射到蓝斑核并正向调节其去甲肾上腺素能神经元，而蓝斑核与注意、唤醒和惊恐有关。
claims.sample: Laboratory mice
claims.limitations: Animal model; genetic ablation, not voluntary slow breathing; does not show that human paced breathing acts through this circuit.
claims.app_implication: Usable only as background that breathing rhythm and arousal are linked in the brainstem; never as evidence that the app's exercises calm users via this pathway.

citation.authors: Yackle K, Schwarz LA, Kam K, et al.
citation.title: Breathing control center neurons that promote arousal in mice

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; PubMed abstract (PMID 28360327); PMC full text PMC5505554 (author manuscript, via NCBI efetch), including main text and figure legends
verification.problems: No material discrepancies. Metadata (Science 355:1411-1415, 2017; DOI; PMID) is correct. The finding and finding_zh match the abstract and are consistent with the full text: breathing patterns and regulation intact, a shift from active toward calm behaviours, fewer active ECoG states, and a monosynaptic projection to and positive regulation of locus coeruleus noradrenergic neurons. Minor note: the body text gives about 175 Cdh9/Dbx1 neurons per preBötC (about 350 bilaterally); the claim follows the abstract's '~175'. Evidence weight 'very-low' is appropriate for applying this to human breathing practice.

claims.topic: Diaphragmatic slow breathing training, attention, affect and cortisol (Chinese adults)
claims.finding: Controlled trial in 40 healthy employees of a Beijing IT company with no mind-body training experience. Allocation was by alternating registration order with gender balance (10 women and 10 men per group), though the abstract describes random assignment. The breathing group (19 analysed) completed 20 coach-led sessions over 8 weeks (every other weekday). Each session was 15 min of normal resting breathing followed by 15 min of seated, eyes-closed diaphragmatic breathing. Breathing waveforms were recorded and monitored in real time by experimenters (mean about 3.5 breaths/min, reported as about 4). The control group (20) received no training. Negative affect (PANAS, past week) fell within the breathing group (MD 2.55, p = 0.02), but the group x time interaction was only marginal (p = 0.07); positive affect did not change (interaction p = 0.68). Sustained attention (number cancellation test) showed a group x time interaction (p = 0.004, partial eta squared 0.21): both groups improved (MD 6.7 vs 4.2), the breathing group more. Salivary cortisol showed a group x time interaction (F(3,111) = 9.06, p < 0.001, partial eta squared 0.20): it was lower at the final tests than at baseline in the breathing group and unchanged in controls.
claims.finding_zh: 对照试验，40名北京某IT公司无身心训练经验的健康员工。分组按报名顺序交替进行并平衡男女（每组10男10女），并非真正随机，尽管摘要称“随机分配”。呼吸组（分析19人）在8周内隔天完成20次教练带领的训练，每次先15分钟自然呼吸，再15分钟闭眼坐姿腹式呼吸，研究人员通过记录设备实时监测呼吸波形（平均约每分钟3.5次，文中称约4次）；对照组（20人）不训练。呼吸组的负面情绪（PANAS，回顾过去一周）较基线下降（均数差2.55，p=0.02），但组别×时间交互作用仅为边缘显著（p=0.07）；正面情绪无变化。持续注意力（数字划消测验）有显著交互作用（p=0.004）：两组都有提高（6.7分对4.2分），呼吸组提高更多。唾液皮质醇有显著交互作用（p<0.001）：呼吸组训练后降低，对照组无变化。
claims.study_type: controlled trial with alternating (quasi-random) allocation, described by the authors as randomized
claims.sample: n = 40 healthy IT employees allocated (20 vs 20); 39 analysed (19 vs 20)
claims.limitations: Allocation by alternation, not true randomization; small; no active or attention control; unblinded. The coach-led protocol with live breath monitoring is unlike self-guided app use. The negative-affect benefit is shown only within group (between-group interaction p = 0.07), and controls also improved on the attention test (practice effect). Cortisol assay CVs were 9.8% intra-assay and 15% inter-assay, and the authors note the physiological relevance of the drop is unknown. There are some internal reporting inconsistencies (e.g., Table 1 p-values).
claims.app_implication: At most supports using diaphragmatic breathing as a cue inside the slow-paced mode and offering a multi-week programme; the study involved Chinese office workers. The protocol was coach-led with live breath monitoring, so do not claim attention, mood or cortisol benefits from app use.

citation.authors: Ma X, Yue ZQ, Gong ZQ, et al.
citation.title: The Effect of Diaphragmatic Breathing on Attention, Negative Affect and Stress in Healthy Adults

verification.checked_against: Crossref + PubMed metadata; PubMed abstract; full text PMC5455070 (Europe PMC XML: participants, protocol, results, limitations)
verification.problems: Metadata is correct (Front Psychol 8:874, 2017; PMID 28626434). Problems from the full text: (1) It is not a true RCT. Participants were 'assigned ... by alternating the order of their registration' with gender balance (10 women and 10 men per group), even though the abstract and discussion call it random/randomized. (2) Negative affect fell only within the breathing group (MD 2.55, p = 0.02); the group x time interaction was marginal (F(1,37) = 3.43, p = 0.07). Positive affect did not change (interaction p = 0.68). Both nulls are omitted. (3) Sustained attention also improved significantly in controls (MD 4.19 vs 6.73 in the breathing group, both p < 0.001); the interaction (p = 0.004) means the breathing group improved more. finding_zh's '对照组无变化' is therefore wrong for attention; it is correct only for cortisol. (4) 'Real-time feedback device': participants kept their eyes closed, experimenters monitored the waveforms, and the coach intervened if the rate stayed above 6/min. This was coach-led, monitored training, not self-viewed biofeedback. (5) Mean rate was 3.45 +/- 1.86 breaths/min, reported as about 4. (6) Reporting inconsistencies (Table 1 p-values; 'paired t-tests' used for between-group comparisons) and an inter-assay cortisol CV of 15% further weaken the evidence, so evidence_weight is lowered from low to very-low.

claims.topic: Loudness normalisation standard (EBU R 128)
claims.finding: EBU Recommendation R 128 (version 5.0, November 2023) specifies that programme loudness, measured with the level-gated ITU-R BS.1770 method, be normalised to a target of -23.0 LUFS. A ±1.0 LU tolerance applies only where the target is not practically achievable (e.g. live programmes), and a ±0.2 LU measurement tolerance is allowed in quality-control workflows. It allows a deliberately lower target in special cases, which must be clearly indicated so the lower loudness is not compensated. It states that the true-peak level shall not exceed -1 dBTP during production, noting that maximum true-peak levels may be lower for some distribution systems and data-reduced (lossy) formats.
claims.finding_zh: 欧洲广播联盟R 128建议（2023年11月第5.0版）规定：节目整体响度按ITU-R BS.1770带门限方法测量，归一到−23.0 LUFS；只有在实际难以达到时（例如直播）才允许±1.0 LU的偏差，质量控制中允许±0.2 LU的测量误差。特殊情况下可有意采用更低的目标响度，但须明确标示，以免被重新调高补偿。制作阶段真峰值不得超过−1 dBTP；对某些分发系统和有损压缩格式，允许的真峰值可能需要更低。
claims.sample: Not applicable
claims.limitations: Broadcast standard for consistent loudness between programmes; says nothing about health or the listening level at the ear.
claims.app_implication: Calibrate every preset offline to -23 LUFS integrated (sleep presets deliberately lower, e.g. -28 LUFS, and labelled as such) with a -3 dBTP true-peak ceiling for lossy delivery, so switching presets causes no loudness jumps. When users stack layers, normalise or gain-compensate the summed mix: two equally loud uncorrelated layers are about 3 LU louder than either alone.

citation.authors: European Broadcasting Union (EBU)
citation.title: R 128: Loudness normalisation and permitted maximum level of audio signals

verification.checked_against: EBU official page (tech.ebu.ch/publications/r128: version 5.0, 21 November 2023) and the R 128 v5.0 PDF (r128v5_0.pdf, Geneva, November 2023, items g-v)
verification.problems: Citation and core content are accurate: -23.0 LUFS target; ±1.0 LU only where the target is not practically achievable (e.g. live); a deliberately lower target allowed in special cases if clearly indicated; level-gated BS.1770 measurement; true peak not above -1 dBTP. Imprecisions: the -1 dBTP limit applies 'during production (linear audio)', and R 128 adds that permitted maximum true-peak levels may be lower for some distribution systems and data-reduced formats. This matters because the app delivers lossy audio, and it supports its -3 dBTP choice. The ±0.2 LU QC measurement tolerance is omitted. app_implication error: normalising each preset/layer to -23 LUFS does not prevent loudness jumps when layers are added. Two equally loud uncorrelated layers sum to about +3 LU unless the summed mix is re-normalised or gain-compensated.

claims.topic: Safe listening dose limits (WHO-ITU H.870)
claims.finding: The WHO-ITU global standard for safe listening devices (H.870) defines a weekly sound allowance using the equal-energy principle: Mode 1 (adults) 1.6 Pa2h per 7 days, derived from 80 dBA for 40 h/week; Mode 2 (sensitive users such as children) 0.51 Pa2h, derived from 75 dBA for 40 h/week. Each 3 dB increase halves the allowed time (Mode 1 examples: 83 dB 20 h, 89 dB 5 h, 95 dB 75 min, 101 dB 18.75 min per week). Devices should track level and listening time, offer volume limiting and parental volume control, and give personalised warnings and cues for action.
claims.finding_zh: 世卫组织与国际电信联盟的安全聆听标准（H.870）按“等能量原则”设定每周声音配额：成人模式为每7天1.6 Pa²h（相当于80 dBA每周40小时）；敏感人群（如儿童）模式为0.51 Pa²h（75 dBA每周40小时）。音量每增加3 dB，允许时间减半（成人示例：83 dB每周20小时，89 dB 5小时，95 dB 75分钟，101 dB 18.75分钟）。设备应记录音量和时长、提供音量上限与家长控制，并给出个性化提醒。
claims.sample: Not applicable (based on occupational and leisure noise hearing-loss evidence)
claims.limitations: A web app cannot measure the actual level at the ear (depends on device volume and headphones); the standard targets device makers and concerns hearing damage, not sleep or wellbeing.
claims.app_implication: Show weekly headphone listening time, warn before long high-volume use, start at low gain, never auto-raise volume, and offer a sensitive/children mode with a lower in-app ceiling.

citation.authors: World Health Organization; International Telecommunication Union
citation.title: Safe listening devices and systems: a WHO-ITU standard

verification.checked_against: WHO IRIS record via DSpace REST API (handle 10665/280085: 'Safe listening devices and systems: a WHO-ITU standard', authors WHO and ITU, publisher WHO, issued 2019-02-08, ISBN 9789241515276) and full PDF (executive summary, Recommendations 1-3, Tables 1-2, glossary)

claims.topic: Listening to music for insomnia (Cochrane)
claims.finding: Cochrane review of 13 RCTs (N=1,007) in adults with sleep complaints. Participants listened to prerecorded music daily for 25-60 min (mean 36 min) over 3 days to 3 months; controls received no treatment or usual care. Music improved self-reported sleep quality (PSQI MD -2.79, 95% CI -3.86 to -1.72; 10 studies, 708 participants; moderate certainty; SMD -0.86, 95% CI -1.19 to -0.54). No clear effect on insomnia severity (MD -6.96, 95% CI -15.21 to 1.28; 2 studies, 63 participants; very low certainty). Low-certainty evidence that music may improve subjective sleep-onset latency, total sleep time and sleep efficiency (PSQI component scores; 3 studies, 197 participants). It may have no effect on perceived sleep interruption (MD -0.53, 95% CI -1.47 to 0.40; very low certainty). Three studies (136 participants) that measured sleep with polysomnography found music may not improve objective sleep-onset latency, total sleep time, sleep efficiency or sleep interruption. Researcher-selected music (MD -3.31) and participant choice among preselected playlists (MD -2.33) did not differ (P=0.40). The 4 trials that described their music used low tempo (52-85 bpm), stable dynamics and no strong rhythmic accentuation. None of the included studies reported adverse events.
claims.finding_zh: Cochrane综述纳入13项随机对照试验（1007名有睡眠困扰的成人）：每天听录制音乐25–60分钟（平均36分钟），持续3天至3个月；对照组为不干预或常规照护。音乐使自评睡眠质量改善（PSQI平均降低2.79分，95%CI −3.86至−1.72；10项研究、708人；中等确定性；标准化均差−0.86）。对失眠严重程度无明确作用（2项研究、63人；极低确定性）。低确定性证据显示，主观入睡时间、总睡眠时间和睡眠效率可能改善，但主观的睡眠中断可能没有改善（极低确定性）。3项用多导睡眠图客观测量的研究（136人）显示，音乐可能不改善客观睡眠指标。研究者选曲与从预选歌单中自选效果无差异（P=0.40）。描述了音乐特点的4项试验所用音乐为：慢速（52–85拍/分钟）、动态平稳、无强烈节奏重音。纳入研究均未报告不良事件。
claims.sample: 13 RCTs, 1,007 participants (PSQI analysis: 10 RCTs, 708 participants)
claims.limitations: Participants could not be blinded, so all trials are at high risk of performance bias. Mostly small trials. Controls received no treatment or usual care rather than an attention control. The benefits rest on self-report; the 3 polysomnography studies showed no objective improvement. Only 4 trials described their musical features.
claims.app_implication: Sleep-music preset: slow (about 50-85 bpm) or beatless, stable dynamics, no rhythmic accents; 30-45 min timer with a long fade-out. Copy: '坚持每晚聆听，可能改善你对睡眠质量的主观感受；不能替代就医'. Do not claim faster sleep onset, fewer awakenings or objectively better sleep.

citation.authors: Jespersen KV, Pando-Naude V, Koenig J, et al.
citation.title: Listening to music for insomnia in adults

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata + PubMed abstract + PMC full text HTML (PMC9400393: summary of findings table, results, included-study characteristics)
verification.problems: Metadata and every reported number confirmed: 13 RCTs with 1,007 participants; sessions of 25-60 min, mean 36; 3 days to 3 months; PSQI MD -2.79 [-3.86, -1.72], 10 studies, 708 participants, moderate certainty; SMD -0.86 [-1.19, -0.54]; ISI MD -6.96 [-15.21, 1.28], very low certainty; music-selection subgroup P=0.40; the 4 trials that described their music had 52-85 bpm, stable dynamics and no strong rhythmic accentuation; no adverse events reported. One omitted null: perceived sleep interruption, a primary outcome of the review, showed no effect (MD -0.53, 95% CI -1.47 to 0.40; 3 studies, 197 participants; very low certainty). The finding lists only the positive low-certainty subjective outcomes. The source hedges the objective (PSG) results as 'may not improve'.

claims.topic: Music interventions and stress: overall effect
claims.finding: Two multilevel (three-level) meta-analyses of 104 RCTs in adults (327 effect sizes, N=9,617) found that music interventions reduced physiological stress outcomes (61 studies, 197 effect sizes, N=3,188; d=0.380, 95% CI 0.296 to 0.465) and psychological stress outcomes such as state anxiety and nervousness (79 studies, 130 effect sizes, N=6,800; d=0.545, 95% CI 0.432 to 0.657). The interventions were mostly listening to pre-recorded music, plus some music therapy and live music, and controls were mostly care as usual or another intervention. Among physiological outcomes the effect was larger for heart rate (d=0.456) than for blood pressure (d=0.343) or stress hormones (d=0.349). Trim-and-fill imputed no missing studies, so publication bias was judged unlikely. Most trials were surgical or procedural; only 10 (physiological) and 12 (psychological) studies were in non-medical settings. Setting did not significantly moderate effects (non-medical d=0.523 physiological, d=0.694 psychological).
claims.finding_zh: 对104项成人随机对照试验（327个效应量，9617人）的两项多层元分析发现：音乐干预能降低生理压力指标（61项研究，197个效应量，3188人；d=0.380，95%CI 0.296–0.465），也能降低状态焦虑、紧张等心理压力指标（79项研究，130个效应量，6800人；d=0.545，95%CI 0.432–0.657）。这些干预多数是聆听预先录制的音乐，少数为音乐治疗或现场演奏；对照多为常规护理或其他干预。生理指标中，对心率的作用（d=0.456）大于血压（d=0.343）和应激激素（d=0.349）。剪补法没有补入缺失研究，作者认为存在发表偏倚的可能性不大。多数试验在手术或医疗操作场景中进行，非医疗场景的研究只有10项（生理）和12项（心理）；场景对效果没有显著影响（非医疗场景：生理d=0.523，心理d=0.694）。
claims.study_type: systematic review with two multilevel meta-analyses of RCTs
claims.sample: 104 RCTs, 327 effect sizes, 9,617 participants
claims.limitations: Pools music listening, music therapy and live music across many mostly clinical contexts. Music, outcomes and controls are heterogeneous (controls often care as usual), and participants cannot be blinded. The non-medical subgroup is small (10/12 studies), also includes chronically ill participants, and did not show smaller effects, so this review cannot settle the effect size for healthy everyday users. Meta-analyses restricted to healthy samples found smaller or non-significant effects: Panteleeva 2018 found self-report d=-0.30 and no physiological effect, and Adiasto 2022 found no significant effect on stress recovery.
claims.app_implication: Justifies offering calm music as a relaxation option with modest copy (e.g. '可能帮助你感觉放松一些'). Does not support claims such as 'treats anxiety' or 'lowers cortisol' for app users, because the physiological effects come mostly from patients in medical settings.

citation.authors: de Witte M, Spruit A, van Hooren S, et al.
citation.title: Effects of music interventions on stress-related outcomes: a systematic review and two meta-analyses

verification.checked_against: Crossref and PubMed metadata (PMID 31167611; online 2019, Health Psychol Rev 14(2):294-324, 2020); PubMed abstract; full publisher PDF (CC BY-NC-ND) from the UvA Pure repository: Methods, Results, Tables 1-3, Discussion and Limitations
verification.problems: All metadata and every number in finding and finding_zh match the source (104 RCTs, 327 ES, N=9,617; 61/197/N=3,188, d=0.380 [0.296-0.465]; 79/130/N=6,800, d=0.545 [0.432-0.657]; HR 0.456, BP 0.343, hormones 0.349; trim-and-fill imputed nothing; non-medical 10 and 12 studies). Problem in limitations: 'few non-medical studies, so effects for healthy everyday users may be smaller' reads as if this review pointed that way. In fact its own non-medical subgroup had numerically larger effects (d=0.523 physiological, d=0.694 psychological), setting was not a significant moderator, and the 'non-medical' category also included chronically ill participants doing music activities. The smaller-effect inference rests on other meta-analyses (Panteleeva 2018, Adiasto 2022). The finding also left out this setting null, the intervention mix (mostly pre-recorded listening, some music therapy and live music) and the comparators (mostly care as usual). The app_implication 'rules out lowers cortisol' could be misread: this review found a significant pooled hormone effect (d=0.349), but in mostly clinical samples.

claims.topic: WHO night-time and leisure noise guideline levels
claims.finding: The WHO Environmental Noise Guidelines for the European Region strongly recommend reducing night-time noise below 45 dB Lnight for road traffic, 44 dB Lnight for railway and 40 dB Lnight for aircraft, because night noise above these levels is associated with adverse effects on sleep. The sleep-disturbance evidence behind these levels was rated moderate quality. The matching strong recommendations for average exposure are 53, 54 and 45 dB Lden. No night-time recommendation was made for wind turbines because the evidence quality was too low. For leisure noise, including loud music through personal listening devices, WHO conditionally recommends reducing the yearly average from all leisure sources combined to 70 dB LAeq,24h. Because direct evidence on leisure noise and hearing loss was of insufficient quality, this level was derived from workplace hearing-loss prevention knowledge.
claims.finding_zh: 世卫组织《欧洲区域环境噪声指南》强烈建议：夜间道路交通噪声应低于45 dB Lnight，铁路低于44 dB，航空低于40 dB，因为高于这些水平的夜间噪声与睡眠受损有关；支持这些夜间限值的睡眠干扰证据质量被评为“中等”。对应的昼-晚-夜加权平均声级（Lden）强烈建议值分别为53、54、45 dB。风电噪声因夜间证据质量太低，未给出夜间建议。对包括用个人听音设备听大声音乐在内的娱乐性噪声，有条件地建议所有来源合计的年平均暴露不超过70 dB LAeq,24h；由于娱乐噪声与听力损失的直接证据质量不足，这一数值是参照职场听力保护的知识推导出来的。
claims.study_type: WHO guideline (GRADE-based, adapted for observational exposure studies)
claims.sample: Guideline Development Group synthesis of 8 systematic reviews of health-outcome evidence plus 1 review of interventions
claims.limitations: Lnight and Lden are yearly-average outdoor levels at the most exposed façade, set for population noise policy on transport sources; they are not limits for sound a person chooses to play in a bedroom. For aircraft, WHO notes that the 40 dB Lnight level still far exceeds its 3% highly-sleep-disturbed benchmark; it was not set lower only because reliable data below it were lacking. The leisure-noise recommendation is conditional and extrapolated from occupational hearing-loss knowledge; direct evidence was rated very low quality or absent.
claims.app_implication: Treat sleep audio as added night-time exposure: as quiet as masking allows, timers and fade-outs by default, never encourage loud playback, and count app listening toward the WHO-ITU weekly sound allowance.

citation.authors: World Health Organization Regional Office for Europe
citation.title: Environmental noise guidelines for the European Region
citation.venue: WHO Regional Office for Europe, Copenhagen

verification.checked_against: WHO IRIS record via DSpace REST API (handle 10665/279952: 'Environmental noise guidelines for the European Region', WHO Regional Office for Europe, issued 2018, ISBN 9789289053563) and full guideline PDF (executive summary recommendation tables, sections 3.1-3.5, glossary)
verification.problems: All numbers and wording verified against the guideline: strong recommendations of 45/44/40 dB Lnight (road/rail/aircraft) and 53/54/45 dB Lden; no wind-turbine Lnight recommendation because the evidence quality was too low; conditional 70 dB LAeq,24h yearly average for all leisure sources combined, explicitly including personal listening devices. Citation, handle and year are correct. Problems: (1) evidence_weight 'high' overstates the evidence. WHO rated the sleep-disturbance evidence behind the 45/44/40 dB Lnight levels as moderate quality. It rated direct leisure-noise/hearing evidence as very low quality or absent, and derived the 70 dB value from workplace hearing-loss knowledge. (2) finding_zh calls Lden a '全天平均值'; it is a day-evening-night-weighted level, not a plain 24-h average. (3) The limitation 'based on hearing-loss evidence' is imprecise; the value was extrapolated from occupational data. (4) app_implication's 'daily sound dose' matches neither WHO metric: here it is a yearly LAeq,24h, and in H.870 a weekly allowance.

claims.topic: Does heart rate entrain to musical tempo?
claims.finding: Factorial experiment with 36 listeners of varying musical backgrounds. On each trial, the tempo of ambient instrumental music with a salient rhythm was set relative to the listener's current heart rate in a 2x2x2 design: faster vs slower, by 3% vs 30%, finger tapping vs still listening. Listeners also reported felt arousal and valence. There was little evidence of entrainment. In general, heart rate neither aligned with the target tempo (entrainment proper) nor changed in its direction (entrainment tendencies). Instead, heart rate and felt arousal showed a similar small increase regardless of the direction and size of the tempo change. The authors consider this consistent with a general arousal effect of musical rhythm.
claims.finding_zh: 36名音乐背景各异的听者参加实验。每一轮把带明显节奏的氛围器乐速度设定为比其当时心率快或慢3%或30%，并比较用手指打拍与静听（2×2×2设计）；听者同时评价主观唤醒和愉悦度。结果几乎没有“节律同步”的证据：总体上，心率既没有与音乐速度对齐，也没有朝目标速度的方向变化。无论速度加快还是放慢、幅度大还是小，心率和主观唤醒都出现了相似的小幅上升，作者认为这更符合“音乐节奏带来一般性唤醒”的解释。
claims.study_type: 2x2x2 factorial listening experiment (repeated trials per listener)
claims.sample: n=36 listeners
claims.limitations: Single small experiment. One musical style (ambient instrumental music with a salient rhythm) in a controlled experimental setting. Trial durations and full statistics were not checked because the full text is paywalled. The abstract describes no non-rhythmic or silent comparison, so the small rise in arousal cannot be pinned specifically on rhythm. The study does not exclude other ways slow music might relax listeners.
claims.app_implication: Never market 'music tempo syncs or slows your heart'. Do not build heart-rate-following tempo, since it produced no entrainment here. As a precaution, keep rhythmic pulse minimal in relaxation and sleep content: rhythmic music was followed by a small rise in heart rate and felt arousal whatever the tempo.

citation.authors: Juslin PN, Harmat L, Barradas G, et al.
citation.title: Rhythmic entrainment of heart rate as a mechanism for musical emotion induction: A plausible hypothesis in need of evidence?

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata + the publisher's abstract deposited in Crossref (matches the SAGE listing). Full text not accessible: SAGE is paywalled and the Salford repository manuscript is behind a Cloudflare block (403); no archived copy.
verification.problems: Metadata is correct: Psychology of Music 54(1):42-62, issue Jan 2026, online 17 Dec 2024; authors Juslin, Harmat, Barradas, Omstedt, Redtzer. Every design detail and result in the finding matches the abstract. Issues: (1) The limitations assert 'short trials' and a 'laboratory setting'. Neither is stated in the abstract and neither could be checked in the full text, so they are removed or softened. (2) The finding drops the abstract's 'In general' qualifier on the entrainment null. (3) finding_zh '设定为每个人当时心率的±3%或±30%' is ambiguous (it can be read as 3% of heart rate). Tempo was set 3% or 30% faster or slower than the listener's current heart rate. (4) The app_implication states 'rhythm itself can raise arousal' as fact. The abstract reports a small rise in HR and arousal across all conditions, all of which used rhythmic music, and the authors interpret it as a general arousal effect of rhythm. The abstract describes no non-rhythmic or silent comparison. (5) study_type 'within-subject … laboratory' is not stated explicitly; the abstract only says tempo was set per trial relative to each listener's heart rate.

claims.topic: Binaural beats and isochronic tones during oral surgery (RCT, null on anxiety)
claims.finding: RCT of 90 patients having impacted mandibular third-molar surgery, randomized equally to binaural beats, isochronic tones or no intraoperative auditory stimulation: no significant between-group differences in pre- or postoperative anxiety questionnaires (MDAS, DFS, STAI-S, VAS). Only isolated physiological differences appeared: mean systolic blood pressure at incision was lowest in the binaural group (p=0.041), and mean respiratory rate at anaesthesia was lowest in the isochronic group (p=0.015). 78.3% of stimulated patients said they would prefer auditory stimulation in future dental treatments. The authors conclude that binaural beats and isochronic tones have a limited effect on dental anxiety and do not support a definitive anxiolytic benefit.
claims.finding_zh: 随机对照试验：90名接受阻生下颌第三磨牙手术的患者平均分为双耳节拍组、等时音组和术中无声音刺激组。三组术前、术后焦虑量表（MDAS、DFS、STAI-S、VAS）得分均无显著差异。仅有个别生理指标出现组间差异：切开时双耳节拍组平均收缩压最低（p=0.041），麻醉时等时音组平均呼吸频率最低（p=0.015）。接受声音刺激的患者中78.3%表示今后的牙科治疗中更愿意接受声音刺激。作者认为，双耳节拍和等时音减轻牙科焦虑的作用有限，不支持其有明确的抗焦虑效果。
claims.sample: n=90 (30 per arm)
claims.limitations: Probably single-centre (both authors are from one university dental faculty; not stated in the abstract, and no registry entry found). Dental-surgery context. No active non-beat audio control. Five physiological parameters were compared at eight surgical stages, so the isolated p-values may be chance. Published online in July 2026 ahead of issue assignment; full text not reviewed.
claims.app_implication: Isochronic tones and binaural beats are not adopted. Because acceptability is high, any future experimental option must be clearly labelled as an experience with no anxiety-relief claim.

citation.authors: Akkurt O, Ekici Ö
citation.title: Effect of binaural beats and isochronic tones on anxiety during impacted mandibular third molar surgery: a randomized controlled trial
citation.venue: International Journal of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata + PubMed abstract (PMID 42471303; Int J Oral Maxillofac Surg, online ahead of print 18 Jul 2026). Full text paywalled (IJOMS and ScienceDirect blocked). ClinicalTrials.gov searched; no registration found.
verification.problems: Metadata, design and all numbers match the abstract: 90 patients assigned equally to BB, IT and no-stimulation arms; no between-group differences on MDAS, DFS, STAI-S or VAS; SBP at incision P=0.041; respiratory rate at anaesthesia P=0.015; 78.3% preference. The two issues are minor. (1) 'Single centre' is not stated in the abstract. It is inferred from both authors sharing one dental faculty, and no registry entry was found, so it is now flagged as probable. (2) finding_zh '以后还愿意使用' softens the abstract's 'would prefer auditory stimulation in future dental treatments'; made precise. Added the authors' own conclusion that BB and IT have a limited effect and do not support a definitive anxiolytic benefit.

claims.topic: Session duration and music selection (umbrella review, preoperative anxiety)
claims.finding: PROSPERO-registered umbrella review of 6 systematic reviews (AMSTAR 2: 1 high, 4 moderate, 1 low quality) covering 40 primary studies in adults awaiting surgery or invasive procedures, with updated meta-analyses of the primary studies (RCTs plus non-randomized controlled trials). In 19 studies using STAI-S, music lowered preoperative anxiety (MD -5.20 points, 95% CI -6.32 to -4.07, I2=49%). Restricting to adequately randomized trials gave MD -4.95 (95% CI -6.50 to -3.41; 7 studies). Duration subgroups differed (p<0.01): longer than 20 min MD -7.25 (95% CI -9.31 to -5.20; 7 studies), 20 min -4.11 (-4.32 to -3.91; 7), under 20 min -2.95 (-4.91 to -0.98; 4). On VAS-A the duration difference was not significant (p=0.53). No significant difference was found between researcher-selected and patient-selected music (STAI-S p=0.28; VAS-A p=0.17), and in most studies 'patient-selected' meant choosing from a researcher-provided list. On VAS-A, two sessions reduced anxiety more than one (p<0.01; only 2 two-session studies). The most common protocol was a single 20-min headphone session. Separately, the Discussion cites an RCT that was not in the analysis (McClurkin & Smith 2016, self-selected music before ambulatory surgery), which found no significant difference between 15- and 30-min sessions.
claims.finding_zh: 这项伞状综述在PROSPERO注册，纳入6篇系统综述（AMSTAR 2评级：1篇高质量、4篇中等、1篇低质量），覆盖40项原始研究，对象是等待手术或有创操作的成人；作者对原始研究（含随机与非随机对照试验）重新做了元分析。19项使用STAI-S量表的研究显示，术前听音乐使焦虑平均降低5.20分（95%CI −6.32至−4.07，I²=49%）；只纳入随机化充分的试验时，平均降低4.95分（95%CI −6.50至−3.41；7项研究）。按时长分组：超过20分钟降低7.25分（7项研究），20分钟降低4.11分（7项），不足20分钟降低2.95分（4项），组间p<0.01；但用视觉模拟量表（VAS-A）评估时，时长差异不显著（p=0.53）。研究者选曲与患者选曲之间未发现显著差异（STAI-S p=0.28；VAS-A p=0.17），而且多数研究中的“患者选曲”是指从研究者提供的曲目中挑选。VAS-A分析中，两次聆听比一次降低更多（p<0.01，但两次组只有2项研究）。最常见方案是一次20分钟、戴耳机。另外，作者在讨论中引用了一项未纳入本分析的随机试验（McClurkin与Smith 2016，门诊手术前聆听自选音乐），发现15分钟与30分钟效果没有显著差别。
claims.study_type: umbrella review with updated meta-analysis of primary studies
claims.sample: 6 systematic reviews, 40 primary studies (19 with STAI-S: 12 RCTs and 7 non-randomized controlled trials)
claims.limitations: Participants were preoperative adult patients rather than general users. Duration and selection subgroups are non-randomized, cross-study comparisons with 4–15 studies per subgroup and are inconsistent across scales (STAI-S vs VAS-A); the authors warn they may be chance findings. 7 of 19 STAI-S studies were non-randomized, and only 1 of 6 reviews was high quality. Intervention reporting was poor (tempo reported in only 7 studies), and primary studies were not searched beyond the included reviews.
claims.app_implication: Default 'listen to relax' session = 20 min, the most commonly studied protocol, with 10 and 30 min options. Do not present 'longer is better' as a dose-response: it is a cross-study association in surgical patients. Curated presets are reasonable: no significant difference was found between researcher- and patient-selected music, and most 'patient-selected' arms chose from curated lists.

citation.authors: Yang KL, Detroyer E, Niu MM, et al.
citation.title: Music intervention as a strategy to reduce preoperative anxiety: an umbrella review

verification.checked_against: Crossref and PubMed metadata (PMID 40836211, PMC12366122, BMC Anesthesiol 25:410); PMC full text: Methods, Results, Table 2 (all subgroup analyses), Discussion, and reference list (ref 75 checked against the included-study range, refs 32-71)
verification.problems: Metadata and all quoted numbers match the full text (6 SRs, AMSTAR 2 1/4/1; 40 primary studies; STAI-S MD -5.20 [-6.32, -4.07], I2=49%, 19 studies; duration subgroups and p<0.01; VAS-A p=0.53; selection p=0.28; 20-min single headphone session most common). Factual error: 'an included RCT found no difference between 15- and 30-min sessions' is wrong. That RCT is ref 75 (McClurkin & Smith 2016, J Perianesth Nurs; self-selected music, ambulatory surgery), cited only in the Discussion; it is not among the included primary studies (refs 32-71). 'Did not differ' overstates a non-significant cross-study comparison: researcher-selected MD -6.36 (4 studies) vs patient-selected -4.96 (15 studies). In most studies 'patient-selected' meant choosing from a researcher list. Omitted: the randomized-only sensitivity analysis (MD -4.95, 7 studies) and the VAS-A finding that two sessions beat one (p<0.01; 2 studies). Evidence weight is too high for this claim, whose actionable content (duration, selection) rests on small cross-study subgroups. The authors say these may be chance findings; only 1 of 6 reviews was high quality, and 7 of 19 STAI-S studies were non-randomized.

claims.topic: Binaural beats for perioperative anxiety (recent meta-analysis, contradicting our non-adoption)
claims.finding: Meta-analysis of 15 RCTs in surgical patients. Compared with blank audio, binaural-beat audio reduced perioperative anxiety (14 trials, n=1,047; SMD -1.38, 95% CI -1.89 to -0.87; I2=91.6%) and postoperative pain (5 trials, n=433; SMD -0.61, 95% CI -1.03 to -0.19). Compared with non-binaural audio, binaural beats also reduced anxiety (8 trials, n=598; SMD -1.01, 95% CI -1.99 to -0.03; I2=95.4%) and pain (3 trials, n=265; SMD -0.52, 95% CI -0.77 to -0.28).
claims.finding_zh: 对15项手术患者随机对照试验的元分析：与空白音频相比，双耳节拍音频降低围术期焦虑（14项试验，1047人；SMD −1.38，95%CI −1.89至−0.87；I²=91.6%）和术后疼痛（SMD −0.61）。与不含双耳节拍的音频相比，焦虑也更低（8项，598人；SMD −1.01，95%CI −1.99至−0.03；I²=95.4%），疼痛更低（3项，265人；SMD −0.52）。
claims.study_type: systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs
claims.sample: 15 RCTs (anxiety vs blank audio: 14 trials, 1,047 patients)
claims.limitations: Extreme heterogeneity (I2 about 92–95%); the confidence interval vs non-binaural audio barely excludes zero; perioperative populations and small trials; several P-values in the abstract appear to be heterogeneity tests; no certainty grading reported in the abstract.
claims.app_implication: Shown as the strongest current contradicting evidence: binaural beats are labelled 待观察 rather than debunked, and the decision is revisited if a pre-registered trial against matched non-beat audio replicates the effect.

citation.authors: Xiong J, Jiang X, Cai B, et al.
citation.title: Binaural beats for perioperative anxiety and pain: A systematic review and meta-analysis

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata (Complement Ther Med 2025;95:103299; 6 authors) + PubMed abstract (PMID 41176178, Epub 30 Oct 2025). Every trial count, n, SMD, 95% CI and I² in the finding and finding_zh matches the abstract. The article is gold OA per OpenAlex, but ScienceDirect blocked full-text access, so the checks rest on the abstract. The limitation that several abstract P-values look like heterogeneity tests is supported (e.g., SBP P=0.3041 with a CI excluding zero; DBP P=0.0334 with a CI including zero).

claims.topic: Chinese Five-Element Music (五行音乐): what the trials can and cannot show
claims.finding: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 18 RCTs (Web of Science, PubMed, CNKI, Wanfang, CQVIP; 1,463 participants per the review's Table 1). Participants were adults aged 50 or over (the authors' definition of older adults; most trial mean ages 50-65) with depression and/or anxiety, mostly patients with a specific illness. In 12 trials, Chinese Five-Element Music (CFEM) was added to care that the control group also received (e.g. progressive muscle relaxation + CFEM vs progressive muscle relaxation; usual nursing + CFEM vs usual nursing). In 4, the music arm also got Baduanjin, physical activity, Tai Chi or ear acupressure. One control arm got exercise plus Chinese medicine, and only one small trial used Western music as the control. Music was usually 20-30 min once or twice daily, most often for 4 weeks (range 3 days to 8 weeks). Pooled random-effects results vs control: HAMD MD -3.63 (95% CI -4.97 to -2.30; 8 RCTs, n=657); HAMA MD -3.89 (-5.80 to -1.97; 4 RCTs, n=230); SDS MD -6.69 (-8.32 to -5.07; 9 RCTs); SAS MD -6.84 (-10.76 to -2.92; 5 RCTs, I2=90%); PSQI MD -1.86 (-2.54 to -1.17; only 2 RCTs, n=150). Quality of life showed no significant difference (MD -0.58, 95% CI -15.65 to 14.48; 2 RCTs, n=172, I2=89%). Participant and personnel blinding was unclear in every trial, and 2 trials allocated patients by admission order. The authors rated certainty (GRADE) moderate for HAMD, SDS and PSQI, low for HAMA, SAS and response rate, and very low for quality of life.
claims.finding_zh: 系统综述与元分析纳入18项随机对照试验（检索Web of Science、PubMed、知网、万方、维普；按文中表1合计1463人），对象为50岁及以上（作者对“老年人”的定义，多数试验平均年龄50–65岁）、伴抑郁和/或焦虑的人，多为患有某种疾病的病人。其中12项是在对照组同样接受的照护之上加用五行音乐（如渐进性肌肉放松+五行音乐 对 渐进性肌肉放松；常规护理+五行音乐 对 常规护理）；4项试验组还额外加了八段锦、体力活动、太极或耳穴压豆；1项对照组为运动加中药；只有1项小试验用西方音乐作对照。音乐通常每次20–30分钟、每天1–2次，最常见疗程4周（3天至8周不等）。与对照相比的合并结果：HAMD降低3.63分（95%CI −4.97至−2.30；8项，657人），HAMA降低3.89分（−5.80至−1.97；4项，230人），SDS降低6.69分（−8.32至−5.07；9项），SAS降低6.84分（−10.76至−2.92；5项，异质性I²=90%），PSQI降低1.86分（−2.54至−1.17；仅2项，150人）；生活质量无显著差异（MD −0.58，95%CI −15.65至14.48；2项，172人，I²=89%）。所有试验对受试者和实施者的盲法都不清楚，2项按入院顺序分组。作者的GRADE证据确定性评级：HAMD、SDS、PSQI为中等，HAMA、SAS和总有效率为低，生活质量为极低。
claims.study_type: systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs
claims.sample: 18 RCTs, 1,463 participants (20-63 per arm)
claims.limitations: Unblinded add-on designs against usual care, with rating-scale outcomes. The pooled effects reflect extra attention, time and co-interventions as much as the music. No trial isolated five-element theory (tone-organ matching); the one music-vs-music comparison was small. Almost all trials were Chinese-language studies from CNKI/Wanfang; grey literature was excluded and there was no long-term follow-up. PSQI and quality of life each rest on two trials. The review also has reporting errors: 'SAD' for SDS in the abstract, SAS and SDS mixed up in the text, and outcome citations that do not match Table 1 (e.g. the PSQI trials). This lowers confidence further.
claims.app_implication: Chinese pentatonic modes (宫商角徵羽) are offered as a cultural aesthetic. No 五行/脏腑 matching, no 'organ tone' therapy, and no claim that the music treats depression, anxiety or insomnia.

citation.authors: Li J, Chen K, Wang IT, et al.
citation.title: The effectiveness of the Chinese Five-Element Music intervention on older adults with depression and anxiety disorder: A systematic review and meta-analysis

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; PubMed abstract (PMID 41054154); PMC full text (PMC12499668) incl. Table 1, risk-of-bias section and limitations; supplementary GRADE summary-of-findings table (https://links.lww.com/MD/Q81)
verification.problems: Metadata is correct (Li J, Chen K, Wang IT, Beh WF; Medicine 2025;104(40):e44764). The pooled HAMD, HAMA, PSQI and QoL numbers match. (1) 'No effect on quality of life' overstates a null. The paper reports no significant difference from only 2 RCTs (n=172), with a 95% CI of -15.65 to 14.48 and I2=89%, so neither benefit nor harm is excluded; zh '生活质量无差异' has the same problem. (2) Population: inclusion was age 50 or over, most trial mean ages were 50-65, and most trials enrolled patients with one specific illness, so 'older adults with depression or anxiety' needs qualifying. (3) Design: in 12 of 18 trials the co-intervention (PMR, nursing care, TCM) was given to both arms, i.e. an add-on design. Only 4 trials gave extra components (Baduanjin, physical activity, Tai Chi, ear acupressure) to the music arm alone, so 'usually combined with other therapies vs conventional care' misdescribes the comparison. (4) The limitations say there was no ordinary-music control, but one trial (Wang 2011, n=45) used Western music plus conventional therapy as its control. (5) 'Mostly single-centre trials' is not stated in the paper; it says the trials were mostly Chinese-language, from CNKI/Wanfang. (6) Table 1 arms range from 20 to 63 participants (the text says 20-60); the total is 1,463. (7) Sessions were once or twice daily, most often for 4 weeks (range 3 days to 8 weeks). The claim omits that PSQI pooled only 2 RCTs (n=150). (8) Participant and personnel blinding was unclear in every trial, not just 'often', and 2 trials allocated patients by admission order. The authors' GRADE ratings: moderate for HAMD, SDS and PSQI; low for HAMA, SAS and ORR; very low for QoL.

claims.topic: Acoustic features of music people use for sleep
claims.finding: Analysis of 225,626 tracks from Spotify sleep playlists (130,150 unique tracks compared with 3,706,388 general-music tracks): sleep music was much softer (mean loudness -19.78 vs -9.6 dB; d=-1.25), lower in energy (d=-1.46), more acoustic (d=1.20) and more instrumental (d=1.10), lower in valence (d=-0.93), and only modestly slower (mean tempo 104.93 vs 120.07 BPM; d=-0.47). Sleep music clustered into six subgroups, three of which contained popular tracks that were faster, louder and more energetic than average sleep music.
claims.finding_zh: 分析Spotify睡眠歌单中的225,626首曲目（其中130,150首与370万首普通音乐比较）：睡眠音乐明显更轻（平均响度−19.78对−9.6 dB；d=−1.25）、能量更低（d=−1.46）、更多原声乐器（d=1.20）和纯器乐（d=1.10）、情绪效价更低（d=−0.93），速度只是略慢（平均104.9对120.1拍/分钟；d=−0.47）。睡眠音乐可分为六类，其中三类是比一般睡眠音乐更快、更响、更有活力的流行曲。
claims.study_type: observational big-data analysis of audio features
claims.sample: 225,626 sleep-playlist tracks (130,150 unique analysed) vs 3,706,388 general tracks
claims.limitations: Describes what people choose, not what improves sleep; relies on proprietary Spotify features (algorithmic tempo can be halved or doubled); playlist inclusion is not proof of use.
claims.app_implication: Sleep presets: low loudness and energy, acoustic-like timbres, no lyrics; offer several distinct presets because individual preferences vary widely, rather than one 'optimal' track.

citation.authors: Scarratt RJ, Heggli OA, Vuust P, et al.
citation.title: The audio features of sleep music: Universal and subgroup characteristics

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata + PubMed abstract + Europe PMC full text (PMC9847986: Methods, Table 3, subgroup/cluster results, Discussion)

claims.topic: Do binaural beats entrain brain oscillations? (EEG systematic review)
claims.finding: Systematic review of 14 EEG studies of binaural-beat stimulation: 5 reported results consistent with the brainwave-entrainment hypothesis, 8 reported contradictory results and 1 mixed results. Studies were highly heterogeneous in stimulation (4 embedded beats in pink noise, 10 used pure tones), design and EEG analysis. The review notes that binaural beats require each tone to reach one ear (headphones), carrier frequencies below about 1000 Hz (best perceived near 400 Hz) and frequency differences up to about 30 Hz.
claims.finding_zh: 对14项脑电研究的系统综述：5项结果支持“脑波同步”假说，8项结果相反，1项结果混合。各研究在刺激方式（4项把节拍嵌在粉红噪声中，10项用纯音）、设计和脑电分析上差异很大。综述指出，双耳节拍需要戴耳机让两耳分别接收不同频率，载波频率需低于约1000 Hz（约400 Hz最易感知），两耳频差上限约30 Hz。
claims.sample: 14 studies
claims.limitations: Small heterogeneous studies, no meta-analysis; EEG changes alone would not establish psychological benefit.
claims.app_implication: Ban 'brainwave entrainment' and alpha/theta-wave language in all copy; any future experimental binaural option must require headphones, use a carrier near 400 Hz and carry no claims.

citation.authors: Ingendoh RM, Posny ES, Heine A
citation.title: Binaural beats to entrain the brain? A systematic review of the effects of binaural beat stimulation on brain oscillatory activity, and the implications for psychological research and intervention

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata + PubMed abstract (PMID 37205669) + open-access full text (PMC10198548) via Europe PMC. Confirmed: 14 studies; 5 consistent with entrainment, 8 no entrainment, 1 mixed; 'Four studies embedded the binaural beats in pink noise, while ten studies presented pure binaural beats'; tones 'typically presented via headphones' so each frequency reaches one ear only; carriers at most 1000 Hz, best perceived around 400 Hz; maximum difference around 30 Hz; heterogeneity judged too great for a meta-analysis.

claims.topic: Music listening for stress recovery in healthy adults (null result)
claims.finding: Pre-registered systematic review and meta-analysis of 14 controlled experiments (random assignment required; quasi-experiments with a control group were also eligible) in 706 healthy adults, yielding 90 effect sizes. After an acute laboratory stressor, participants listened to music or a control condition (silence or another auditory stimulus such as white noise or an audiobook). The pooled effect of music on stress recovery was not significant (g=0.15, 95% CI -0.21 to 0.52, p=0.374; random-effects meta-regression with robust variance estimation), and heterogeneity was high (I2=89%). Omnibus moderator tests suggested that effects varied by genre, who selected the music, tempo and outcome type. However, nearly all subgroup estimates were non-significant: music at or below 80 bpm (g=0.084, 95% CI -0.06 to 0.23; 2 studies), experimenter-selected music (g=0.030, 95% CI -0.33 to 0.45), self-selected music (g=0.336, 95% CI -0.29 to 0.96), physiological outcomes (g=0.135) and psychological outcomes (g=0.298, 95% CI -0.11 to 0.71). The only significant estimates (pop, jazz, and choosing from an experimenter-made list) each came from a single study. Instrumental and lyrical music did not differ, and listening duration (2–45 min) did not moderate effects. The authors concluded that no definite conclusions can yet be drawn.
claims.finding_zh: 一项预注册的系统综述与元分析纳入14项对照实验（要求随机分组，带对照组的准实验也可纳入；706名健康成人，90个效应量）：参与者在实验室急性压力之后听音乐，或处于对照条件（安静，或白噪音、有声书等其他声音）。音乐对压力恢复的合并效应不显著（g=0.15，95%CI −0.21至0.52，p=0.374），研究间差异很大（I²=89%）。总体调节检验提示，效果可能随曲风、由谁选曲、速度和结局类型而不同，但几乎所有亚组估计都不显著，包括≤80拍/分钟的音乐（g=0.084，95%CI −0.06至0.23，仅2项研究）、研究者选曲（g=0.030）、自选音乐（g=0.336，95%CI −0.29至0.96）、生理指标（g=0.135）和心理指标（g=0.298）；仅有的几个显著亚组（流行乐、爵士乐、从研究者清单中自选）各自只来自1项研究。纯器乐与有歌词音乐没有差别，聆听时长（2–45分钟）也不影响效果。作者认为目前还不能得出明确结论。
claims.study_type: pre-registered systematic review and meta-analysis of controlled experiments (robust variance estimation)
claims.sample: 14 experiments (90 effect sizes), 706 healthy adults
claims.limitations: Only 14 small experiments, with high heterogeneity (I2≈89%). The pooled CI (-0.21 to 0.52) is compatible with no effect or a small-to-moderate benefit, so this is absence of evidence rather than evidence of no effect. All studies were rated 'some concerns' on RoB 2, and many moderator levels rest on 1–2 studies. Exposures were short (2–45 min) and followed acute lab stressors. Some control conditions were themselves sounds (white noise, audiobooks). In an exploratory analysis with relaxed quality criteria, the 7 higher-quality studies showed a small significant effect (g=0.178, 95% CI 0.00 to 0.35).
claims.app_implication: Honest copy for healthy users: music after a stressful moment may feel pleasant, but it has not been shown to speed recovery more than quiet rest. The evidence is imprecise, so a small benefit is not ruled out. A 'silence' option is presented as an equally valid choice.

citation.authors: Adiasto K, Beckers DGJ, van Hooff MLM, et al.
citation.title: Music listening and stress recovery in healthy individuals: A systematic review with meta-analysis of experimental studies

verification.checked_against: Crossref and PubMed metadata (PMID 35714120, PMC9205498); PMC full text: Methods (eligibility, RoB 2), Results (overall effect, moderator sections), Table 3 (all moderator levels), Appendix B (exploratory quality analysis), Limitations
verification.problems: Metadata, N=706, 14 studies, pooled g=0.15 (95% CI -0.21 to 0.52, p=0.374) and the three quoted subgroup estimates are correct. 'Subgroups were all non-significant' (zh: 所有亚组均不显著) is false. Omnibus moderator tests were significant for genre (QM(4)=27.19), selection (QM(2)=19.13), tempo (QM(5)=43.66) and outcome type (QM(2)=164.22), all p<.001. Three subgroup estimates were significant: pop g=0.317 (p=.025), jazz g=0.137 (p=.049) and pseudo-self-selected g=0.377 (p=.004), though each came from a single study. The abstract itself says effects 'seemed to vary depending on' genre, selection, tempo and outcome type. The ≤80 bpm estimate rests on only 2 studies. Quasi-experiments with a control group were eligible, so 'randomized' needs qualifying. The heterogeneity figure was not given (I2=89%). Evidence weight is too high: 14 small studies, I2≈89%, a pooled CI compatible with no effect or a moderate benefit, and every study rated 'some concerns' on RoB 2. An exploratory analysis also found a small significant effect in the 7 higher-quality studies (g=0.178, 95% CI 0.00 to 0.35, p=.046), so the null is imprecise rather than evidence of no effect.

claims.topic: Music for sleep in adults without a diagnosed sleep disorder
claims.finding: Systematic review of 22 articles (1,514 participants) on music-based interventions in adults without a formally diagnosed sleep disorder. Per the registered protocol, this can include people who report sleep problems and people with medical or psychological conditions. Meta-analysis of 6 studies (424 participants) found no significant improvement in sleep quality when music was added to standard care, compared with standard care alone (MD -0.80, 95% CI -2.15 to 0.54; low-quality evidence). A subgroup of 3 studies with interventions lasting at least 3 weeks showed improvement (MD -2.09, 95% CI -3.84 to -0.34). No difference in sleep-onset latency (SMD -0.32, 95% CI -0.88 to 0.25; 4 studies; very low quality) or sleep efficiency (SMD -0.59, 95% CI -3.15 to 1.97; 2 studies; very low quality). Effects on anxiety, depression and quality of life were mixed.
claims.finding_zh: 针对没有确诊睡眠障碍成人的系统综述（22篇文献，1514人；按注册方案，也包括自述有睡眠问题或患有躯体、心理疾病的人）：6项研究（424人）的元分析显示，在常规照护基础上加音乐，与单纯常规照护相比，睡眠质量无显著改善（平均差−0.80，95%CI −2.15至0.54；证据质量低）。干预持续至少3周的3项研究亚组显示有改善（−2.09，95%CI −3.84至−0.34）。入睡时间（4项研究）和睡眠效率（2项研究）无差异（证据质量极低）。对焦虑、抑郁和生活质量的作用结果不一。
claims.sample: 22 articles, 1,514 participants; main meta-analysis 6 studies, 424 participants
claims.limitations: Few, heterogeneous studies. The 3-week subgroup rests on 3 studies and compares across trials, not within randomized groups. Certainty is low to very low. The comparator was standard care, not an attention or placebo control. The population is mixed, not specifically good sleepers. Only the abstract and the PROSPERO protocol were checked; the full text was paywalled and the repository copy embargoed.
claims.app_implication: For users without a diagnosed sleep disorder, do not promise better sleep from sleep music; present it as an optional wind-down ritual. If duration is mentioned, say only that a possible benefit appeared in a small subgroup of 3 studies that lasted 3 weeks or more.

citation.authors: Tang YW, Teoh SL, Yeo JHH, et al.
citation.title: Music-based intervention for improving sleep quality of adults without sleep disorder: a systematic review and meta-analysis

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata + PubMed abstract + PROSPERO record CRD42018081193 (eligibility criteria). Full text not read: Taylor & Francis returned 403 and the University of Lincoln repository file is embargoed.
verification.problems: Metadata and all numbers in the abstract confirmed (Behav Sleep Med 20(2):241-259; epub 2021, issue 2022). (1) The app_implication targets 'good sleepers', but the registered population is adults without a formally diagnosed chronic sleep disorder. The protocol explicitly includes people who report sleep problems or disturbances and people with medical or psychological conditions. (2) 'State that any benefit appeared only with 3 or more weeks of regular use' turns a subgroup of 3 studies into a general rule. (3) Minor omissions: the finding leaves out the sleep-efficiency estimate and that music was added to standard care. Details beyond the abstract could not be checked.

claims.topic: White, pink and multi-audio stimulation and sleep
