claims.finding: Systematic review of 34 studies in adults (1,103 participants): positive sleep findings in 6 of 18 white-noise studies (33%), 9 of 11 pink-noise studies (81.9%) and 4 of 6 multi-audio studies (66.7%); the 'pink noise' category also included nature and ocean sounds. Only 2 pink-noise studies had low risk of bias (one positive, one mixed). 7 of the 9 positive pink-noise studies were small laboratory studies (4-40 participants), several of which played short pink-noise bursts during NREM sleep rather than continuous noise (e.g. 1-Hz bursts in studies of 16 and 35 people). Heterogeneity prevented a meta-analysis. The authors found no strong evidence supporting auditory stimulation; none of the studies reported adverse effects of short-term use.
claims.finding_zh: 针对成人的系统综述纳入34项研究（共1103人）：白噪声研究18项中6项结果积极（33%），粉红噪声11项中9项（81.9%），多种声音组合6项中4项（66.7%）；其中“粉红噪声”类别还包含自然声和海浪声。粉红噪声研究只有2项偏倚风险低（1项结果积极，1项结果不一）。9项积极结果中有7项是小样本实验室研究（每项4–40人），其中数项是在非快速眼动睡眠期播放短促的粉红噪声脉冲，而不是持续播放（例如每秒一次脉冲、样本分别为16人和35人的研究）。研究之间差异太大，无法做元分析。作者认为没有强证据支持用声音刺激助眠；各研究均未报告短期使用的不良反应。
claims.sample: 34 studies, 1,103 participants
claims.limitations: Vote counting of mostly weak-to-moderate-quality studies. 3 (possibly 4) of the 9 positive pink-noise studies used pulsed/burst stimulation in the lab, which differs from continuous playback. The others used non-pulsed pink noise in lab studies of 5-40 people, or nature/ocean sounds in hospital patients. White-noise results are reported inconsistently: abstract 6 (33%), results text 6 (38%), Table 4 7/18 (38.0%).
claims.app_implication: Do not market pink noise as 'deep sleep' enhancement; continuous pink/brown noise is a comfort and masking option only.

citation.authors: Capezuti E, Pain K, Alamag E, et al.
citation.title: Systematic review: auditory stimulation and sleep

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata (DOI 10.5664/jcsm.9860; JCSM 18(6):1697-1709); Europe PMC abstract (PMID 34964434); PMC full text PMC9163611 (results, Tables 3-4, discussion)
verification.problems: Metadata and the headline numbers match the abstract and full text: 34 studies, 1,103 persons; white 6/18 (33%), pink 9/11 (81.9%), multiaudio 4/6 (66.7%); only 2 low-risk pink-noise studies; 7 of 9 positive pink-noise studies done in a lab; no strong evidence; no adverse effects with short-term use. Errors: (1) 'brief pink-noise pulses during NREM sleep to 4-16 participants' is wrong. The review's table lists Simor 2018 (1-Hz pink-noise bursts during daytime NREM sleep, n=35, positive), describes Santostasi 2015 (n=4) only as 'bursts' and Santostasi 2017 (n=7) only as 'Pink Noise'. Positive lab studies ranged from 4 to 40 participants. (2) The limitation 'pink-noise positives largely from pulsed or closed-loop lab paradigms' overstates it. Only 3 (possibly 4) of the 9 positives used pulsed/burst stimulation; the rest were non-pulsed pink noise in 5-40-person lab studies, or nature/ocean sounds in hospital patients (Nasari 2018, Williamson 1992). (3) The finding omitted that the 'pink noise' category includes nature and ocean sounds. (4) The white-noise inconsistency is broader than stated: abstract 6 (33%), results text '6 (38%)', Table 4 7/18 (38.0%).

claims.topic: Music therapy vs listening to recorded music (Cochrane, cancer)
claims.finding: Cochrane review of 81 RCTs and quasi-RCTs (N=5,576; 74 adult and 7 pediatric trials; 38 music therapy, 43 music medicine), with music interventions compared with standard care. In adults with cancer, music interventions may reduce anxiety (STAI -7.73 points on a 20–80 scale, 95% CI -10.02 to -5.44; 17 studies, 1,381 participants; very low certainty). They may also reduce depression (SMD -0.41, 95% CI -0.67 to -0.15; 12 studies, 1,021 participants; very low), pain (SMD -0.67, 95% CI -1.07 to -0.26; 12 studies, 632 participants; very low) and fatigue (SMD -0.28, 95% CI -0.46 to -0.10; 10 studies, 498 participants; low). There was no support for an effect on mood (SMD 0.47, 95% CI -0.02 to 0.97; 5 studies; very low). The pooled quality-of-life effect was highly inconsistent and not significant (SMD 0.88, 95% CI -0.31 to 2.08; 7 studies). For anxiety, depression, pain, fatigue and QoL, music therapy delivered by trained music therapists produced consistent effects across studies. Music medicine (listening to pre-recorded music offered by medical staff) produced inconsistent effects, and effects on QoL and fatigue were found for music therapy but not for music medicine. Most trials were at high risk of bias.
claims.finding_zh: Cochrane综述纳入81项随机或半随机对照试验（5576人；74项成人、7项儿童；38项为由音乐治疗师实施的音乐治疗，43项为由医护人员提供录制音乐的单纯聆听），对照为常规护理。在成年癌症患者中，音乐干预可能降低焦虑（STAI量表范围20–80分，平均降低7.73分，95%CI −10.02至−5.44；17项研究，1381人；证据确定性很低）、抑郁（SMD −0.41，95%CI −0.67至−0.15；很低）、疼痛（SMD −0.67，95%CI −1.07至−0.26；很低）和疲劳（SMD −0.28，95%CI −0.46至−0.10；低）。对情绪的作用没有得到支持（SMD 0.47，95%CI −0.02至0.97），对生活质量的合并效应不一致且不显著（SMD 0.88，95%CI −0.31至2.08）。在焦虑、抑郁、疼痛、疲劳和生活质量等结局上，音乐治疗的效果在各研究间较一致；单纯聆听录制音乐的效果则不一致，而且对生活质量和疲劳的效果只在音乐治疗中出现，在单纯聆听中未见。多数试验偏倚风险高。
claims.sample: 81 RCTs/quasi-RCTs, 5,576 participants (74 adult, 7 pediatric trials)
claims.limitations: Very low to low certainty. Most trials were at high risk of bias (no blinding; self-reported outcomes). The population is people with cancer, mostly adults. The music therapy vs music medicine contrast is an indirect, across-study comparison. The comparator was standard care, not an attention or relaxation control.
claims.app_implication: 回神 provides music listening, not music therapy: never use 音乐治疗/音乐疗法/疗愈 for app audio, and explain that therapist-led music therapy is a different, clinician-delivered intervention. Do not borrow this review's anxiety, pain, fatigue or quality-of-life results for app audio, because they come from people with cancer and the consistent effects came from therapist-delivered music therapy.

citation.authors: Bradt J, Dileo C, Myers-Coffman K, et al.
citation.title: Music interventions for improving psychological and physical outcomes in people with cancer

verification.checked_against: Crossref and PubMed metadata (PMID 34637527, PMC8510511); full Cochrane structured abstract via PubMed (main results, GRADE ratings and authors' conclusions; the full text is not downloadable as XML from PMC or Europe PMC, and every number below is in the abstract)
verification.problems: Metadata and all quoted numbers match the abstract (81 trials, N=5,576, 38 music therapy / 43 music medicine; anxiety -7.73 [-10.02, -5.44], 17 studies, 1,381 participants, very low; depression SMD -0.41 [-0.67, -0.15]; pain -0.67 [-1.07, -0.26]; fatigue -0.28 [-0.46, -0.10], low). Nulls are omitted: the review found no support for an effect on mood (SMD 0.47, 95% CI -0.02 to 0.97; 5 studies), and the quality-of-life effect was highly inconsistent and not significant (SMD 0.88, 95% CI -0.31 to 2.08; 7 studies). Also omitted: effects on QoL and fatigue were found for music therapy but not for music medicine, which bears directly on a listening app. The comparator (standard care) is not stated.

claims.topic: Health effects of natural sounds (meta-analysis): water vs birdsong
claims.finding: Systematic review of 36 publications. Random-effects meta-analyses of 18 of them found that natural sounds decreased stress and annoyance outcomes (g=-0.60, 95% CI -0.97 to -0.23) and improved 'health and positive affect' outcomes (g=1.63, 95% CI 0.09 to 3.16). The authors attribute the large variance of the latter to one study with particularly large effects, a study of water sounds in urban spaces. Only 19% of reviewed studies (n=7) measured traditional health outcomes such as heart rate, blood pressure, pain or cortisol. In separate moderator models by sound type, water sounds had the largest mean effect on health/positive affect (2.01, 95% CI 0.35 to 3.67). Bird sounds had the largest effect on stress/annoyance (-1.11, 95% CI -1.82 to -0.40), but that rests on only 11 effect sizes from 2 studies, and no test of differences between sound types was reported. Heterogeneity was significant in all models (Q>248.4, P<0.001). 61% of studies (n=22) were in laboratories or hospitals. Among comparison types, natural sound vs noise showed the largest effects (1.7 for health/positive affect; -0.81 for stress/annoyance).
claims.finding_zh: 系统综述纳入36篇文献，其中18篇进入随机效应元分析：自然声能降低压力和烦躁类指标（g=−0.60，95%CI −0.97至−0.23），改善“健康与积极情绪”类指标（g=1.63，95%CI 0.09至3.16；作者指出后者的大变异主要来自一项效应特别大的研究，该研究考察的是城市空间中的水声）。纳入研究中只有19%（7项）测量了心率、血压、疼痛、皮质醇等传统健康指标，其余多为主观感受、情绪或认知。按声音类型分别建模：水声对“健康与积极情绪”的平均效应最大（2.01，95%CI 0.35–3.67），鸟鸣对“压力与烦躁”的平均效应最大（−1.11，95%CI −1.82至−0.40），但鸟鸣只有2项研究的11个效应量，论文也没有检验不同声音类型之间的差异。所有模型均存在显著异质性（Q>248.4）；61%的研究在实验室或医院进行；各类对照中，“自然声对比噪声”的效应最大。
claims.sample: 36 publications reviewed; 18 meta-analysed
claims.limitations: Very heterogeneous outcomes and designs, with wide confidence intervals. Few studies per sound type and no head-to-head test between sound types. One study with very large effects drives the health/positive-affect estimate. Most outcomes were perceptions, mood or cognition rather than clinical health measures. Many comparisons were against noise rather than silence. Mostly laboratory studies in Western populations.
claims.app_implication: Offer water and birdsong as nature layers, but do not present either as proven better. This meta-analysis does not rank them: water had the larger estimate for positive affect and birds for stress, both imprecise and never tested against each other. If water is the default for sleep, base that on other grounds, e.g. steady, continuous sound that masks noise (which the authors mention), and keep birdsong optional for daytime. Copy is limited to '许多人觉得自然声更放松', with no numeric health claims.

citation.authors: Buxton RT, Pearson AL, Allou C, et al.
citation.title: A synthesis of health benefits of natural sounds and their distribution in national parks
citation.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the USA

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata + Europe PMC abstract + PMC open-access full text (PMC8040792)
verification.problems: Metadata and every number match the full text: 36/18 publications, g=-0.60 [-0.97,-0.23], g=1.63 [0.09,3.16], water 2.01 [0.35,3.67], birds [-1.82,-0.40] from 11 effect sizes in 2 studies, Q>248.4, 61% (n=22) lab or hospital, natural sound vs noise largest. The paper's text prints the bird estimate as '1.11' with a negative CI; -1.11 is the consistent value (it is the CI midpoint). Issues: (1) Omitted: the authors attribute the large variance of the health/positive-affect estimate to one study with particularly large effects. That study (ref. 28, Jeon et al. 2012) is about water sounds in urban open spaces, which matters for the water result. (2) Omitted: only 19% of studies (n=7) measured traditional health outcomes such as heart rate, blood pressure, pain or cortisol; most measured perception, mood or cognition. (3) Each sound type was estimated in a separate moderator model and tested only against zero. The paper reports no test of water vs birds. (4) The app_implication puts water first for 'relax', but for stress/annoyance, the outcome closest to relaxation, birds had the larger point estimate. This source does not support that ranking. (5) finding_zh '异质性都很大' (heterogeneity was large) should be '显著异质性' (significant heterogeneity).

claims.topic: Closed-loop acoustic stimulation of slow-wave sleep
claims.finding: Meta-analysis of 10 studies (11 experiments, 177 healthy participants) of acoustic slow-wave enhancement during sleep: the overall effect on overnight episodic-memory consolidation was g=0.25 (p=0.07); phase-locked stimulation subgroup g=0.36 (p=0.047); young adults with phase-locked stimulation g=0.44 (p=0.01). No indication of publication bias. The authors concluded the evidence is not sufficient to recommend commercially available devices.
claims.finding_zh: 对10项研究（11个实验，177名健康人）的元分析：睡眠中用声音刺激增强慢波，对次日情景记忆巩固的总体效应g=0.25（p=0.07，未达显著）；与慢波相位锁定的刺激亚组g=0.36（p=0.047）；年轻人加相位锁定亚组g=0.44（p=0.01）。作者认为现有证据不足以推荐市售设备。
claims.sample: 10 studies, 11 experiments, 177 participants
claims.limitations: Small studies; outcome is memory rather than sleep quality; requires real-time EEG; a separate 2022 meta-analysis on this topic (Stanyer et al., J Sleep Res) was retracted for data errors.
claims.app_implication: 回神 does not offer 'deep-sleep pink-noise pulses' (needs a closed EEG loop) and makes no claims about slow waves, memory or brain effects for any sleep audio.

citation.authors: Wunderlin M, Züst MA, Hertenstein E, et al.
citation.title: Modulating overnight memory consolidation by acoustic stimulation during slow-wave sleep: a systematic review and meta-analysis

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata (DOI 10.1093/sleep/zsaa296; Sleep 44(7):zsaa296, online 2021-01-06); Europe PMC/PubMed abstract (PMID 33406249); Europe PMC/PubMed records for Stanyer et al. 2022 (PMID 34850995, flagged Retracted Publication) and its retraction notice (PMID 40519131, J Sleep Res 2025)

claims.topic: Which music features moderate stress effects: tempo, selection, lyrics, number of sessions
claims.finding: Within the same meta-analyses no intervention characteristic significantly moderated effects. For psychological outcomes, music described as 60–80 bpm showed a non-significant trend toward larger effects than music with no specified tempo (d=0.625 vs 0.413; p=.064). For physiological outcomes tempo made no difference (d=0.361 vs 0.409). Participants bringing their own music did not differ significantly from music selected by researchers/therapists, a category that included choosing from a pre-selected list (psychological d=0.611 vs 0.498; physiological d=0.329 vs 0.415). Lyrics did not moderate effects (psychological: instrumental d=0.556, lyrics only d=0.264 from just 5 studies, mixed d=0.581). For psychological outcomes, a single session showed a non-significant trend toward larger effects than two or more sessions (d=0.601 vs 0.379; p=.078). For physiological outcomes there was no difference (d=0.375 vs 0.402). Session duration did not moderate either outcome.
claims.finding_zh: 同一元分析中，没有任何干预特征显著影响效果。心理结局方面，标明60–80拍/分钟的音乐比未注明速度的音乐效果有偏大的趋势（d=0.625对0.413，p=0.064，未达显著）；生理结局方面速度没有差别（0.361对0.409）。参与者自带音乐与研究者/治疗师选定的音乐（包括让参与者从预选曲目中挑选）差异不显著（心理0.611对0.498；生理0.329对0.415）。有无歌词也不显著影响效果（心理结局：纯器乐d=0.556，只含有歌词音乐的d=0.264但仅5项研究，两者混合d=0.581）。心理结局方面，单次干预比两次及以上效果有偏大的趋势（0.601对0.379，p=0.078，未达显著）；生理结局方面没有差别（0.375对0.402）。每次干预的时长也不影响效果。
claims.study_type: moderator analyses within multilevel meta-analyses of RCTs
claims.sample: Physiological: 61 studies / 197 effect sizes; psychological: 79 studies / 130 effect sizes
claims.limitations: Moderator analyses are cross-study comparisons confounded by setting, population and music. 'No specified tempo' means the tempo was not reported, not that the music was fast. Few studies used lyrics only (5 psychological, 2 physiological), and the authors flag low power for several moderator categories. Non-significant moderators may reflect low power rather than true equivalence.
claims.app_implication: Generative music defaults to slow or beatless, instrumental material. Curated presets are acceptable, since there is no evidence that self-selection is required. One 10–30 min session is a reasonable unit, and session length did not moderate effects. Slowness is a comfort convention backed only by a weak trend and is never presented as a proven 'dose'.

citation.authors: de Witte M, Spruit A, van Hooren S, et al.
citation.title: Effects of music interventions on stress-related outcomes: a systematic review and two meta-analyses

verification.checked_against: Full publisher PDF (UvA Pure repository): Table 2 (physiological moderators), Table 3 (psychological moderators), Results text (p=.064 tempo, p=.078 frequency) and Discussion/Limitations; Crossref and PubMed metadata
verification.problems: All quoted numbers match Tables 2-3, and 'no intervention characteristic significantly moderated effects' is correct. Minor issues only. (1) The single- vs multiple-session trend (d=0.601 vs 0.379, p=.078) holds only for psychological outcomes, which the finding does not say; physiological outcomes showed no difference (one session 0.375 vs more 0.402). (2) finding_zh says '单次聆听', but the sessions were music-intervention sessions that also included music therapy and live music. (3) In the paper, 'own preference' means participants brought their own music; choosing from a pre-selected list was coded as researcher/therapist selection. (4) The lyrics-only subgroup (d=0.264, 5 studies) was itself not significantly different from zero, and a 'both' category (22 studies, d=0.581) also existed.

claims.topic: Which bird sounds are perceived as restorative
claims.finding: Online study of 174 UK residents; 149 were analysed after excluding 23 who found the sounds uncomfortably loud and 2 with hearing difficulties. Each rated 10 of 50 ten-second clips (25 UK and 25 Australian bird species). They rated perceived restorative potential (PRP) while imagining being stressed and mentally fatigued, plus arousal, valence and aesthetic qualities. Per-sound means were analysed by hierarchical regression (N=50 sounds). With acoustic predictors alone (about 43% of PRP variance), the sounds highest in PRP were harmonic, higher in frequency and low in sound level. Perceived familiarity and complexity added predictive value, as did pattern in the full model, and frequency was no longer significant once familiarity and complexity were included. Sounds rated as more arousing had higher sound levels and lower harmonicity; acoustic properties explained about 14% of arousal variance after controlling for valence. More complex sounds were also rated more arousing.
claims.finding_zh: 线上研究：174名英国居民参与（排除23名觉得声音过响者和2名有听力问题者后，分析149人）。每人只评价50段10秒鸟鸣中的10段（英国和澳大利亚鸟种各25种），在想象自己“又累又烦”的情境下评价每段声音的“恢复潜力”，并评价唤醒、愉悦和审美特征；分析以50段声音的平均分为单位，采用分层回归。只看声学特征时（约解释恢复潜力方差的43%），被认为最具恢复感的是谐波性强（声音干净、有明确音高）、频率较高、音量较低的鸟鸣；主观熟悉度和复杂度还有额外预测作用（完整模型中“有规律感”也有作用），而加入熟悉度和复杂度后，频率不再显著。被评为更令人兴奋紧张的是较响、谐波性低（更像噪声）的鸟鸣（控制愉悦度后，声学特征约解释唤醒评分方差的14%）；越复杂的鸟鸣也被评为越唤醒。
claims.study_type: online correlational rating study with hierarchical regression
claims.sample: 174 participants (149 analysed), 50 bird sounds; each participant rated 10
claims.limitations: Ratings of perceived restorativeness under an imagined scenario, using single-item measures; no measured stress, attention or health outcomes. Correlational, with only 50 sounds as units of analysis. UK participants; species were half UK, half Australian. Online playback was only roughly calibrated by a loudness-matching task, and equipment and setting were uncontrolled. Isolated 10-s clips rather than full soundscapes.
claims.app_implication: Synthesize birdsong as soft, tonal, harmonic songbird phrases kept well below the bed. Favour songbirds likely to sound familiar to the app's users: in this UK sample, perceived familiarity predicted higher restorative ratings and lower arousal. Avoid loud, harsh or noisy (low-harmonicity) calls, and keep very complex song out of sleep content, since complexity was rated more arousing. Specific species exclusions (e.g. crows, magpies) rest on the authors' earlier interview work, not on this study.

citation.authors: Ratcliffe E, Gatersleben B, Sowden PT
citation.title: Predicting the perceived restorative potential of bird sounds through acoustics and aesthetics

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata + abstract + the authors' accepted manuscript (University of Surrey Open Research repository, manuscript E&B-17-0462.R3)
verification.problems: Metadata is correct: online 19 Oct 2018, issue 2020, 52(4):371-400. Confirmed: PRP highest for harmonic, higher-frequency, low-level sounds; familiarity and complexity add predictive value; more arousing sounds had higher levels and lower harmonicity; acoustics explain about 14% of arousal variance; hierarchical regression. Issues: (1) Sample: 174 took part, but 25 were excluded (23 found the sounds uncomfortably loud, 2 had hearing difficulties), leaving 149 analysed. Each participant rated only 10 of the 50 sounds, and analyses used per-sound means (N=50 sounds). (2) The limitations say 'UK … species', but half the clips were Australian (25 UK, 25 New South Wales). (3) 'Playback level uncontrolled' is overstated: participants calibrated output with a loudness-matching task, though equipment and setting were uncontrolled. (4) The frequency effect on PRP held only with acoustic predictors alone; it became non-significant once familiarity and complexity were added. Pattern was also a positive predictor in the full model. (5) Not stated: PRP was rated under an imagined stress/fatigue vignette with single-item measures. (6) The app_implication's species exclusions are not results of this study. Crows and magpies come from the authors' 2013 interview study and gulls from older work, both cited in the introduction; raptors are not mentioned at all.

claims.topic: Nature vs urban soundscapes and directed attention
claims.finding: Randomized between-participants experiment: 65 enrolled, 63 analysed (31 nature, 32 urban). After a pre-test, participants listened to and rated either 40 nature soundscapes (birdsong, moving water, insects, wind) or 40 urban soundscapes (traffic, café ambiance, machinery), each 20 s at about 70 dB SPL. This phase took about 15 min, after which the tasks were repeated, so the sounds were heard between tests, not during them. The nature group improved more on a composite of backward digit span and dual n-back (time x soundscape F(1,61)=7.92, p=.007, d=0.71). The result also held among participants who had not guessed the study purpose (F(1,44)=6.58, p=.014). Natural sounds were aesthetically preferred, but changes in positive and negative affect did not differ significantly between groups.
claims.finding_zh: 随机分组的组间实验（招募65人，分析63人：自然组31人、城市组32人）。先做前测，再聆听并评价40段自然声（鸟鸣、流水、昆虫、风）或40段城市声（交通、咖啡馆、机器），每段20秒、约70 dB，这一环节约15分钟，之后做后测。声音是在两次测验之间听的，不是做题时的背景音。自然声组在倒背数字与双重n-back组合测验上的进步更大（F(1,61)=7.92，p=0.007，d=0.71；排除猜到研究目的者后结果仍成立）。自然声更受喜爱，但两组在正、负性情绪变化上的差异不显著。
claims.sample: n=63 analysed (31 nature, 32 urban)
claims.limitations: Single laboratory session with a mostly young-adult sample. Modest sample size. Urban sounds were the only comparator, with no silence or neutral arm. Sounds were heard during a listening break, not as background during tasks. Task-specific cognitive outcomes. Not yet widely replicated.
claims.app_implication: Offer short (about 15-minute) mixed nature-soundscape breaks (birds, water, wind) between focus blocks. This study does not support playing them as background during focused work. It also gives no basis for claiming they improve mood, since mood changes did not differ significantly from urban sounds.

citation.authors: Van Hedger SC, Nusbaum HC, Clohisy L, et al.
citation.title: Of cricket chirps and car horns: The effect of nature sounds on cognitive performance

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata + PubMed/Europe PMC abstract + published full text on SpringerLink (read via WebFetch) + the authors' manuscript (UChicago APEX lab PDF)
verification.problems: Metadata and every design detail and statistic match the published article: 65 participated, 63 analysed (31 nature, 32 urban); 40 nature clips (birdsong, moving water, insects, wind) vs 40 urban clips; 20 s each at about 70 dB SPL; listening phase about 15 min; time x soundscape F(1,61)=7.92, p=.007, d=0.71; random assignment stated. Issues: (1) The app_implication says nature soundscapes 'suit focus … sessions'. In the study, sounds were heard in a separate listening phase between pre- and post-tests, not as background during the tasks, so only use as a break is supported. (2) finding_zh '无差别' (no difference) overstates the non-significant affect interactions (positive affect p=.644; negative affect p=.119). (3) Worth adding: the result held among participants who had not guessed the study purpose (F(1,44)=6.58, p=.014, d=0.76).

claims.topic: Binaural beats: meta-analysis reporting a positive effect
claims.finding: Meta-analysis of 22 studies (35 effect sizes) on binaural beats for memory, attention, anxiety and pain perception found an overall medium, statistically significant effect (g = 0.45). In meta-regression, beats masked with white or pink noise and unmasked beats gave similar effects; exposure before, or before and during, a task gave larger effects than exposure only during the task; and longer exposure time was associated with larger effects. The authors conclude that the direction and size of the effect depend on the beat frequency used, the exposure time and when exposure occurs.
claims.finding_zh: 对22项研究（35个效应量）的元分析：双耳节拍对记忆、注意、焦虑和疼痛感知的总体效应为中等且有统计学意义（g=0.45）。元回归显示：用白噪声或粉红噪声掩蔽与不掩蔽的效果相近；任务前（或任务前加任务中）聆听比只在任务中聆听效果更大；聆听时间越长，效应量往往越大（这是关联，不是因果证明）。作者认为，效应的方向和大小取决于所用节拍频率、聆听时长和聆听时机。
claims.sample: 22 studies, 35 effect sizes
claims.limitations: Pools different outcomes (memory, attention, anxiety, pain) from mostly small studies, and some studies contribute several effect sizes. Control conditions varied: of 12 of the 22 included studies whose abstracts were checked, 7 used matched non-beat audio (a constant or carrier tone, or the same soundtrack or noise without the beats), while 5 used blank tape, no intervention, music or white noise. Beat frequencies varied, and some included trials were null (e.g., Kennel 2010 on inattention). Heterogeneity statistics, publication-bias results and outcome-specific estimates were not verified because the full text is paywalled.
claims.app_implication: Listed as supporting evidence in the 证据库. Binaural beats are still not a default feature and carry no health claim, because the meta-analysis pools different outcomes from small studies (some with only silence or no-treatment controls) and EEG evidence for the proposed brainwave-entrainment mechanism is inconsistent (Ingendoh 2023).

citation.authors: Garcia-Argibay M, Santed MA, Reales JM
citation.title: Efficacy of binaural auditory beats in cognition, anxiety, and pain perception: a meta-analysis

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata incl. the paper's reference list (asterisks mark the 22 included studies) + PubMed abstract (PMID 30073406); PubMed abstracts of 12 of the 22 included primary studies to check their control conditions. Full text paywalled (Springer and the UNED portal blocked, OpenAlex shows closed access), so not read.
verification.problems: Citation metadata, DOI and PMID are correct; print issue 2019;83(2):357-372, online 2 Aug 2018. Every number and moderator result in the finding matches the abstract: 22 studies, 35 effect sizes, g=0.45, masked vs unmasked similar, before or before+during the task better than during only, exposure time significant. PROBLEM: the limitations and app_implication say comparators 'rarely isolate the beat from the audio itself'. The included studies contradict this. Of 12 included studies whose abstracts I checked, 7 used a matched non-beat control: Padmanabhan 2005 (identical soundtrack without the added tones), Hommel 2016 and Colzato 2017a (constant 340 Hz tone), Beauchene 2016 (pure tone), Wahbeh 2007b (same pink-noise overlay without beat carriers), McConnell 2014 (carrier-tone placebo) and Kennel 2010 (sham audio without beats). The other 5 used blank tape, no intervention, music or white noise. Minor: the zh '聆听时间越长效应越大' reads more causal/monotonic than a meta-regression association. Added the authors' own statement that effects depend on beat frequency, exposure time and timing.

claims.topic: 'Weightless' (Marconi Union) vs midazolam before a nerve block
claims.finding: Single-centre (University of Pennsylvania), open-label RCT in 157 analysed adults (midazolam n=80, music n=77; 160 enrolled) about to receive an ultrasound-guided single-injection peripheral nerve block. One group got IV midazolam 1-2 mg. The other listened through noise-cancelling headphones to Marconi Union's 'Weightless', which BMJ's press release names; the trial registry says only 'research-selected music'. Each began about 3 minutes before the block. The change in STAI-6 anxiety was similar: music -1.6 (SD 10.7) vs midazolam -4.2 (SD 11); mean difference -2.5, 95% CI -5.9 to 0.9, p=0.1. Patient satisfaction was higher with midazolam (p=0.01) and physician satisfaction did not differ (p=0.07). Both patients (p=0.005) and physicians (p=0.0007) reported more difficulty communicating in the music group.
claims.finding_zh: 单中心（美国宾夕法尼亚大学）、不设盲的随机对照试验，分析157名即将接受超声引导下单次外周神经阻滞的成人（咪达唑仑组80人，音乐组77人；共入组160人）：一组静脉注射咪达唑仑1–2 mg，另一组用降噪耳机听Marconi Union乐队的《Weightless》（曲名见BMJ新闻稿；试验注册只写“研究者选定的音乐”），两者都在阻滞前约3分钟开始。STAI-6焦虑变化相近（音乐组−1.6［标准差10.7］，咪达唑仑组−4.2［标准差11］；差值−2.5，95%CI −5.9至0.9，p=0.1）。患者满意度咪达唑仑组更高（p=0.01），医生满意度无差异（p=0.07）；音乐组的患者（p=0.005）和医生（p=0.0007）都觉得沟通更困难。
claims.sample: n=157 adults analysed (160 enrolled)
claims.limitations: One centre and one anaesthesia setting, unblinded. The intervention lasted only about 3 minutes. Patients with anxiety or depressive disorders or very high anxiety (STAI-6 of 50 or more) were excluded, and baseline anxiety was low (median STAI-6 about 30-33 on a 20-80 scale). Patients could not choose the music, and satisfaction was measured on a non-validated scale. A similar change is not proof of equivalence. Headphones impaired communication.
claims.app_implication: No 'world's most relaxing song' or '65% less anxiety' claims; that figure traces to a Mindlab International test reported only in the press, with no peer-reviewed report found. The only published peer-reviewed clinical trial we found (this one) showed no advantage over a sedative after a 3-minute exposure. A registered labour-epidural RCT of the song (NCT03844659, n=100, completed 2020) has no published results.

citation.authors: Graff V, Cai L, Badiola I, et al.
citation.title: Music versus midazolam during preoperative nerve block placements: a prospective randomized controlled study

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; PubMed abstract (PMID 31320504); ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03069677 record with posted results (77 music / 80 midazolam analysed; STAI-6 change -1.6 SD 10.7 vs -4.2 SD 11; exclusion criteria; masking none; single site); BMJ press release as republished by Medical Xpress and Neuroscience News (157 adults, 80/77, Marconi Union's 'Weightless series', 3-minute exposure, stated limitations); PubMed, Europe PMC and web searches for other 'Weightless' trials and for the Mindlab 65% figure; NCT03844659 registry record
verification.problems: Metadata and all numbers are correct (n=157 with 80/77; STAI-6 changes; MD -2.5, 95% CI -5.9 to 0.9, p=0.1; patient satisfaction p=0.01; communication p=0.005 and p=0.0007). Single-centre is confirmed. The corrections are additive. The claim omits the null for physician satisfaction (p=0.07). It also omits key context: music or midazolam started only about 3 minutes before the block; patients with STAI-6 of 50 or more or with anxiety/depressive disorders were excluded; baseline anxiety was low (median STAI-6 about 30-33); the trial was open-label; satisfaction used a non-validated scale; and patients could not choose the music. BMJ's release calls the music 'Marconi Union's Weightless series of music', while the registry says only 'research-selected music'. The app_implication's 'the only peer-reviewed trial' is an absolute that cannot be fully confirmed. I found no other published peer-reviewed clinical trial of the track, but a completed registered labour-epidural RCT of 'Weightless' exists (NCT03844659, n=100) with no published or posted results. The 65% figure traces to a Mindlab International test that appears only in press coverage; I found no peer-reviewed report of it.

claims.topic: Music and anxiety in non-clinical samples
claims.finding: Meta-analysis of 21 studies (19 articles, N=1,144 healthy participants): music listening produced a small decrease in self-reported anxiety (d=-0.30, 95% CI -0.55 to -0.04; I2=66%) but no significant effect on psychophysiological anxiety markers (d=-0.07, 95% CI -0.28 to 0.13). Slow music (16 studies, N=659) gave d=-0.28 (95% CI -0.55 to -0.01); classical-genre and major-mode subgroups were not significant. Mean listening time was 22 min (25 min in studies showing a benefit).
claims.finding_zh: 对21项研究（19篇文章，1144名健康人）的元分析：听音乐使自评焦虑小幅下降（d=−0.30，95%CI −0.55至−0.04），但对心率、血压、皮质醇等生理指标无显著影响（d=−0.07，95%CI −0.28至0.13）。慢速音乐亚组d=−0.28；古典音乐、大调亚组均不显著。平均聆听时长22分钟（显示有效的研究中为25分钟）。
claims.sample: 21 studies (19 articles), 1,144 healthy participants
claims.limitations: Small, methodologically weak studies (poor CONSORT adherence), high heterogeneity, mostly experimenter-prepared music, inconsistent physiological measures.
claims.app_implication: No physiological claims (heart rate, blood pressure, cortisol) for app music in healthy users; describe benefits only as subjective calm. Presets of about 20–25 min match studied durations.

citation.authors: Panteleeva Y, Ceschi G, Glowinski D, et al.
citation.title: Music for anxiety? Meta-analysis of anxiety reduction in non-clinical samples

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata (Psychology of Music 46(4):473-487, 2018; online 2017); full published PDF from Archive ouverte UNIGE (unige:109589): abstract, Methods, Results, Table 1, Table 2 (CONSORT ratings), Discussion, Appendix; PubMed and Europe PMC searched by title and DOI (not indexed, so the empty PMID is correct)

claims.topic: Lyrics and reading comprehension
claims.finding: Within-subject study of 30 undergraduates, all native English speakers; people who liked thrash metal were excluded. Each did SAT reading-comprehension passages under four counterbalanced sound conditions, via headphones at 65-75 dB(A): quiet, self-chosen liked songs with lyrics, disliked lyrical thrash metal, and a non-lyrical (instrumental) thrash-metal track. Comprehension differed by condition (F(3,87)=8.05, eta2=.22). In planned contrasts, quiet beat disliked lyrical music (F(1,29)=16.96, eta2=.37) and liked lyrical music (F(1,29)=10.43, eta2=.26). Quiet vs non-lyrical music, and liked vs disliked lyrical music, showed no significant difference. Participants rated the non-lyrical track as more distracting than quiet but less distracting than either lyrical condition.
claims.finding_zh: 被试内研究：30名大学生（母语为英语；喜欢鞭挞金属的人不参加）戴耳机，在4种声音条件下（音量65–75 dB(A)，顺序平衡）完成SAT阅读理解：安静、自选的喜欢的有歌词歌曲、不喜欢的有歌词音乐（鞭挞金属）、无歌词音乐（一首鞭挞金属器乐曲）。声音条件显著影响成绩（F(3,87)=8.05，η²=0.22）。安静时成绩优于不喜欢的有歌词音乐（η²=0.37）和喜欢的有歌词音乐（η²=0.26）；无歌词音乐与安静之间、喜欢与不喜欢的有歌词音乐之间，差异都不显著（只有30人，不能据此认为两者完全一样）。参与者觉得无歌词音乐比安静更干扰，但不如有歌词音乐干扰。
claims.sample: n=30 undergraduates
claims.limitations: Small sample: the non-significant contrasts cannot show equivalence. One task type (SAT passages). Both the disliked-lyrical and the instrumental tracks were thrash metal by one band, while the liked music was self-chosen popular songs, so genre, familiarity and liking are confounded with condition. No direct test of lyrical vs instrumental music was reported. Short-term performance only.
claims.app_implication: Focus and study soundscapes contain no lyrics or intelligible speech, and the guidance voice never overlaps reading or work blocks. Do not claim that instrumental music is as good as silence for reading; this study cannot show that.

citation.authors: Perham N, Currie H
citation.title: Does listening to preferred music improve reading comprehension performance?

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata + full text of the published Wiley article (Appl Cognit Psychol 28:279-284, PDF mirror) + PubMed search (no record, so the empty PMID is correct)
verification.problems: Metadata and all statistics match the full text: F(3,87)=8.05, eta2=.22; quiet vs disliked lyrical F(1,29)=16.96, eta2=.37; quiet vs liked lyrical F(1,29)=10.43, eta2=.26; quiet vs non-lyrical and liked vs disliked lyrical both non-significant. The instrumental track was indeed thrash metal (Death Angel, 'The Ultra Violence'). Wording issues: (1) Non-significant contrasts in n=30 are written as 'did not differ' and, in Chinese, '无差别' (no difference), which lay readers take as equivalence. (2) Missing context: the instrumental track was disliked (likeability 29.9/100), and participants rated it as significantly more distracting than quiet (46.4 vs 10.4/100). (3) The paper reports no direct statistical test of lyrical vs instrumental music; the claim correctly does not assert one.

claims.topic: Relaxing music vs rippling-water sound before a stressor
claims.finding: Randomized three-arm laboratory experiment in 60 healthy women (mean age 25). Before the Trier Social Stress Test, participants spent 10 min listening to relaxing music (Allegri's 'Miserere'), listening to rippling water (designed as an acoustic control), or resting without sound. Cortisol: no group difference without covariates (group-by-time p=0.146). After adjusting for depression, emotion regulation, trait anxiety and chronic stress, responses differed (p=0.025), highest after music and lowest after water sound. Only music vs water differed; neither differed from silent rest. Salivary alpha-amylase: overall responses did not differ (adjusted p=0.23). A secondary recovery analysis found levels returned to baseline sooner after music than after rest (p=0.026) or water (p=0.039); the authors describe this as only a trend. Heart rate, perceived stress and state anxiety did not differ. Respiratory sinus arrhythmia (RSA) recovered faster after water sound than after rest (p=0.015). The authors conclude that music before a stressor may not reduce the stress response and might even add to it.
claims.finding_zh: 随机三组实验室研究（60名健康女性，平均25岁）：在特里尔社会压力测试前，受试者分别听10分钟放松音乐（阿莱格里《求主垂怜》）、听潺潺流水声（设计为声音对照），或无声静坐。皮质醇：不校正时各组无差异（p=0.146）；校正抑郁、情绪调节、特质焦虑和慢性压力后各组反应不同（p=0.025），音乐组最高、流水声组最低，但只有音乐组与流水声组之间有差异，两者与无声静坐都无差异。唾液淀粉酶：整体反应各组无差异（校正后p=0.23）；次要的恢复分析显示音乐组比静坐组（p=0.026）和流水声组（p=0.039）更早回到基线，作者自己称之为“趋势”。心率、主观压力和状态焦虑各组无差异；流水声组压力后的呼吸性窦性心律不齐（RSA）比静坐组恢复更快（p=0.015）。作者结论：压力前听音乐未必能减轻压力反应，甚至可能加强压力反应。
claims.study_type: randomized controlled trial (three-arm, between-subjects laboratory experiment)
claims.sample: n=60 healthy women (mean age 25); 3 cortisol outliers excluded from cortisol analyses
claims.limitations: Women only. One music piece and one water recording. A single 10-min exposure before (not during or after) the stressor. About 20 per group. Many outcomes and analyses with no correction for multiple comparisons. The cortisol difference appears only after covariate adjustment and is music vs water, not either sound vs silence. The sAA and RSA effects come from secondary recovery analyses. The water sound was designed as a control, not as an intervention.
claims.app_implication: Rippling water can be offered as a pleasant, neutral background: participants liked both sounds and rated them equally relaxing. But this study does not show that water sound lowers stress compared with silence. Do not assume 'relaxing music' lowers cortisol before a stressor, and make no hormone or stress-reduction claims for any audio.

citation.authors: Thoma MV, La Marca R, Brönnimann R, et al.
citation.title: The effect of music on the human stress response

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata + PubMed abstract + Europe PMC full text (PMC3734071: Methods, Results, Discussion)
verification.problems: Metadata correct (PLoS ONE 8(8):e70156). The numbers match the abstract, but the finding leaves out nulls and context that the full text gives. (1) The cortisol difference (p=0.025) appears only after adjusting for 4 covariates (BDI, ERQ, STAI-trait, TICS); without them p=0.146. Pairwise, only music vs water differed (p=0.009); neither differed from silent rest. 3 cortisol outliers were excluded. (2) The sAA result comes from a secondary univariate recovery-delta analysis. The overall sAA group-by-time interaction was null (p=0.318 unadjusted, p=0.23 adjusted). Music also recovered faster than water (p=0.039), and the Discussion calls this 'only a statistical trend'. The reported F(1/31)=0.547 for music vs rest does not fit p=0.026; with eta-squared 0.15 it should be about 5.47, so probably a typo. (3) Not mentioned: RSA recovery was faster after water sound than after rest (p=0.015). (4) The app_implication that water sound is 'a credible default calm layer' goes too far: water sound did not differ from silence on cortisol, heart rate or self-reported stress or anxiety.

claims.topic: Crescendos, uniform dynamics and 10-second musical phrases
claims.finding: In 24 healthy young adults (12 choristers, 12 non-musicians), vocal and orchestral crescendos produced increases in blood pressure and skin vasoconstriction proportional to the crescendo and correlated with the music profile (P=0.05 or better), whereas music with uniform emphasis induced skin vasodilation and reductions in blood pressure. Rhythmic phrases with a 10-second period (similar to Mayer waves) entrained cardiovascular autonomic variables. No qualitative differences were seen between musicians and non-musicians.
claims.finding_zh: 24名健康青年（12名合唱团员、12名非音乐人）中：人声和管弦乐的渐强使血压升高、皮肤血管收缩，且与音乐强弱曲线同步（P≤0.05）；强弱均匀的音乐则使皮肤血管舒张、血压下降。周期约10秒的乐句能带动心血管自主神经节律同步。音乐人与非音乐人反应无本质差异。
claims.sample: n=24 (12 choristers, 12 non-musicians)
claims.limitations: Small sample; acute laboratory responses to specific classical/opera excerpts; entrainment shown for cardiovascular oscillations only, not for health outcomes.
claims.app_implication: No crescendos in calm presets (slow loudness drift capped at about ±2–3 dB); phrase and chord changes may be aligned to the breathing cycle (e.g. 10 s at 6 breaths/min) as an aesthetic choice, without 'resonance' or cardiovascular claims.

citation.authors: Bernardi L, Porta C, Casucci G, et al.
citation.title: Dynamic interactions between musical, cardiovascular, and cerebral rhythms in humans

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata (Circulation 119(25):3171-3180) + PubMed abstract. Full text not read: the AHA site returned 403. Every statement in the finding, including n=24 (12 choristers), P=0.05 or better, the uniform-emphasis vasodilation and BP reduction, 10-s phrase entrainment and no qualitative musician difference, appears directly in the abstract.

claims.topic: Tempo, style and pauses: cardiorespiratory responses
claims.finding: Laboratory study in 24 healthy young adults (12 musicians, 12 non-musicians; mean age 23-25) lying supine with headphones. They heard six music styles in random order (first 2-min, then 4-min tracks), with a randomly inserted 2-min pause. Faster tempi and simpler rhythmic structures increased breathing rate, ventilation, blood pressure and heart rate, and tended to reduce baroreflex sensitivity. Effects depended on tempo rather than style and were not influenced by participants' music preferences. Among the music tracks, the slowest (raga, 55 bpm) produced a significantly larger fall in heart rate than baseline or any other track (p<0.01), but slow music had no significant effect on breathing or blood pressure. The 2-min pause produced the lowest heart rate, blood pressure and minute ventilation, even below the pre-music baseline. Musicians showed greater respiratory sensitivity to tempo.
claims.finding_zh: 实验室研究（24名健康青年，12名音乐人、12名非音乐人，平均23–25岁）仰卧戴耳机，按随机顺序听6种风格的音乐（先各2分钟，再各4分钟），并随机插入2分钟静默：节奏越快、节奏结构越简单，呼吸频率、通气量、血压和心率越高，压力感受性反射有降低趋势；影响取决于速度而不是风格，也不受个人喜好影响。在各段音乐中，最慢的拉格音乐（55拍/分钟）使心率下降最多（显著低于基线和其他曲目，p<0.01），但慢音乐对呼吸和血压没有显著影响。2分钟静默时心率、血压和每分通气量最低，甚至低于听音乐前的基线。音乐人的呼吸对速度更敏感。
claims.sample: n=24 healthy young adults (12 musicians, 12 non-musicians)
claims.limitations: Very small sample. 2-4 min exposures. Healthy young adults only. Acute physiological measures only, no clinical outcomes. One track per style, so tempo is tied to particular pieces. Only one 2-min pause was tested. The abstract and results differ on some details, such as baroreflex 'decreased' vs 'tended to reduce'.
claims.app_implication: Keep generative music slow or beatless and build silence into sessions; control tempo, not genre. Rest lengths such as 20-40 s pauses or a 20-60 s silent ending before the closing bell are design choices: the study tested only one 2-min pause. Make no blood-pressure claims for slow music.

citation.authors: Bernardi L, Porta C, Sleight P
citation.title: Cardiovascular, cerebrovascular, and respiratory changes induced by different types of music in musicians and non-musicians: the importance of silence

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata + PubMed abstract + PMC full text (PMC1860846: Methods, Tables 1-3, Results, Discussion)
verification.problems: Metadata correct (Heart 2006;92(4):445-52; epub September 2005). Confirmed: raga at 55 bpm, effects not influenced by preference, pause below baseline, musicians more sensitive to tempo. Discrepancies: (1) The Results say faster tempi only 'tended to reduce' baroreflex sensitivity; the abstract says 'decreased'. (2) 'The slowest track produced the largest fall in heart rate' is true only among the music tracks; the 2-min pause had the lowest heart rate overall. (3) Omitted null: the Discussion states that slow meditative music lengthened the RR interval but had no significant effect on respiration or blood pressure. (4) The app_implication's 20-40 s rests and 20-60 s silent ending are not tested by this study, which used a single 2-min pause.

claims.topic: Guide's voice: pitch, volume and speech rate during relaxation training
claims.finding: RCT in 48 highly anxious young adult women (students, mean age about 21; 12 per arm) who had one session in one of four conditions. These were progressive relaxation training (PRT) with a 'recommended' therapist voice that fell in tone, volume and rate across the session; the same PRT with a conversational voice; systematic self-relaxation (a credible control); or no treatment. Self-reported tension, anxiety and heart rate fell significantly in all groups. Only the recommended-voice group showed significantly greater reductions in muscle tension (EMG) than the other three groups. Its participants also rated the therapist's voice as more facilitating of relaxation than the conversational-voice group did. The recommended voice showed no advantage on state anxiety: effect sizes vs no treatment, as extracted in a 2008 meta-analysis (Manzoni et al.), were d=0.16 for the recommended voice, 0.54 for the conversational voice and 0.50 for self-relaxation.
claims.finding_zh: 随机对照试验：48名高焦虑的青年女大学生（平均约21岁，每组12人），只训练一次，分为四组：用“推荐式”嗓音（随训练逐渐降低音调、音量和语速）指导的渐进式肌肉放松；用日常对话式嗓音指导的同样训练；系统性自我放松（可信的对照）；不处理。各组自评紧张、焦虑和心率都显著下降。只有推荐式嗓音组的肌电（肌肉紧张）下降显著大于其他三组，该组也比对话式嗓音组更认为指导者的嗓音有助于放松。但在自评状态焦虑上，推荐式嗓音没有优势：2008年一项元分析（Manzoni等）提取的与不处理组相比的效应量为：推荐式嗓音d=0.16，对话式嗓音0.54，自我放松0.50。
claims.study_type: randomized controlled trial (four arms, single session)
claims.sample: n=48 highly anxious young women (12 per arm)
claims.limitations: Small (12 per arm), women students only, a single session. EMG was the only outcome favouring the recommended voice, and self-reported anxiety did not favour it. The full text was not accessible, so how the voices were produced (number of therapists, live or recorded) and the actual size of the pitch, volume and rate changes could not be checked.
claims.app_implication: A guide voice that gradually becomes slower, softer and lower over a session is a reasonable, low-risk style choice consistent with this small trial. Specific targets (how many dB quieter, pause lengths) are design decisions, not values tested here. Do not claim that the voice style itself lowers anxiety.

citation.authors: Knowlton GE, Larkin KT
citation.title: The influence of voice volume, pitch, and speech rate on progressive relaxation training: application of methods from speech pathology and audiology

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; PubMed abstract (PMID 16941239); Manzoni et al. 2008 BMC Psychiatry meta-analysis (PMC2427027), Table 1 extraction of this trial (12 per arm, mean age 20.8, 100% women, 'very anxious' students, between- and within-group STAI-state effect sizes); Soma et al. 2021 (Couns Psychother Res) description of the voice manipulation. The Springer full text was not accessible.
verification.problems: Metadata and the abstract-level finding are correct: n=48 highly anxious young women, four arms, a single PRT session; all groups reduced self-reported tension, anxiety and heart rate; only the recommended voice (RV) reduced EMG compared with the other three groups; and RV participants rated the voice as more facilitating than the conversational-voice (CV) group did. (1) The claim does not make clear that self-reported anxiety did not favour the recommended voice. Manzoni 2008's extraction gives between-group STAI-state effect sizes vs no treatment of d=0.16 (RV), 0.54 (CV) and 0.50 (self-relaxation). (2) The limitation 'one therapist's voice' could not be verified: the abstract does not say, and the full text was inaccessible. (3) The app_implication's specific targets ('about 2-3 dB' quieter, 'longer pauses toward the end', 'start at a calm conversational pace') appear nowhere in the abstract or in any secondary description found. They are design extrapolations, not study findings. (4) finding_zh leaves out that the 'more facilitating' rating was relative to the conversational-voice group.

claims.topic: Music loudness preferred for relaxation
claims.finding: 144 college-age music and non-music majors listened to music for 27 min while relaxing. Amplitude changed every 3 min in randomized order, so each person heard loud (80-90 dB), medium (70-80 dB) and soft (60-70 dB) music three times each. Continuous dial (CRDI) responses showed an overall, overwhelming preference for the soft level for relaxation. Males preferred loud music more than females did, and non-music majors preferred louder music than music majors. In the subsample who wore heart-rate monitors (size not given in the abstract), heart rate did not differ by amplitude. Self-reported individual preferences varied widely and were not always consistent with the dial data. Reported relaxation increased over the session.
claims.finding_zh: 144名大学生（音乐专业与非音乐专业）边放松边听27分钟音乐，响度每3分钟按随机顺序在响（80–90 dB）、中（70–80 dB）、轻（60–70 dB）之间切换，每种各3次。连续旋钮（CRDI）数据显示，总体上参与者明显偏好用轻柔音量放松；男性比女性、非音乐专业比音乐专业学生更偏好较大音量。部分参与者佩戴了心率监测（摘要未给出人数），不同响度下心率没有差异。自我报告中的个人偏好差别很大，且不总与旋钮数据一致；整个过程中自评放松程度有所上升。
claims.study_type: within-subject experiment with randomized amplitude order
claims.sample: n=144 college students (heart rate recorded in a subsample of unreported size)
claims.limitations: Young students only. Three-minute segments. Measures preference rather than outcomes. Heart rate was recorded only in a subsample of unreported size. The abstract does not say which music was used, how it was played or where the dB levels were measured, and the full text was not checked. The softest level tested was 60-70 dB, so the study says nothing about quieter playback.
claims.app_implication: Default playback is soft: onboarding guides users to a comfortable low volume rather than a loud one. In this study the softest level tested (60-70 dB, roughly conversational loudness) was preferred, and louder levels gave no heart-rate advantage. Levels below 60 dB were not tested. Hearing-risk warnings at high volume rest on general hearing-safety guidance, not on this study.

citation.authors: Staum MJ, Brotons M
citation.title: The effect of music amplitude on the relaxation response

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata + PubMed/Europe PMC abstract (PMID 10806471). The OUP full text is paywalled and the DeepDyve preview is blocked.
verification.problems: Metadata, amplitude ranges, timing, randomization and the preference results all match the abstract. Issues: (1) Heart rate was recorded only in 'a sample of subjects' (size not given in the abstract), so 'Heart rate did not differ by amplitude' overstates how much weight the null can carry. (2) Omitted: self-reports showed a wide variety of individual preferences, not always consistent with the dial (CRDI) data, and reported relaxation rose over the session. finding_zh '绝大多数人认为' (the vast majority of people thought) turns an aggregate dial preference into a claim about individuals. (3) The app_implication 'set a level quieter than normal conversation' goes beyond the data. The softest level tested was 60-70 dB, roughly conversational loudness, and nothing quieter was tested. The hearing-risk point comes from general guidance, not from this study.

claims.topic: Continuous white or broadband noise as a sleep aid
claims.finding: Systematic review (PROSPERO CRD42020148736) of 38 articles on continuous white or similar broadband noise and sleep; animal studies and studies using intermittent noise to disrupt sleep or enhance slow-wave activity were excluded. Findings ranged from improved to disrupted sleep, with heterogeneity in noise characteristics, sleep measurement, adherence, control conditions and simultaneous co-interventions. Following GRADE, the quality of evidence that continuous noise improves sleep was very low. The authors say more research with objective sleep measures and detailed noise descriptions is needed before continuous noise is promoted as a sleep aid, especially since it may also negatively affect sleep and hearing.
claims.finding_zh: 系统综述（PROSPERO注册号CRD42020148736）纳入38篇关于持续白噪声或类似宽频噪声与睡眠的研究，排除了动物研究，以及用间歇噪声干扰睡眠或增强慢波的研究。结果从改善睡眠到干扰睡眠都有；噪声参数、睡眠测量方法、依从性、对照条件以及同时进行的其他干预差异很大。按GRADE评价，“持续噪声能改善睡眠”的证据质量为极低。作者认为，在有客观睡眠测量、噪声描述详细的研究之前，不宜把持续噪声当作助眠手段推广，何况它也可能对睡眠和听力不利。
claims.sample: 38 articles
claims.limitations: Mostly very small studies (the authors said in an interview that most had no more than 10 participants). Narrative synthesis with no pooled estimate reported; the closed-access full text was not read. Populations and settings were mixed: the reference list includes studies in newborns and young children, students, tinnitus patients, laboratory volunteers and hospital/critical-care patients, so results do not map neatly onto healthy adults sleeping at home. The hearing-risk warning is a precautionary concern, not a measured outcome.
claims.app_implication: White/pink/brown noise appears only as optional masking of disturbing environmental noise, badged '证据很弱，非助眠疗法'; timer and lowest effective volume by default; never default to all-night playback.

citation.authors: Riedy SM, Smith MG, Rocha S, et al.
citation.title: Noise as a sleep aid: A systematic review

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata (DOI 10.1016/j.smrv.2020.101385); Europe PMC/PubMed abstract (PMID 33007706, pub types: Systematic Review only); Crossref reference list (58 refs); authors' Q&A on HMP Global Learning Network. Full text is closed access (OpenAlex/Europe PMC) and was not read.
verification.problems: Metadata and the finding/finding_zh match the abstract: 38 included articles; heterogeneity in noise characteristics, measurement, adherence and controls; findings from improved to disrupted sleep; GRADE very low; may harm sleep and hearing. Year 2021 is correct (online Sept 2020, issue Feb 2021, vol 55). Problem: the limitation 'many hospital or ICU settings' is unsupported. Neither the abstract nor the authors' interview says it. The reference list shows a mixed set: newborns/infants, toddlers/children (autism, ADHD), college students, tinnitus patients, laboratory volunteers, and only a few hospital/CCU/critical-care studies. 'No meta-analysis' fits the abstract and PubMed indexing (no pooled estimate) but could not be confirmed from the full text. Also added: the exclusion of intermittent/slow-wave-enhancement studies, the authors' statement that most studies had no more than 10 participants, and that the hearing concern is precautionary.

claims.topic: Singing bowls: human health effects
claims.finding: Systematic review (7 databases searched October 2019; descriptive synthesis, no meta-analysis) that found only four peer-reviewed studies of singing-bowl interventions. These were an RCT in chronic spinal pain (n=54; quartz bowl struck on the back vs a placebo bowl that was not struck vs no treatment); a randomised crossover trial in healthy adults (51 analysed; 12 min of bowl sound vs silence, each followed by guided relaxation); and two uncontrolled pre-post studies (12 outpatients with metastatic cancer; 62 adults in one group sound-meditation session). The abstract lists improvements in affect, anxiety, depression, fatigue, tension, blood pressure, heart rate and other measures, but these came mostly from the uncontrolled studies. In the crossover trial, affect fell equally after silence; only systolic blood pressure and heart rate fell more with the bowl. In the RCT, current pain fell about as much with the placebo bowl as with the struck bowl (0-100 VAS: 64.4 to 48.6 vs 59.8 to 43.7), and objective measures did not differ. The cancer pilot found no significant change in anxiety, depression, fatigue or quality of life. Citing the few studies and the risk of bias, the authors said they could not recommend singing-bowl therapies.
claims.finding_zh: 系统综述（2019年10月检索7个数据库，只做描述性汇总，没有做荟萃分析）只找到4项关于颂钵的同行评审研究：1项慢性脊柱疼痛的随机对照试验（54人；在背上敲击石英颂钵、放上颂钵但不敲的“安慰剂”、不处理三组），1项健康成人的随机交叉试验（分析51人；先听12分钟颂钵或静坐，再做引导放松），以及2项没有对照组的前后比较研究（12名转移性癌症门诊患者；62名参加一次团体颂钵冥想的成人）。摘要列出情绪、焦虑、抑郁、疲劳、紧张、血压、心率等方面的改善，但这些大多来自没有对照的研究：交叉试验中，静坐组的情绪变化与颂钵组相同，只有收缩压和心率下降更多；随机对照试验中，“安慰剂”组当前疼痛的下降与真颂钵组相近（0–100分视觉模拟评分：64.4→48.6 对 59.8→43.7），客观指标无组间差异；癌症小样本研究中焦虑、抑郁、疲劳和生活质量均无显著变化。由于研究太少且偏倚风险高，作者表示目前不能推荐颂钵疗法。
claims.sample: 4 studies (n=54, 51 analysed, 12 and 62; about 179 participants)
claims.limitations: Only four small studies. Two were uncontrolled pre-post designs, and neither randomised study reported blinding or allocation concealment (PEDro 3/10 and 6/10). The review's own results do not fully support its abstract's list of improvements: the cancer pilot's Distress Thermometer score rose (2.4 to 5.3) and its breathing-rate change had p=0.063. Adverse events were not systematically reported. Per-study details were checked in the authors' submitted manuscript (University of Adelaide repository), whose abstract matches the published one. Later reviews do not change the picture: Cai et al. 2025 (Integr Med Res; 19 studies including 9 RCTs, all RCTs at high risk of bias) and Lin et al. 2025 (Healthcare; 14 studies, narrative synthesis only, no meta-analysis).
claims.app_implication: Bowl and bell timbres may be used for cues and ambience as an aesthetic choice. Never label them 颂钵疗愈 or credit them with physiological effects: in the only parallel RCT, an unstruck placebo bowl relieved pain at least as much as a struck one.

citation.authors: Stanhope J, Weinstein P
citation.title: The human health effects of singing bowls: A systematic review

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; PubMed abstract (PMID 32507429); full text of the authors' submitted manuscript incl. Table 1 (University of Adelaide repository, hdl 2440/124409), whose abstract matches PubMed; PubMed abstracts and PMC full text of Lin et al. 2025 (PMC12385955) and Cai et al. 2025 (PMC12063014)
verification.problems: Metadata is correct (Stanhope J, Weinstein P; Complement Ther Med 2020;51:102412; DOI and PMID resolve to this work). The finding accurately paraphrases the abstract but leaves out the nulls in the full text. In the two randomised studies most effects were matched by the comparison. Landry crossover: affect fell equally after silence; only systolic BP and heart rate showed a group-by-time interaction. Wepner RCT: current pain fell about as much with an unstruck placebo bowl (64.4 to 48.6 vs 59.8 to 43.7), and objective measures did not differ. The anxiety, depression, fatigue and tension improvements came from an uncontrolled pre-post study (Goldsby, n=62). The cancer pilot (Bidin, n=12) found no significant change in anxiety, depression, fatigue or QoL. The abstract's 'improvements in distress' and 'respiratory rate' conflict with the review's own results: the Distress Thermometer rose from 2.4 to 5.3, and the breathing-rate change had p=0.063. The limitation 'mostly uncontrolled studies' is wrong: 2 of the 4 were randomised (an RCT and a randomised crossover) and 2 were pre-post. The Lin et al. 2025 detail (Healthcare; 14 studies; narrative only, no meta-analysis) is confirmed. In finding_zh, '其中2项设计等级低' sits right after the cancer and spinal-pain studies, so it can be misread as referring to them; one of those was an RCT.

claims.topic: 432 Hz vs 440 Hz tuning
claims.finding: Double-blind crossover pilot study in 33 volunteers without acute or chronic disease who, on different days, listened for 20 min to the same film-soundtrack music tuned to 440 Hz and to 432 Hz. Compared with 440 Hz, 432 Hz music was associated with a 'marked decrease' in mean heart rate (-4.79 bpm, p = 0.05), slight non-significant decreases in systolic and diastolic blood pressure, and a slight decrease in respiratory rate (about 1 breath/min, p = 0.06, not significant). Participants reported being more focused and more satisfied after the 432 Hz sessions (significance not stated in the abstract). The authors conclude that the data suggest 432 Hz music can decrease heart rate more than 440 Hz, and call for larger randomized controlled trials. A corrigendum to the article was published in 2020.
claims.finding_zh: 双盲交叉预实验：33名无急、慢性疾病的志愿者在不同日子各听20分钟同一套电影配乐，分别以440 Hz和432 Hz调音。与440 Hz相比，432 Hz时平均心率“明显下降”（−4.79次/分，p=0.05，处于显著性边缘）；收缩压和舒张压略降，但不显著；呼吸频率略降（约1次/分，p=0.06，不显著）。受试者自述听432 Hz时更专注、总体更满意（摘要未说明是否有统计学意义）。作者认为数据提示432 Hz音乐可能比440 Hz更能降低心率，并呼吁开展更大样本的随机对照试验。该文于2020年发表过一则更正。
claims.sample: n=33 volunteers without acute or chronic disease
claims.limitations: Very small pilot with a borderline p-value (p=0.05). Several outcomes, and the abstract describes no correction for multiple comparisons. A single music set. Session order and randomization are not described in the abstract, and neither the paywalled full text nor the 2020 corrigendum was reviewed. Studies of 432 Hz tuning by other groups are few, small and inconsistent: a 2025 randomized crossover in 43 cancer patients found a slightly larger heart-rate drop with a 432 Hz than a 443 Hz monochord (median -3 vs -1 bpm, p=0.04), while a 2025 warm-up study in 28 kickboxers reported the lowest mean heart rate with 440 Hz music. 432 vs 440 Hz is only a ~32-cent (1.8%) pitch shift.
claims.app_implication: Generative music is tuned to A4=440 Hz. A 432 Hz setting may exist only as a tuning preference marked 无健康声明, never as a 'healing frequency'.

citation.authors: Calamassi D, Pomponi GP
citation.title: Music tuned to 440 Hz versus 432 Hz and the health effects: a double-blind cross-over pilot study

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata + PubMed abstract (PMID 31031095); Crossref and PubMed records of the 2020 corrigendum (10.1016/j.explore.2020.01.001, PMID 32113613; no text available). Full text paywalled; a copy was available only on a piracy site and was not used. Also read the PubMed abstracts of later 432 Hz studies by other groups (Aravena 2020; Jebabli 2025 PeerJ and Sci Rep; Hohneck 2025, including Table 2 of its PMC full text).
verification.problems: Metadata, PMID and the 2020 corrigendum (Explore 16(1):8) are confirmed. (1) The abstract reports 'a marked decrease in the mean of heart rate (-4.79 bpm, p = 0.05)... compared to 440 Hz' and concludes 432 Hz 'can decrease heart rate more than 440 Hz'. The claim's 'lower mean heart rate' (zh '432 Hz时平均心率低4.79次/分') states it as a level difference, which the abstract does not establish; reworded to the abstract's framing. (2) For focus and satisfaction, the abstract gives no significance; this is now stated. (3) The limitation 'no independent replication' is inaccurate: studies by other groups exist with mixed results. Hohneck 2025 (randomized crossover, 43 cancer patients) found a larger heart-rate drop with a 432 Hz than a 443 Hz monochord (median -3 vs -1 bpm, between-condition p=0.04). Jebabli 2025 (PeerJ, 28 kickboxers) reported the lowest warm-up heart rate with 440 Hz music. Aravena 2020 found similar anxiety reduction with both tunings. (4) 'Many uncorrected outcomes' cannot be confirmed without the full text, so it was softened. The content of the corrigendum is unknown.

claims.topic: 528 Hz ('Solfeggio') music
claims.finding: Small within-subject experiment in 9 healthy adults (1 man, 8 women, aged 26-37). On separate days they listened through a speaker for 5 min to two versions of the same soothing piano music: '528 Hz music' (tuned to A4 = 444 Hz so that its scale contains 528 Hz) and standard A4 = 440 Hz. Participants were not told which version they heard. Only within-condition pre-post changes were tested (Wilcoxon signed-rank). After the 528 Hz version, salivary cortisol was significantly lower 30 min later (0.43 to 0.25, analysed with lag-shifted samples), oxytocin rose significantly immediately after listening (37.57 to 73.58), and POMS-2 tension-anxiety (48.44 to 43.67) and Total Mood Disturbance (45.56 to 42.00) fell significantly. After the 440 Hz version, no salivary marker or mood score changed significantly, although cortisol, oxytocin and most mood scores moved in the same direction. LF/HF fell significantly after both versions (ECG analysed in 8 participants). The paper reports no direct 528 vs 440 Hz comparison.
claims.finding_zh: 小型受试者内实验：9名健康成人（1男8女，26–37岁）在不同日子通过音箱各听5分钟同一首舒缓钢琴曲的两个版本：“528 Hz音乐”（以A4=444 Hz定音，使音阶中包含528 Hz）和标准A4=440 Hz版本。受试者不知道自己听的是哪个版本。论文只检验了各条件内部的前后变化（Wilcoxon符号秩检验）。听528 Hz版本后，唾液皮质醇30分钟后显著降低（0.43→0.25，按时滞平移样本分析），催产素在听完即刻显著升高（37.57→73.58），POMS-2紧张-焦虑（48.44→43.67）和情绪困扰总分（45.56→42.00）显著下降。听440 Hz版本后，唾液指标和情绪评分均无显著变化，但皮质醇、催产素和多数情绪评分的变化方向相同。两个版本听后LF/HF都显著下降（心电数据来自8人）。论文没有对528 Hz与440 Hz做直接比较。
claims.study_type: within-subject experiment (two listening sessions on separate days; order not reported)
claims.sample: n=9 healthy adults (ECG analysed in 8)
claims.limitations: Tiny sample and a single 5-min exposure. Only within-condition tests were run, so a significant change in one session and a non-significant change in the other does not show that the two versions differ. Condition order and randomization not reported. Many outcomes and time points, with no correction for multiple comparisons. The '528 Hz' manipulation is only A4 = 444 vs 440 Hz tuning (~16 cents, about 0.9% higher pitch). Published in a Scientific Research Publishing open-access journal not indexed in PubMed. No independent replication of the 528 vs 440 Hz comparison found; a 2026 RCT by other authors compared 528 Hz and 432 Hz music with no music on different salivary markers.
claims.app_implication: No 528 Hz or Solfeggio presets and no 'DNA repair' or 'healing frequency' language. Users searching for them are shown this evidence card.

citation.authors: Akimoto K, Hu A, Yamaguchi T, et al.
citation.title: Effect of 528 Hz music on the endocrine system and autonomic nervous system

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata (Akimoto K, Hu A, Yamaguchi T, Kobayashi H; Health 2018;10(9):1159-1170) + publisher full text on SCIRP (paperid=87146; DOI resolves there). PubMed and Europe PMC searches confirm it is not indexed. PubMed search for later 528 Hz studies.
verification.problems: Metadata and the reported results are confirmed against the full text. (1) The paper never calls itself a pilot. It is a small within-subject experiment; condition order and randomization are not reported. (2) The full text shows only within-condition Wilcoxon signed-rank tests ('differences between time points in each condition'), so no 528 vs 440 Hz comparison exists anywhere in the paper, not just 'in the abstract'. In the 440 Hz session, cortisol, oxytocin and most mood scores moved in the same direction without reaching significance. (3) A key design detail was omitted: '528 Hz music' is the same piano music tuned to A4=444 Hz so that its scale contains 528 Hz (only ~16 cents above 440 Hz). It was played through a speaker, and participants were not told which version they heard. (4) Total Mood Disturbance also fell significantly after 528 Hz. ECG was analysed in 8 of 9 participants, and cortisol was analysed with lag-shifted samples. (5) 'No independent replication' is refined: a 2026 RCT by other authors (Bozok et al., Brain Behav, n=162) compared 528 Hz and 432 Hz music with no music on other salivary markers, which does not replicate the 528 vs 440 Hz comparison.

claims.topic: Reference model: wellness claims vs disease claims (US FDA)
claims.finding: FDA final guidance 'General Wellness: Policy for Low Risk Devices' (issued 6 Jan 2026; supersedes the version of 27 Sep 2019). Claims about 'relaxation or stress management', 'mental acuity' and 'sleep management' that do not refer to diseases count as general wellness (e.g., 'Claims to promote relaxation or manage stress'). 'A claim that a product helps treat an anxiety disorder' does not. A second category allows healthy-lifestyle claims that 'may help living well with' a condition, e.g., software that 'coaches breathing techniques and relaxation skills, which, as part of a healthy lifestyle, may help living well with migraine headaches'.
claims.finding_zh: 美国FDA最终指南《一般健康：低风险设备政策》（2026年1月6日发布，取代2019年9月27日版）。不提及疾病的“放松或压力管理”“思维敏锐”“睡眠管理”类声明属于一般健康用途（如“帮助放松或管理压力”）；“帮助治疗焦虑症”则不属于。第二类允许“作为健康生活方式的一部分，可能有助于与某种疾病更好地共处”的表述，例如教授呼吸和放松技巧的软件“作为健康生活方式的一部分，可能有助于偏头痛患者更好地生活”。
claims.sample: n/a
claims.limitations: US policy and not binding in China. China's Advertising Law is stricter (no disease-treatment claims at all in non-medical ads), so the second-category 'living well with [disease]' phrasing must not be copied into Chinese marketing.
claims.app_implication: Use FDA category-1 wording as a positive template for what Huishen is: 放松、压力管理、睡前放松、专注练习. In China, never name a disease in an efficacy claim.

citation.authors: U.S. Food and Drug Administration, Center for Devices and Radiological Health
citation.title: General Wellness: Policy for Low Risk Devices. Guidance for Industry and Food and Drug Administration Staff

verification.checked_against: FDA guidance landing page (Final; issued January 2026; docket FDA-2014-N-1039; CDRH; content current as of 01/06/2026) and the guidance PDF (fda.gov/media/90652/download): cover page, Section III and Section V
verification.problems: No discrepancies. The cover page reads 'Document issued on January 6, 2026. This document supersedes "General Wellness: Policy for Low Risk Devices" issued on September 27, 2019.' Every quote is verbatim: the first-category list (relaxation or stress management, mental acuity, sleep management), 'Claims to promote relaxation or manage stress', 'A claim that a product helps treat an anxiety disorder' (listed among claims outside the category), and the Software Product U migraine example. Minor simplification, not an error: the second category is limited to chronic diseases or conditions where the role of a healthy lifestyle is well understood and accepted, and the policy also requires the product to be low risk. The 2026 text also gives the example 'may help living well with anxiety' (Software Product V). The claim's limitation rightly says such wording must not be copied into Chinese marketing.

claims.topic: Mainland China national psychological assistance hotline 12356
claims.finding: National Health Commission notice 国卫医政函〔2024〕259号 (dated 6 Dec 2024) set 12356 as the national unified psychological assistance hotline number and required it to connect nationwide by 00:00 on 1 May 2025. In principle each prefecture-level city has at least 1 line with at least 2 seats, providing 'not less than 18 hours' of service per day. Old numbers and 12356 both work during a transition period, and linkage with 110, 119 and 120 is to be built. Xinhua (8 May 2025) reported nationwide use from 1 May 2025 (500+ lines, 1,000+ seats, nearly 8,000 counsellors). People's Daily (28 Nov 2025) reported all existing local hotlines connected to 12356, with Beijing's line staffed 24 hours.
claims.finding_zh: 国家卫生健康委《关于应用“12356”全国统一心理援助热线电话号码的通知》（国卫医政函〔2024〕259号，2024年12月6日）将12356设为全国统一心理援助热线，要求2025年5月1日0时前全国可拨通。原则上每个设区的市至少开通1条热线，每条至少2个坐席，每日服务不少于18小时。过渡期内原号码与12356均可接通，并推进与110、119、120的联动。新华社（2025年5月8日）报道，自5月1日起全国统一使用12356（热线500余条、坐席1000余个、咨询员近8000名）。人民日报（2025年11月28日）报道，各地既有心理援助热线均已接入12356，北京热线24小时服务。
claims.study_type: government notice with official media confirmation
claims.sample: n/a
claims.limitations: Official text checked on the State Council policy document library (gov.cn, which lists the NHC website as its source); the nhc.gov.cn page refused automated access. Rollout confirmed by China Daily (26 Dec 2024), Xinhua (8 May 2025, https://www.news.cn/politics/20250508/b45e439c15bb4732858ad5c7640e9ba9/c.html) and People's Daily (28 Nov 2025, p. 13). Hours vary by region: the notice requires at least 18 h/day per line, cities without capacity may rely on the provincial line, and some regions (e.g., Beijing) run 24 h. Xinhua reported low connection rates and queues as a real problem in some regions; answer rate and quality were not evaluated.
claims.app_implication: Primary in-app crisis number for mainland China is 12356, labelled 各地服务时段不同（每日不少于18小时，部分地区24小时）. Lines can be busy, so always show 120/110 for immediate danger and a 24-hour alternative (希望24热线 400-161-9995) next to it. Re-verify every 6 months.

citation.authors: National Health Commission of the People's Republic of China (国家卫生健康委员会)
citation.title: 国家卫生健康委关于应用“12356”全国统一心理援助热线电话号码的通知（国卫医政函〔2024〕259号）
citation.venue: National Health Commission notice; official text in the State Council policy document library (gov.cn)

verification.checked_against: Official text on gov.cn State Council policy document library (source: NHC website; 成文日期 2024-12-06); cn-healthcare.com reprint; Xinhua 8 May 2025 article (full text); People's Daily 28 Nov 2025 p.13 (full text); China Daily 26 Dec 2024 (search listing only)
verification.problems: Content matches the official text: 259号, dated 6 Dec 2024; connection by 00:00 on 1 May 2025; at least 1 line per prefecture-level city with at least 2 seats and at least 18 h/day; transition period; 110/119/120 linkage. Xinhua (500+ lines, 1,000+ seats, nearly 8,000 counsellors; all 31 provinces) and People's Daily (all local hotlines connected; Beijing 17 seats, 24 h) also match. claims.topic: PRC Advertising Law limits on disease-treatment and medical claims
claims.finding: PRC Advertising Law (revised 2015; amended 2018 and 2021). Art. 17: 'Except for medical, drug and medical-device advertisements, no other advertisement may involve disease-treatment functions, or use medical terminology or terms likely to confuse the promoted goods with drugs or medical devices.' Art. 28: false advertising includes using fabricated, forged or unverifiable research results, statistics, survey results, abstracts or quotations as proof (item 3), and fabricating the effects of using a product or service (item 4). Art. 58 penalties for violating Art. 17: fines of 1–3× the advertising cost (¥100,000–200,000 if the cost cannot be calculated or is clearly too low); in serious cases 3–5× (¥200,000–1,000,000), with possible revocation of the business licence. Art. 19: internet information service providers may not publish disguised medical, drug, medical-device or health-food advertisements in the form of health or wellness knowledge.
claims.finding_zh: 《中华人民共和国广告法》（2015年修订，2018年、2021年修正）。第十七条：“除医疗、药品、医疗器械广告外，禁止其他任何广告涉及疾病治疗功能，并不得使用医疗用语或者易使推销的商品与药品、医疗器械相混淆的用语。”第二十八条：使用虚构、伪造或者无法验证的科研成果、统计资料、调查结果、文摘、引用语等作证明材料，或虚构使用商品、接受服务的效果，构成虚假广告。第五十八条：违反第十七条的，处广告费用一倍以上三倍以下罚款（广告费用无法计算或明显偏低的，处十万元以上二十万元以下）；情节严重的，处三倍以上五倍以下罚款（或二十万元以上一百万元以下），可吊销营业执照。第十九条：互联网信息服务提供者不得以介绍健康、养生知识等形式，变相发布医疗、药品、医疗器械、保健食品广告。
claims.sample: n/a
claims.limitations: Applies to commercial advertising (store listings, ads, marketing pages, and arguably promotional in-app copy). How 'medical terminology' is interpreted in enforcement varies. Not legal advice. The amendment of 29 April 2021 only removed the advertising-release registration rules (Art. 29, related wording in Arts. 55, 57 and 58 para. 3, and the former Art. 60) and renumbered the later articles. Arts. 17, 19 and 28 and the first paragraph of Art. 58 read the same in the 2018 and 2021 texts.
claims.app_implication: Marketing and app-store copy must never claim to treat or relieve any disease (失眠症、焦虑症、抑郁症、高血压等) or use medical terms (治疗、疗效、治愈、疗程、处方等). Every number shown must trace to a real, citable source, so the in-app citation system doubles as compliance. Evidence pages must stay neutral and separate from purchase prompts.

verification.checked_against: gov.cn page at the cited URL (2018-amended text); consolidated 2021 text on samr.gov.cn (State Administration for Market Regulation) and scjgj.beijing.gov.cn; NPC Standing Committee decision of 29 April 2021 amending eight laws (Wikisource transcription)

These articles read the same in the 2018 and 2021 texts. The problem is the link. The citation names the 2021 version, so the URL does not lead to the version cited. Replaced it with SAMR's official consolidated 2021 text and updated the venue and limitations.

claims.topic: Software becomes a medical device in China when its intended use is medical
claims.finding: Regulations on the Supervision and Administration of Medical Devices (State Council Decree No. 739, 2021), Art. 103: a medical device includes 'the required computer software'. Its purposes include 'diagnosis, prevention, monitoring, treatment or alleviation of disease' and 'examination, replacement, regulation or support of physiological structure or physiological processes'.
claims.finding_zh: 《医疗器械监督管理条例》（国务院令第739号，2021年）第一百零三条：医疗器械包括“所需要的计算机软件”，其目的包括“疾病的诊断、预防、监护、治疗或者缓解”以及“生理结构或者生理过程的检验、替代、调节或者支持”等。
claims.sample: n/a
claims.limitations: Classification turns on the intended use the maker claims. NMPA software guidance and later revisions of the regulation were not reviewed here. Not legal advice.
claims.app_implication: Keep Huishen's stated intended use within relaxation, attention and sleep-routine wellness. Do not claim to diagnose (e.g., labelling users 'anxious' or 'depressed'), monitor, treat or alleviate disease, or to regulate physiological processes for medical ends (e.g., 降血压, 调节自主神经以治疗……). Such claims may make the software a regulated medical device.

citation.authors: State Council of the People's Republic of China (国务院)
citation.title: 医疗器械监督管理条例（国务院令第739号）

verification.checked_against: Official text on gov.cn (State Council Gazette 2021 No. 9, Decree No. 739: promulgation note and Art. 103); State Council Decree No. 797 (2024) list of amendments (official text reposted on mee.gov.cn)

Art. 103 contains '包括所需要的计算机软件', purpose (一) '疾病的诊断、预防、监护、治疗或者缓解' and purpose (三) '生理结构或者生理过程的检验、替代、调节或者支持', exactly as quoted.
