The device definition quoted here is unchanged, so the limitation 'later revisions not reviewed' could now say this.

claims.topic: WHO-ITU safe listening dose limits for personal audio
claims.finding: WHO-ITU safe-listening standard ITU-T H.870 (08/2018) recommends a weekly 'sound allowance' with two selectable modes. Mode 1 (adults): 1.6 Pa²h per 7 days, derived from 80 dBA for 40 h/week. Mode 2 (sensitive users, e.g., children): 0.51 Pa²h, derived from 75 dBA for 40 h/week. Under the equal-energy principle, Mode 1 allows about 2.5 h/week at 92 dBA and 75 min at 95 dBA. Recommended features include dose tracking, warnings at preset levels of allowance use, volume limiting with automatic reduction if the user does not respond, and parental volume locks.
claims.finding_zh: 世界卫生组织与国际电信联盟的安全聆听标准ITU-T H.870（2018年8月版）建议设立“每周声音额度”，分两档。成人档：每7天1.6 Pa²h，相当于80 dBA每周40小时。敏感人群档（如儿童）：0.51 Pa²h，相当于75 dBA每周40小时。按等能量原则，成人在92 dBA下每周约2.5小时、95 dBA下约75分钟就用完额度。建议功能：剂量追踪、额度用到预设比例时提醒、音量限制（用户不处理则自动降低音量）、家长音量锁。
claims.sample: n/a (standard based on the equal-energy principle and occupational exposure limits)
claims.limitations: Designed for music on personal audio devices, not overnight sleep sounds. Actual dBA at the ear depends on headphones and device and cannot be measured by a web app. A 03/2022 revision exists; figures were verified against the 2018 text. WHO's 2026 consumer Q&A gives the same adult figure and advises keeping device volume at no more than 60% of maximum.
claims.app_implication: Sleep sounds play for hours: default to low volume, use an auto-fade timer, recommend a speaker across the room over earbuds, and warn above 60% device volume. Any child or baby context uses the lower sensitive-user reference.

citation.authors: ITU-T (with World Health Organization)
citation.title: Recommendation ITU-T H.870 (08/2018): Guidelines for safe listening devices/systems
citation.venue: International Telecommunication Union, Telecommunication Standardization Sector

verification.checked_against: ITU-T H.870 (08/2018) full-text PDF (Summary; clause 7.1 operational modes; Tables 1-2; clause 11 warnings and auto volume reduction; 13.1 volume limiting; 13.2 parental control); H.870 V2 (03/2022) full text; Erratum 1 (03/2019); ITU version listing page; WHO Q&A 'Deafness and hearing loss: Safe listening' (dated 6 March 2026)
verification.problems: No discrepancies in the finding, figures or citation. Mode 1 = 1.6 Pa²h/7 days and Mode 2 = 0.51 Pa²h/7 days, from 80/75 dBA for 40 h/week; Table 1 gives 2.5 h at 92 dBA and 75 min at 95 dBA. Dose tracking, warnings at preset allowance levels, automatic volume reduction when unacknowledged, and a parental lock are all present. Context: the 08/2018 edition is superseded by H.870 V2 (approved 2022-03-16), which keeps the same figures and tables and makes Mode 1 exposure determination and the password-protected volume lock 'shall' requirements. Erratum 1 (03/2019) only replaced Figure 11-1. The WHO Q&A (6 Mar 2026) confirms 80 dB for up to 40 h/week and 'no more than 60% of maximum'. 'High' reflects the source's authority; the thresholds are precautionary values extrapolated from occupational limits (EU Decision 2009/490/EC).

claims.topic: APA App Evaluation Model as a public transparency checklist
claims.finding: The American Psychiatric Association's App Evaluation Model (App Advisor) has six steps: Background; Access; Privacy and Security; Clinical Foundation; Usability; Integration toward patient-centered goals. Questions include: 'Has the app been updated in the last 180 days?'; 'Does the app claim to be medical?'; 'Can users opt out of data collection or delete data?'; 'Is the app equipped to respond to potential clinical safety concerns? Does the app disclose how it responds to these safety concerns?'; 'Does the app use AI? If so, does it describe how AI is used?'; 'Are there relevant sources of evidence supporting effectiveness of the app?'; 'Does the app disclose clinical retention rates?'
claims.finding_zh: 美国精神医学学会（APA）App评估模型（App Advisor）分六步：背景；可及性；隐私与安全；临床基础；可用性；与以患者为中心的目标整合。问题包括：“过去180天内是否更新过？”“是否自称有医疗用途？”“用户能否拒绝数据收集或删除数据？”“能否应对潜在的临床安全问题？是否公开应对方式？”“是否使用AI？如使用，是否说明如何使用？”“是否有支持有效性的证据来源？”“是否公开临床留存率？”
claims.study_type: professional association evaluation framework (official web page)
claims.sample: n/a
claims.limitations: A framework to help clinicians and patients choose apps, not a certification. It has no numeric score or pass mark: the page calls it a hierarchical rating system but says an app need not meet any minimum number of levels. APA's glossary defines 'clinical retention rates' as the percentage of patients or participants who stay engaged in a clinical program, treatment or trial over a set period. Undated page (©2026), accessed 2026-10-22.
claims.app_implication: Publish a 安全与证据 page that answers each APA question: last update date, a not-medical statement, how safety concerns are handled, data deletion, AI use, evidence with citations, and honest retention data (the share of users who stay engaged over a stated period).

citation.authors: American Psychiatric Association
citation.title: The App Evaluation Model

verification.checked_against: psychiatry.org page 'The App Evaluation Model' (fetched 2026-10-23, ©2026) and the APA App Advisor glossary
verification.problems: The English finding is verbatim and correct: the six steps (Background; Access; Privacy and Security; Clinical Foundation; Usability; Integration toward Patient-Centered Goals) and all seven quoted questions. Two small issues. (1) finding_zh renders 'Does the app disclose clinical retention rates?' as '是否公开留存率', dropping 'clinical'. APA's glossary defines clinical retention rates as the percentage of patients or participants who stay engaged in a clinical program, treatment regimen or trial over a set period, which is not the same as ordinary app user retention. (2) The limitation 'no scoring' oversimplifies. The page calls the model a 'hierarchical rating system', but it sets no numeric score and no minimum number of levels an app must meet, and it says Step 3 has no scoring system.

claims.topic: Hyperventilation is the clinical seizure-provocation test; contraindications
claims.finding: The IFCN/ILAE minimum standards for routine and sleep EEG suggest that hyperventilation (HV), intermittent photic stimulation and eyes-open/eyes-closed recording be part of routine or sleep EEG unless contraindicated (a conditional, consensus-based recommendation). Protocol: 'The patient is instructed to breathe deep 15–30 times/minute at least three minutes', and the patient should be under continuous surveillance during the recording. 'In some patients, numbness or tingling of perioral region and fingers may occur; if so, this is not a reason to discontinue hyperventilation.' Patients should be told in advance about the adverse effects of activation procedures, particularly seizures. Listed HV contraindications: sickle cell disease or trait; Moya-Moya disease and syndrome; cerebrovascular malformations including aneurysms; cerebrovascular events in the last three months; raised intracranial pressure; myocardial infarction; cardiac arrhythmias and other severe cardiac disorders; severe pulmonary disorders; pregnancy. In the evidence reviewed, seizures during HV were 'relatively rare'. Of patients referred for suspected epilepsy, 2.2% (69/3,170) had HV-provoked seizures and 1/3,170 had a generalised tonic-clonic seizure, with no significant cerebrovascular, cardiovascular or respiratory events. In a study of 100 healthy young men, HV elicited no epileptiform activity.
claims.finding_zh: 国际临床神经生理联盟与国际抗癫痫联盟（IFCN/ILAE）2023年常规及睡眠脑电图最低标准建议，除非有禁忌，常规或睡眠脑电图应包括过度通气、闪光刺激和睁闭眼记录。这是基于专家共识的有条件推荐。做法是让患者“每分钟深呼吸15–30次，持续至少3分钟”，记录全程应有人持续监护。部分患者会出现口周和手指麻木、刺痛，指南明确说这“不是停止过度通气的理由”。检查前应告知患者诱发试验可能的不良反应，尤其是癫痫发作。过度通气的禁忌包括：镰状细胞病或携带者；烟雾病及烟雾综合征；含动脉瘤在内的脑血管畸形；近3个月内脑血管事件；颅内压增高；心肌梗死；心律失常及其他严重心脏病；严重肺部疾病；妊娠。指南汇总的证据显示，过度通气诱发的发作“相对少见”。在因疑似癫痫转诊的患者中，2.2%（69/3170）出现过度通气诱发的发作，其中1/3170为全面强直阵挛发作，未见明显的脑血管、心血管或呼吸系统事件。在一项100名健康年轻男性的研究中，过度通气没有诱发任何癫痫样放电。
claims.study_type: international clinical practice standard (IFCN/ILAE; systematic evidence review, GRADE plus modified Delphi)
claims.sample: n/a (guideline; overall evidence quality rated low to moderate)
claims.limitations: The guideline rates the evidence for HV's diagnostic yield as moderate. However, all included provocation studies were at high risk of bias, overall evidence was rated low, and the contraindication list is expert consensus with no graded evidence or risk estimates. It is written for a continuously observed HV test of at least 3 minutes in people being investigated for seizures, not for self-guided breathwork. It does not quantify risk for healthy people or for longer or repeated sessions. The seizure figures come from Kane et al. 2014 (Seizure 23:129-134), a UK multicentre service evaluation cited by the guideline.
claims.app_implication: Several minutes of sustained fast or deep breathing (the EEG test uses 15–30 deep breaths per minute for at least 3 minutes) is closely related to the manoeuvre clinicians use to provoke seizures in people with suspected epilepsy. Wim Hof-style power breathing, conscious connected breathing and fast pranayama rounds such as bhastrika or kapalabhati can produce it, so Huishen does not offer these practices. Use this contraindication list, plus epilepsy, in the breathing-safety check. Tingling around the mouth or in the fingers is a sign of over-breathing. The guideline says tingling is not a reason to stop a supervised EEG test. Huishen's rule to return to gentle, normal breathing is a conservative choice for unsupervised use, not a guideline requirement.

citation.authors: Peltola ME, Leitinger M, Halford JJ, et al.
citation.title: Routine and sleep EEG: Minimum recording standards of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology and the International League Against Epilepsy

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; Europe PMC abstract; PMC author-manuscript full text (PMC10006292, via NCBI efetch), sections 3.5.1–3.5.4.1, Table 3 and Key points; PubMed abstract of Kane et al. 2014 (PMID 24252807)
verification.problems: (1) 'Recommend' overstates the guideline. It 'suggest[s]' that HV, photic stimulation and eyes-open/closed recording be part of routine or sleep EEG unless contraindicated, and calls this a conditional recommendation formulated by modified Delphi. (2) A key sentence is left out: 'In some patients, numbness or tingling of perioral region and fingers may occur; if so, this is not a reason to discontinue hyperventilation.' The app_implication's 'tingling ... stop' reads as if it came from the source, but the source says the opposite for supervised EEG. (3) Minor: the contraindication is 'Moya-Moya disease and syndrome'. (4) Balancing context from the guideline is missing. Seizures during HV were 'relatively rare': 2.2% (69/3,170) of patients with suspected epilepsy, 1/3,170 a generalised tonic-clonic seizure, and no significant cerebrovascular, cardiovascular or respiratory events. HV elicited no epileptiform activity in 100 healthy young men. (5) The guideline's Key points say overall evidence was low and recommendations were consensus-based. The HV yield evidence was rated moderate, but the contraindications are not graded. The protocol quote, the continuous-surveillance requirement and the full contraindication list are otherwise verbatim and correct. The Kane et al. 2014 figures in the limitations match the PubMed abstract and are also cited in the guideline. Metadata (authors, year, title, Epilepsia 64(3):602-618, DOI, PMID) is correct.

claims.topic: Population prevalence of meditation-related adverse effects; trauma and app exposure as correlates
claims.finding: Pre-registered US online survey (Prolific, quota-sampled to census proportions by age, gender and race): 953 screened, 470 reported lifetime meditation exposure, 434 completed follow-up (92.3%). Meditation-related adverse effects (MRAE) were reported by 32.3% on a general item and by 50.0% on at least one item of a specific checklist (MRAES-MBP). 10.4% reported an MRAE lasting at least 1 month; the most common duration of the longest-lasting one was a few days to a week (30.0%). Most common: anxiety (27.0%), traumatic re-experiencing (25.8%), emotional sensitivity (22.8%). Functional impairment: 10.6% (severe 0.2%); lasting more than 1 day 6.0%, at least 1 month 1.2%. More adverse childhood experiences were associated with any MRAE (r = .19) and with impairment (r = .15), but not with impairment lasting more than 1 day (r = .05). 88.7% were glad to have practised (87.9% among those reporting MRAE). Exploratory: only 17 people (3.9%) were first introduced to meditation through a smartphone app. First app exposure was not associated with MRAE occurrence (r = .06), but was associated with impairment (r = .16) and impairment lasting more than 1 day (r = .20). Lifetime app exposure (n = 199) was not associated with any MRAE measure.
claims.finding_zh: 预注册的美国网络调查（Prolific平台，按人口普查的年龄、性别、种族比例配额抽样）：筛查953人，470人有冥想经历，434人完成随访（92.3%）。总括题上32.3%报告过冥想相关不良反应，具体症状清单（MRAES-MBP）上50.0%至少勾选一项。10.4%有持续至少1个月的不良反应；最长一次最常见的持续时间是几天到一周（30.0%）。最常见的是焦虑（27.0%）、创伤记忆重现（25.8%）和情绪敏感（22.8%）。10.6%对日常功能有影响（严重的0.2%）；持续超过1天的6.0%，至少1个月的1.2%。童年不良经历越多，出现不良反应（r=0.19）和功能受影响（r=0.15）的可能越大，但与影响持续超过1天无关（r=0.05）。88.7%仍庆幸练习过冥想，有不良反应者中为87.9%。探索性分析：只有17人（3.9%）是通过手机App初次接触冥想。这与是否出现不良反应无关（r=0.06），但与功能受影响（r=0.16）及影响超过1天（r=0.20）相关。曾经用过App的199人，与任何不良反应指标都无关。
claims.study_type: pre-registered cross-sectional online survey with quota (census-matched) sampling
claims.sample: n=434 US adults with lifetime meditation exposure (953 screened)
claims.limitations: Retrospective lifetime self-report with participant attribution; cross-sectional, so causality uncertain. Internet panel that was older, more educated and more non-Hispanic White than the US population, with lower follow-up among minority participants. Practice was mostly light (60% had 100 lifetime hours or fewer; 6.9% had attended a retreat). Correlations are small (all r < .30), with many exploratory tests; the app finding rests on 17 people. US sample; transfer to Chinese users unknown.
claims.app_implication: First-run copy: difficult experiences are common (reported by about 1 in 3 to 1 in 2 meditators) and usually short, but about 1 in 10 report one lasting a month or more; impairment lasting a month or more is rare (about 1 in 100). Childhood adversity is a reason to offer gentler options and clear stop guidance; specific adaptations such as eyes-open practice or external anchors were not tested in this study. Do not claim apps are riskier: that signal comes from 17 people in an exploratory analysis, and lifetime app use showed no link. As a precaution, the app should still supply what a teacher would: stop guidance, check-ins and a route to human help.

citation.authors: Goldberg SB, Lam SU, Britton WB, et al.
citation.title: Prevalence of meditation-related adverse effects in a population-based sample in the United States

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata + PubMed abstract (PMID 34074221) + PMC author-manuscript full text (PMC8636531), including Tables 1–3
verification.problems: All reported numbers match the full text (953/470/434, 92.3%, 32.3%, 50.0%, 10.4%, 10.6%, 1.2%, r = .19/.15, 88.7%/87.9%, app r = .06/.16/.20). Problems: (1) Omitted base and nulls. The app finding rests on only 17 people (3.9%) whose first exposure was an app, and lifetime app exposure (n = 199, 45.9%) was not associated with any adverse-effect measure. Adverse childhood experiences were not associated with impairment lasting more than 1 day (r = .05). (2) app_implication overstates. 'App-introduced users reported more impairment, so...' treats an exploratory correlation in 17 people as established. 'Rarely long-lasting' understates the 10.4% who reported an effect lasting at least 1 month; only impairment of that length was rare (1.2%). (3) Limitations omit that the sample was older, more educated and more non-Hispanic White than the US population, with lower minority follow-up, and that practice amounts were mostly modest. (4) The trauma-informed adaptations proposed (eyes open, external anchors) were not tested in this study.

claims.topic: Whether MBSR causes more worsening than no treatment (contradicting / nuancing evidence)
claims.finding: Pooled pre/post data (about 10 weeks apart; intent-to-treat with multiple imputation) from a non-randomised community MBSR cohort (n = 2,155) and from the MBSR (n = 156) and waitlist (n = 118) arms of 3 RCTs taught by the same teachers in the same US city. Clinically significant harm (moving into a worse SCL-90-R global-severity band) among people at functional levels at baseline: community MBSR 3.59% [3.19, 5.03], RCT MBSR 4.41% [1.55, 7.65], waitlist 9.01% [4.07, 14.19]; differences not significant (ps > .05). In the randomised comparison, any increase in global psychological symptoms occurred in 43.7% of MBSR vs 57.6% of waitlist participants (13 fewer per 100, p = .041), and an increase of more than 35% in 32.3% vs 38.7% (6 fewer per 100, not significant). Community MBSR differed more from waitlist (41 fewer per 100 with any increase; 31 fewer with an increase of more than 35%), but that comparison is not randomised and community participants started with higher symptoms. Across 44 MBSR-vs-waitlist contrasts on 22 harm indices, none showed significantly more harm with MBSR and 22 showed significantly less, most of them community-vs-waitlist. The authors found no evidence that MBSR increases harm compared with no treatment, and called the evidence that it protects only suggestive.
claims.finding_zh: 汇总分析约10周前后的数据（意向性分析，多重插补）：非随机的社区诊所MBSR队列（2155人），以及3项随机对照试验中由同一批老师在同一城市授课的MBSR组（156人）和等待对照组（118人）。以SCL-90-R总体严重度衡量，基线功能正常者中出现“临床显著恶化”（落入更差的严重度区间）的比例：社区MBSR 3.59%，RCT中的MBSR 4.41%，等待对照组9.01%，差异不显著。随机对照比较中，总体心理症状有任何上升的：MBSR组43.7%，等待组57.6%（每100人少13人，p=0.041）；上升超过35%的：32.3%对38.7%（每100人少6人，差异不显著）。社区MBSR与等待组的差距更大（每100人少41人症状上升、少31人上升超过35%），但这是非随机比较，且社区学员基线症状更重。在22项伤害指标的44个比较中，没有一项显示MBSR比不干预伤害更多，22项显示更少，其中多数来自社区组与等待组的比较。作者认为没有证据显示MBSR比不干预伤害更多；至于它是否有保护作用，证据只是提示性的。
claims.study_type: secondary analysis of pooled data: non-randomised community MBSR cohort plus MBSR and waitlist arms of 3 RCTs (waitlist arms from 2 of them)
claims.sample: community MBSR n=2,155; RCT MBSR n=156; waitlist n=118
claims.limitations: Only the RCT MBSR vs waitlist contrast is randomised. Community participants self-selected, paid, and had higher baseline symptoms, so regression to the mean may inflate their apparent benefit. About 23% of community post-tests were missing and were imputed. Harm was measured only as worsening on symptom scales, which misses meditation-specific experiences such as depersonalisation. Waitlist comparisons can be biased (e.g., nocebo effects). Teacher-led, in-person programmes in one US city; the RCTs excluded people with current psychiatric diagnoses. The first author is a contracted provider at the community clinic.
claims.app_implication: Honest framing on the evidence page: many people's symptoms rise over any 8–10-week period whether or not they meditate (in the randomised comparison, 58% of the waitlist vs 44% of MBSR participants), and a structured, teacher-led programme was not linked to more worsening than waiting. Do not claim meditation prevents harm; the large protective figures come from a non-randomised comparison. Show this next to Britton and Goldberg so users see both 'unpleasant experiences are common' and 'net worsening versus no practice was not found in MBSR'. Applies to in-person, teacher-led MBSR, not to unguided app use.

citation.authors: Hirshberg MJ, Goldberg SB, Rosenkranz M, et al.
citation.title: Prevalence of harm in mindfulness-based stress reduction

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata + PubMed abstract (PMID 32807249) + PMC author-manuscript full text (PMC7889774), including Results, Discussion, Limitations and Table 1
verification.problems: Metadata, the clinically-significant-harm rates and CIs (3.59/4.41/9.01%, ps > .05), the 44 contrasts with 22 favouring MBSR, and the 41/31 per-100 figures all match. Problems: (1) The headline '41 fewer / 31 fewer per 100' comes only from the non-randomised comparison of community MBSR vs the RCT waitlist. The randomised RCT MBSR vs waitlist figures are omitted: 13 fewer per 100 with any increase (43.7% vs 57.6%, p = .041), 6 fewer with an increase of more than 35% (not significant) and 5 fewer with clinically significant harm (not significant). (2) Most of the 22 significant 'less harm' contrasts were community-vs-waitlist. The authors say the data do not allow concluding that MBSR is protective. (3) Missing limitations: community participants had higher baseline symptoms (regression to the mean) and about 23% missing post-tests (imputed); the RCTs excluded current psychiatric diagnoses; the first author is a contracted provider at the community clinic. (4) Waitlist data came from only 2 of the 3 RCTs.

claims.topic: Official NIH position on meditation safety and not replacing care
claims.finding: NCCIH (US NIH) consumer page, marked 'Last Updated: June 2022': 'Meditation and mindfulness practices usually are considered to have few risks. However, few studies have examined these practices for potentially harmful effects, so it isn't possible to make definite statements about safety.' It cites a 2020 review of 83 studies with 6,703 participants. In that review, 55 studies reported negative experiences and about 8% of participants had a negative effect, similar to psychological therapies; the most common were anxiety and depression. It also cites an analysis of 3 MBSR studies (521 participants), which found the practices were not more harmful than no treatment. Tip: 'Don't use meditation or mindfulness to replace conventional care or as a reason to postpone seeing a health care provider about a medical problem.'
claims.finding_zh: 美国国立卫生研究院NCCIH科普页（标注2022年6月更新）：“冥想和正念练习通常被认为风险较少。但很少有研究检验其潜在危害，因此无法对其安全性下定论。”页面引用了2020年的一篇综述：共83项研究、6703人，其中55项研究报告了负面体验；约8%的参与者出现负面影响，与心理治疗相近，最常见的是焦虑和抑郁。页面还引用了一项只含3项MBSR研究（521人）的分析，发现正念练习并不比不接受任何治疗更有害。建议：“不要用冥想或正念替代常规医疗，也不要因此推迟就医。”
claims.sample: summary of reviews (83 studies / 6,703 participants; 3 MBSR studies / 521 participants)
claims.limitations: Secondary, US-oriented consumer summary. The safety section rests on a 2020 systematic review (Farias et al., Acta Psychiatr Scand) and a 3-study MBSR harm analysis. In Farias et al., the pooled 8.3% rate varied from 3.7% in experimental studies to 33.2% in observational studies. The page does not cite other adverse-effect studies such as Britton et al. 2021 or Goldberg et al. 2022, even though both were published before its June 2022 date. The 'Last Updated: June 2022' stamp does not reflect every edit, because the page quotes 2022 National Health Interview Survey figures.
claims.app_implication: Mirror NCCIH's calibrated wording ('usually low risk, but not well studied') rather than 'completely safe'. Put the 'do not replace or delay medical care' line into the disclaimer and into any content that mentions a health condition.

citation.authors: National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health (NCCIH)
citation.title: Meditation and Mindfulness: Effectiveness and Safety
citation.venue: NCCIH, U.S. National Institutes of Health (web page)

verification.checked_against: Official NCCIH page (fetched HTML and full text: H1 title, 'Are meditation and mindfulness practices safe?' section including the expandable 'More' text, 'Tips To Consider', Key References, 'Last Updated: June 2022' stamp); Europe PMC records for Farias 2020, Hirshberg 2020, Britton 2021 and Goldberg 2022
verification.problems: All quotes and numbers in the finding and finding_zh match the page verbatim: few risks / few studies; 83 studies, 6,703 participants; about 8%; anxiety and depression; 3 MBSR studies, 521 participants; the 'replace conventional care' tip. The problem is in the limitations field. It says that because the page was last updated in 2022, 'later work (e.g., Britton 2021, Goldberg 2022)' is not included. Both papers predate June 2022: Britton et al. was first published in May 2021, and Goldberg et al. was published online in June 2021. The page simply does not cite them. Also, the 'June 2022' stamp does not reflect every edit, because the page quotes 2022 National Health Interview Survey figures. A useful context point from the cited review is missing too: Farias et al. 2020's pooled 8.3% was 3.7% in experimental and 33.2% in observational studies.

claims.topic: Adverse effects in an 8-week mindfulness program when measured actively
claims.finding: 96 adults (completers of 104 randomised; mild-to-severe depression and persistently high negative affect) took one of three 8-week MBCT variants: standard MBCT, focused attention only or open monitoring only. At the 3-month follow-up, an independent assessor interviewed them with the 44-item MedEx-I. 83% (80/96) reported at least one meditation-related side effect. 58% (56/96) had at least one with negative valence and 37% (30/81) at least one with a negative impact on functioning. 'Lasting bad effects' (negative-impact effects) are cumulative thresholds, not separate groups: more than 1 day 14.1% (11/78), more than 1 week 9.0% (7/78), more than 1 month (1–5 months or ongoing) 6.4% (5/78). Executive dysfunction, insomnia, emotional blunting and self-disturbance were each reported by fewer than 5%, but raised the risk of lasting bad effects (more than 1 week) 6- to 14-fold. Derealisation, social impairment and seeing lights also predicted them. Anxiety, time-space distortions and traumatic re-experiencing were reported by 10–25%, but most instances were not linked to lasting impairment. Lasting bad effects were associated with signs of dysregulated arousal (hyperarousal and dissociation). People with lasting bad effects did not do more formal practice, but did more frequent informal practice after the course (13.5 vs 4.3 times/week, p = .028). A single open-ended question identified only 26 of the 80 people with side effects, underestimating prevalence by nearly 70%. Rates did not differ significantly between variants, and the authors judged them similar to other psychological treatments. 83% of the final Lindahl 2017 categories replicated.
claims.finding_zh: 96名成人（104名随机分组者中的完成者；轻至重度抑郁、负性情绪持续偏高）参加了三种8周正念认知疗法（MBCT）课程之一：标准MBCT、仅专注注意、仅开放觉察。3个月随访时，由独立评估者用44项MedEx-I访谈。83%（80/96）至少有一种与冥想有关的副作用。58%（56/96）有过负性体验，37%（30/81）对日常功能产生过负面影响。“持续性不良影响”按累计口径统计，三个数字不能相加：超过1天的14.1%（11/78），超过1周的9.0%（7/78），超过1个月（1–5个月或仍未消退）的6.4%（5/78）。执行功能下降、失眠、情感麻木、自我感紊乱各不足5%，但出现后，持续超过1周的不良影响风险高6–14倍；现实解体感、社交受损和看到光感也有预测作用。焦虑、时空感改变、创伤记忆重现较常见（10%–25%），但多数没有带来持久的功能受损。持续性不良影响与唤醒失调（过度唤醒、解离）的表现有关。有持续性不良影响的人正式练习并不更多，但课程结束后非正式练习更频繁（每周13.5次对4.3次，p=0.028）。只问一个开放式问题，80名有副作用的人中只识别出26人，低估约70%。三种课程之间差异不显著，作者认为比例与其他心理治疗相近。
claims.study_type: harms analysis within a 3-arm randomized dismantling trial (all arms were MBCT variants; no non-meditation control); independent-assessor semi-structured interview
claims.sample: n=96 completers (of 104 randomized) in 8-week MBCT variants; impact data n=81; lasting-effect data n=78
claims.limitations: No non-meditation control, so causality rests on participants' attribution, timing and new-or-worse criteria. Single US site; 97% White, 73% female, self-selected meditation seekers. The lasting-effect rates rest on 5–11 people, so confidence intervals are wide. Completers only; at least one dropout left because of increased stress, so rates may be underestimated. Excluded bipolar, psychotic, borderline or antisocial personality disorders, current PTSD, panic, OCD, eating or substance-use disorders, and active suicidal ideation, so rates in these groups are unknown. Retrospective recall at 3 months after the course. Not powered to compare the variants.
claims.app_implication: Use active, symptom-specific check-ins instead of only an open feedback box (a single open question missed about 70%). Treat new insomnia, depersonalisation or derealisation, emotional numbness, trouble thinking clearly, or reduced ability to function that persists beyond a day as a 'pause and seek support' signal. The study's risk ratios were for effects lasting more than a week, so a 1-day trigger is a deliberate precaution. Do not gamify frequent all-day informal practice (the link is an association only). Tell users that brief discomfort is common and usually passes.

citation.authors: Britton WB, Lindahl JR, Cooper DJ, et al.
citation.title: Defining and measuring meditation-related adverse effects in mindfulness-based programs

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata + PubMed abstract (PMID 35174010) + PMC author-manuscript full text (PMC8845498), including Methods definitions, Results and Table 2
verification.problems: Metadata and the main percentages match (83%, 58%, 37%, 6–14%, <5% categories with 6- to 14-fold risk, 10–25% categories, open question missing nearly 70%, no difference between variants). Problems: (1) The lasting-bad-effect (LBE) figures are cumulative thresholds, not mutually exclusive duration bins: more than 1 day 14.1%, more than 1 week 9.0%, more than 1 month 6.4%. This is per the Methods definition, Table 2 ('LBE > 1 day / > 1 week / > 1 month'), the Discussion and the abstract's '6–14%'. The claim copies an ambiguous Results sentence and labels them '1 day to 1 week' and '1 week to 1 month', which readers could add up to about 30%. The bin reading also conflicts with the paper's own duration data: only about 9 participants had any side effect lasting more than a week. (2) study_type says 'meditation arms only', implying a non-meditation arm existed; all three randomized arms were MBCT variants. (3) The informal-practice association is narrower than stated. Formal practice did not differ; the significant difference was more frequent informal practice after the course (13.5 vs 4.3/week, p = .028), with a trend for minutes during the course (p = .075). (4) The 6- to 14-fold risk ratios refer to lasting bad effects of more than 1 week. (5) Missing limitations: completers only (one dropout left because of increased stress), LBE rates rest on 5–11 people, and the sample was 97% White and 73% female.

claims.topic: Some mental health apps list faulty crisis helpline numbers
claims.finding: Systematic assessment of depression-management and suicide-prevention apps on Google Play and the Apple App Store. The search ran in January 2019 and covered English-language apps launched or updated since January 2017. It identified 2,690 apps (2,591 after duplicates were removed). 69 met the inclusion criteria and were assessed, with Android and iOS versions counted separately. Only 5/69 (7%) included all six guideline-recommended suicide-prevention strategies. 6/69 (9%) gave a faulty crisis helpline number: one that did not exist, did not connect, or led to an organisation offering non-evidence-based treatment. These included two apps that had each been downloaded more than 1 million times. 65/69 (94%) gave emergency contact information, and 46/69 (67%) let users contact a crisis helpline directly from within the app.
claims.finding_zh: 对Google Play和苹果App Store中抑郁管理和自杀预防类App的系统评估（2019年1月检索，范围为2017年1月以后发布或更新的英文App）：初步检索到2690款（去重后2591款），69款符合纳入标准并接受评估（安卓版和iOS版分别计数）。只有5款（7%）包含指南推荐的全部6项自杀预防策略。6款（9%）给出了有问题的危机热线号码（号码不存在、无法接通，或指向提供非循证疗法的机构），其中有2款各自的下载量超过100万次。65款（94%）提供了紧急联系方式，46款（67%）可在App内直接联系危机热线。
claims.sample: 69 apps (Android and iOS versions counted separately; 44 distinct apps), from 2,690 search results
claims.limitations: Single snapshot from January 2019. Only English-language apps were included (no country restriction), so Chinese-language apps were not covered. Android and iOS versions of the same app were counted separately. Helpline numbers were checked by online search. The 50-question checklist was developed by the study team. Two popular apps fixed their numbers after the authors notified the developers. The paper's Results text gives a count for depression apps with direct helpline access (11/20) that conflicts with its Table 2 (9/20); the 46/69 total used here matches the abstract and Table 2.
claims.app_implication: Treat crisis numbers as safety-critical content: keep them in one config, show a 'last verified' date, re-verify on a fixed schedule and after any official change, and test tap-to-call on real devices.

citation.authors: Martinengo L, Van Galen L, Lum E, et al.
citation.title: Suicide prevention and depression apps' suicide risk assessment and management: a systematic assessment of adherence to clinical guidelines

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; Europe PMC abstract (PMID 31852455); PMC6921471 full text (Methods, Results, Tables 2 and 4)
verification.problems: Main numbers are correct: Jan 2019 search, 5/69 (7%), 6/69 (9%), two apps with >1 million downloads each, 65/69 (94%) and 46/69 (67%). (1) '2,690 screened' is wrong. 2,690 was the initial search yield. 2,591 apps remained after duplicates were removed and were screened (102 downloaded, 69 included). (2) The 69 'apps' count Android and iOS versions separately: 9 Android-only, 10 iOS-only and 25 on both platforms, so 44 distinct apps. The six faulty-number 'apps' are 2 cross-platform apps (4 versions) plus 2 Android-only apps. The claim does not say this. (3) 'Erroneous' in the paper covers non-existent (dummy) numbers, numbers that did not connect, and numbers leading to an organisation offering non-evidence-based treatments. (4) The topic 'frequently publish wrong crisis numbers' overstates a 9% rate. (5) Limitations: the study included English-language apps with no country restriction (not 'English-language app stores'), and two popular apps fixed the errors after the authors notified the developers. (6) Note: the paper's Results text says '11/20 (24%)' depression apps had direct helpline access. That conflicts with Table 2 (9/20, 45%). The claim's 46/69 matches the abstract and Table 2.

claims.topic: Asking research participants about suicide did not increase risk
claims.finding: Meta-analysis of 18 studies (17 published, 1 unpublished; 2000–2017; 20 samples; N = 13,192; ages 13–92) on exposing research participants to suicide-related questions or content. No analysis showed an increase in distress, suicidal ideation or suicide attempts. Distress: no increase from before to after exposure (small reductions after one-to-one interviews, no change after questionnaires), and no difference from unexposed controls either immediately (g = -0.01, p = .894) or two days later (g = 0.04, p = .293). Suicidal ideation: a small drop from before to after exposure (g = -0.13, 95% CI -0.16 to -0.10, p < .001; 4 studies, 3,699 participants), but no difference from controls in between-group comparisons (OR = 0.973, p = .749; 7 studies, 7,398 participants). The before–after drop was nearly twice as large in the single adolescent sample (89 adolescent inpatients) as in the five adult samples. Suicide attempts: exposed groups reported fewer attempts than controls (OR = 0.714, 95% CI 0.56–0.91, p < .05; 4 studies, 5,261 participants). The authors conclude that asking does not increase risk and may bring small benefits.
claims.finding_zh: 荟萃分析纳入18项研究（17项已发表、1项未发表；2000–2017年；20个样本，共13,192人，年龄13–92岁），考察在研究中被问及或接触自杀相关内容的影响。没有任何一项分析显示痛苦情绪、自杀意念或自杀未遂增加。痛苦情绪：接触前后没有上升（一对一访谈后略有下降，填写问卷后无变化）；与未接触的对照组相比，接触后即刻（g=−0.01，p=0.894）和两天后（g=0.04，p=0.293）均无差异。自杀意念：接触前后小幅下降（g=−0.13，95%CI −0.16至−0.10，p<0.001；4项研究，3,699人），但在设有对照组的比较中与对照组无差异（OR=0.973，p=0.749；7项研究，7,398人）。前后下降幅度在唯一的青少年样本（89名住院青少年）中约为5个成人样本的两倍。自杀未遂：接触组报告的自杀未遂少于对照组（OR=0.714，95%CI 0.56–0.91，p<0.05；4项研究，5,261人）。作者结论：询问自杀不会增加风险，可能带来小幅益处。
claims.sample: 18 studies, 20 samples, N = 13,192
claims.limitations: All studies were research settings with ethics-approved risk-management protocols; none was app-based. The drop in ideation comes only from uncontrolled before–after comparisons (the authors name regression to the mean as a possible explanation); controlled comparisons showed no difference. The attempt result rests on 4 studies, 3 of which tested interventions (a school prevention programme, and telephone follow-up after a suicide attempt), so it cannot be credited to being asked alone. The age finding rests on one adolescent sample. In the controlled ideation analysis, three studies with clinical samples showed non-significant increases, which the authors flag for further research. Figures beyond the abstract were checked against the authors' accepted manuscript. A later meta-analysis (Polihronis et al. 2022, Archives of Suicide Research; 17 studies reviewed, 8 pooled) likewise found no significant effect of asking on suicide-related behaviour, self-harm or distress, but called for more RCTs with low risk of bias.
claims.app_implication: Asking directly about thoughts of self-harm did not raise risk in research settings. Optional, skippable, plainly worded check-in questions (for example at onboarding or in periodic check-ins) are therefore acceptable, as long as every 'yes' leads straight to verified crisis resources. Every study had a risk-management protocol, so never ask without a tested safety response, and do not present the question itself as protective.

citation.authors: Blades CA, Stritzke WGK, Page AC, et al.
citation.title: The benefits and risks of asking research participants about suicide: A meta-analysis of the impact of exposure to suicide-related content

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; Europe PMC/PubMed abstract (PMID 30014862); authors' accepted manuscript full text from the UWA repository (Results, Discussion, Limitations, Tables 1, 3 and 4); Europe PMC abstract of Polihronis et al. 2022 (PMID 32715986, DOI 10.1080/13811118.2020.1793857)
verification.problems: Citation metadata and the abstract figures are correct: 18 studies, 2000–2017, g = -0.13 (p < .001), OR = 0.714 (p < .05). Problems: (1) The g = -0.13 drop in ideation comes only from uncontrolled before–after comparisons (4 studies, 6 samples, 3,699 participants). The controlled between-group comparison (7 studies, 7,398 participants) found no difference in ideation (OR = 0.973, p = .749). The claim leaves out this null and says exposure 'led to' the drop, which overstates cause; the authors themselves name regression to the mean as a possible explanation. (2) 'Reductions were nearly twice as large in adolescents' applies only to the before–after drop in ideation. It rests on one adolescent sample (89 adolescent inpatients, g = -0.22) against five adult samples (g = -0.13). (3) The null distress results are left out. (4) The attempt result comes from 4 controlled studies. Three of them tested interventions (a school prevention programme, and telephone contact after a suicide attempt), so the result cannot be credited to being asked alone. (5) 'and safer' in app_implication is not supported. The evidence shows no added risk in research settings that had risk-management protocols; it does not show that asking protects users in an app. (6) The topic generalises beyond research participants. The description of Polihronis et al. 2022 in the limitations is accurate.

claims.topic: Current synthesis of meditation adverse effects and clinical safeguards
claims.finding: Narrative review: recent studies report adverse effects in 25–87% of people who engage in meditation, and functional impairment (e.g., inability to work) in 3–37%. It remains unclear how much reflects transitory discomfort versus lasting harm. Common AEs: anxiety, depression, traumatic re-experiencing. Retreat attendance and pre-existing mental-health conditions may increase risk (causality unclear). Recommendations: thorough screening, informed consent, ongoing monitoring, clear expectations, psychoeducational support, and adapting interventions where needed.
claims.finding_zh: 叙述性综述：近年研究报告，参与冥想者中有25%–87%出现不良反应，3%–37%出现功能受损（如无法工作）。其中多少是一过性不适、多少是持久伤害，目前仍不清楚。常见的有焦虑、抑郁和创伤记忆重现。参加闭关、已有心理健康问题可能增加风险，因果关系未定。作者建议：认真筛查、知情同意、持续监测、设定清晰预期、提供心理教育支持，必要时调整练习方式。
claims.sample: review of recent studies (not a meta-analysis)
claims.limitations: Not systematic. The ranges combine very different definitions and settings, from brief courses to retreats. Recommendations are expert opinion. Only the abstract was verified in this session.
claims.app_implication: Translates into four product requirements: (1) a brief optional pre-use safety check; (2) an informed-consent-style first-run notice; (3) ongoing active check-ins; (4) adaptable practices (eyes open, shorter, external anchor, skip sections).

citation.authors: Matko K, Van Dam NT
citation.title: Beyond serenity: Adverse effects of meditation and mindfulness in clinical practice

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata (Current Opinion in Psychology 67:102197, Feb 2026, CC BY) + PubMed record and abstract (PMID 41176868; publication type 'Review'; epub 17 Oct 2025). Full text was not accessible: ScienceDirect returned 403 and the Elsevier API requires a key. Verification therefore covers the abstract, which is the only content the claim relies on, as its limitations state.

claims.topic: Practice-based suitability criteria for mindfulness courses
claims.finding: Oxford Mindfulness Foundation page 'Is mindfulness for me?'. Its courses, except MBCT for Depression, are designed for everyday life rather than clinical settings. They 'are not suitable for you if: You've experienced a manic or hypomanic episode in the past six months; You're currently self-harming; You're currently experiencing suicidal thoughts'. This is not because mindfulness cannot help ('we know it might very well be'), but because 'it would need to be delivered in a group led by a specialist who can fully support you'. People feeling suicidal are strongly advised to speak to a doctor or mental health professional. On depression: if you are currently depressed 'to such an extent that it's difficult for you to manage your everyday life, it's probably not the right time'. Past depression or current mild-to-moderate low mood may be suitable after a discussion. After a recent bereavement, 'give yourself some time' before starting. Current or recent major life events (e.g., pregnancy or a new baby, job loss, moving home, relationship breakdown) may make a course an added stress, so timing should be assessed. Insulin-dependent people should tell their doctor, because reduced stress may affect blood glucose and insulin requirements. Home practice should be done only when not impaired by recreational drugs or alcohol. People in psychological therapy should check the timing with their therapist.
claims.finding_zh: 牛津正念基金会网页《正念适合我吗？》（Is mindfulness for me?）：除“抑郁症MBCT”课程外，该机构的课程面向日常生活，而非临床场景。以下情况不适合参加：过去6个月内有过躁狂或轻躁狂发作；目前正在自伤；目前有自杀念头。这并不是说正念没有帮助（“我们知道它很可能有帮助”），而是“需要在能充分支持你的专业人员带领的小组中进行”。有自杀念头的人，网页强烈建议先与医生或精神卫生专业人员沟通。关于抑郁：如果当前抑郁到难以应付日常生活，“可能不是合适的时机”；有抑郁史或目前为轻中度情绪低落的人，可以先沟通再决定。近期失去亲近的人，宜先给自己一些时间再开始。正在或刚经历重大生活事件（如怀孕或生育、失业、搬家、感情破裂）时，课程可能成为额外压力，应先评估时机。依赖胰岛素的人应告知医生，因为压力减轻可能影响血糖和胰岛素需求。家庭练习只应在未受酒精或娱乐性药物（毒品）影响时进行。正在接受心理治疗的人应先与治疗师商量时机。
claims.sample: n/a (organizational guidance)
claims.limitations: Written for multi-week courses with weekly sessions and up to about an hour of daily home practice, not for brief app practices. The criteria are experience-based organisational guidance, not derived from trials. The page is undated (accessed October 2026).
claims.app_implication: Use as the onboarding list of reasons to talk to a professional first: mania or hypomania in the past 6 months, current self-harm, current suicidal thoughts, depression severe enough to disrupt daily life, and a recent bereavement or major upheaval. For current suicidal thoughts or self-harm, show crisis resources before any practice and point to professionally supported options. Add the insulin note and a line not to practise under the influence of alcohol or recreational drugs.

claims.topic: Developer of a popular hyperventilation method warns of fainting and lists exclusions
claims.finding: Wim Hof Method official safety page: 'Never attempt the exercises before or during diving, driving, swimming, or taking a bath, or in any other environment where passing out could potentially cause injury. The simplest way to avoid risk is to sit on a couch or floor. The breathing exercises may cause tingling sensations and/or lightheadedness. If you've fainted, that means you went too far, and have to take it easier next time.' Also: 'Do not practice the method while pregnant, or if you have a potentially debilitating condition, such as epilepsy. If you have cardiovascular issues, or any other medical condition, always consult a doctor before starting with the Wim Hof Method.'
claims.finding_zh: Wim Hof呼吸法官网安全页写明：“切勿在潜水、驾驶、游泳或泡澡之前或期间练习，也不要在任何晕倒可能造成伤害的环境中练习。最简单的避险办法是坐在沙发或地上。练习可能引起刺麻感和/或头晕。如果你晕倒了，说明做过头了，下次要放缓。”另写明：“怀孕期间，或患有癫痫等可能导致身体失能的疾病时，不要练习本方法；如有心血管问题或其他任何疾病，开始练习Wim Hof呼吸法之前务必咨询医生。”

claims.limitations: Not research evidence; undated page (footer © 2026), accessed 2026-10-22 and re-checked 2026-10-23. Causality in individual cases is not established.
claims.app_implication: The method's own developer acknowledges that its breathing can cause tingling, light-headedness and fainting, and tells people never to practise it in or near water, in the bath or while driving. Huishen must not include hyperventilation-plus-retention protocols, and its evidence page should explain why.

claims.topic: Safety of mindfulness-based interventions for people with psychosis (contradicting a blanket contraindication)
claims.finding: Pre-registered systematic review of 39 randomised trials (51% full RCTs, 49% randomised pilot studies; n = 2,684) of mindfulness-based interventions (MBIs) for adults with schizophrenia-spectrum diagnoses. MBIs were defined broadly: 14 types, including ACT in 11 trials, and formal meditation practice was not required. Harm reporting was sparse. Side effects of therapy were reported by 0/39 studies, crisis-service use and symptom deterioration by 2/39 each, deaths by 9/39, hospitalisation by 14/39, adverse events by 19/39 and dropout by 36/39 (92%). Meta-analyses of risk differences found less hospitalisation in MBI arms (14 studies; 15% vs 33%; RD −0.136, 95% CI −0.23 to −0.05, p = .003; I² = 83%). They also found less crisis-service use (2 studies, 91 participants; 2/47 vs 9/44; RD −0.160, 95% CI −0.299 to −0.024, p = .02). There were no significant differences in adverse events (8/604 vs 11/601), death (no reported death was attributed by authors to trial participation or suicide), symptom deterioration (2 studies, 40 participants), non-completion of therapy or dropout (12% vs 13%). Side effects could not be analysed because no study reported them, although the abstract lists them among the non-significant indices. The authors conclude that MBIs for psychosis 'appear to be safe' and may reduce hospitalisation. They add that poor harm reporting makes these conclusions 'necessarily provisional'.
claims.finding_zh: 这是一项预注册的系统综述，纳入39项随机试验（51%为正式随机对照试验，49%为随机化预试验；共2684人），研究对象是精神分裂症谱系障碍成人。纳入的正念相关疗法范围较宽，共14种，其中11项为接纳承诺疗法，纳入时不要求包含正式冥想练习。各项研究对不良结局的报告很少。39项研究中，报告疗法副作用的为0项，报告危机服务使用和症状恶化的各2项，报告死亡的9项，报告住院的14项，报告不良事件的19项，报告脱落的36项（92%）。风险差荟萃分析显示，正念组住院更少（14项研究；15%对33%；风险差−0.136，95%CI −0.23至−0.05，p=0.003；异质性I²=83%）。正念组的危机服务使用也更少，但这一结果只来自2项研究、91人（2/47对9/44；风险差−0.160，95%CI −0.299至−0.024，p=0.02）。两组在不良事件（8/604对11/601）、死亡、症状恶化（仅2项研究、40人）、未完成治疗和脱落（12%对13%）上都没有显著差异。作者没有把任何一例死亡归因于参加试验或自杀。副作用因没有任何研究报告而无法分析，尽管论文摘要把它列为“无显著差异”的指标。作者认为，正念干预对精神病性障碍患者“看来是安全的”，并可能减少住院。但由于不良结局报告不足，这些结论“只能是初步的”。
claims.study_type: pre-registered systematic review (PROSPERO CRD42021274649) with meta-analyses of risk differences from randomised trials
claims.sample: 39 randomised trials (51% RCTs, 49% randomised pilot studies), 2,684 participants
claims.limitations: Harm was poorly defined and inconsistently reported: only 2/39 trials defined adverse events, 11/39 described how harm data were collected, and side effects were never reported. Trial quality was rated with a reporting checklist (CONSORT; mean 16/22), not a risk-of-bias tool. The hospitalisation result is highly heterogeneous (I² = 83%), and the crisis-service and symptom-deterioration results rest on 2 small trials each. The interventions varied widely: ACT, mindfulness-based psychoeducation and other adapted MBIs, compassion-focused therapy, yoga with meditation and bibliotherapy. Most were delivered in groups (62%) or individually (33%) within trials. Participants were recruited from community and acute services and online. The review covers schizophrenia-spectrum diagnoses only, not bipolar disorder. Results do not transfer directly to unsupervised app use.
claims.app_implication: Do not shame or exclude people with a history of psychosis. Randomised trials show no signal of excess harm from mindfulness-based programmes, but harm was poorly monitored, so present this as reassuring but provisional. Explain that the evidence comes mainly from adapted, professionally run programmes, which typically use shorter practices and less home practice. Recommend practising with the care team's knowledge and keeping sessions short. Tell people to stop and seek help if unusual perceptions or distress increase. Eyes-open practice and external anchors are design choices from the adaptation literature; this review did not test them. This review covered schizophrenia-spectrum diagnoses only, so bipolar disorder or recent mania needs separate guidance.

citation.authors: O'Brien-Venus B, Ellett L, Burgess-Barr S, et al.
citation.title: Systematic review of the safety of mindfulness-based interventions for psychosis

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; Europe PMC/PubMed abstract (PMID 38851179); full text of the peer-reviewed accepted manuscript (University of Bath Pure repository), including Methods, Table 3, the meta-analysis results paragraph, Discussion and Limitations
verification.problems: (1) The finding lists 'side effects' among the indices with no significant difference. This repeats an error in the paper's own abstract. In the results, 0/39 studies reported side effects and no meta-analysis of side effects was run: the non-significant analyses were dropout, non-completion, death, symptom deterioration and adverse events. The finding also contradicts its own '0% reported side effects' sentence. (2) Key caveats are left out. Crisis-service use rests on only 2 studies (2/47 vs 9/44). Symptom deterioration rests on 2 studies (1/20 vs 2/20). The hospitalisation analysis has I² = 83%. The authors call their conclusions 'necessarily provisional' and say it is 'too soon to draw even tentative conclusions' on symptom deterioration and side effects. (3) '39 RCTs' is wrong: 49% of the included trials were randomised pilot studies. (4) The limitation that interventions were 'adapted and delivered by clinicians in clinical services' is not supported as stated. The review counted 14 intervention types (ACT in 11 trials, plus yoga with meditation and bibliotherapy) and did not require formal meditation. Participants came from community and acute services and from online recruitment, and the paper does not report who delivered the sessions. (5) The app_implication extends the finding to bipolar disorder, but the review included schizophrenia-spectrum diagnoses only. (6) evidence_weight 'moderate' is too high for these safety conclusions. Harms were poorly defined and reported (only 2/39 trials defined adverse events), quality was rated with a CONSORT reporting checklist rather than a risk-of-bias tool, heterogeneity was high and estimates were imprecise. 'low' fits better. Metadata (authors, year, title, journal, volume/article number, DOI, PMID) and the RD values are all correct.

claims.topic: Adverse effects and contraindications of high-ventilation breathwork
claims.finding: Narrative review of high-ventilation breathwork (HVB). Transient adverse physical effects of HVB include nausea, tetany, palpitations, light-headedness, dizziness, visual disturbance, shakiness, anxiety and exhaustion; this list is cited to a 1997 hyperventilation fMRI study. Hyperventilation can have panic- and anxiety-provoking effects in vulnerable individuals. In the studies cited, brief experimental hyperventilation challenges provoked panic in 16–51% of patients with panic disorder, although these effects were described as much weaker than CO2 or lactate challenges. Hyperventilation might also lower the seizure threshold in epilepsy, and short voluntary hyperventilation is routinely used to provoke seizures for diagnosis. The authors say specific contraindications are needed for pregnancy, epilepsy, panic disorder and psychotic disorders. They advise caution, with physician screening, for respiratory conditions (e.g., COPD), cardiovascular conditions (e.g., severe hypertension, arrhythmias, heart failure, ischaemic heart disease, aneurysms) and cerebrovascular conditions. Anyone practising alone 'must be in a safe environment, especially away from water, hard surfaces' or anywhere fainting could prove fatal. A 2023 meta-analysis of breathwork RCTs, led by the same first author, found no reported adverse events directly attributed to fast-paced breathwork, but only about 20% of the included studies actively reported adverse events.
claims.finding_zh: 这是一篇关于高通气呼吸法（HVB）的叙述性综述。HVB的一过性不良身体反应包括恶心、手足抽搐、心悸、头晕目眩、眩晕、视觉异常、发抖、焦虑和疲惫；这份清单引自1997年一项过度通气功能磁共振研究。对易感人群，过度通气可能诱发惊恐和焦虑。在所引用的研究中，短时过度通气试验让16%–51%的惊恐障碍患者出现惊恐，但作者指出，这一作用远弱于二氧化碳或乳酸激发试验。过度通气还可能降低癫痫患者的发作阈值，临床上也常用短时自主过度通气来诱发发作，以辅助诊断。作者认为，孕期、癫痫、惊恐障碍和精神病性障碍需要明确的禁忌。有呼吸系统疾病（如慢阻肺）、心血管疾病（如严重高血压、心律失常、心衰、缺血性心脏病、动脉瘤）或脑血管疾病的人应慎用，并先由医生筛查。独自练习“必须处在安全环境，尤其远离水和坚硬表面”，并避开任何晕倒可能致命的场合。同一第一作者2023年对呼吸法随机对照试验做的荟萃分析，没有发现直接归因于快速呼吸法的不良事件，但只有约20%的纳入研究主动报告了不良事件。
claims.sample: n/a (narrative review of physiological, clinical and experimental literature)
claims.limitations: Narrative rather than systematic, with no search strategy. The contraindications are reasoned from physiology and small experimental studies rather than trials. The adverse-effect list comes from a small 1997 imaging study, so no rates are given. The 'no adverse events' meta-analysis is the first author's own, and most of its trials did not monitor harms. The first author is a trained breathwork teacher (declared). Wording was verified against the published journal version.
claims.app_implication: Huishen does not offer HVB; it offers slow, gentle breathing only. The breathing-safety check covers epilepsy, panic disorder, psychosis, pregnancy, and heart (including high blood pressure), brain and lung disease. Every breathing session shows: sit or lie down; never in water, in the bath or while driving.

citation.authors: Fincham GW, Kartar A, Uthaug MV, et al.
citation.title: High ventilation breathwork practices: An overview of their effects, mechanisms, and considerations for clinical applications

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; Europe PMC/PubMed record (PMID 37923236); full text of the published CC BY journal version (publisher PDF on the University of Sussex figshare repository): sections 2.2, 4.2, 5.2, 5.3.1–5.3.2 and the declaration of interest

The quoted passages ('must be in a safe environment, especially away from water, hard surfaces'), the adverse-effect list, the 16–51% panic figure, the seizure-threshold statement, the contraindication and caution lists and the ~20% adverse-event reporting figure all match the published journal version. The first author's declared interest (trained breathwork teacher with the Breath-Body-Mind Foundation) is confirmed.

claims.topic: Prevalence and types of meditation adverse events
claims.finding: Systematic review (PROSPERO-registered; search to October 2019) of meditation adverse events (MAEs) in adult experimental, observational and case studies, excluding physical practices such as yoga postures. It covers 83 studies and 6,703 meditating participants (the Results section gives 6,464). 55 studies (65%) reported at least one type of MAE. Pooled prevalence across 57 reports (case studies excluded; random effects) was 8.3% (95% CI 5-12%), with extreme heterogeneity (I2=95%). By design: 3.7% (2-5%; I2=73%) in experimental studies vs 33.2% (25-41%; I2=95%) in observational studies, which relied largely on retrospective self-report. Among the 55 studies reporting MAEs, the most common were anxiety (18 studies, 33%), depression (15, 27%) and cognitive anomalies (14, 25%); gastrointestinal problems and suicidal ideation/behaviour were least frequent (6 studies each, 11%). Most MAEs were reported during or shortly after practice. Experimental and observational data were insufficient to examine who is at risk, but in the case reports most individuals had no history of mental-health problems. The authors conclude MAEs are not uncommon and may occur in people with no previous mental-health history.
claims.finding_zh: 冥想不良事件的系统综述（检索至 2019 年 10 月；纳入成人的实验、观察和个案研究，不含瑜伽体式等身体练习）：83 项研究、6703 名练习者。65% 的研究至少报告了一种不良事件。对 57 项研究（不含个案）的合并估计：总体发生率 8.3%（95% CI 5%–12%），但各研究差异极大（I² = 95%）；实验研究 3.7%，观察性研究 33.2%（多为回顾性自我报告）。在报告不良事件的 55 项研究中，最常见的是焦虑（33% 的研究）、抑郁（27%）和认知异常（25%），胃肠问题和自杀意念/行为最少（各 11%）。实验和观察研究的数据不足以判断哪些人风险更高；个案报告中多数当事人既往没有心理问题。作者认为不良事件并不罕见，也可能发生在既往没有心理问题的人身上。
claims.study_type: systematic review with random-effects pooled prevalence
claims.sample: 83 studies (54 experimental, 14 observational, 15 case studies), 6,703 participants; prevalence pooled from 57 reports
claims.limitations: No standard adverse-event assessment across studies. RCTs likely under-report, and many record only serious adverse events. Observational data are mostly retrospective self-report, and two large surveys make up 58% of the total sample. Extreme heterogeneity (I2=95%). Evidence about people without prior mental-health history comes mainly from case reports (31 individuals). Participant totals are inconsistent within the paper (6,703 vs 6,464).
claims.app_implication: Onboarding should say that unpleasant experiences (anxiety, low mood, unusual perceptions) can occur during or after meditation, including in people without prior mental-health problems. Present rates as uncertain: estimates ranged from about 4% in trials to about 33% in observational surveys. Every session needs a visible way to stop or switch to eyes-open grounding. Route detailed screening and crisis signposting to the safety module.

citation.authors: Farias M, Maraldi E, Wallenkampf KC, et al.
citation.title: Adverse events in meditation practices and meditation-based therapies: a systematic review

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; Europe PMC/PubMed abstract; full published article PDF (open-access copy in the Coventry University repository): Methods, Results, Discussion
verification.problems: Metadata correct (Farias M, Maraldi E, Wallenkampf KC, Lucchetti G; Acta Psychiatr Scand 2020;142(5):374-393; PMID 32820538). A publisher correction replaced Figure 2 (Oct 2020); there is no numerical erratum. Numbers match the abstract and full text, and the symptom percentages are of the 55 studies reporting MAEs (18/55 = 33%). The finding states as fact that MAEs 'occurred in individuals with no previous history'. The abstract says they 'may occur', and the full text says experimental and observational data were insufficient to examine participant factors. That evidence comes from case studies (15 studies, 31 individuals), where most people had no prior history. Omitted context: the pooled prevalence covers 57 reports with case studies excluded, and I2 was 95% overall (73% experimental, 95% observational). The authors say prevalence results 'were inconsistent and require further scrutiny'. The limitation 'wide confidence intervals' misplaces the problem: the CIs are moderate, and the real issue is extreme heterogeneity plus non-standardised adverse-event assessment. The participant total differs within the paper (6,703 in the abstract vs 6,464 in Results). evidence_weight 'moderate' is too high for these prevalence estimates; 'low' fits.

claims.topic: How often meditation adverse events occur overall
claims.finding: Systematic review (PROSPERO-registered; PubMed, PsycINFO, Scopus, Embase and AMED searched to 31 Oct 2019) of 83 studies of adult meditators: 54 experimental, 14 observational and 15 case studies (6,703 participants per the abstract; 6,464 in the results text). Yoga-posture and qigong practices were excluded. 55 of the 83 studies (reported as 65%) described at least one meditation adverse event (MAE). The random-effects pooled prevalence across 57 reports (case studies and 11 other studies excluded) was 8.3% (95% CI 5%–12%). Heterogeneity was very high (I² = 95%), and the rate differed sharply by design: 3.7% (95% CI 2%–5%; I² = 73%) in experimental studies vs 33.2% (95% CI 25%–41%; I² = 95%) in observational studies. The authors call the prevalence results inconsistent and probably under-reported, especially in trials; most trials did not say whether they recorded anything beyond serious adverse events. Among the 55 studies reporting MAEs, the most common types were anxiety (18 studies, 33%), depression (15, 27%) and cognitive anomalies (14, 25%); gastrointestinal problems and suicidal ideation or behaviour were least frequent (6 studies each, 11%). In 33 studies (64%), AEs occurred during or immediately after practice; effects lasting more than 6 months were reported by 9 studies, all observational or case reports. Of the 31 people in case reports, 17 (55%) had no prior mental-health history. Trial and survey data were insufficient to test whether a mental-health history raises risk.
claims.finding_zh: 系统综述（已在PROSPERO注册；检索PubMed、PsycINFO、Scopus、Embase和AMED至2019年10月31日）纳入83项成人冥想研究：实验研究54项、观察性研究14项、个案研究15项（摘要称6703人，正文为6464人），不含瑜伽体式和气功。其中55项（文中报告为65%）记录了至少一种冥想不良事件。基于57份报告（排除个案研究和另外11项研究）的随机效应合并发生率为8.3%（95%CI 5%–12%）。但研究间异质性极高（I²=95%），且因研究类型差异很大：实验研究3.7%（95%CI 2%–5%，I²=73%），观察性研究33.2%（95%CI 25%–41%，I²=95%）。作者认为发生率结果并不一致，而且很可能被低报，尤其是临床试验：多数试验没有说明是否记录了严重不良事件以外的情况。在报告不良事件的55项研究中，最常见的是焦虑（18项，33%）、抑郁（15项，27%）和认知异常（14项，25%）；胃肠问题和自杀意念或行为最少（各6项，11%）。33项研究（64%）中，不良事件发生在练习中或刚结束时；持续超过6个月的情况见于9项研究，均为观察性研究或个案报告。个案报告中的31人里，17人（55%）此前没有心理健康问题。试验和调查数据不足以判断既往心理问题是否会增加风险。
claims.study_type: systematic review with random-effects pooled prevalence (PROSPERO CRD42016040177)
claims.sample: 83 studies (54 experimental, 14 observational, 15 case studies); 6,703 meditators per abstract (6,464 in results text); prevalence pooled from 57 reports
claims.limitations: The pooled figure is extremely heterogeneous (I² = 95%), so 8.3% is not a reliable single base rate. Most trials monitored harms passively or reported only serious events, so 3.7% is probably an undercount. About 58% of observational participants came from two large online surveys of self-selected, experienced meditators, and 42% of observational participants had attended retreats, so 33.2% may overstate rates for light practice. Observational data are retrospective self-reports with little causality assessment. The point about people with no mental-health history rests on 31 case-report individuals and gives no rate. AE definitions varied widely, and the paper's participant counts are internally inconsistent.
claims.app_implication: Do not present 'about 8%' as a calibrated base rate: the pooled figure is very heterogeneous. Show the range instead (about 4% in trials, which mostly did not ask, to about 33% in surveys) and explain that rates depend on how carefully people are asked. Pair it with actively measured studies (Britton 2021, Goldberg 2022). Never describe practice as side-effect-free. Name anxiety and low mood first in warnings. Do not imply that only people with a mental-health history are affected.

citation.authors: Farias M, Maraldi E, Wallenkampf KC, et al.
citation.title: Adverse events in meditation practices and meditation-based therapies: a systematic review

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata + PubMed record/abstract (PMID 32820538) + published full-text PDF (Coventry University repository copy of the Acta Psychiatr Scand version): methods, results, Table 1, discussion
verification.problems: Citation metadata and all headline numbers match (83 studies, 55 with MAEs, 8.3% [5-12%], 3.7% [2-5%], 33.2% [25-41%], anxiety 18/55, depression 15/55, cognitive anomalies 14/55, GI and suicidal 6/55 each). Problems: (1) Omits that the pooled prevalence came from only 57 of 83 reports (case studies plus 11 others excluded) and that heterogeneity was extreme (I2 = 95% overall, 73% experimental, 95% observational). The authors themselves call the prevalence results 'inconsistent' and in need of 'further scrutiny'. (2) 'AEs also occurred in people with no previous mental-health history' rests only on case reports (17 of 31 individuals). The authors state that trial and survey data were insufficient to assess this, so the claim should be framed that way. (3) Minor inconsistencies within the source: 55/83 is 66%, but the paper reports 65%. Participants are 6,703 in the abstract vs 6,464 in the results. (4) evidence_weight 'moderate' is too high for a pooled prevalence with I2 = 95% built mostly on passive or serious-only AE monitoring; 'low' fits. (5) app_implication presents 'about 8%' as a calibrated base rate, which this heterogeneity does not support.

claims.topic: Slow paced breathing (6/min) can cause mild over-breathing; a brief 'don't breathe too deeply' instruction reduces it
claims.finding: Randomised two-group lab experiment in 46 healthy university students (45 analysed for end-tidal CO2, 39 for self-reports). After a 5-minute baseline, participants breathed through the nose at 0.1 Hz (6 breaths/min; 4 s in, 6 s out, paced by a sound cue) for 10 minutes. Without an instruction, end-tidal CO2 (PetCO2) fell by 5.21 mmHg (36.17 to 30.96 mmHg). A brief two-sentence on-screen instruction shown just before the task ('In order to avoid hyperventilation during the paced breathing task, please avoid excessively deep breathing. Breathe shallowly and naturally.') reduced the fall to 2.7 mmHg (35.66 to 32.96 mmHg; group x time F(1,43)=4.24, p<0.05, η²=0.09). The instruction roughly halved the drop but did not eliminate it. A composite score of five hyperventilation symptoms (dizziness, tingling/pricking, numbness, headache, muscle tension in hands and feet; 0-6 scale) rose by 0.63 points without the instruction and did not change significantly with it (F(1,37)=4.63, p<0.05, η²=0.11); the author describes these symptoms as minor. Among participants whose PetCO2 fell, larger falls predicted larger symptom increases (R²=0.20). Air hunger rose in both groups with no group difference; task difficulty did not differ; the instruction had no significant effect on affect.
claims.finding_zh: 随机分组实验室研究，46名健康大学生（呼气末二氧化碳分析45人，自评结果分析39人）。在5分钟基线后，受试者用鼻子按每分钟6次（0.1 Hz；吸气4秒、呼气6秒，由声音提示节拍）呼吸10分钟。没有提示的组呼气末二氧化碳（PetCO2）下降5.21 mmHg（36.17→30.96 mmHg）。练习前在电脑屏幕上显示两句简短提示（“为避免在节律呼吸任务中过度通气，请不要呼吸过深。浅而自然地呼吸。”），下降幅度减为2.7 mmHg（35.66→32.96 mmHg；组别×时间交互作用F(1,43)=4.24，p<0.05，η²=0.09）。提示让下降幅度大约减半，但没有完全消除。五项过度通气症状（头晕、刺麻感、麻木、头痛、手脚肌肉发紧；0–6分）的平均分在无提示组上升0.63分，在提示组没有显著变化（F(1,37)=4.63，p<0.05，η²=0.11）；作者认为这些症状程度轻微。在二氧化碳下降的人中，下降越多，症状增加越多（R²=0.20）。两组“吸不够气”的感觉都有所上升，但组间无差异；任务难度无组间差异；提示对情绪没有显著影响。
claims.sample: n=46 healthy University of Warsaw students aged 19-26 (23 women, 23 men); 45 analysed for PetCO2, 39 for self-reported outcomes
claims.limitations: Single small lab study; young, healthy, untrained students; one 10-minute session at one rate (6/min, sound-paced, nasal breathing). The instruction was shown once as on-screen text before the task, so repeating it during practice was not tested. Symptom effects were small (five-item composite; control rise 0.63 on a 0-6 scale) and rated retrospectively. Self-report data were lost for 6 participants through a procedural error and 1 participant was excluded. Blinding not reported; no long-term outcomes.
claims.app_implication: Before every paced-breathing session, show the tested idea in plain words: 不要吸得过深，浅而自然地呼吸. The study showed it once, before the task; repeating it once during the session is a reasonable but untested extension. Add: dizziness or tingling may mean you are breathing too deeply, so return to natural breathing. Beginners may feel short of air at 6 breaths/min (this rose in both groups), so do not force the pace. Pacers (sound or visual) must not cue maximal inhalation.

citation.authors: Szulczewski MT
citation.title: An anti-hyperventilation instruction decreases the drop in end-tidal CO2 and symptoms of hyperventilation during breathing at 0.1 Hz

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata + Europe PMC/PubMed record + PMC6685922 open-access full text (methods, procedure, Table 1, ANOVA results, regression, discussion, 2019 correction notice)
verification.problems: (1) The instruction is two sentences, not 'one-sentence' (EN) / '一句提示' (ZH). (2) ZH renders 'Breathe shallowly and naturally' as '轻柔、自然地呼吸' (gently); the tested wording is 'shallowly' (浅). (3) Topic overstates: the instruction reduced but did not prevent the CO2 drop (still -2.7 mmHg, 35.66 to 32.96), and the over-breathing was mild (author: 'minor hyperventilation symptoms'; control symptom rise 0.63 on a 0-6 scale); 'breathe gently' is not the tested wording. (4) The symptom outcome is a mean of five items; the parenthetical list can read as each symptom being reduced. (5) Sample details missing: healthy University of Warsaw students aged 19-26; 45 analysed for PetCO2, 39 for self-reports (6 lost to a procedural error, 1 excluded). (6) Omitted: air hunger rose in both groups at 6/min (no group difference); breathing was paced by a sound cue, nose only. (7) App implication 'repeated once during it' was not tested (shown once, before the task). Metadata (DOI, PMID, 44(3):247-256, 2019) correct; the 2019 correction only fixed the abstract's participant count (36 to 46).

claims.topic: Range and severity of challenging meditation experiences in intensive practitioners
claims.finding: Mixed-methods study (qualitative interviews plus a follow-up survey) of 60 Western Buddhist practitioners (20 each from Theravāda, Zen and Tibetan traditions), deliberately selected ('deviant case' sampling) because they had challenging meditation experiences, plus 32 meditation teachers or clinicians (11 of whom also gave practitioner interviews). 43% of practitioners had more than 10,000 lifetime practice hours. The analysis yielded 59 categories of meditation-related experience in 7 domains (cognitive, perceptual, affective, somatic, conative, sense of self, social) and 26 influencing-factor categories in 4 domains (practitioner, practice, relationships, health behaviours). Challenges began during a retreat for 72% and during daily practice for 28%; at onset, 25% were practising less than 1 hour a day. In this selected sample, median symptom duration was 1–3 years (range: days to more than 10 years). 73% reported moderate-to-severe impairment in at least one domain, 17% suicidality and 17% inpatient hospitalisation.
claims.finding_zh: 混合方法研究（质性访谈加随访问卷）：访谈60名西方佛教禅修者（上座部、禅宗、藏传各20人）和32名导师或临床医生（其中11人也以禅修者身份受访）。禅修者是按“偏离个案”方法特意挑选的有困难体验者，43%累计练习超过1万小时。研究归纳出7个领域（认知、知觉、情感、躯体、意志、自我感、社交）共59类冥想相关体验，以及4个领域（练习者、练习方式、人际关系、健康行为）共26类影响因素。72%的困难始于闭关期间，28%始于日常练习；困难出现时，25%每天练习不到1小时。在这一特选样本中，症状持续时间中位数为1–3年（数天至10年以上）。73%至少在一个方面有中重度功能受损，17%出现自杀倾向，17%曾住院。
claims.sample: 60 practitioners + 32 experts (11 overlap)
claims.limitations: The sample was chosen for difficulties and was mostly highly experienced and retreat-based, so the percentages are not prevalence estimates and do not describe brief app practice. With no comparison group, the study cannot show that shorter practice is safer. Experiences were attributed to meditation retrospectively (practitioners met on average 4.2 of 6 causality criteria). Mostly US-based (85%), 94.5% White and highly educated. Funding included NIH (NCCIH) and the Bial Foundation.
claims.app_implication: Defines the vocabulary for warnings and check-ins: perceptual changes, depersonalisation, sleep and emotional changes. Consistent with, but not proof of, keeping Huishen to short, non-intensive sessions with no retreat-style modes: in this sample most difficulties began on retreat, but 28% began in daily practice and 25% of people were practising under an hour a day. State plainly that persistent difficulties mean 'reduce or stop and get support'.

citation.authors: Lindahl JR, Fisher NE, Cooper DJ, et al.
citation.title: The varieties of contemplative experience: A mixed-methods study of meditation-related challenges in Western Buddhists

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata + PubMed abstract (PMID 28542181) + PMC open-access full text (PMC5443484), including Tables 1, 3, 4, sampling methods and impairment results
verification.problems: Metadata and all numbers verified: 60 practitioners and 32 experts, 43% with more than 10,000 hours, 59 categories in 7 domains, 26 influencing-factor categories in 4 domains, median 1–3 years, 73%/17%/17%, purposive deviant-case sampling. The problems are omissions that matter for the app inference. (1) 11 of the 32 experts also gave practitioner interviews, so these are not 92 distinct people. (2) Challenges began on retreat for 72%, but 28% began in daily practice and 25% were practising less than 1 hour a day at onset. The claim omits this, while app_implication says the study 'supports' short, non-intensive sessions. A selected sample with no comparison group cannot support that dose inference, so it is softened to 'consistent with'.

claims.topic: Hyperventilation and breath-holding before or during underwater swimming can cause blackout and drowning
claims.finding: CDC MMWR case series. The New York City health department, with the New York State Department of Health, reviewed fatal and nonfatal drownings in New York State from 1988-2011, mainly from incident reports at regulated swimming facilities. After excluding 6 of 22 identified cases with medical conditions or substance use, they found 16 cases (15 incidents, 4 deaths; ages 7-47, mean 17; 13 male) linked to three 'dangerous underwater breath-holding behaviors': intentional hyperventilation, static apnea (breath-holding games/contests), and hypoxic training (prolonged underwater distance swimming or extended breath-hold intervals). Static apnea was the most common (6 cases). All 4 deaths were in advanced/expert swimmers aged 17-22 who had deliberately hyperventilated (2 hyperventilation alone, 2 combined with hypoxic training); none of the cases involving only static apnea or only hypoxic training was fatal. 15 of 16 occurred in pools, and all but one incident at regulated facilities happened with a lifeguard on duty. Mechanism described: hyperventilating or breath-holding before submersion lowers CO2 and delays the urge to surface and breathe until falling oxygen causes loss of consciousness underwater. The authors state that, in this small sample, practising more than one such behaviour increased the risk of death; this rests on 2 cases.
claims.finding_zh: 美国CDC《发病率与死亡率周报》（MMWR）病例系列：纽约市卫生部门与纽约州卫生部门回顾了1988–2011年纽约州的致死和非致死溺水事件（主要来自受监管游泳场所的事故报告）。在找到的22例中排除6例有基础疾病或物质使用的病例后，共有16例与三类“危险的水下屏气行为”有关（15起事件，4人死亡；7–47岁，平均17岁；13名男性）：故意过度通气、静态憋气（憋气游戏或比赛），以及低氧训练（长距离水下潜游或反复长时间憋气）。最常见的是静态憋气（6例）。4名死者都是17–22岁、水平较高的游泳者，且都做过故意过度通气（2人单纯过度通气，2人同时进行低氧训练）；只做静态憋气或只做低氧训练的病例无一死亡。16例中15例发生在泳池，受监管场所的事件除1起外都有救生员在岗。报告描述的机制：入水前过度通气或憋气会降低体内二氧化碳，推迟想浮出水面呼吸的冲动，直到血氧下降使人在水下失去意识。作者称在这个小样本中同时做多种此类行为的人死亡风险更高，但这只基于2个病例。
claims.sample: 16 cases (15 incidents, 4 deaths), New York State, 1988-2011
claims.limitations: Small case series from incident reports, mostly at regulated pools; no denominator, so no risk estimates; the 'more than one behaviour' observation rests on 2 cases. Cases may be missed because drownings are often unwitnessed and behaviours are under-reported. Subjects were swimmers, not meditators. The physiological mechanism is well established in earlier literature. A July 2015 erratum (MMWR 64(25):704) added an author (E. Wiegert), corrected 'Lilly Huang' to 'Li Huang' and reworded a sentence on facility permits; no case numbers changed.
claims.app_implication: Absolute rule in all breathing content: never practise breathing exercises or breath-holds in or near water, in the bath or while driving. Never combine over-breathing with breath-holding: every death in this series involved deliberate hyperventilation before going under. No retention rounds, breath-hold timers or breath-hold challenges in Huishen.

citation.authors: Boyd C, Levy A, McProud T, et al.
citation.title: Fatal and nonfatal drowning outcomes related to dangerous underwater breath-holding behaviors - New York State, 1988-2011
citation.venue: MMWR Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report 64(19):518-521

verification.checked_against: PubMed record (PMID 25996093) + PMC4584570 full text including the case table + MMWR erratum 2015;64(25):704 (PMC4584684)
verification.problems: (1) Lists four behaviours; the report defines three DUBBs. 'Underwater distance swimming' is part of 'hypoxic training' (prolonged underwater distance swimming or extended breath-hold intervals), not a separate category. (2) 'Practising more than one such behaviour increased the risk of death' is stated as fact. The authors qualify it 'for this small sample', it rests on 2 cases (both fatal) with no statistical test, and it contradicts the claim's own 'no risk estimate' limitation. (3) Omits the most relevant fact for a breathing app: all 4 deaths (advanced/expert swimmers aged 17-22) involved deliberate hyperventilation, and no static-apnea-only or hypoxic-training-only case was fatal. (4) Not stated: 6 of 22 identified cases were excluded; the review drew mainly on incident reports from regulated facilities; all but one incident at regulated facilities happened with a lifeguard on duty. (5) Erratum (MMWR 2015;64(25):704) adds an author (Wiegert E), corrects 'Lilly Huang' to 'Li Huang' and rewords a facility-permit sentence; 'et al.' still fine, no case numbers changed. Minor source inconsistency: the report's text says 4 hypoxic-training cases, its table says 5. Other numbers (16 cases, 15 incidents, 4 deaths, ages 7-47, mean 17, 13 male, 15/16 in pools) correct; no DOI exists (pii mm6419a3).

claims.topic: Infant sleep machines can reach hazardous sound levels
claims.finding: Fourteen infant sleep machines were measured at maximum volume at 30, 100 and 200 cm, with correction for a 6-month-old's ear canal. At 30 cm, maximum levels exceeded 50 dBA for all devices; 50 dBA is the recommended noise limit for hospital nurseries. Three machines exceeded 85 dBA, which, if played for more than 8 hours, would exceed adult occupational limits for accumulated noise and risk noise-induced hearing loss.
claims.finding_zh: 在最大音量下测量14款婴儿睡眠白噪音机（30、100、200厘米处，按6个月婴儿耳道校正）。30厘米处所有机器的最大音量都超过50 dBA，即医院新生儿室的推荐噪声上限。3款超过85 dBA，若连续播放8小时以上，累计噪声将超过成人职业限值，有致噪声性听力损失的风险。
claims.sample: 14 commercial infant sleep machines
claims.limitations: Only maximum output was measured, not real-world use; no hearing outcomes. The safer-use advice (place far from the infant and never in the crib, lowest volume, short duration; manufacturers to limit output and add auto-off timers) is from the NEJM Journal Watch summary of the paper; the full text was not accessed.
claims.app_implication: Do not market sleep sounds for infants. If a baby or child context is ever offered, use the sensitive-user cap, default to low volume with a mandatory timer, and show: 把手机或音箱放在远离宝宝的地方，不要放进婴儿床.

citation.authors: Hugh SC, Wolter NE, Propst EJ, et al.
citation.title: Infant sleep machines and hazardous sound pressure levels

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata + Europe PMC/PubMed abstract + NEJM Journal Watch summary (Bell LM, 18 Apr 2014); AAP full text blocked (HTTP 403)
