verification.problems: No discrepancies against the abstract: 14 machines, maximum volume, 30/100/200 cm, 6-month-old ear-canal correction, all >50 dBA at 30 cm (hospital-nursery limit), 3 >85 dBA with the >8 h occupational comparison. Metadata (authors, Pediatrics 133(4):677-681, DOI, PMID) correct. Full text was not readable; per the Journal Watch summary, the three >85 dBA machines were measured at 30 cm, and the safer-use advice in the limitations (far from infant, never in or on the crib, lowest volume, short duration; manufacturers to limit output, print warnings and add timers) matches. Minor ZH nuance: '白噪音机' simplifies 'infant sleep machines' (ambient or masking sounds), and '连续播放' adds 'continuously' to 'played for >8 hours'; neither changes the meaning materially.

claims.topic: WCAG 2.2 requirements for a timer/player web app
claims.finding: WCAG 2.2 (W3C Recommendation; current version 12 December 2024) success criteria relevant to a timer/player PWA: 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum, AA), text contrast at least 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text); 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast (AA), UI components and meaningful graphics at least 3:1 against adjacent colours; 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable (A), content-imposed time limits can be turned off, adjusted or extended; 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide (A), moving or blinking content that starts automatically, lasts more than 5 seconds and is shown alongside other content needs a pause/stop/hide mechanism unless essential; 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions (AAA), motion animation triggered by interaction can be disabled unless essential; 2.5.7 Dragging Movements (AA, new in 2.2), functionality using dragging must be achievable with a single pointer without dragging; 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum, AA, new in 2.2), pointer targets at least 24 by 24 CSS px, with spacing and other exceptions; 2.5.5 Target Size (Enhanced, AAA), at least 44 by 44 CSS px.
claims.finding_zh: WCAG 2.2（W3C 推荐标准，现行版本 2024 年 12 月 12 日）中与计时/播放类网页应用相关的条款：文字对比度至少 4.5:1（大字 3:1）；按钮等界面元素和有意义的图形至少 3:1；内容设置的时间限制必须可关闭、调整或延长；自动开始、持续超过 5 秒且与其他内容同时出现的动态内容必须可暂停/停止/隐藏；由交互触发的动画应可关闭（AAA）；任何拖动操作都要有无需拖动的单指替代方式（AA，2.2 新增）；点击目标至少 24×24 CSS 像素（AA，2.2 新增），增强级 44×44（AAA）。
claims.sample: not applicable
claims.limitations: Conformance criteria rather than outcome evidence; AAA criteria are not required for AA conformance; WCAG does not specify breathing-pacer design; vestibular guidance sits in the non-normative Understanding documents.
claims.app_implication: Target WCAG 2.2 AA plus selected AAA: primary controls at least 44 by 44 CSS px and never below 24 by 24; text at least 4.5:1 and timer ring/progress at least 3:1 in both themes; check-in scale usable by tapping alone; ambient animation pausable; under prefers-reduced-motion, replace the expanding breath circle with a non-moving cue (text count, opacity, optional sound or haptic).

citation.authors: W3C; Campbell A, Adams C, Bradley Montgomery R, et al. (eds.)
citation.title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2

verification.checked_against: W3C TR page https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/ (W3C Recommendation 12 December 2024; editors Campbell, Adams, Bradley Montgomery, Cooper, Kirkpatrick); normative text of SC 1.4.3, 1.4.11, 2.2.1, 2.2.2, 2.3.3, 2.5.5, 2.5.7 (marked New), 2.5.8 (marked New)
verification.problems: No factual discrepancies. Minor simplifications that do not change the guidance: 2.2.1 also allows real-time, essential and 20-hour exceptions; 1.4.11 applies to the visual information needed to identify components and their states, and inactive components are exempt; the Chinese '单指' stands for WCAG's 'single pointer', which also covers a mouse or stylus.

claims.topic: Strength of evidence for phone-based mental-health interventions, and how effects shrink against more rigorous comparison conditions
claims.finding: Preregistered systematic meta-review of 14 meta-analyses (databases searched to 31 October 2020) representing 145 RCTs and 47,940 participants. It yielded 34 unique participant-intervention-comparison-outcome effect sizes, graded with umbrella-review criteria. None provided convincing evidence (n > 1000, p < 10^-6, I² < 50%, no publication bias); publication bias was rarely assessed. Eight effect sizes were highly suggestive (n > 1000, p < 10^-6). These included smartphone interventions outperforming inactive controls (such as waitlist or no treatment) on psychological symptoms and quality of life (ds = 0.32-0.47), and text-message interventions for smoking cessation (d = 0.31 vs non-specific and 0.19 vs active controls). Four were suggestive, 14 weak and 8 non-significant. The magnitude of effects and strength of evidence tended to diminish as comparison conditions became more rigorous (inactive to active, non-specific to specific). Meditation-app estimates, all from one included meta-analysis, were d = 0.31 for anxiety (suggestive), 0.35 for depression and 0.62 for stress (both weak) versus inactive controls, and d = 0.28 for depression (weak) and 0.26 for anxiety (not significant) versus specific active controls. Despite substantial heterogeneity, no moderators were identified, and only one meta-analysis tested moderators. Only 1 of the 14 meta-analyses evaluated adverse events, and the trials it included did not report them, so harms were essentially unassessed.
claims.finding_zh: 预先注册的系统性“荟萃分析的综述”：汇总 14 项荟萃分析（文献检索截至 2020 年 10 月 31 日，共 145 项随机对照试验、47940 名参与者）的 34 个效应量，按伞状综述标准分级。没有一项达到“令人信服”的证据标准，发表偏倚也很少被评估。8 项属于“高度提示性”证据，例如智能手机干预与等待名单、不干预等非活性对照相比，在心理症状和生活质量上有小幅改善（d=0.32–0.47），以及短信干预帮助戒烟（对非特异对照 d=0.31，对积极对照 d=0.19）；另有 4 项为“提示性”、14 项为“弱”证据，8 项不显著。对照组越严格（从非活性到积极对照、从非特异到特异），效果和证据强度往往越弱。冥想 App 的数据都来自其中一项荟萃分析：与非活性对照相比，焦虑 d=0.31（提示性），抑郁 d=0.35、压力 d=0.62（均为弱证据）；与其他旨在治疗的干预相比，抑郁 d=0.28（弱证据），焦虑 d=0.26（不显著）。异质性较大，但没有找到调节因素（只有一项荟萃分析检验过）。14 项荟萃分析中只有 1 项评估了不良事件，而它纳入的试验都没有报告不良事件，因此安全性基本没有被评估过。
claims.study_type: umbrella review (preregistered meta-review of meta-analyses of RCTs)
claims.sample: 14 meta-analyses, 145 RCTs, 47,940 participants; 34 representative effect sizes
claims.limitations: Covers phone-based mental-health interventions broadly. Meditation-app estimates rest on a single meta-analysis (Gál et al. 2021) and were graded only suggestive or weak. Most included meta-analyses were rated good quality (NIH tool mean 7.07 of 8), but publication bias was rarely assessed, and primary trials relied heavily on self-report with unblinded participants. Heterogeneity was substantial, and moderators were tested in only one meta-analysis. Harms were essentially unassessed. The review did not measure expectancy effects; the authors only note that specific active controls are needed to separate intervention-specific effects from expectancy and other non-specific factors. The literature was searched only to October 2020.
claims.app_implication: Check-in summaries must not imply the practice caused the change: label them 自评, and add that changes also reflect rest itself, expectation and measurement error. Marketing and onboarding use 'may help a little' language. The evidence page reports effects against active controls where they exist. Nothing should describe the app as safe or free of side effects on the basis of this literature, because harms were rarely assessed.

citation.authors: Goldberg SB, Lam SU, Simonsson O, et al.
citation.title: Mobile phone-based interventions for mental health: A systematic meta-review of 14 meta-analyses of randomized controlled trials

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; PubMed abstract (PMID 35224559); PMC full text PMC8881800 via Europe PMC fullTextXML: methods (registration, comparator coding, grading), results by outcome, moderator and adverse-event sections, discussion
verification.problems: Metadata and the abstract numbers are correct. Problems: (1) finding_zh '研究均未报告不良反应' reads as if harms were checked and none were found. The full text says only 1 of the 14 meta-analyses evaluated adverse events, and the trials it included did not report them, so harms were essentially unassessed. The English 'adverse effects were not reported' has the same ambiguity. (2) finding_zh drops 'tended to' ('越弱'), turning a trend into a rule. '手机干预…优于无干预对照' also simplifies 'smartphone interventions vs inactive controls', a category that includes waitlist, no treatment, assessment only and shared treatment-as-usual. (3) The limitations say the review does not cover meditation apps specifically, but it includes 6 meditation-app effect sizes from one meta-analysis (Gál et al. 2021), graded suggestive or weak. (4) The topic says 'expectancy', but the review did not measure expectancy effects; it mentions expectancy only as a reason to use specific active controls.

claims.topic: NICE Evidence Standards Framework: classification and reliable-content standard
claims.finding: NICE's Evidence Standards Framework for digital health technologies (ECD7; published 10 December 2018, last updated 9 August 2022) classifies DHTs by intended purpose into risk tiers with proportionate evidence requirements, using 21 standards in 5 groups. Tier B 'promoting good health' covers non-personalised information and resources that may encourage healthy behaviours (examples include DHTs that aid good sleep habits) and excludes DHTs that describe themselves as a treatment for a diagnosed condition; Tier B 'health and care diaries' covers user-recorded information (e.g., symptom or mood diaries) that stays with the user and is not automatically shared. DHTs that provide personalised information or guidance using behaviour-change techniques to promote healthy living fall in Tier C ('inform clinical management'). Standard 7 (Tiers B and C) requires processes keeping health information valid (aligned to best available sources), accurate, reviewed and updated by relevant experts at defined intervals such as every year, and sufficiently comprehensive; standard 14 (effectiveness evidence) applies only to Tier C.
claims.finding_zh: 英国 NICE 数字健康技术证据标准框架（ECD7，2018 年 12 月发布，2022 年 8 月更新）按用途把数字健康产品分级，证据要求与风险相称，共 21 条标准。B 级“促进健康”：提供非个性化的信息和资源（例如帮助养成良好睡眠习惯的产品），但不包括自称能治疗已确诊疾病的产品；B 级“健康日记”：用户自己记录、数据留在用户手中、不自动分享（如情绪日记）。利用行为改变技术提供个性化指导的产品属于 C 级。第 7 条标准要求健康信息有效、准确，并由相关专家按固定周期（例如每年）审核更新；第 14 条（有效性证据）只适用于 C 级。
claims.sample: not applicable
claims.limitations: UK NHS commissioning context, not a Chinese regulatory requirement; a framework for evaluators, not proof that any design works; tier assignment of adaptive features can be a judgement call.
claims.app_implication: Position 回神 as a Tier B wellness tool: never claim to treat anxiety, insomnia or depression; keep check-ins as a private diary; accept the higher Tier C evidence burden before adding personalised coaching. Every content and evidence page shows last-reviewed and next-review dates (at least yearly) and the reviewer's role.

citation.authors: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
citation.title: Evidence standards framework for digital health technologies (ECD7)

verification.checked_against: NICE ECD7 official pages fetched 2026-10-23: overview (Published 10 December 2018, Last updated 09 August 2022), Section B classification table (Table 1), Section C evidence standards tables (21 standards in 5 groups, tier applicability), and 'How to meet the standards' text for standards 7 and 14

claims.topic: China's Personal Information Protection Law: sensitive data, separate consent, access/copy/transfer, deletion
claims.finding: PRC Personal Information Protection Law (effective 1 November 2021). Article 28: sensitive personal information is information whose leakage or illegal use can easily harm personal dignity or personal and property safety, including biometric, religious belief, specific identity, medical and health, financial account and whereabouts information, and the personal information of minors under 14; it may be processed only with a specific purpose, sufficient necessity and strict protective measures. Article 29: processing sensitive personal information requires the individual's separate consent. Article 45: individuals have the right to access and copy their personal information, which processors must provide promptly, and to request transfer to a designated processor where conditions set by the national cyberspace department are met. Article 47 requires deletion when, among other cases, the processing purpose has been achieved or is no longer necessary, the service has ended, or consent is withdrawn.
claims.finding_zh: 《中华人民共和国个人信息保护法》（2021 年 11 月 1 日起施行）。第二十八条：敏感个人信息包括生物识别、宗教信仰、特定身份、医疗健康、金融账户、行踪轨迹等信息，以及不满十四周岁未成年人的个人信息，只有在具有特定目的和充分必要性、并采取严格保护措施的情形下才可处理。第二十九条：处理敏感个人信息应当取得个人的单独同意。第四十五条：个人有权查阅、复制其个人信息，处理者应当及时提供；符合国家网信部门规定条件的，应当提供转移途径。第四十七条：处理目的已实现或不再必要、停止提供服务、个人撤回同意等情形下应当删除。
claims.sample: not applicable
claims.limitations: Legal text, not evidence of effect; whether mood/stress check-ins count as medical and health information is an interpretation question not resolved here; implementing regulations and national standards were not reviewed; not legal advice.
claims.app_implication: Treat check-in and practice data as potentially sensitive: keep them on the device by default; any future cloud sync needs separate, unbundled opt-in consent; provide one-tap export (JSON + CSV) and one-tap delete-all; collect no location, contacts or identifiers. Account-free, on-device storage minimises the personal information the developer processes at all.

citation.authors: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress of the PRC
citation.title: 中华人民共和国个人信息保护法 (Personal Information Protection Law of the People's Republic of China)
citation.venue: Official text as published by the Cyberspace Administration of China (cac.gov.cn)

verification.checked_against: Official text at the cited cac.gov.cn URL (fetched 2026-10-23): adoption note (13th NPC Standing Committee, 30th session, 20 August 2021), Articles 28, 29, 45, 47 and 74 (effective 1 November 2021)
verification.problems: No material discrepancies. The summaries leave out qualifiers that do not change the app implication: Article 29's rule that written consent applies where laws or administrative regulations require it; Article 45's exceptions (cases under Article 18(1) and Article 35); and Article 47's fallback (if a legal retention period has not expired or deletion is technically difficult, all processing except storage and necessary security measures must stop).

claims.topic: APA App Evaluation Model: features evaluators check
claims.finding: The American Psychiatric Association's App Evaluation Model, part of its App Advisor initiative, is described as a hierarchical rating system with content-specific questions in six steps: Background; Access; Privacy and Security; Clinical Foundation; Usability; Integration toward Patient-Centered Goals (tab label 'Data Integration'). Example questions for Access: does the app function in low-bandwidth or offline environments, work on a computer or web browser, offer accessibility features and identify its reading level. For Privacy and Security: is the privacy policy easy to understand, does the app declare data use and purpose, say where it stores its data, let users opt out of data collection or delete data, say which third parties it shares data with, and say whether and how it uses AI. For Clinical Foundation: is content clinically accurate, up to date and relevant, is there evidence supporting effectiveness, and are clinical retention rates disclosed. For Integration: can users access and export or download their data. The page states there is no minimum or maximum number of levels an app must meet to be considered good or useful, and no scoring system for the privacy and security step.
claims.finding_zh: 美国精神医学学会（APA）的 App 评估模型（属于其 App Advisor 项目）是一个分层评估体系，分六步：背景、可及性、隐私与安全、临床基础、可用性、数据整合（服务于以患者为中心的目标）。示例问题包括：能否离线或在低带宽下使用、能否在电脑或浏览器中使用、是否有无障碍功能、是否标明阅读难度；隐私政策是否易懂、是否说明数据用途和存储位置、能否退出数据收集或删除数据、与哪些第三方共享数据、是否使用 AI 以及怎样使用；内容在临床上是否准确、及时、贴合使用者，是否有支持有效性的证据，是否公开临床留存率；用户能否查看并导出或下载自己的数据。页面说明：没有“必须达到几级才算好”的标准，隐私与安全这一步也不打分。
claims.sample: not applicable
claims.limitations: A professional-society checklist of questions, not an evidence-graded guideline. It is written mainly for clinicians choosing apps together with patients, though the page says it is also for patients and other providers. US-centred. The page is undated (© 2026; accessed 2026-10-23). Archived versions from June 2021 and May 2023 used a five-step model ('Access and Background' combined; 'Data Integration towards Therapeutic Goal') with no AI questions, so the current six-step version is a later revision and may change again.
claims.app_implication: Design to answer every applicable APA question well: an offline-capable PWA that works in the browser; an accessibility statement; a plain-language privacy page stating that data stay on this device; export and delete-all controls; an evidence page with citations; and if retention is ever measured (opt-in, aggregate), publish it.

citation.authors: American Psychiatric Association
citation.title: The App Evaluation Model
citation.venue: American Psychiatric Association (psychiatry.org), official web page

verification.checked_against: Live official page at the cited psychiatry.org URL (fetched 2026-10-23; footer © 2026), plus Wayback Machine snapshots of the same URL from 2021-06-09 and 2023-05-31
verification.problems: Core content matches the live page: the six steps, every quoted example question, and the 'no minimum or maximum number of levels' statement. Minor problems: (1) finding_zh renders Step 6 'Integration toward Patient-Centered Goals' as '与个人目标的整合', which loses its meaning. The page's tab label is 'DATA INTEGRATION', and the step is about accessing, exporting and sharing data in care. (2) The limitations say the model is aimed at clinicians, but the page says it is for APA members, patients and other providers. (3) The 'revised over time (e.g., AI items)' limitation is confirmed. Archived 2021 and 2023 versions had five steps ('Access and Background' combined; 'Data Integration towards Therapeutic Goal') and no AI questions, so the revision is now stated specifically.

claims.topic: Night-time phone use: does a warm night display mode protect sleep?
claims.finding: Randomized experiment: 167 emerging adults (ages 18-24, 71.3% female) with iPhones were assigned for seven consecutive nights to use the iPhone in the hour before bed with Night Shift enabled, use it with Night Shift disabled, or not use the phone; sleep latency, duration, efficiency and wake after sleep onset were measured with wrist-worn accelerometers. There were no significant differences in sleep outcomes across the three groups. Post-hoc exploratory analyses in participants averaging more than 6.8 h of sleep found a significant effect of condition on sleep efficiency (P = .014) and WASO (P = .013), with the no-phone condition best; for those averaging under 6.8 h there was no effect of phone condition.
claims.finding_zh: 随机实验：167 名 18–24 岁 iPhone 用户（71.3% 女性），连续 7 晚在睡前一小时分别：开启“夜览”使用手机、关闭“夜览”使用手机、或不用手机，用腕部加速度计测量睡眠。三组在入睡时间、睡眠时长、睡眠效率和夜间醒来时间上均无显著差异。探索性分析显示，平时睡眠超过 6.8 小时的人中，不用手机组的睡眠效率和夜间醒来指标最好。
claims.sample: n=167 emerging adults
claims.limitations: Seven nights only; young university sample; actigraphy rather than polysomnography; subgroup findings exploratory; does not test dark UI themes directly.
claims.app_implication: Do not present dark mode or a warm tint as sleep protection. Night and sleep sessions are audio-first: one tap starts audio, the screen can lock or switch off, a sleep timer fades sound out, and no notifications, check-ins or prompts appear once a sleep session starts. The dark theme follows the system setting for comfort only.

citation.authors: Duraccio KM, Zaugg KK, Blackburn RC, et al.
citation.title: Does iPhone night shift mitigate negative effects of smartphone use on sleep outcomes in emerging adults?

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata (Sleep Health 7(4):478-484, Aug 2021; 4 authors) + PubMed/Europe PMC structured abstract (PMID 33867308); full text paywalled, but every number in the claim is in the abstract

claims.topic: Attrition and adherence in smartphone mental-health RCTs
claims.finding: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 70 RCTs of smartphone-delivered mental-health interventions. Mean study attrition was 24.1% (95% CI 19.3-29.6) at short-term follow-up and 35.5% (95% CI 26.7-45.3) at longer-term follow-up, varying by target condition. Attrition was significantly lower in trials that delivered acceptance-based interventions, offered monetary compensation or reminded participants to engage with the intervention. It was higher in trials that used online enrolment (vs telephone or in-person). No participant-level baseline characteristic reliably predicted attrition. Many RCTs did not conduct intention-to-treat analyses; in trials reporting both, per-protocol and intention-to-treat between-group effect sizes differed by a mean of only Δd = 0.18. A qualitative synthesis found adherence suboptimal: some participants never downloaded the intervention, and usage consistently declined over the course of trials.
claims.finding_zh: 荟萃分析：70 项手机心理健康干预随机对照试验。短期随访平均流失率 24.1%（95% CI 19.3–29.6），长期随访 35.5%（95% CI 26.7–45.3），并因目标问题而异。采用接纳类干预、给予报酬、提醒参与者使用干预的试验流失更少；线上招募（相对电话或面对面招募）的试验流失更多。没有哪项基线个人特征能可靠预测流失。许多试验没有做意向性（ITT）分析；在同时报告两种分析的试验中，符合方案分析与 ITT 分析的组间效应量平均只相差 Δd=0.18。定性综合显示依从性欠佳：有人从未下载干预程序，使用量在试验期间持续下降。
claims.study_type: systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs
claims.sample: 70 RCTs
claims.limitations: Trial attrition (missing follow-up data) is not the same as real-world app abandonment. Moderator findings are between-trial associations, not tested causes. The adherence findings come from a qualitative synthesis. Some trials paid participants, and payment was linked to lower attrition, so trial retention may overstate real-world retention.
claims.app_implication: Offer opt-in reminders: trials that reminded participants lost fewer, though this is a between-trial association. Do not profile or label users from demographics. Expect usage to decline, and design for easy re-entry rather than a fixed curriculum. The evidence page should note that a quarter to a third of app-trial participants are missing at follow-up and that many trials did not use intention-to-treat analyses.

citation.authors: Linardon J, Fuller-Tyszkiewicz M
citation.title: Attrition and adherence in smartphone-delivered interventions for mental health problems: A systematic and meta-analytic review
citation.venue: Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology 88(1):1-13

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; Europe PMC/PubMed abstract (PMID 31697093). The full text is under permanent embargo in the Deakin repository and was not read.
verification.problems: Metadata and all numbers match the abstract. The issues are minor. (1) The claim omits the abstract's point that many RCTs did not run intention-to-treat analyses (its evidence of attrition bias), so 'differed by only Δd = 0.18' reads more reassuring than the authors intended. (2) The usage-decline result comes from a qualitative synthesis, not the meta-analysis. (3) The limitation 'trial participants were often paid' cannot be confirmed from the abstract; payment was a moderator, but how common it was is not reported there. Evidence weight 'moderate' fits.

claims.topic: Healthy Minds Program app RCT: efficacy, retention and real usage
claims.finding: Preregistered, three-arm, fully remote RCT (October 2019 to April 2020) of the self-guided Healthy Minds Program (HMP) smartphone app, which its nonprofit developer offers free. Adults without extensive meditation experience did 8 weeks of Awareness+Connection or Awareness+Insight, or were waitlisted. 343 were randomized (121/107/115). 186 (54.2%) completed at least one follow-up assessment (week 4 or week 8), fewer in the app arms than on the waitlist (109/228, 47.8% vs 77/115, 67.0%). 166/228 (72.8%) of those assigned to the app downloaded and used it at least once. The two app versions did not differ on any outcome (time x group Ps >= .29), so they were combined. In intention-to-treat multilevel models, compared with waitlist the app arms showed: a greater decrease in psychological distress, the primary outcome (d = -0.28, the difference between within-group pre-post effects of -0.74 for the app and -0.46 for the waitlist); a greater decrease in rumination (d = -0.18); and greater increases in social connectedness, self-reflection, insight, defusion and mindfulness (d = 0.13 to 0.41; FDR-adjusted Ps <= .02). Empathy (d = 0.02) and compassion (d = 0.12) did not differ from waitlist. In exploratory, non-randomized analyses, using the app on at least the median number of days was associated with larger improvements in distress. Across all 228 assigned to the app, with non-users counted as zero, use averaged 10.52 days (SD 13.31; median 4) and 102 total minutes of meditation (SD 188; median 26). The median time to last use was 12 days.
claims.finding_zh: 预注册的三臂远程随机对照试验（2019 年 10 月至 2020 年 4 月）：研究对象是没有丰富冥想经验的成年人，比较 8 周自助冥想 App“Healthy Minds Program”（由非营利开发方免费提供）的两个版本（觉察+联结、觉察+洞察）与等待对照。343 人随机分组；54.2% 至少完成一次随访测评（第 4 或第 8 周），App 组的完成率（47.8%）低于等待组（67.0%）。分配到 App 组的人中，72.8% 下载并至少用过一次。两个版本效果没有差别。与等待组相比，App 组的心理困扰（主要结局）下降更多（d=-0.28，属小效应；等待组自身也有改善），反刍思维下降更多，社会联结、自我反思、洞察、认知解离和正念的提高也更多（d=0.13–0.41）；共情和慈悲与等待组没有差别。使用天数较多的人困扰改善更大，但这是非随机的探索性分析。按全部 228 名 App 组成员计算（未使用者记为 0）：平均使用 10.52 天（中位数 4 天），总练习约 102 分钟（中位数 26 分钟），最后一次使用的中位时间为第 12 天。
claims.sample: n=343 adults randomized (228 to two app arms, 115 waitlist)
claims.limitations: Waitlist (inactive) control with unblinded self-reported outcomes, and the waitlist group also improved (distress within-group d = -0.46). Attrition was high and uneven: 45.8% gave no follow-up data overall, 52.2% in the app arms vs 33.0% on the waitlist; this was handled with maximum-likelihood intention-to-treat analysis plus sensitivity analyses. Allocation was automated by sequentially assigned participant ID numbers (1:1:1). The sample was mostly White (81.6%), female (84.5%) and graduate-educated (55.4%), mean age 41.7, recruited largely through the University of Wisconsin-Madison. Participants were paid US$25 for completing assessments. The usage-outcome and mediation analyses are non-randomized and exploratory. Conflicts of interest: one author founded and presides over the nonprofit developer Healthy Minds Innovations, another is its Chief Contemplative Officer, and another a paid consultant and content contributor.
claims.app_implication: Use this as a benchmark for honest copy. A free, research-based app produced a small benefit over an inactive waitlist (distress d = -0.28), only about half of app-arm participants provided follow-up data, and median use was 4 days. Progress displays should emphasise days with practice (more practice days went with larger gains, though this was not randomized). The first run must deliver value immediately, because 27% of those assigned never downloaded or used the app.

citation.authors: Goldberg SB, Imhoff-Smith T, Bolt DM, et al.
citation.title: Testing the Efficacy of a Multicomponent, Self-Guided, Smartphone-Based Meditation App: Three-Armed Randomized Controlled Trial

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata + Europe PMC abstract + PMC full text (PMC7732708): methods, CONSORT numbers, Table 3 effect sizes, utilization, attrition analysis, limitations and COI; Center for Healthy Minds news item (3 Oct 2019) for the app being offered free
verification.problems: Metadata, randomized n, retention, download rate, usage figures (10.52 days, median 4; 102.16 min, median 26), the 12-day median time to last use and the COI all match the full text. Problems: (1) Nulls are left out. Empathy (d = 0.02, P = .63) and compassion (d = 0.12, P = .14) did not differ from waitlist. (2) '186 (54.2%) completed at least one post-test' means any follow-up, at week 4 or week 8. Attrition was also uneven: 47.8% of app-arm participants gave follow-up data vs 67.0% of waitlist participants, and the limitations leave this out. (3) The d values are differences between within-group pre-post effect sizes, and the waitlist group improved too (distress d = -0.46), so the distress benefit (d = -0.28) should be called small. (4) The usage means count non-users as zero, which should be stated. (5) The trial report never calls the app 'free'; the developer's 2019 announcement confirms it. Evidence weight 'moderate' is kept, but it is generous given the waitlist control and uneven attrition.

claims.topic: Real-world engagement and retention of mental-health apps
claims.finding: Independent usage-panel data (SimilarWeb, 12 months from Aug 2017 to Jul 2018) for 93 Android apps targeting anxiety, depression or emotional well-being with at least 10,000 installs (median 100,000). The median daily open rate (daily active users as a share of people who had the app installed) was 4.0% (IQR 4.7%). Apps whose primary technique was a stand-alone breathing exercise had the lowest open rate (median 1.6%, 7 apps), significantly lower than trackers (6.3%) and peer-support apps (17.0%). Among active users, daily minutes were higher for mindfulness/meditation apps (median 21.47) than for tracker, breathing or psychoeducation apps (medians 3.53-8.32). Among the 59 apps with retention data, the median share of new users who opened the app on day 15 and on day 30 was 3.9% (IQR 10.3%) and 3.3% (IQR 6.2%). On day 30, mindfulness/meditation apps retained a median 4.7% vs 0.0% for breathing-exercise apps. Among apps large enough to have hourly data, meditation apps showed two daily usage peaks, morning (7-9 am) and late evening (10 pm-midnight); most other app types peaked in the evening.
claims.finding_zh: 独立用户行为面板数据（SimilarWeb，2017 年 8 月至 2018 年 7 月）：93 个下载量至少 1 万的安卓心理健康 App（中位下载量 10 万）。每天打开 App 的人占已安装人数的比例，中位数为 4.0%；以单独呼吸练习为主的 App 最低（1.6%，仅 7 个 App）。活跃用户中，正念/冥想类每天使用时长中位数为 21.47 分钟，高于记录、呼吸、心理教育类（3.53–8.32 分钟）。在有留存数据的 59 个 App 中，新用户在第 15 天、第 30 天打开 App 的比例中位数只有 3.9% 和 3.3%；第 30 天时冥想类为 4.7%，呼吸练习类为 0.0%。在有分时数据的大型 App 中，冥想类的使用高峰在早晨（7–9 点）和深夜（22–24 点），其他多数类型的高峰在晚上。
claims.study_type: observational analysis of independent usage-panel data
claims.sample: 93 Android apps (at least 10,000 installs); retention data for 59
claims.limitations: Android only. The data come from a single proprietary panel (SimilarWeb) with only partial external validation, collected Aug 2017 to Jul 2018. Category comparisons rest on few apps (7 breathing, 2 peer support) and may reflect app quality or user mix rather than the technique. Retention was tracked only to day 30 and was available for 59 of 93 apps. Hourly patterns exist only for very large apps. The data cannot show whether brief use still helped people.
claims.app_implication: Assume most people use the app only a few times. Each session must be complete on its own, with no locked multi-week path before value, and the first practice should be reachable in under 60 seconds. Give the stand-alone breathing tool extra care: stand-alone breathing apps had the lowest open and retention rates, though that rests on only 7 apps, so treat it as a warning sign, not a proven effect. Suggested reminder slots are morning and before sleep, matching meditation apps' observed usage peaks.

citation.authors: Baumel A, Muench F, Edan S, et al.
citation.title: Objective User Engagement With Mental Health Apps: Systematic Search and Panel-Based Usage Analysis

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; Europe PMC/PubMed abstract (PMID 31573916); PMC full text PMC6785720 (Methods, Tables 2-4, retention section, Limitations)
verification.problems: Metadata and all headline numbers match the PMC full text. The limitations contain an error: the usage data cover Aug 1 2017 to Jul 31 2018 (apps were identified in Nov 2018), not 2019. The claim also lacks context. Retention data existed for only 59 of 93 apps, and it means the share of day-0 openers who open the app on that particular day. The breathing category was only 7 apps (peer support 2), and breathing apps' lower open rate was significant only against trackers and peer support. Hourly patterns were available only for very large apps (meditation peaks 7-9 am and 10 pm-midnight). The 'breathing apps retained worst' implication rests on these few apps and may reflect app quality. Evidence weight 'moderate' is acceptable for descriptive data.

claims.topic: Privacy and third-party data sharing by mental-health apps
claims.finding: Cross-sectional technical assessment (April-June 2018) of 36 top-ranked depression and smoking-cessation apps for Android and iOS in the US and Australia, comparing privacy-policy disclosures with intercepted data transmissions. 25/36 (69%) had a privacy policy; 22/25 (88%) described primary uses of collected data but only 16 (64%) described secondary uses. 23/25 policies (92%) stated data would go to a third party, but transmission was detected in 33/36 apps (92%). 29/36 (81%) transmitted data for advertising/marketing or analytics to just two companies, Google and Facebook, yet only 12 of 28 (43%) transmitting to Google and 6 of 12 (50%) transmitting to Facebook disclosed it.
claims.finding_zh: 横断面技术评估（2018 年）：36 个排名靠前的抑郁和戒烟 App。69% 有隐私政策；实际检测到 92% 的 App 向第三方传输数据；81% 把数据发给谷歌或脸书用于广告、营销或分析，但向谷歌传数据的 App 只有 43% 披露，向脸书传数据的只有 50% 披露。
claims.sample: 36 apps
claims.limitations: 2018 snapshot of English-language apps in the US and Australia; platform privacy rules have changed since; Chinese apps and domestic SDKs were not studied.
claims.app_implication: Ship no third-party analytics, advertising, social-login or crash SDKs; no account required; practice and check-in data stay on the device by default. Publish a plain-language data statement listing every network request the app makes, so the policy matches actual behaviour.

citation.authors: Huckvale K, Torous J, Larsen ME
citation.title: Assessment of the Data Sharing and Privacy Practices of Smartphone Apps for Depression and Smoking Cessation

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; PubMed abstract (PMID 31002321); PMC full text PMC6481440 via Europe PMC fullTextXML: methods (app search, traffic interception), results, Table 2, limitations
verification.problems: No material discrepancies. Minor: 'English-language apps' in the limitations is an inference. The paper says the apps were found with the English search terms 'depression' and 'smoking cessation' in US and Australian stores (January 2018), but it does not state the apps' language.

claims.topic: Headspace and Smiling Mind RCT: short-term effects and the post-programme usage drop
claims.finding: Pre-registered RCT: 208 university students (aged 18-49) were randomly assigned to Headspace, Smiling Mind or a note-taking app used as an attention control (Evernote). They were asked to use it 10 minutes a day for 10 days, then had 30 days of discretionary access. Depressive symptoms, anxiety, stress, college adjustment, flourishing, resilience and mindfulness were measured at baseline, day 10 and day 40. From baseline to day 10, mindfulness-app users improved relative to control in depressive symptoms, college adjustment, resilience (Smiling Mind only) and mindfulness (Headspace only). Anxiety, stress and flourishing are not reported as improved. In the first author's thesis report of the same trial, anxiety and stress (pre-registered primary outcomes alongside depressive symptoms) and flourishing did not differ from control at day 10 or day 40. Self-reported use was high during the first 10 days (the app was used on 8 of 10 days) but low during the extended period (less than 20% used it 2 or more times per week). Participants who kept using the app frequently were more likely to maintain improvements to day 40, 'e.g. in depressive symptoms and resilience (Headspace only)' in the abstract's wording. This usage link is correlational.
claims.finding_zh: 预注册随机对照试验：208 名大学生（18–49 岁）被随机分配使用 Headspace、Smiling Mind，或作为注意力对照的笔记软件 Evernote。前 10 天每天用 10 分钟，之后 30 天自愿使用。在基线、第 10 天和第 40 天测量抑郁症状、焦虑、压力、大学适应、心盛（flourishing）、心理韧性和正念。第 10 天时，冥想 App 组在抑郁症状、大学适应、心理韧性（仅 Smiling Mind）和正念（仅 Headspace）上优于对照。焦虑、压力和心盛没有报告改善；第一作者博士论文对同一试验的报告显示，焦虑和压力（与抑郁症状同为预注册主要结局）以及心盛，在第 10 天和第 40 天都与对照没有差异。前 10 天使用率高（10 天中约用 8 天），之后不到 20% 的人每周使用 2 次以上；坚持频繁使用的人更可能把部分改善保持到第 40 天，但这只是相关关系。
claims.sample: n=208 university students
claims.limitations: Short: 10 prescribed days, 40 days in total. Convenience sample of students at one New Zealand university. Outcomes and usage were self-reported. Most outcomes did not improve versus control, including two of the three pre-registered primary outcomes (anxiety, stress). According to the first author's thesis, allocation was by enrolment session (everyone in a session got the same app), and control-app users' depressive symptoms rose slightly over the first 10 days, which adds to the between-group difference. The usage-maintenance links are correlational. The publisher full text was not read; the abstract and the thesis chapter on this trial were checked.
claims.app_implication: Expect a steep drop once any programme ends. Design the after-course home screen as carefully as day 1: a quiet default practice, the user's own plan, no guilt messaging. Describe app benefits as modest and outcome-specific, and never say 'reduces anxiety' or 'reduces stress'.

citation.authors: Flett JAM, Hayne H, Riordan BC, et al.
citation.title: Mobile Mindfulness Meditation: a Randomised Controlled Trial of the Effect of Two Popular Apps on Mental Health

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata (Mindfulness 10(5):863-876; online 31 Oct 2018, issue May 2019; not in PubMed or Europe PMC). Full publisher abstract read verbatim from a mirror (ifp.nyu.edu) and matched against the Otago repository record. Also read the first author's open-access PhD thesis (University of Otago, 2019), whose Chapter 3 reports the same trial: design, pre-registered outcomes, usage and between-group regression table. The publisher full text is paywalled and was not read.
verification.problems: Metadata and all numbers match the publisher abstract. Problems: (1) The claim says only that the abstract does not report anxiety, stress or flourishing as improved. It does not say that anxiety and stress were pre-registered primary outcomes (with depressive symptoms), so most of the improved outcomes it lists are secondary. In the same trial's thesis report, anxiety, stress and flourishing did not differ from control at day 10 or day 40. (2) The maintenance clause rewrites the abstract's ambiguous 'e.g. in depressive symptoms and resilience (Headspace only)' as 'depressive symptoms, and resilience for Headspace'. The abstract does not settle that reading, and the thesis version of this usage-moderation analysis reports different outcomes, a sign the finding is fragile. (3) The limitations leave out design points from the same trial: allocation was by enrolment session, and control-app (Evernote) users' depressive symptoms rose slightly, which adds to the between-group difference. The 'attention-control' label is confirmed by the thesis.

claims.topic: Push notifications: micro-randomized trial
claims.finding: Micro-randomized trial in 1,255 users of a commercial workplace well-being app (JOOL) over 89 days (March-August 2017). Only users with push notifications enabled were included; 2,045 of 3,300 users with the app installed had them switched off and were excluded. At one randomly selected time per day (8:30, 12:30, 17:30, 18:30, 19:30 or 20:30; never before noon on weekends), available users were randomized with equal probability to be sent or not sent a push notification containing a contextually tailored health message. Availability rules allowed at most one decision per day and spaced decisions 2-15 days apart depending on how long the user had been inactive, so users were available about 20% of the time. Users were 3.9% more likely to self-monitor in the app within the next 24 h when a message was sent (risk ratio 1.039, 95% CI 1.01-1.08, P<.05). The effect attenuated over the study, but not significantly (P=.84). It was larger on weekends (8.7%, 95% CI 1.01-1.17) than on weekdays (2.5%, 95% CI 0.98-1.07), but the difference was not significant (P=.18). In exploratory time-of-day analyses (no hypothesis tests; 90% CIs), the weekend effect was greatest at 12:30 (risk ratio 1.118, 90% CI 1.02-1.23 in the Results section; the abstract misprints this as 1.02-1.13), with a similar effect at 19:30 on weekends. On weekdays the largest effect was also at 12:30 (risk ratio 1.074, 90% CI 1.02-1.13).
claims.finding_zh: 微随机试验：某商业职场健康 App（JOOL）的 1255 名用户，持续 89 天（2017 年 3–8 月）。只纳入开启了推送通知的用户（3300 名安装者中有 2045 人关闭了通知，被排除）。每天随机抽取一个时间点（8:30、12:30、17:30、18:30、19:30 或 20:30；周末中午前不推送），对当时处于“可推送”状态的用户，以各 50% 的概率决定推送或不推送一条个性化健康提示。按规则每天最多决定一次，并根据用户不活跃的天数间隔 2–15 天，因此用户平均只有约 20% 的时间处于可推送状态。推送后 24 小时内在 App 中做自我记录的可能性相对提高 3.9%（风险比 1.039，95% CI 1.01–1.08），效果很小；效果随时间减弱，但不显著（P=0.84）。周末提高 8.7%（95% CI 1.01–1.17），工作日提高 2.5%（95% CI 0.98–1.07），两者差异不显著（P=0.18）。探索性分析（未做假设检验，用 90% CI）显示：周末 12:30 效果最大（风险比 1.118，90% CI 1.02–1.23；论文摘要误印为 1.02–1.13），周末 19:30 效果相近；工作日也是 12:30 效果最大（风险比 1.074，90% CI 1.02–1.13）。
claims.sample: n=1,255 users with push notifications enabled (of 3,300 with the app installed), 89 days, March-August 2017
claims.limitations: The outcome is proximal app engagement (self-monitoring within 24 h), not practice or wellbeing. It is one commercial workplace app whose users were mainly office workers, and only the 38% of installers who had notifications enabled were studied. Prompts were rationed (at most one per day, 2-15-day gaps, none on weekend mornings), so frequent or daily reminders were not tested. The relative effect is small. Time-of-day results are exploratory (no hypothesis tests, 90% CIs), and the abstract misprints the weekend 12:30 CI.
claims.app_implication: Reminders are worth offering but are a small lever. Make them opt-in, at most one per day, at a user-chosen time, with an optional separate weekend time. Midday or early evening looked best on weekends, but only in exploratory analyses. Do not remind lapsed users more often; the trial itself sent fewer prompts to inactive users and never tested daily reminders. Never stack several nudges.

citation.authors: Bidargaddi N, Almirall D, Murphy S, et al.
citation.title: To Prompt or Not to Prompt? A Microrandomized Trial of Time-Varying Push Notifications to Increase Proximal Engagement With a Mobile Health App

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; Europe PMC/PubMed abstract (PMID 30497999); PMC full text PMC6293241 (Europe PMC fullTextXML), incl. Methods availability rules, Results, Tables 1-5 and Limitations
verification.problems: Metadata (authors, title, venue, DOI, PMID) is correct and the core numbers match. (1) The weekend 12:30 90% CI is wrong. The full-text Results give RR 1.118 with 90% CI 1.02-1.23. The claim copied the abstract's '1.02 to 1.13', which repeats the weekday 12:30 interval and sits implausibly lopsided around 1.118. (2) The claim omits that the weekend 19:30 effect was similar to 12:30, which weakens the 'midday on weekends' implication. (3) It omits context that limits the reminder implication. The sample was only users with notifications enabled (2,045 of 3,300 installers were excluded). Prompts were rationed: at most one decision per day, none before noon on weekends, and gaps of 2-15 days depending on inactivity, so users were available only about 20% of the time. Daily reminders were therefore not tested. (4) The time-of-day analyses were exploratory, with no hypothesis tests. Evidence weight 'moderate' is appropriate.

claims.topic: Self-monitoring of goal progress
claims.finding: Meta-analysis of 138 studies (N = 19,951) that randomly allocated participants to an intervention designed to promote monitoring of goal progress vs a control condition. Almost all concerned health goals (e.g., weight, diet, physical activity, blood pressure, blood glucose, asthma, depression). Interventions increased the frequency of progress monitoring (d+ = 1.98, 95% CI 1.71-2.24) and promoted goal attainment (d+ = 0.40, 95% CI 0.32-0.48; k = 138, N = 18,398). Changes in monitoring frequency mediated the effect on goal attainment. Effects were highly heterogeneous (goal attainment Q(137) = 837.77, I² about 84%). Egger's test showed funnel-plot asymmetry for both outcomes. Trim-and-fill adjustment reduced the estimates to d+ = 1.16 (95% CI 0.89-1.44) for monitoring and d+ = 0.19 (95% CI 0.10-0.28) for goal attainment; the authors judged the influence of publication bias modest rather than severe. Goal attainment improved more when the information was physically recorded (d+ = 0.43 vs 0.29 when not recorded). It also improved more when progress was reported to someone else (d+ = 0.47, k = 95) or made public (d+ = 0.55, k = 3) than when it was kept private and unreported (d+ = 0.19, k = 14). Passive and active monitoring did not differ.
claims.finding_zh: 荟萃分析：138 项随机研究（N=19951），比较促进“监测目标进展”的干预与对照条件，几乎都是健康相关目标（如体重、饮食、运动、血压、血糖、哮喘、抑郁）。干预大幅提高了监测频率（d=1.98，95% CI 1.71–2.24），并促进了目标达成（d=0.40，95% CI 0.32–0.48）；监测频率的变化起中介作用。各研究结果差异很大（目标达成的 I² 约 84%）。Egger 检验提示存在小样本研究偏倚的迹象，用剪补法校正后，目标达成效应降至 d=0.19（95% CI 0.10–0.28）；作者认为发表偏倚的影响有限，不算严重。把进展实际记录下来时效果更大（d=0.43，不记录为 0.29）。把进展告诉他人（d=0.47，95 项研究）或公开（d=0.55，仅 3 项研究）时，效果大于完全私下且不告诉任何人（d=0.19）。被动监测与主动监测之间没有差异。
claims.sample: 138 studies, N=19,951 (goal-attainment analysis N=18,398)
claims.limitations: Heterogeneity is very high (I² about 84% for goal attainment). The funnel plot is asymmetric, and the bias-adjusted goal-attainment effect is about half the headline value (d+ = 0.19). Almost all studies concern health goals and none involve meditation. Moderator tests were not corrected for multiple comparisons, and the moderators overlap. The 'public' subgroup is only 3 studies, with a CI that crosses zero.
claims.app_implication: Keep an automatic practice log (date, minutes, type) with a weekly summary people can look back on. Add an optional one-tap note so they can record something themselves, since physically recording progress was linked to larger effects. If any sharing is offered, make it opt-in and private to one chosen person; the benefit came mainly from reporting progress to someone, not from public display. No leaderboards or default social sharing.

citation.authors: Harkin B, Webb TL, Chang BPI, et al.
citation.title: Does monitoring goal progress promote goal attainment? A meta-analysis of the experimental evidence

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; Europe PMC/PubMed abstract (PMID 26479070); accepted-manuscript full text from White Rose eprints 91437 (Results, publication-bias section, Tables 3-4, Limitations, reference list)
verification.problems: Metadata and every number quoted match the abstract and the accepted manuscript. However, the finding omits qualifiers from the full text that matter. Heterogeneity is very high (goal attainment Q(137)=837.77, I² about 84%; monitoring I² about 98%). Egger's test was significant for both outcomes. Trim-and-fill adjusted the estimates to d+ = 1.16 (0.89-1.44) for monitoring and d+ = 0.19 (0.10-0.28) for goal attainment, about half the headline effect, so 'publication bias possible' understates the issue. The 'made public' moderator rests on only 3 studies (d+ = 0.55, CI -0.16 to 1.26). The robust contrast is private-but-reported (d+ = 0.47, k=95) vs private-unreported (d+ = 0.19, k=14); recorded vs not recorded is 0.43 vs 0.29. Moderator tests were not corrected for multiple testing. The goal-attainment N is 18,398; 19,951 is the overall total. Given the inconsistency, small-study bias and indirectness (almost all health goals, no meditation studies found in the full text), 'high' overstates the evidence and 'moderate' fits.

claims.topic: If-then plans (implementation intentions)
claims.finding: Meta-analysis of 94 independent tests (63 reports, 8,461 participants; literature searched 1990-2003). Forming implementation intentions ('If situation Y is encountered, then I will initiate goal-directed behaviour X!'), which spell out when, where and how to act, had a positive effect of medium-to-large magnitude on goal attainment (d = .65, 95% CI .60-.70), with significant heterogeneity across studies. Effects were similar for experimental (83 tests) and correlational designs, for self-report and objective outcomes, and for published and unpublished tests. Implementation intentions helped initiate goal striving, shield goal pursuit from unwanted influences, disengage from failing courses of action and conserve capability for future striving. Forming them enhanced the accessibility of the specified situation and automated the goal-directed response.
claims.finding_zh: 荟萃分析（94 项独立检验，来自 63 篇报告，共 8461 名参与者，检索 1990–2003 年文献）：事先制定“如果遇到情境 Y，我就做行为 X”的执行意图（写明何时、何地、如何做），对达成目标有中到大的正效应（d = 0.65，95% CI 0.60–0.70），各研究之间差异显著。实验研究与相关研究、自评与客观结果、已发表与未发表研究的效应大小都相近。执行意图有助于启动行动、抵御干扰、及时放弃无效的做法并保留精力；它让设定的情境更容易被注意到，并让相应的行动更自动化。
claims.sample: 94 independent tests from 63 reports; 8,461 participants (79 tests, N = 6,855, in university students)
claims.limitations: 2006 synthesis dominated by university-student samples (79 of 94 tests) and many laboratory tasks. It used fixed-effect (inverse-variance) pooling despite significant heterogeneity (Q(93) = 173.46, p < .001). The chapter found no difference between published and unpublished tests (d = .65 vs .67), but domain-specific syntheses find smaller effects (physical activity SMD 0.31 post-intervention, 0.24 at follow-up; Bélanger-Gravel et al., Health Psychol Rev 2013). No meditation-specific trials.
claims.app_implication: Offer an optional one-sentence plan builder after the first session: 在【刷牙后】，我会做【3 分钟呼吸】, plus a backup plan 如果【太累】，就只做【1 分钟】. Show the plan on the home screen and reuse it as the reminder text; editable any time.

citation.authors: Gollwitzer PM, Sheeran P
citation.title: Implementation Intentions and Goal Achievement: A Meta-analysis of Effects and Processes

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; University of Konstanz KOPS repository record and scanned chapter PDF, read directly: p. 69 (abstract), p. 87 (Method, sample of studies), p. 92 (overall effect size), p. 93 (moderators, Table II); Bélanger-Gravel et al. 2013 abstract via OpenAlex and Crossref (doi 10.1080/17437199.2011.560095)
verification.problems: Finding matches the chapter (94 tests, d = .65, medium-to-large). The sample is now verifiable: 94 tests from 63 reports, 8,461 participants, 95% CI .60-.70. The limitations need correction. 'Publication bias likely' is not supported by the source: unpublished (k = 46, d = .67) and published (k = 48, d = .65) tests gave nearly identical effects. The more accurate caveats are fixed-effect (inverse-variance) pooling despite significant heterogeneity (Q(93) = 173.46, p < .001) and dominance of university-student samples (79 of 94 tests; N = 6,855). The Bélanger-Gravel et al. figures are verified: SMD 0.31 [0.11, 0.51] post-intervention and 0.24 [0.13, 0.35] at follow-up, 26 studies.

claims.topic: Single-item measure of stress symptoms
claims.finding: Validation of a single stress-symptom item in four independent cross-sectional datasets (N = 1,014; 1,015; 773; 2,156). Item: 'Stress means a situation in which a person feels tense, restless, nervous or anxious or is unable to sleep at night because his/her mind is troubled all the time. Do you feel this kind of stress these days?', answered on a 5-point scale from 1 'not at all' to 5 'very much'. The item converged with psychological-symptom and sleep-disturbance items and with validated well-being measures, had theoretically grounded associations with health and psychosocial work characteristics, and discriminated between gender, age and industry groups in line with a validated emotional-exhaustion scale. The authors concluded it showed satisfactory content, criterion and construct validity for group-level analysis.
claims.finding_zh: 在 4 组独立横断面数据（N=1014、1015、773、2156）中验证一个单题压力测量：“压力是指一个人感到紧张、坐立不安、神经紧绷或焦虑，或者因为心事重重而夜里睡不着的状态。你这些天有这种压力吗？”按 5 级作答，从 1“完全没有”到 5“非常多”。该题与心理症状、睡眠困扰及成熟量表的结果一致，作者认为它在群体层面分析中具有令人满意的效度。
claims.sample: 4 datasets of Finnish/Nordic workers, N = 1,014 / 1,015 / 773 / 2,156
claims.limitations: Validated for group-level analysis in Nordic working populations, not for individual diagnosis or momentary pre/post change; asks about 'these days', not this moment; no validated Simplified Chinese version found in this session; no test-retest reliability in the abstract.
claims.app_implication: Use this item (carefully translated and labelled as adapted) for an optional weekly check-in about recent days, not for the 5-second session check-in. Show results only as a personal trend, with no thresholds or diagnostic wording.

citation.authors: Elo AL, Leppänen A, Jahkola A
citation.title: Validity of a single-item measure of stress symptoms
citation.venue: Scandinavian Journal of Work, Environment & Health 29(6):444-451

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; PubMed abstract (PMID 14712852); full-text PDF from the journal site sjweh.fi (CC-BY 4.0): item wording (pp. 444-446), data sets and methods, Tables 1-4, discussion

claims.topic: Extrinsic rewards and intrinsic motivation (risk of over-gamification)
claims.finding: Meta-analysis of 128 experiments. Engagement-contingent, completion-contingent and performance-contingent rewards significantly undermined free-choice intrinsic motivation (d = -0.40, -0.36 and -0.28), as did all rewards, all tangible rewards and all expected rewards. Engagement- and completion-contingent rewards also undermined self-reported interest (d = -0.15 and -0.17, the latter after removing two outlier studies), as did all tangible and all expected rewards (small effects). Performance-contingent rewards did not affect self-reported interest (d = -0.01), and all rewards combined had no effect on it (d = 0.04). Unexpected rewards (free-choice d = 0.01) and task-noncontingent rewards (d = -0.14) did not significantly undermine intrinsic motivation. Positive feedback enhanced free-choice behaviour (d = 0.33) and self-reported interest (d = 0.31), but the free-choice gain was significant for college students (d = 0.43), not for children (d = 0.11). Tangible rewards tended to be more detrimental for children than for college students.
claims.finding_zh: 荟萃分析（128 项实验）：以“参与”“完成”或“表现”为条件的奖励，均显著削弱了人们在自由时间里自发从事该活动的内在动机（d 分别为 -0.40、-0.36、-0.28）；全部奖励合计、全部实物奖励和全部预期奖励也有削弱作用。以“参与”和“完成”为条件的奖励还小幅降低了自评兴趣（d=-0.15、-0.17），以“表现”为条件的奖励对自评兴趣没有影响。意外获得的奖励和与任务无关的奖励没有削弱内在动机。正面反馈（口头表扬）增加了自发行为（d=0.33）和自评兴趣（d=0.31），但对自发行为的提升只在大学生中显著，在儿童中不显著。实物奖励对儿童的削弱作用往往大于对大学生。
claims.sample: 128 studies
claims.limitations: Mostly short laboratory tasks with children and college students. There are essentially no studies of apps, digital gamification or meditation; one included dissertation used a computer-game setting. The interpretation was contested in the same journal issue (Eisenberger, Pierce & Cameron 1999, Psychol Bull 125(6):677-691; Lepper, Henderlong & Gingras 1999, Psychol Bull 125(6):669-676). Several pooled effects were heterogeneous, and some reported values come after outlier removal. App points and badges are not identical to tangible rewards.
claims.app_implication: No points, coins, levels, badges or unlockable content for practising, and content access never depends on streaks. This is a precautionary choice, because the evidence comes from expected, task-contingent rewards in laboratory tasks. Use specific informational feedback instead (这周你有 3 次在睡前做了呼吸练习).

citation.authors: Deci EL, Koestner R, Ryan RM
citation.title: A meta-analytic review of experiments examining the effects of extrinsic rewards on intrinsic motivation

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; Europe PMC/PubMed abstract (PMID 10589297); full-text PDF of the published article (summary Figures 1-2, results text, reference list); Crossref records for the 1999 comments by Eisenberger et al. (125(6):677-691) and Lepper et al. (125(6):669-676)
verification.problems: Metadata and all quoted numbers match the abstract and full text, and the Eisenberger, Pierce & Cameron citation in the limitations is correct. The claim omits several nulls. Unexpected rewards (free-choice d = 0.01) and task-noncontingent rewards (d = -0.14) did not undermine motivation. Performance-contingent rewards did not affect self-reported interest (d = -0.01), and all rewards combined had no effect on it (d = 0.04). Positive feedback did not significantly raise free-choice behaviour in children (d = 0.11, vs 0.43 in college students). The completion-contingent self-report value (-0.17) comes after removing 2 outliers; with all 15 studies it is d = -0.03. The zh text overgeneralises ('都会削弱') and adds '信息性' to positive feedback. The limitations say 'no digital studies', but at least one included dissertation (Liberty 1986) used a computer-game setting. Evidence weight 'moderate' is appropriate.

claims.topic: How long health habits take to form: systematic review and meta-analysis
claims.finding: Systematic review and meta-analysis of experimental intervention studies measuring self-reported habit or automaticity (SRHI or SRBAI) for health behaviours: 20 studies, 2,601 participants (mean ages 21.5-73.5 years); 11 rated high risk of bias (PEDro). Four studies reported time to habit formation. Two reported medians: 59 days (Keller et al.; individual range 4-335 days, with only 23% of participants reaching the habit threshold) and 66 days (Lally et al.; range 18-254 days). Two reported means: 91 days (self-reported, Lally et al.) and 106 vs 154 days (Fournier et al.; morning vs evening stretching). The authors conclude that health habits typically take about 2-5 months, with wide individual variation. Pooling 12 studies (19 intervention arms), habit scores rose from pre- to post-intervention (SMD 0.69, 95% CI 0.49-0.88; I2 = 87%). In narrative synthesis, single studies linked stronger habits to morning (vs evening) practice and to self-chosen (vs assigned) behaviours. Another found that enjoyment, planning and preparatory routines mediated physical-activity habit formation. One study found no difference between time-based and routine-based cues.
claims.finding_zh: 系统综述与荟萃分析：纳入 20 项用自我报告习惯/自动化量表（SRHI 或 SRBAI）评估健康行为的干预研究，共 2601 名参与者（平均年龄 21.5–73.5 岁），其中 11 项偏倚风险高。有 4 项研究报告了习惯形成所需时间：中位数分别为 59 天（Keller 等；个体范围 4–335 天，且只有 23% 的参与者达到习惯标准）和 66 天（Lally 等；18–254 天）；平均数分别为 91 天（Lally 等，参与者自己回忆）以及 106 天和 154 天（Fournier 等，早上与晚上做拉伸）。作者总结：健康习惯通常需要约 2–5 个月，个体差异很大。合并 12 项研究（19 个干预组）后，干预前后习惯评分提高（标准化均数差 0.69，95% CI 0.49–0.88；研究间差异很大，I² = 87%）。叙述性综合中，单项研究分别发现早上练习比晚上、自己选择的行为比被指定的行为形成的习惯更强，另有研究发现喜欢程度、具体计划和准备性习惯在运动习惯形成中起中介作用；还有一项研究发现按固定时间提示与按日常事件提示没有差别。
claims.study_type: systematic review and meta-analysis (pre-post meta-analysis of 12 studies plus narrative synthesis)
claims.sample: 20 studies, 2,601 participants; meta-analysis of 12 studies (19 intervention arms); time-to-habit data from only 4 studies
claims.limitations: Most included studies at high risk of bias. Time-to-habit figures come from just 4 studies, and the 4-335-day range from one study in which only 23% reached the threshold. The abstract's 'means 106-154 days' omits a 91-day self-reported mean. The pooled SMD is a pre-post change without control comparison, with I2 = 87% and no publication-bias assessment. Determinants (morning timing, self-selection) each rest on single studies. Behaviours (flossing, diet, physical activity, water, vitamin C, dishcloth microwaving, reducing sitting) differ from meditation.
claims.app_implication: Onboarding copy: 养成习惯通常需要两到五个月，因人而异; never '21 days'. Let users choose their own practice and time slot (self-chosen habits were stronger in one study). Offer a morning slot as an option, not a rule, since the morning advantage comes from a single stretching study. Consider offering to reduce reminders only after roughly 2-3 months of regular practice.

citation.authors: Singh B, Murphy A, Maher C, et al.
citation.title: Time to Form a Habit: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Health Behaviour Habit Formation and Its Determinants

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; Europe PMC record PMID 39685110 with abstract; PMC full text PMC11641623 (Methods, Results 3.3-3.5 incl. time-to-habit paragraph, meta-analysis paragraph with I2, determinants, Discussion, Conclusions)
verification.problems: Abstract-level numbers are reproduced correctly, but the full text shows several problems. (1) The four time-to-habit studies reported medians of 59 days (Keller et al.; range 4-335 days, and only 23% of participants reached the habit threshold) and 66 days (Lally et al.; 18-254). They also reported means of 91 days (SD 55; Lally et al., retrospective self-report) and 106 vs 154 days (Fournier et al., morning vs evening stretching). So the means span 91-154 days, not the abstract's 106-154, and the 4-335-day range comes from a single study. (2) The SMD of 0.69 pools only 12 of the 20 studies (19 intervention arms) with very high heterogeneity (I2 = 87%). It is a pre-post change, and publication bias was not assessed. (3) The determinants come from narrative synthesis of single studies: morning > evening from one stretching study (Fournier), self-selected > assigned from one study (van der Weiden). 'Generally' therefore overstates. The finding also omits a null: Keller et al. found no difference between time-based and routine-based cues. Metadata correct.

claims.topic: Habit formation in large objective datasets; time since last session as the key predictor
claims.finding: Machine-learning analysis (person-specific LASSO models, 'Predicting Context Sensitivity') of two objective panel datasets. The first is gym check-ins from a North American chain (24 Hour Fitness): over 12 million check-ins from 60,277 users, with an analytic sample of 30,110 members followed for a median of about 4 years. The second is RFID-monitored hospital handwashing: over 40 million opportunities from 5,246 workers in 30 hospitals, with an analytic sample of 3,124. Habit formation was defined as the time for behavioural predictability (AUC) to reach 95% of its asymptote. Because this could not be estimated reliably for individuals, curves were fitted to groups (deciles). Median time to habit formation was about 4-7 months (122-226 days) for gym attendance but about 9-10 shifts (a couple of weeks) for handwashing, i.e., no single 'magic number'. The strongest predictor of gym attendance was time since the previous visit: for 76% of members, the longer the gap, the lower the chance of going. Going on the same weekdays as before predicted attendance for 69%. These directions lack standard errors, and the authors call them suggestive. More predictable gym-goers responded less to a randomised intervention to increase attendance (r = -.48), but other reward-insensitivity tests (unusual weather; handwashing incentive programs) were null.
claims.finding_zh: 用机器学习分析两组客观追踪数据（为每个人单独建立 LASSO 预测模型）：北美连锁健身房（24 Hour Fitness）的签到记录（60277 名用户、超过 1200 万次签到，分析样本为 30110 名会员，中位追踪约 4 年），以及医院用 RFID 记录的洗手情况（30 家医院 5246 名医护人员、超过 4000 万次洗手机会，分析样本为 3124 人）。研究把“行为可预测性达到平台期 95% 所需时间”定义为习惯形成时间；由于在个人层面估计不稳定，曲线是按分组（十分位）拟合的。去健身房的中位时间约 4–7 个月（122–226 天），医院洗手只需约 9–10 个班次（几周），并不存在固定天数。预测去健身房最重要的因素是距上一次的时间间隔：76% 的会员间隔越久越不可能去；69% 的会员更可能在以往常去的星期几再去（这些方向性结果没有标准误，作者称其为提示性证据）。可预测性越高（习惯越固定）的人，对一项随机鼓励干预的反应越小（r = −0.48），但其他“对奖励变化不敏感”的检验（异常天气、洗手激励项目）都没有发现差异。
claims.study_type: observational analysis of large objective panel datasets (machine learning; group-level habit-time curves)
claims.sample: Gym: 30,110 members analysed (from 60,277 users; >12 million check-ins in the full dataset). Handwashing: 3,124 hospital workers analysed (from 5,246; >40 million opportunities in the full dataset).
claims.limitations: Observational and predictive, not causal. Habit is operationalised as behavioural predictability, not automaticity. Time-to-habit could not be estimated reliably per person and was fitted to decile groups. Individual predictors have no standard errors, so directional findings are suggestive. Reward-insensitivity evidence is mixed (one positive test, two null). Gym attendance and workplace handwashing differ from home meditation. Single study.
claims.app_implication: Treat 'days since last practice' as the key engagement signal: after a gap (e.g., 3 or more days) the home screen offers a 1-minute re-entry practice and a neutral 'welcome back', never a broken-streak notice. Suggest keeping the same weekdays and time; tell users that more complex routines can take months.

citation.authors: Buyalskaya A, Ho H, Milkman KL, et al.
citation.title: What can machine learning teach us about habit formation? Evidence from exercise and hygiene
citation.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the USA 120(17):e2216115120

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; Europe PMC record PMID 37068252 with abstract; PMC full text PMC10151500 (Study 1 and 2 data and analytic samples, habit-curve method, Table 2 predictors, reward-sensitivity analyses, Discussion)
verification.problems: (1) Time-to-habit was not estimated per person. The authors state the time-varying procedure 'did not work reliably at the individual level', so curves were fitted to decile groups by data length. The 122-226 days (4-7 months) is the median across gym-goers well fit by the exponential model; the handwashing 9-10 shifts is per decile. (2) The 12 million check-ins and 40 million observations describe the full raw datasets (60,277 gym users; 5,246 workers in 30 hospitals), not the analytic samples of 30,110 and 3,124. The handwashing sample had a median of ~3,000 observations per worker, far fewer than 40 million in total. (3) Omitted nulls: there was no reduced sensitivity to unusual weather after habit formation, and no differential response of more predictable caregivers to handwashing incentive programs. Only the randomised StepUp gym intervention showed the effect (r = -.48). (4) 'Moderate' overstates a single observational, predictive analysis whose predictor directions the authors call suggestive (no standard errors); 'low' fits and matches how comparable single-cohort studies are graded. Verified as stated: 76%, 69%, 122-226 days, 9-10 shifts, the less-responsive-to-intervention finding and the citation metadata.

claims.topic: Streak counters: intact vs broken streaks
claims.finding: Seven studies on logged 'streaks' (a behaviour performed consecutively three or more times): one correlational field study of a step-count app and six online experiments with simulated apps. Highlighting an intact streak in a behavioural log increased subsequent engagement relative to highlighting a broken streak. In Study 3, highlighting a broken streak lowered engagement even below showing no log (45% vs 61%), while highlighting an intact streak raised it (92% vs 65%). The effect was independent of actual past behaviour and depended on how the behaviour was represented in the log, because consumers treat maintaining a logged streak as a goal in itself. The effect was amplified when people attributed the break to themselves: engagement was 29%, vs 53% with an intact streak. An externally caused break gave 42%, a marginal difference from intact (p = .064). The effect was attenuated when people could 'repair' a broken streak (93% intact, 85% repairable, 69% broken). Broken streaks also produced more momentary negative emotion, which the repair option did not reduce.
claims.finding_zh: 7 项研究考察“连续记录”（同一行为连续完成 3 次及以上）：其中 1 项是使用真实计步 App 的相关性现场研究，6 项是使用模拟 App 的在线实验。在记录中突出“连续未中断”，比突出“已中断”带来更多后续参与；在研究 3 中，突出“已中断”甚至让参与率低于完全不显示记录（45% 对 61%），而突出“未中断”则让参与率升高（92% 对 65%）。这种影响与实际做过多少无关，只取决于记录如何呈现，因为人们会把“保持连续”本身当成目标。如果人们把中断归咎于自己，影响更大（参与率 29%，未中断为 53%；外部原因造成的中断为 42%，与未中断的差异仅接近显著，p = 0.064）；如果允许“修复”中断，影响会减弱（未中断 93%、可修复 85%、已中断 69%）。中断还会带来更多即时负面情绪，“可修复”并没有减少这种情绪。
claims.study_type: multi-study paper: 1 correlational field study + 6 online experiments (consumer research)
claims.sample: Study 1: 980 university employees (30-day step challenge, field data). Studies 2-7: MTurk adults, 601-805 recruited per experiment (analysed samples about 400-600).
claims.limitations: Experiments used simulated apps and mostly immediate, single-session choices; the field study is correlational; no meditation apps. Outcomes were engagement. Only momentary negative emotion and sense of accomplishment were measured (Study 7), with no measures of longer-term pressure, guilt or wellbeing. One research team, with no independent replication.
claims.app_implication: No fragile consecutive-day streak by default; show days practised this week/month. If an optional goal exists, make it weekly with rest days and an explicit repair (a short session the next day keeps the week). Never highlight a broken streak, since showing one lowered engagement below showing no log at all. Use neutral, externally attributing copy after a break (生活总有起伏), never 你中断了 12 天连续记录.

citation.authors: Silverman J, Barasch A
citation.title: On or Off Track: How (Broken) Streaks Affect Consumer Decisions

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata (JCR 49(6):1095-1117; online 30 Jun 2022); authors' accepted manuscript from University of Delaware UDSpace (abstract, Studies 1-7 methods and results, General Discussion)
verification.problems: Finding matches the abstract; the problems are in sample and limitations. (1) Per-study samples are verifiable. Study 1 was a correlational field study of 980 university employees in a 30-day, 7,000-step challenge using a real step-count app. Studies 2-7 were MTurk experiments with simulated fitness, language-learning and game apps (601-805 recruited; analysed samples about 400-600). (2) The limitation 'not ... health apps' is inaccurate: Studies 1-2 used fitness or step-count apps. (3) The limitation 'did not measure ... costs' is partly inaccurate. Study 7 measured momentary negative emotion: it was higher after broken than intact streaks, and the repair option did not reduce it. Study 6 found no effect on willingness to recommend or keep using the app. (4) Omitted nuance: in Study 6, intact vs externally-caused break was only marginal (53% vs 42%, p = .064), while a self-attributed break cut engagement to 29%. In Study 3, highlighting a broken streak lowered engagement below showing no log (45% vs 61%).

claims.topic: Short vs long practice sessions for novices
claims.finding: Randomized controlled experiment: 71 healthy adults with limited mindfulness experience (71.8% female) were assigned to four 20-min mindfulness practices, four 5-min practices, or an audiobook control, held in person over 2 weeks, with every group listening to the same total length of material each session. Both practice groups improved trait mindfulness, depression, anxiety and stress compared with control. Unexpectedly, the shorter practice had a significantly greater effect than the longer practice on trait mindfulness (d = 2.17, p < .001) and stress (d = -1.18, p < .01), with trends in the same direction for depression and anxiety.
claims.finding_zh: 随机对照实验：71 名冥想经验很少的健康成年人，分为 4 次 20 分钟练习组、4 次 5 分钟练习组和有声书对照组，2 周内线下完成（每次聆听总时长相同）。两个练习组在正念、抑郁、焦虑和压力上都优于对照组；出乎意料的是，5 分钟组在正念（d=2.17）和压力（d=-1.18）上的改善显著大于 20 分钟组，抑郁和焦虑也有同方向趋势。
claims.sample: n=71 healthy novice adults
claims.limitations: Very small groups; only 4 sessions in 2 weeks; in-person delivery; implausibly large, imprecise effect sizes; short follow-up; says nothing about experienced practitioners or long-term dose.
claims.app_implication: Default first sessions to 3-5 minutes and make 1- and 3-minute options prominent; offer 10-20+ minute sessions as choices, never as levels to unlock; never describe short practice as inferior.

citation.authors: Strohmaier S, Jones FW, Cane JE
citation.title: Effects of Length of Mindfulness Practice on Mindfulness, Depression, Anxiety, and Stress: a Randomized Controlled Experiment

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata (and Semantic Scholar/OpenAlex for journal pages). The published abstract was read via the Springer Medizin mirror (mijn.bsl.nl) through WebFetch, with verbatim fragments. Also the authors' Psychonomic 2020 poster abstract (pure.canterbury.ac.uk, verbatim quotes) and ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03797599. PubMed, PMC and Europe PMC were searched. The Springer full text was blocked or paywalled.
verification.problems: No material discrepancies. Metadata matches Crossref (online 6 Oct 2020; issue 12(1), 2021), and the empty PMID is correct because the paper is not indexed in PubMed or Europe PMC. N=71, 71.8% female, healthy novices, the three arms, in-person delivery over 2 weeks, the equal total listening time, both arms beating control, d = 2.17 (p<.001) for trait mindfulness, d = -1.18 (p<.01) for stress, and the same-direction trends for depression and anxiety all match the abstract. The poster abstract agrees. The registry confirms 2 sessions a week for 2 weeks, each 25 min, with audiobook filler (the 5-min arm heard 20 min of audiobook plus 5 min of practice), and an FFMQ-15 primary outcome at post-intervention. Minor notes: '正念' in the zh means trait mindfulness, and the abstract's mixed mediation results are omitted. Because the full text was not readable, the effect-size CIs were not checked. Evidence weight 'low' is appropriate.

claims.topic: Calm app RCT: efficacy and real adherence
claims.finding: Wait-list RCT: 109 full-time undergraduates with elevated stress (Perceived Stress Scale >= 14) were randomized (56 Calm, 53 wait-list) and asked to meditate with the Calm app at least 10 minutes per day for 8 weeks. Only 88 (41 Calm, 47 control) were analysed. Those who did not complete the post-intervention survey (n=18), never set up a Calm account (n=2) or never meditated (n=1) were excluded, so the analysis was not intention-to-treat. After covariate adjustment, the Calm group improved more than controls in perceived stress, mindfulness and self-compassion post-intervention (all P < .04). These effects persisted at the 12-week follow-up (all P < .03), except for the nonreacting mindfulness subscale (P = .08). Effect sizes ranged from 0.59 (mindfulness 'describing' subscale) to 1.24 (perceived stress). Among the exploratory health behaviours, sleep disturbance showed a significant group-by-time interaction; binge drinking, physical activity and fruit and vegetable intake showed no significant effects. Adherence, from Calm usage reports and counting analysed participants only: mean 37.9 (SD 30.5) minutes per week over the 8 weeks, about half of the roughly 70 minutes requested; 56% (23/41) exceeded 30 minutes per week and 22% (9/41) exceeded 60 minutes. About one-third (14/41, 34%) kept meditating during the 4-week follow-up, averaging 20.4 (SD 23.9) minutes (the abstract reports about 20 minutes per week).
claims.finding_zh: 等待对照随机试验：109 名压力偏高（压力知觉量表 ≥14 分）的全日制大学生随机分组（Calm 组 56 人，等待组 53 人），要求 8 周内每天用 Calm 冥想至少 10 分钟。只有 88 人（Calm 组 41 人，对照组 47 人）纳入分析：没完成干预后问卷（18 人）、没开通 Calm 账号（2 人）或从未冥想（1 人）的人被排除，所以不是意向性治疗（ITT）分析。校正协变量后，Calm 组在压力、正念和自我关怀上的改善大于对照组（效应量 0.59–1.24）；12 周随访时，除正念“不反应”分量表外，效果仍在。探索性指标中，睡眠困扰出现显著的组别×时间交互作用，饮酒、运动和蔬果摄入没有显著变化。实际使用（只统计纳入分析的人）远低于要求：平均每周 37.9 分钟（要求约 70 分钟），56% 每周超过 30 分钟，只有 22% 超过 60 分钟；之后 4 周随访期内约三分之一（34%）继续练习，平均约 20 分钟（摘要称约每周 20 分钟）。
claims.sample: n=109 randomized; 88 analysed undergraduates with elevated stress
claims.limitations: Not intention-to-treat: 21 of 109 randomized were excluded (15 of 56 in the Calm arm), including people who never set up or used Calm, which can inflate both the effect sizes and the adherence figures. Small sample; inactive wait-list control; unblinded self-reported outcomes. Participants received gift cards (US$5, 10 and 15) and free Calm memberships, which the authors say may have affected results and adherence. Participants were mostly young, female (79/88) students at one university in the US Southwest. The health-behaviour outcomes were exploratory. The first author later became Calm's Director of Science, disclosed as starting almost a year after the study's design, data collection and analysis.
claims.app_implication: Set defaults around realistic use (about 5 minutes a day, 35-40 minutes a week, and less once a programme ends) rather than a prescribed 10 minutes a day. Weekly summaries should acknowledge any practice without implying a quota. When citing app RCTs in the app, show the control type, whether everyone randomized was analysed, and any conflicts of interest.

citation.authors: Huberty J, Green J, Glissmann C, et al.
citation.title: Efficacy of the Mindfulness Meditation Mobile App 'Calm' to Reduce Stress Among College Students: Randomized Controlled Trial

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata + Europe PMC abstract + PMC full text (PMC6614998): methods, enrollment flow, results, adherence ('Demand') section, incentives, limitations and conflict-of-interest statement
verification.problems: Metadata and every number reported (P values, effect-size range 0.59-1.24, adherence 37.9 [SD 30.5] min/week, 23/41, 9/41, 14/41, 20.4 min) match the full text, as does the COI disclosure. Problems: (1) The claim leaves out that 109 were randomized (56 Calm, 53 wait-list) and only 88 analysed. People who did not complete the post-survey (18), never set up Calm (2) or never meditated (1) were excluded, so this was a completers analysis, not intention-to-treat. That can inflate the effect sizes and the adherence figures, which come only from analysed users. (2) finding_zh describes the sample as '88 名…大学生' without saying this. (3) In the Results the follow-up figure of 20.4 (SD 23.9) minutes has no time unit; only the abstract says about 20 min/week. (4) 'Other health behaviours did not change' overstates the source, which reports no significant effects.

claims.topic: Computerized visual analogue scale for state anxiety (VAS-A)
claims.finding: Two experiments tested a computerized single-item visual analogue scale for state anxiety (VAS-A). It is a 100-mm horizontal line anchored 'calm' (left) and 'anxious' (right) and scored 0-30. Participants used a mouse to move a marker that started at the midpoint, in answer to 'How anxious do you feel right now?'. Experiment 1 (172 non-selected undergraduates, 125 female; two sessions exactly one week apart; Spearman correlations): test-retest r = .44 (p < .001), against r = .56 for the 20-item STAI-State in the same sample, which the authors describe as the low-to-medium stability expected for measures of momentary anxiety. Convergent validity with STAI-State was r = .60 in session 1 and .62 in session 2 (p < .001). For discriminant validity, correlations with trait anxiety, social anxiety, depression and state anger (r = .24-.31) were significantly smaller than with STAI-State and became non-significant after controlling for STAI-State. Experiment 2 (49 undergraduates with high social anxiety, 40 female; no no-stress control group): mean VAS-A rose from 12.4 before to 19.5 during a public-speaking stressor (F(1,48) = 25.13, p < .001, partial eta squared = .34; rise in 41 of 49 participants), and the rise correlated with the STAI-State rise (r = .51). The authors describe administration as simple and rapid.
claims.finding_zh: 两项实验检验了电脑版单题视觉模拟焦虑量表（VAS-A）：屏幕上一条 100 毫米的横线，左端写“平静”，右端写“焦虑”，参与者用鼠标把起始于中点的滑块拖到代表“你此刻感到多焦虑？”的位置，计 0–30 分。实验 1（172 名未经筛选的大学生，女性 125 名，两次测量相隔一周）：重测相关 r=0.44（同一批人用 20 题的 STAI 状态焦虑量表为 0.56；作者认为测“此刻状态”的工具稳定性偏低在预期之内）；与 STAI 状态分量表相关 r=0.60（第二次为 0.62）；与特质焦虑、社交焦虑、抑郁、状态愤怒的相关（r=0.24–0.31）明显更低，控制状态焦虑后不再显著（区分效度）。实验 2（49 名社交焦虑较高的大学生，女性 40 名，没有不施加压力的对照组）：在公开演讲压力任务中，平均分从 12.4 升到 19.5（F(1,48)=25.13，49 人中 41 人上升），升幅与 STAI 状态分的升幅相关（r=0.51）。作者认为它施测简单、快速。
claims.sample: Experiment 1: 172 Israeli undergraduates (125 female), tested twice one week apart; Experiment 2: 49 undergraduates with high social anxiety (40 female)
