claims.limitations: Non-clinical, mostly female Israeli student samples. Measures were given in a fixed order. Experiment 2 had no no-stress control group and only two time points. Sensitivity was shown only for a stress-induced increase, not for decreases such as after relaxation or meditation. The one-week test-retest value (.44) mixes true change in a momentary state with measurement error, so it is not a direct estimate of single-reading noise. Convergence with the 20-item STAI-State (r = .60-.62) means the single item agrees only partly with the longer scale. The validated format was a 0-30 mouse-driven slider anchored 'calm'-'anxious', with the marker starting at the midpoint; a 0-10 tap scale asking about tension (紧张) is a different instrument that this study did not validate. No Chinese validation.
claims.app_implication: Default 5-second pre/post check-in: one momentary rating (此刻有多紧张？) on a 0-10 tap scale, with nothing preselected and always skippable. Label it as an adapted single item. The validated VAS-A was a 0-30 'calm'-'anxious' slider about anxiety, with the marker starting at the midpoint, and it was shown to detect stress-induced rises, not drops after practice. Because a single pre/post difference mixes real change with measurement error, show medians across several sessions and never highlight a single-session change of 1 point.

citation.authors: Abend R, Dan O, Maoz K, et al.

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; PubMed abstract (PMID 24978117); full text of the published article (PDF on the senior author's lab site, people.socsci.tau.ac.il): methods, results, Tables 1-2, discussion and limitations
verification.problems: The numbers in finding and finding_zh are correct (r = .44, r = .60, F(1,48) = 25.13). Problems: (1) The sample field is incomplete. The full text gives Experiment 1 n = 172 undergraduates (125 female) and Experiment 2 n = 49 (40 female), not 'about 50' with Experiment 1 unverified. (2) The limitations misread the test-retest result. It was a one-week retest of a momentary state measure, which the authors expected to be low; the 20-item STAI-State was itself only .56 in the same sample. So it does not show that single readings are noisy, because it mixes true state change with error. The authors also call r = .60-.62 'highly correlated', not 'moderate'. (3) The app implication carries validity over from a 0-30 'calm'-'anxious' mouse slider (marker starting at the midpoint, asking about anxiety) to a 0-10 tap scale about tension, without saying this is an unvalidated adaptation. (4) The claim leaves out that Experiment 2 had no no-stress control group.

claims.topic: Habit formation timeline and the effect of a missed day
claims.finding: Field study: 96 volunteers (mostly postgraduate students, mean age 27) each chose an eating, drinking or exercise behaviour (4 chose another behaviour, e.g. meditation) to perform once a day in response to the same daily cue (e.g., 'after breakfast') for 12 weeks (84 days). They were asked to complete the Self-Report Habit Index every day. 82 provided sufficient data (logging on a median of 47 of 84 days). An asymptotic automaticity curve could be fitted for 62 and fitted well for 39. Among those 39, the modelled time to reach 95% of their own automaticity plateau had a median of 66 days and ranged from 18 to 254 days (values beyond day 84 are model extrapolations). Performing the behaviour more consistently was associated with better model fit; the authors note that about half of participants did not perform the behaviour consistently enough to reach habit status. A single missed opportunity (140 instances in 55 participants) was followed by a very small next-day dip in automaticity (0.29 points) with no longer-term cost, i.e., it did not materially affect habit formation.
claims.finding_zh: 现场研究：96 名志愿者（多为研究生，平均 27 岁）各自选择一个饮食、饮水或运动行为（另有 4 人选择了冥想等其他行为），在每天固定出现一次的情境中（如“早餐后”）执行，为期 12 周（84 天），并被要求每天填写自我报告习惯指数。82 人数据可用（中位数为 84 天中登录 47 天）；62 人可拟合出渐近曲线，其中 39 人拟合良好。在这 39 人中，达到个人“自动化程度”平台期 95% 所需的模型估计时间中位数为 66 天，范围 18 至 254 天（超过 84 天观察期的数值是模型外推）。执行越规律，曲线拟合越好；作者指出约一半参与者执行得不够规律，没有达到习惯状态。单独漏掉一次（55 人共 140 次）后，第二天的自动化评分只有很小的下降（平均 0.29 分），之后没有持续影响，即并未实质影响习惯形成。
claims.study_type: longitudinal field study (single cohort, daily self-report, individual nonlinear curve fitting)
claims.sample: n=96 recruited (predominantly postgraduate students, mean age 27); 82 analysed; curve fitted for 62, good fit for 39
claims.limitations: Small self-selected, mostly student sample; automaticity is self-reported (SRHI automaticity items); the 66-day median and 18-254-day range come only from the 39 participants (under half of the 82 analysed) whose curves fitted well; estimates beyond day 84 are extrapolated; mostly simple eating, drinking or exercise behaviours (only 4 of 96 chose another behaviour such as meditation); the missed-day analysis covers single omissions only, and the authors suggest (citing other work) that missing a week of opportunities may hinder habit formation. The 66-day median is not in the abstract; it is in the Results and Discussion and is restated by the same group (Gardner et al. 2012, BJGP: plateau 'after an average of 66 days') and by Singh et al. 2024.
claims.app_implication: Never reset or penalise progress for a single missed day, and never promise '21 days'. Expectation copy: 养成习惯通常需要两个月左右甚至更久，个体差异很大；偶尔漏一天没关系. Progress UI counts practice days per week/month instead of a fragile consecutive streak; after several missed days in a row, offer a gentle, low-effort way back rather than a warning.

citation.authors: Lally P, van Jaarsveld CHM, Potts HWW, et al.
citation.title: How are habits formed: Modelling habit formation in the real world
citation.venue: European Journal of Social Psychology 40(6):998-1009 (online 16 July 2009)

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata (vol 40(6):998-1009, online 16 Jul 2009, print Oct 2010); OpenAlex abstract; publisher full text (archived Wiley HTML of doi 10.1002/ejsp.674: Method, Results incl. Table 2 text and missed-opportunity analysis, Discussion); Keller et al. 2021 BJHP (Lally co-author) restatement; Gardner et al. 2012 BJGP (PMC3505409 page); PubMed search (no PMID exists)
verification.problems: Numbers are correct but mis-scoped: the 66-day median and 18-254-day range are reported only for the 39 participants whose curves fitted well (Table 2), not for 'each person' as the finding implies. Missing context: participants were mostly postgraduate students (mean age 27, 66 women/30 men); they were asked to complete the SRHI daily but logged on a median of 47 of 84 days; the authors note about half did not perform consistently enough to reach habit status. The missed-day result concerns single omissions (140 instances in 55 participants; next-day dip of 0.29 points, no longer-term cost); the authors suggest, citing other work, that missing a week may hinder habit formation. Limitation 'not meditation' is slightly inaccurate: 4 of 96 chose another behaviour such as meditation. Citation metadata, empty PMID and the Gardner 2012 'average of 66 days' restatement verified.

claims.topic: Reminders vs event-based cues in habit apps
claims.finding: Four-week randomised field experiment with a 3x2 between-subjects design: cue (none, daily SMS reminder, or lunch as trigger event) by positive reinforcement (none or SMS confirmation). 133 participants (mostly students) were asked to text a report of their lunch every day; 96 (72%) completed and were analysed. Automaticity, measured once at the end with the SRBAI, was lowest in the reminder groups (mean 15). It was higher with the lunch trigger (20; p < .001 vs reminders) or no cue (19; p = .004 vs reminders); trigger and no-cue groups did not differ significantly. Reminders produced the highest adherence (94% vs 75-76%). The authors therefore conclude that reminders supported repetition but may have hindered habit development. Positive-reinforcement messages were associated with slightly lower automaticity (17 vs 19.5; p = .013) and did not improve adherence. A functionality review of 115 habit-formation apps found they mainly offered task tracking (77%) and reminders (44%); only 3 (3%) helped users define contextual cues.
claims.finding_zh: 为期 4 周的随机现场实验（3×2 组间设计：提示方式为无提示、每日短信提醒或以“午餐”作为触发事件 × 有无短信正向回馈），133 名参与者（大多是学生）被要求每天用短信报告午餐内容，96 人（72%）完成并纳入分析。研究结束时用 SRBAI 量表测一次自动化程度：提醒组最低（平均 15 分），午餐触发组（20 分，与提醒组相比 p < 0.001）和无提示组（19 分，p = 0.004）更高，触发组与无提示组之间没有显著差异。提醒组坚持度最高（94%，其他组 75–76%），因此作者认为提醒有助于重复行为，但可能妨碍习惯真正形成。正向回馈短信反而与略低的自动化程度相关（17 分对 19.5 分，p = 0.013），也没有提高坚持度。对 115 个习惯类 App 的功能评估发现，它们主要提供打卡记录（77%）和提醒（44%），只有 3 个（3%）帮助用户设定情境提示。
claims.study_type: randomised 3x2 field experiment (4 weeks) + app functionality review (CHI conference paper)
claims.sample: 133 randomised (82% students, 81% women, mean age 25), 96 analysed (13-20 per condition); 115 apps reviewed
claims.limitations: Small cells (13-20 per condition). Artificial target behaviour (texting a lunch report). Automaticity measured only once at the end, with no baseline. 28% attrition, higher in the trigger and control groups (9 each) than in the reminder groups (2-4), which could bias the automaticity comparisons. Technical glitches in reinforcement messages. Event cues did not outperform no cue. Short 4-week horizon; not meditation.
claims.app_implication: Make the anchor event from the user's if-then plan the primary cue and phrase any notification around it (刷牙后 · 3 分钟呼吸): in this small study, reminders improved adherence but were linked to lower automaticity. Keep reminders available early on, and after about 8 weeks of regular practice offer to reduce or switch them off. Avoid automated praise messages and points, which showed no benefit and possibly harm.

citation.authors: Stawarz K, Cox AL, Blandford A
citation.title: Beyond Self-Tracking and Reminders: Designing Smartphone Apps That Support Habit Formation

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; OpenAlex abstract; Bristol research portal (full title); full text of the authors' version (UCL Discovery eprint 1468224, archived copy): Study I method, findings and discussion; Study II app review
verification.problems: The abstract wording is reproduced, but the full text shows the finding overstates. (1) Event-based (lunch-trigger) groups did not differ significantly from no-cue groups in automaticity (trigger mean 20 vs no cue 19, n.s.). The significant result is that reminder groups were lower (15) than trigger (p < .001) and no-cue (p = .004). (2) Positive reinforcement was not merely ineffective: conditions with confirmation messages had significantly lower automaticity (17 vs 19.5; F(1,90) = 6.39, p = .013), and message-delivery glitches occurred. (3) Design was not described: 133 participants were randomised to a 3x2 between-subjects design. The behaviour was texting a daily lunch report for 28 days. SRBAI was measured only at the end, with no baseline. 96 (72%) were analysed, 13-20 per cell. Dropout was differential: 9 each from trigger and control vs 2-4 from reminder groups. 82% were students. (4) Reminders raised adherence (94% vs 75-76%). (5) 'Apps did not support event-based cues' is slightly overstated: 3 of 115 (3%) helped users define contextual cues. Evidence weight should be very-low.

claims.topic: Brief breathing space as a session add-on: null result and 2-step adaptation
claims.finding: RCT in routine outpatient psychotherapy (n = 162 patients with anxiety or depression). Each of 25 therapy sessions began with either a 5-min audio 'session-introducing intervention with mindfulness elements' (SIIME) adapted from the MBCT breathing space, a short progressive muscle relaxation (PMR), or treatment as usual (TAU). Multilevel models showed symptom reduction and rising therapeutic alliance in all arms, but no significant time x condition interactions: SIIME had no advantage over PMR or TAU. During development (feedback from 20 patient-therapist dyads and 5 mindfulness experts), the three-step hourglass (wide -> narrow -> wide) was reduced to two components, narrow (breath) then wide (whole body), because this was easier for participants with little mindfulness experience.
claims.finding_zh: 在常规门诊心理治疗中进行的随机对照试验（焦虑或抑郁患者162人）。25次治疗的每一次开头，分别做5分钟改编自MBCT呼吸空间的正念导入音频、简短的渐进式肌肉放松，或常规治疗。多层模型显示三组症状都下降、治疗联盟都上升，但时间×组别交互作用不显著：正念导入并不优于放松或常规治疗。开发阶段根据20对患者-治疗师和5位正念专家的反馈，把三步「沙漏」（宽→窄→宽）简化为两步：先收窄到呼吸，再扩展到全身，因为这对正念经验少的人更容易。
claims.sample: n = 162 outpatients with anxiety or depression
claims.limitations: Tests the breathing space as a brief add-on inside individual psychotherapy (little room for incremental benefit), not as a standalone daily practice; co-practised with therapists; German routine-care sample.
claims.app_implication: Do not claim that a brief breathing space adds clinical benefit by itself. Offer a 2-step beginner version (breath -> whole body) as an on-ramp, then the full 3-step version.

citation.authors: Mander J, Blanck P, Neubauer AB, et al.
citation.title: Mindfulness and progressive muscle relaxation as standardized session-introduction in individual therapy: A randomized controlled trial

verification.checked_against: Crossref + Europe PMC abstract + PMC full text (PMC6826255): Methods 2.1-2.5, Results 3.2-3.7, Discussion
verification.problems: None. Context only, not errors: the trial ran at a German university outpatient CBT training centre with 48 trainee therapists who mostly had little mindfulness experience. It was pragmatic and unblinded. SIIME and PMR were both 5-min audio recordings. KIMS mindfulness scores and response/remission rates also showed no group differences. It was published online on 8 Oct 2018; the print issue is Jan 2019 (75(1):21-45). The 5-min audio, the 25 sessions, n = 162, the null time x condition interactions, the 20 dyads plus 5 experts, and the 2-component narrow -> wide adaptation all match the source.

claims.topic: Mainland Chinese terminology in the Chinese edition of Full Catastrophe Living
claims.finding: The mainland Chinese translation of Full Catastrophe Living (2nd ed.; translated by Tong Huiqi and Gao Xubin; China Machine Press, May 2018; ISBN 9787111594963; 540 pp.) renders the MBSR practices in its chapter titles as 正念练习 (mindfulness practice), 坐姿冥想 (sitting meditation, ch. 4), 身体扫描 (body scan, ch. 5, 安住于你的身体中：身体扫描), 瑜伽是冥想 (yoga as meditation, ch. 6), 正念行走 (walking meditation, ch. 7), 一日正念 (day of mindfulness, ch. 8), 坚持正式练习 (formal practice, ch. 34) and 保持非正式正念练习 (informal practice, ch. 35); responding vs reacting to stress is 用回应替代对压力反应 (ch. 20).
claims.finding_zh: 《多舛的生命》（Full Catastrophe Living第2版中文版；童慧琦、高旭滨译；机械工业出版社，2018年5月；ISBN 9787111594963；540页）在章节标题中这样翻译MBSR练习：正念练习、坐姿冥想（第4章）、身体扫描（第5章「安住于你的身体中：身体扫描」）、瑜伽是冥想（第6章）、正念行走（第7章）、一日正念（第8章）、坚持正式练习（第34章）、保持非正式正念练习（第35章）；对压力「回应而非反应」译为「用回应替代对压力反应」（第20章）。
claims.study_type: book (mainland Chinese translation of the MBSR founder's programme book)
claims.sample: None (terminology source)
claims.limitations: Usage verified from the table of contents only. Other mainland translations differ: the MBCT 2nd-edition translation (Yu Hongyu, 2017) renders the breathing space as 3分钟的休息时间 and self-compassion as 自我同情, and Neff's mainland books use 静观 and 自我关怀.
claims.app_implication: Use 正念, 身体扫描, 静坐/坐姿冥想, 正念行走 and 正式/非正式练习 as canonical UI terms, and keep a glossary for variants.

citation.venue: 机械工业出版社 China Machine Press (ISBN 9787111594963)

verification.checked_against: Douban catalogue page book.douban.com/subject/30191409 (metadata and full table of contents); Douban page for the MBCT 2nd-ed. translation (subject 26997353); Douban search results for 静观自我关怀

(b) 正念练习 appears in the Part 1 title '壹 正念练习：加以注意' and in ch. 2 '正念练习的基础', not as a chapter of its own. (c) '静坐' in the app implication does not appear in this book's table of contents. claims.topic: How much home practice people actually do, and its link to outcomes
claims.finding: Systematic review and meta-analysis (Scopus and PubMed, studies published to the end of 2015) of formal home practice in standard-format MBCT and MBSR (8-week group courses assigning about 45 min/day, 6 days/week). Across 43 studies (N = 1427), participants reported completing 64% of the assigned amount (95% CI 60-69%), about 30 min/day on 6 days/week, with substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 89%). Across 28 studies (N = 898), self-reported home practice had a small but significant association with intervention outcomes (r = 0.26, 95% CI 0.19 to 0.34; I2 = 17%). The association appeared in both clinical (22 studies, r = 0.25) and non-clinical samples (5 studies, r = 0.29).
claims.finding_zh: 系统综述与元分析（检索Scopus和PubMed，纳入截至2015年底发表的研究），对象是标准格式MBCT和MBSR（8周团体课程，要求每天约45分钟、每周6天）的正式家庭练习：43项研究（1427人）中，学员自报完成了布置练习量的64%（95%CI 60-69%），约相当于每天30分钟、每周6天，研究间异质性很大（I²=89%）。28项研究（898人）中，自报的家庭练习量与干预结局有小而显著的相关（r = 0.26，95%CI 0.19至0.34；I²=17%），在临床样本（22项研究，r = 0.25）和非临床样本（5项研究，r = 0.29）中都能看到。
claims.sample: 43 studies (N = 1427) for practice amount; 28 studies (N = 898) for the association
claims.limitations: Practice amounts are retrospective self-reports from course completers only; drop-outs are not counted. The authors found signs that low practice amounts were under-reported (trim-and-fill adjusted estimate 61%), so true adherence may be lower. Heterogeneity for the practice estimate was very high (I2 = 89%) and was not explained by study design or quality, and many included RCTs had risk-of-bias problems. The practice-outcome association is correlational, so it cannot show that more practice causes more benefit. Eligible programmes were standard 8-week teacher-led group MBSR/MBCT courses (mostly in person; at least one delivered live online), not self-guided apps. Studies were published only up to the end of 2015.
claims.app_implication: Set realistic defaults: offer 10-30 min/day and about 6 days/week as a goal, not a requirement. Log practice without streak-shaming. Even people who complete teacher-led 8-week MBSR/MBCT courses report doing only about 60-65% of the assigned 45 min/day, and drop-outs are not counted. Describe the link between practice and benefit as an association (r = 0.26), not a promise that more minutes guarantee more benefit.

citation.authors: Parsons CE, Crane C, Parsons LJ, et al.
citation.title: Home practice in Mindfulness-Based Cognitive Therapy and Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction: A systematic review and meta-analysis of participants' mindfulness practice and its association with outcomes

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata for 10.1016/j.brat.2017.05.004; PubMed efetch for PMID 28527330; Europe PMC abstract and full text (PMC5501725: methods/eligibility, results sections 8 and 11, discussion and 12.2 Limitations); doi.org redirect to the Elsevier record
verification.problems: Citation metadata (Parsons CE, Crane C, Parsons LJ, Fjorback LO, Kuyken W; 2017; Behav Res Ther 95:29-41; DOI, PMID and URL) and every number in finding and finding_zh match the abstract and full text. The pooled estimate is 64%, 95% CI 60-69%, about 30 min/day (results section: about 29 min) on 6 days/week, with I2 = 89%. The association is r = 0.26, 95% CI 0.19-0.34, over 28 studies with N = 898. The problems are in the surrounding fields. (1) The limitations say the data come from '8-week in-person group programmes'. Eligibility was standard-format 8-week teacher-led group MBSR/MBCT, and at least one included standard-format study (Johansson et al. 2015) delivered MBSR live over the internet. (2) The limitations leave out caveats the authors themselves state. Practice data are retrospective self-reports from course completers only. There was evidence that low practice amounts were under-reported (trim-and-fill adjusted estimate 61%). I2 = 89% for the practice estimate could not be explained by study design or quality. Many included RCTs were at risk of bias. Searches only ran to the end of 2015. (3) The app_implication's 'about two-thirds' rounds 64% up (the authors' discussion says 'about 60%'), and it does not say the figure comes from completers who reported their practice. The 'moderate' evidence weight is acceptable for a systematic review and meta-analysis giving a descriptive pooled estimate.

claims.topic: 5-min vs 20-min single practice: dose and personalization
claims.finding: Pre-registered online RCT (OSF 10.17605/OSF.IO/VHUFT; ANZCTR ACTRN12624000599572). 636 adults aged 18-79 were recruited via Prolific (57% female, 72.5% white, 55.5% British). They completed personality (Big Five) and trait-mindfulness measures, then were randomized to a single 5-min or 20-min recorded mindfulness-of-the-breath practice (MBSR-style) or an active control (listening to audiobook excerpts). State mindfulness (Toronto Mindfulness Scale curiosity and decentering subscales) and affect (PANAS) were measured before and after. Both doses increased curiosity versus control (group F(2,632) = 5.10, p = .006, partial eta squared = .02; 5 min p = .044; 20 min p < .001), with no significant difference between the two doses. Only the 20-min practice increased decentering versus control (F(2,632) = 3.86, p = .022, partial eta squared = .02). Neither dose changed positive affect. The pre-registered hypotheses that neuroticism, conscientiousness and openness would moderate dose effects were not supported. In unhypothesized median-split analyses, people lower in agreeableness in the 5-min group showed a larger drop in negative affect than people higher in agreeableness (group x agreeableness F(2,164) = 4.25, p = .015, partial eta squared = .018; mean difference -2.17, p = .004). Among people lower in trait mindfulness, the 5-min practice reduced negative affect more than control (mean difference -1.91, p = .009).
claims.finding_zh: 预注册在线随机对照试验（OSF 10.17605/OSF.IO/VHUFT；ANZCTR ACTRN12624000599572）：636名18-79岁成人经Prolific平台招募（57%女性、72.5%白人、55.5%英国人），先填写大五人格和特质正念问卷，再随机进行一次5分钟或20分钟的录音式呼吸正念练习（类似MBSR风格），或积极对照（听有声书片段）；练习前后测量状态正念（多伦多正念量表的好奇心与去中心化分量表）和情绪（PANAS）。两种时长都比对照提高了好奇心（组别 F(2,632) = 5.10，p = .006，偏η² = .02；5分钟 p = .044，20分钟 p < .001），两种时长之间无显著差异；只有20分钟练习比对照提高了去中心化（F(2,632) = 3.86，p = .022，偏η² = .02）。两种时长都没有改变积极情绪。预注册假设中神经质、尽责性和开放性的调节作用均未得到支持。在未预设假设、采用中位数分组的分析中：5分钟组里宜人性较低的人比宜人性较高的人消极情绪下降更多（组别×宜人性 F(2,164) = 4.25，p = .015，偏η² = .018；均值差 −2.17，p = .004）；特质正念较低的人做5分钟练习后，消极情绪比对照组下降更多（均值差 −1.91，p = .009）。
claims.sample: N = 636 adults aged 18-79 recruited online via Prolific (55.5% British)
claims.limitations: Single session with immediate self-report state outcomes only, in mostly novice, mainly British online participants. Effects were small (partial eta squared about .02), and the 5-min curiosity effect only just reached significance (p = .044). There was no significant difference between 5 and 20 min on curiosity, and the control was an audiobook. None of the three pre-registered personality moderators was supported. The agreeableness effect was unhypothesized, and like the trait-mindfulness result it rests on median splits and multiple subgroup tests; the authors acknowledge the Type I error risk and call for replication. The negative-affect analyses report error df = 164 versus 632 elsewhere, without explanation. Full text is open access (CC BY 4.0).
claims.app_implication: Offer 5 min as a fully legitimate option, since it raised state curiosity vs control in one online experiment, and 20 min for those who want more, since only 20 min raised decentering. Let users choose their own length. Don't promise mood benefits from either length (no effect on positive affect), and don't personalize length by personality until the exploratory agreeableness and trait-mindfulness findings are replicated.

citation.authors: Strohmaier S, Jones F, Medvedev O
citation.title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Mindfulness Practice Doses in the General Population Through Personalization—A Randomized Controlled Experiment

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata and verbatim abstract; Springer open-access full-text page (Methods, Results, Limitations), read via web fetch; PubMed search (no PMID exists)
verification.problems: Metadata are correct (Mindfulness 17(3):731-745, online 12 Feb 2026, no PMID), and the claim matches the abstract. The full text shows six problems. (1) The limitations are wrong. The article is open access (CC BY 4.0), not behind an access wall. Personality moderation was not simply 'exploratory': moderation by neuroticism, conscientiousness and openness was pre-registered (H1-H6) and not supported, and only agreeableness and extraversion were exploratory. (2) The agreeableness result is ambiguous. The comparison was low- vs high-agreeableness people within the 5-min group (mean difference -2.17, p = .004), not 5 min vs 20 min. That difference was not significant in the 20-min (p = .248) or control (p = .859) groups. (3) 'State mindfulness' means the TMS curiosity and decentering subscales. Both doses raised curiosity (5 min p = .044, 20 min p < .001; partial eta squared .02), with no significant difference between doses. Only 20 min raised decentering (partial eta squared .02). (4) Omitted null: neither dose changed positive affect. (5) The negative-affect moderation used median splits and reports error df = 164 (vs 632 elsewhere) without explanation; the authors themselves note the Type I error risk. (6) Evidence weight: one online single-session experiment with small, immediate self-report effects and exploratory moderators fits 'low' better than 'moderate'.

claims.topic: Three-step (three-minute) breathing space: steps, hourglass, anchors
claims.finding: Interdisciplinary conceptual synthesis (journal category 'Original Paper'; authors from Kyoto University, Kyoto University of Education, Keio University and the University of Oxford, including Willem Kuyken of the Department of Psychiatry). It proposes weaving MBCT's Three-Step Breathing Space (3SBS) into university classes and says the 3SBS 'requires only a few minutes (schematically three)'. Step 1, 'Becoming Aware': deliberately enlarging awareness to thoughts, emotions and bodily sensations, stepping back from automaticity and approaching them with acceptance and careful interest. Step 2, 'Gathering': progressively narrowing awareness onto one chosen bodily anchor and stabilising attention there. This resting place may vary with individual needs, care for past traumas, mental agitation or highly stressful circumstances. It can involve the parts of the body in contact with the floor or seat, the feet, the hands or the lower abdomen (citing Treleaven 2018, pp. 120-122), but 'in all cases, using the breath as a vehicle for establishing awareness in this location is central' (Fig. 1 labels Step 2 'Mindful Breathing'). When focusing more exclusively on the breath, it may be sensed mainly at the abdomen or the nostrils. Step 3, 'Expanding': gradually re-enlarging awareness to the whole body breathing, then to 'Open Awareness'. The 3SBS is 'generally' taught with an hourglass shape (open -> narrow -> open; citing Feldman & Kuyken 2019, p. 126). The authors also propose a figure-eight version for higher education.
claims.finding_zh: 跨学科概念性综述（期刊栏目为「原创论文」；作者来自京都大学、京都教育大学、庆应义塾大学和牛津大学，其中Willem Kuyken来自牛津大学精神病学系），建议把MBCT的「三步呼吸空间」融入大学课堂。文中说这个练习「只需几分钟（示意性地说是三分钟）」。第1步「觉察」：有意扩大觉察，留意此刻的想法、情绪和身体感受，从自动反应中退后一步，以接纳和细致的兴趣对待它们。第2步「聚集」：逐步把觉察收窄到一个选定的身体锚点，让注意稳定在那里；这个落脚处可以根据个人需要（照顾过往创伤、心绪躁动或压力很大时）变化，可以是身体与地面或座椅接触的部位、双脚、双手或下腹（引用Treleaven 2018第120-122页）——但文章强调，无论哪种情况，以呼吸为载体把觉察安住在该部位都是核心（图1把第2步标为「正念呼吸」）；如果更专注于呼吸本身，可主要在腹部或鼻孔处感受。第3步「扩展」：逐步把觉察重新扩大到整个身体在呼吸，再到「开放的觉察」。教学上通常用「沙漏」形状表示：宽→窄→宽（引用Feldman与Kuyken 2019第126页）；作者另外为高等教育提出了「8字形」版本。
claims.study_type: conceptual synthesis / perspective article (published as an Original Paper; no data)
claims.sample: None (conceptual paper)
claims.limitations: Describes structure, not efficacy. It is a secondary description of the canonical MBCT practice, whose primary source is the Segal, Williams & Teasdale 2013 MBCT manual. It gives only an overall 'schematically three' minutes, with no per-step timing. One co-author (Kuyken) is an MBCT researcher, and the paper is not by MBCT's originators. It also proposes a non-canonical figure-eight variant for higher education.
claims.app_implication: Script the breathing space as three steps within about 3 min, with an hourglass animation (wide -> narrow -> wide). Equal ~1-min steps are a design choice; the source gives only the total. In step 2, let users choose where to rest attention: the breath at the abdomen or nostrils, the feet, the hands, seat or floor contact, or the lower abdomen. This matters especially when focusing on the breath feels agitating or relates to past trauma. The article keeps the breath as the vehicle for that awareness.

citation.authors: Deroche MH, Kuyken W, Uwatoko T, et al.
citation.title: The Mindful Way From Information to Knowledge, to Wisdom, and to Life: Perspectives on Mindfulness (-Based Cognitive Therapy) for Higher Education

verification.checked_against: Crossref + Europe PMC abstract + PMC full text (PMC11993468): the section 'Weaving Mindfulness into the Constitution of Higher Education: The Thread of the Three-Step Breathing Space', the Fig. 1 caption, affiliations, author contributions and reference list
verification.problems: (1) Step 2 is misread. The article says the resting place can be floor/seat contact, the feet, the hands or the lower abdomen, 'But in all cases, using the breath as a vehicle for establishing awareness in this location is central'; Fig. 1 labels Step 2 'Mindful Breathing'. The claim presents these as anchors used 'instead' of the breath, and 'generally the breath' is not the article's wording. (2) finding_zh places Kuyken at the Oxford Mindfulness Centre; the article lists him at the Department of Psychiatry, University of Oxford. (3) The study_type 'MBCT developers' circle' overstates the authorship. This is an interdisciplinary conceptual synthesis (journal category 'Original Paper') by authors from Kyoto University, Kyoto University of Education, Keio University and Oxford. Only Kuyken is an MBCT researcher, and none of the authors originated MBCT. (4) The app_implication's '~1 min each' is a design choice; the source gives only a total of 'schematically three' minutes. Everything else matches the source: step names and content, Treleaven 2018 pp. 120-122, the hourglass citing Feldman & Kuyken 2019 p. 126, the figure-eight proposal, the metadata and the PMID.

claims.topic: Immediate effects of single app exercises incl. mindful breathing and 'leaves on a stream'
claims.finding: Pre-registered online RCT, described by the authors as double-blind, comparing 12 single-session exercises from the Mind Ease app with a reading control and a measurement-only control. Participants were US adults recruited on MTurk via Positly and screened for elevated state anxiety. 1108 completed the study; 1092 remained after the pre-registered exclusion of baseline anxiety <50; the main analyses used 1054 after a non-pre-registered 3-30-min time criterion (results essentially the same). Mean time on the exercises was 9.8 min (SD 4.1). The outcome was a custom 3-slider state-anxiety scale (r = 0.87-0.89 with the STAI state subscale in a 199-person prestudy). Every exercise reduced anxiety significantly more than the measurement-only control (confirmatory) and the reading control (exploratory). All exercises pooled: d = 0.8 [0.6, 1.0] vs either control. Exercise-level d [95% CI] vs the measurement-only control (n = 107): mindful breathing (n = 74) 1.5 [1.2, 1.9]; Leaves on a Stream (n = 74) 1.2 [0.9, 1.5], which also included observing thoughts without the visualisation and a brief 'Is it actually true?' challenge; dropping anchor (sounds -> body sensations -> visual details; n = 72) 1.0 [0.7, 1.3]; body scan with exposure to bodily sensations of anxiety, plus brief diaphragmatic breathing and reappraisal (n = 68), 0.9 [0.6, 1.2]; diaphragmatic breathing (n = 68) 0.6 [0.3, 0.9]. Comparisons between exercises were exploratory. No adverse effects were reported.
claims.finding_zh: 预注册在线随机对照试验（作者称为双盲）：比较Mind Ease应用中12种单次练习与阅读对照、仅测量对照；参与者为通过Positly/亚马逊MTurk招募、筛查时焦虑偏高的美国成人。1108人完成研究，按预注册标准剔除基线焦虑低于50分者后剩1092人；主要分析又按未预注册的用时标准（3-30分钟）剔除，最终1054人（结果基本相同）。练习平均用时9.8分钟（SD 4.1）。结局为自编3滑块状态焦虑量表（预研究中与STAI状态分量表相关r = 0.87-0.89）。每种练习降低即时焦虑的效果都显著优于仅测量对照（验证性分析）和阅读对照（探索性分析）；全部练习合并 d = 0.8 [95%CI 0.6, 1.0]（相对两种对照均如此）。各练习相对仅测量对照（107人）的 d [95%CI]：正念呼吸（74人）1.5 [1.2, 1.9]；「溪流上的落叶」（还包括不借助意象观察想法，以及简短的「这是真的吗？」质疑；74人）1.2 [0.9, 1.5]；「抛锚」（声音→身体感受→视觉细节；72人）1.0 [0.7, 1.3]；含焦虑躯体感受暴露的身体扫描（另含简短腹式呼吸和认知重评；68人）0.9 [0.6, 1.2]；腹式呼吸（68人）0.6 [0.3, 0.9]。练习之间的比较属于探索性分析。未报告不良反应。
claims.study_type: RCT (pre-registered, online, 14 arms, single session; described by the authors as double-blind)
claims.sample: N = 1092 analysable completers (US adults recruited on MTurk via Positly, screened for elevated anxiety; 1108 completed). Main analysis n = 1054: 842 across 12 exercise arms (n = 61-76 each), 107 measurement-only, 105 reading control
claims.limitations: Immediate effects only, measured on a custom 3-slider self-report scale. The exercise-level d values are against a measurement-only control that participants likely recognised as a control (the authors' statement), so expectancy is not controlled. Between-exercise comparisons were exploratory. Funding: Mind Ease paid for the study; the two first authors were funded by Mind Ease and another author by its part-owner Spark Wave. Mind Ease's CEO and founder are co-authors; the senior author was not funded by Mind Ease and had the final say. The pre-registered sample size was cut from 5550 to 1126 after an interim analysis. The time criterion used in the main analyses was not pre-registered. The MTurk sample (66% female, 77% White, mean age 39) limits generalisability. Per-exercise durations are not reported in the main text.
claims.app_implication: A brief guided mindful-breathing or 'leaves on a stream' exercise (exercises averaged about 10 min in this trial) is a reasonable 'right now' option for acute tension. Label the effect as immediate, single-session, self-reported, measured against doing nothing, and industry-funded. Do not extrapolate to lasting change, and do not claim that one exercise is proven better than another.

citation.authors: Sandkühler JF, Kahl F, Sadurska MZ, et al.
citation.title: The Immediate Impact of App-Based Psychotherapeutic Exercises on Anxiety: An RCT

verification.checked_against: Crossref + Europe PMC abstract + PMC full text (PMC11981704): Methods 2.1-2.8, Table 1, Table 2, Discussion, Disclosure, Conflicts of Interest, Funding
verification.problems: (1) 'N = 1092 randomized' is wrong. 1108 people completed the study; 1092 remained after the pre-registered exclusion of baseline anxiety <50; the main analyses used 1054 after a non-pre-registered 3-30-min time criterion. The number randomized appears only in the CONSORT figure. The per-arm n values (61-76) come from the 1054 sample. (2) The exercise-level d values in Table 2 are against the measurement-only control (n = 107), not the reading control. Placed right after the pooled 'vs reading control' figure, the claim implies the wrong comparator. The authors say measurement-only participants likely realised they were controls, so these d values are not expectancy-controlled. (3) 9.8 min (SD 4.1) is the mean time across all exercises; per-exercise durations are not reported in the main text. (4) 'Double-blind' is the authors' label, but blinding of the measurement-only control was likely ineffective. (5) evidence_weight 'moderate' is generous for exercise-specific effects, so I downgraded it to 'low'. Reasons: a single industry-funded trial with the app's CEO and founder as co-authors; a custom self-report outcome; immediate effects only; passive comparators; exploratory between-exercise comparisons; an MTurk sample. All d values and CIs, the arm sizes, the 5550 -> 1126 change and the funding facts match the source.

claims.topic: Loving-kindness interventions: meta-analysis incl. format, length and facilitator moderators
claims.finding: Systematic review and meta-analysis (PROSPERO CRD42023400397; six databases searched 2 November 2023) of 23 randomized controlled studies (2008-2023) of loving-kindness interventions (LKIs) in general adult samples. LKIs were defined as interventions whose core content was solely knowledge and/or practice of sending kindness and care to oneself, loved ones, strangers and all beings. Relative to passive controls, LKIs had small positive pre-post effects: mindfulness g = 0.22 (95% CI 0.03 to 0.40; 5 studies), compassion g = 0.36 (0.06 to 0.65; 3 studies), positive affect g = 0.44 (0.21 to 0.67; 3 studies), negative affect g = 0.44 (0.14 to 0.73; 3 studies) and psychological symptoms g = 0.36 (0.11 to 0.61; 3 studies). Effects were non-significant relative to non-therapeutic active controls (only positive and negative affect could be analysed, 4 studies each) and to therapeutic alternative treatments. The one exception: LKIs reduced negative affect less than alternative treatments (g = -0.19, -0.36 to -0.03; 6 studies). Subgroup analyses pooled all comparison types. In them, effects did not differ significantly by sample type (community vs university), format (individual vs group), length (single- vs multi-session) or presence vs absence of a live researcher/facilitator, though several subgroups had too few studies to estimate.
claims.finding_zh: 系统综述与元分析（PROSPERO预注册；2023年11月2日检索6个数据库），纳入23项针对一般成人的慈心干预随机对照研究（2008-2023年；慈心干预指核心内容只涉及学习或练习向自己、所爱的人、陌生人和一切众生送出善意与关怀）。与被动对照（等待或无干预）相比，慈心干预有小幅改善：正念 g = 0.22（95%CI 0.03至0.40；5项研究）、慈悲 g = 0.36（0.06至0.65；3项）、积极情绪 g = 0.44（0.21至0.67；3项）、消极情绪 g = 0.44（0.14至0.73；3项）、心理症状 g = 0.36（0.11至0.61；3项）。与非治疗性的积极对照（只能分析积极和消极情绪，各4项研究）或其他疗法相比，差异不显著；唯一例外是，在减少消极情绪方面，慈心干预不如其他疗法（g = -0.19，-0.36至-0.03；6项）。在把各类对照合并的亚组分析中，效果没有因样本类型（社区或大学）、形式（个人或小组）、时长（单次或多次）或有无现场带领者而显著不同，但有几个亚组研究太少，无法估计。
claims.study_type: systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs
claims.sample: 23 randomized controlled studies in general adult samples (community and university); 3-8 studies per pooled estimate
claims.limitations: Few studies per outcome (3-5 per passive-control estimate), with Fredrickson 2008 carrying 31-58% of the weight in passive-control analyses. Most studies were at high risk of bias in outcome measurement (unblinded self-report), with some concerns about selective reporting in all. Active-control comparisons were extremely heterogeneous (I² 97-98%). Moderator analyses pooled comparison types, were underpowered and observational, and 'length' meant single vs multi-session, not minutes. Outcomes were measured right after the intervention. Numbers come from the accepted manuscript and are consistent with the published abstract.
claims.app_implication: A self-guided, multi-session LKM course is a reasonable format: the authors call individually administered, independently completed, multi-session LKIs promising. However, the moderator tests were underpowered and did not examine session minutes or app delivery. Present LKM as modestly better than doing nothing, not better than other active practices, and not the strongest option for reducing negative emotions.

citation.authors: Petrovic J, Mettler J, Cho S, et al.
citation.title: The effects of loving-kindness interventions on positive and negative mental health outcomes: A systematic review and meta-analysis

verification.checked_against: Crossref and PubMed metadata and abstract; author accepted manuscript (McGill eScholarship, COAR version type AM, CC BY-NC-ND): Methods, Table 2 (effects by comparison type), Table 3 (subgroups), risk-of-bias, publication-bias, Discussion and Limitations sections
verification.problems: Metadata is correct and the finding matches the abstract, but the full text shows several problems. (1) Omitted unfavourable result: against therapeutic alternative treatments, LKIs reduced negative affect significantly less (g = -0.19, 95% CI -0.36 to -0.03, p = .022, k = 6). (2) Active-control comparisons were possible only for positive and negative affect (k = 4 each, I² about 97-98%). (3) Passive-control effects rest on 3-5 studies per outcome, with Fredrickson 2008 carrying 31-58% of the weight. (4) 'Format' means individual vs group and 'length' means single vs multi-session, not minutes. The subgroup tests pooled all comparison types, were underpowered and could not estimate several cells, so the app inference about 'modest length' and app delivery is unsupported. (5) Under RoB 2, most studies were at high risk of bias in outcome measurement (unblinded self-report), with some concerns about selective reporting in all, so the 'moderate' evidence weight is too high; low fits better. (6) The limitations say effect sizes were not extracted; they are available and are now given.

claims.topic: Evidence for the body scan used on its own
claims.finding: Systematic review and meta-analysis (robust variance estimation) of RCTs of body scan meditation used on its own: 14 independent articles, with outcomes grouped into 7 categories. Body scan showed only a small effect on mindfulness compared with passive controls (Hedges' g = 0.268, 95% CI 0.032 to 0.504, p < .05). Study quality was low and heterogeneity high; attrition in longer interventions was low. The authors conclude that a sole body scan meditation 'is not effective enough to improve health-related outcomes'.
claims.finding_zh: 对单独使用身体扫描的随机对照试验所做的系统综述与元分析（稳健方差估计）：纳入14篇独立文章，结局分为7类。与无干预对照相比，身体扫描只对正念水平有小效应（Hedges g = 0.268，95%CI 0.032至0.504，p < .05）。研究质量低、异质性高；较长干预的脱落率低。作者结论：单独做身体扫描不足以改善健康相关结局。
claims.study_type: systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs
claims.sample: 14 RCT articles (total N not reported in the abstract)
claims.limitations: Only 14 trials, rated low quality, with high heterogeneity and no population restriction. The closed-access full text was not read in this check, so total N and the range of intervention lengths could not be verified (the abstract only distinguishes 'long-term' interventions). The null result for health outcomes may partly reflect low power rather than a proven absence of effect.
claims.app_implication: Present the body scan as a body-awareness and settling skill inside a broader programme; make no standalone health claims for it, and show this weak result on its evidence card.

citation.authors: Gan R, Zhang L, Chen S
citation.title: The effects of body scan meditation: A systematic review and meta-analysis

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata + Europe PMC/PubMed abstract (PMID 35538557). Full text is closed access (Wiley returned 403; OpenAlex lists no open-access copy)
verification.problems: Citation metadata (Gan R, Zhang L, Chen S; 2022; Appl Psychol Health Well Being 14(3):1062-1080) and every number in finding and finding_zh match the abstract: 14 articles, 7 outcome categories, robust variance estimation, g = .268 [0.032, 0.504] vs passive control, low attrition in long-term interventions, low quality, high heterogeneity, and the quoted conclusion. The limitations contain details I could not verify without the full text: the dose range 'single sessions to multi-week' and that the trials were 'small'. The abstract only mentions 'long-term interventions' and 'no population restriction'. The revised limitations state this uncertainty.

claims.topic: Single brief LKM toward a disliked person: unsuccessful adjusted replication
claims.finding: Adjusted replication of Hutcherson et al. (2008) using a German translation of the same brief LKM and control instructions. 82 students were recruited and 13 were excluded for >=50% missing or wrong responses in the implicit task, leaving 69 analysed. Participants heard either a 6-min audio LKM or a length-matched imagery task. In the LKM they imagined beloved people or friends, then looked at a photo of the politician they disliked most, sent love to this person and repeated 'May you be well, may you be happy, may you be free from all physical and mental pain'. There were no significant time x group interactions: explicit attitudes F(1,67) = 3.50, p = .066, partial eta squared = .050; implicit attitudes F(1,67) = 3.33, p = .072, partial eta squared = .047. These were trend-level, medium-sized effects in LKM's favour. Mood did not improve. Positive mood fell over time (time effect F(1,67) = 7.65, p = .007), numerically more after LKM (3.32 to 3.05) than after imagery (3.27 to 3.22; time x group F(1,67) = 3.58, p = .063). Negative mood also fell (F(1,67) = 6.61, p = .012).
claims.finding_zh: 对Hutcherson等（2008）的调整重复研究，使用同一段简短慈心练习及对照指导语的德语译本：招募82名学生，13人因内隐任务缺失或错误反应≥50%被排除，分析69人。参与者听6分钟音频慈心练习，或听等长的想象任务。慈心组先想象所爱的人或朋友，再看自己最讨厌的那位政治人物的照片，向其送出爱意，并重复「愿你安好，愿你快乐，愿你远离一切身心痛苦」。时间×组别交互作用均不显著：外显态度 F(1,67) = 3.50，p = .066，偏η² = .050；内隐态度 F(1,67) = 3.33，p = .072，偏η² = .047（只是趋势，效应量中等，方向对慈心组有利）。情绪没有改善：积极情绪随时间下降（时间效应 F(1,67) = 7.65，p = .007），慈心组降得更多（3.32→3.05，想象组3.27→3.22；交互 F(1,67) = 3.58，p = .063）；消极情绪也下降（F(1,67) = 6.61，p = .012）。
claims.study_type: RCT (single-session lab experiment; adjusted replication; block randomization)
claims.sample: n = 69 university students analysed (82 recruited; 38 women, 31 men; applied movement sciences; 39% meditated regularly)
claims.limitations: Small sample, below the authors' own power targets (N = 76 explicit, 82 implicit), so underpowered for small effects. The target was a disliked politician rather than a neutral stranger, so this is not a direct replication. Allocation used block randomization according to time of participation. The ~45-min lab session may have caused fatigue. Mood was measured with the broad PANAS. Trend-level, medium effect sizes can be neither confirmed nor excluded.
claims.app_implication: Do not market a single 5-6-min LKM as making people feel more connected, kinder or happier. Keep the 'difficult person' step optional, mild and late in a course (a design choice, not tested here). Show this unsuccessful replication on the evidence card.

citation.authors: Schroter FA, Jansen P
citation.title: Making peace with disliked others: the effects of a short loving-kindness meditation on implicit and explicit emotional evaluations

verification.checked_against: Crossref and PubMed metadata; PMC full text PMC9055729: Methods (Participants, Procedure, Measures), Results with Tables 1-3, Discussion, Limitations; Europe PMC record of Hutcherson et al. 2008 (abstract only)
verification.problems: Metadata and every reported statistic are correct (explicit F(1,67) = 3.50, p = .066, ηp² = .050; implicit F(1,67) = 3.33, p = .072, ηp² = .047; positive-mood time effect F(1,67) = 7.65, p = .007; 82 recruited, 13 excluded, 69 analysed; 6-min audio). Minor issues: (1) finding_zh says the phrase was 默念 (recited silently), but the paper only says participants were asked to repeat it. (2) The topic calls it a 'failed replication'. It is an adjusted replication with a changed target (the most disliked politician instead of a neutral stranger), so 'unsuccessful adjusted replication' is more accurate. (3) The finding omits that negative mood also fell (F(1,67) = 6.61, p = .012) and that positive mood fell numerically more after LKM than after imagery (time x group F(1,67) = 3.58, p = .063), so the mood trend did not favour LKM. (4) The limitations omit that the analysed N of 69 fell below the authors' own power targets (76 and 82) and that 39% of participants meditated regularly.

claims.topic: STOP micro-practice: definition and only RCT found (China, WeChat delivery)
claims.finding: Online two-arm wait-list RCT in China (April-July 2020; n = 1090 randomized, 545 per arm; NCT04330352) of 'STOP touching your face'. It was delivered remotely, mainly via WeChat/QQ, as Chinese text plus a 5-min audio, and participants were asked to practise for at least 15 min after learning it. Steps: S, stop whatever you are doing or about to do and remind yourself to stop for a minute; T, take a deep breath to connect with your body; O, observe what is happening to you now (e.g., feeling distracted or anxious, itching or tingling on the face); P, proceed with what you were doing. Face touching was self-monitored for 60 min before and after the intervention. ITT with LOCF: the proportion of participants who touched their T-zone (eyes, nose, mouth) fell from 81.1% to 73.0% in the intervention group (RR 0.901, OR 0.631, RD -0.081, p = 0.002) vs 80.0% to 79.4% in controls (p = 0.821). After the intervention it was 73.0% vs 79.4% (RR 0.919, OR 0.700, RD -0.064, p = 0.015). T-zone touches per 60 min fell by 1.7 ± 5.13 vs 0.7 ± 3.98 (mean difference 1.03, 95% CI 0.48 to 1.58, p < 0.001; Cohen's d = -0.218). Overall face touches fell by 5.7 ± 12.14 vs 2.2 ± 9.49 (mean difference 3.52, 2.23 to 4.82; d = -0.321). Complete-case analysis gave similar results.
claims.finding_zh: 中国在线两组等待对照随机试验（2020年4-7月，随机1090人，每组545人；NCT04330352）：主要通过微信/QQ推送「STOP不摸脸」练习，含中文文字和5分钟音频，要求学会后先练至少15分钟。四步：S停——停下正在做或将要做的事，提醒自己停一下；T吸——深吸一口气，与身体连接；O观——观察此刻自己身上发生了什么（如分心、焦虑、脸上发痒或刺麻）；P行——继续原来的事。干预前后各自我记录60分钟的摸脸情况。意向性分析（缺失数据按「无变化」填补）：干预组摸过「T区」（眼、鼻、口）的人数比例从81.1%降到73.0%（RR 0.901，OR 0.631，RD -0.081，p = 0.002），对照组从80.0%到79.4%（p = 0.821）；干预后两组为73.0%对79.4%（RR 0.919，OR 0.700，RD -0.064，p = 0.015）。每60分钟摸T区的次数减少1.7±5.13对0.7±3.98（均差1.03，95%CI 0.48至1.58，p < 0.001，Cohen's d = -0.218）；整张脸的摸脸次数减少5.7±12.14对2.2±9.49（均差3.52，95%CI 2.23至4.82，d = -0.321）。只分析完成者时结果相近。
claims.sample: n = 1090 adults in China (mean age about 30, about 31% male, most in medical occupations)
claims.limitations: The outcome is self-monitored face touching over 60 min, with no stress or mental-health outcomes. The post-test could be as soon as 1 h after baseline, with no longer follow-up. Only 71.6% (intervention) vs 63.9% (control) reported the post-test, and missing data were imputed as no change (LOCF), though complete-case results were similar. Baseline imbalances: the intervention arm was younger, more often in medical occupations and touched more overall. Effects were small. Wait-list control with unblinded delivery. Self-monitoring itself may change behaviour. Practice length was not associated with reduction.
claims.app_implication: STOP (停·吸·观·行) can be offered as a ~1-min habit-interrupt micro-practice with a Chinese-language precedent. The only RCT found measured self-reported face touching over a single hour, not stress or anxiety, so label it 'preliminary evidence' and make no stress-relief claims.

citation.authors: Tang J, Wang L, Luo T, et al.
citation.title: Effectiveness of a Brief Mindfulness-Based Intervention of 'STOP touching your face' During the COVID-19 Pandemic: a Randomized Controlled Trial

verification.checked_against: Crossref and PubMed metadata; PMC full text PMC9645303: Methods (procedure, interventions, measures, analyses), Tables 1-3, Results, Discussion and Limitations; Europe PMC searches for other STOP-practice RCTs (none found)
verification.problems: Metadata and the T-zone percentages, RR/OR/RD and p values are correct. (1) '1.7 ± 5.13 vs 0.7 ± 3.98' is the reduction in T-zone (eyes, nose, mouth) touches per 60 min, not overall face touching, and finding_zh wrongly labels it 摸脸次数. Overall face touching fell by 5.7 ± 12.14 vs 2.2 ± 9.49 (MD 3.52, 95% CI 2.23 to 4.82, d = -0.321). (2) The 81.1% to 73.0% figures are the proportion of participants who touched the T-zone at least once in 60 min, which should be stated. (3) The limitations omit several points: high and unequal attrition (post-test from 71.6% vs 63.9%) handled by LOCF 'no change' imputation; baseline imbalances (younger, more often in medical occupations at 76% vs 57%, more overall touching in the intervention arm); a very short follow-up (post-test >=1 h after baseline); and no association between practice length and reduction. (4) 'Works as a 1-min habit-interrupt' overstates a small, self-reported, short-term effect.

claims.topic: Invitational, harm-aware guidance; steady guidance instead of long silence for vulnerable users
claims.finding: Review of potential harm in mindfulness-based programmes (MBPs). During courses, teachers 'often remind participants not to push beyond limits of safety or tolerance and suggest ways to adapt practices if difficulties that feel overwhelming arise'; rationales should be clear and participants 'should feel invited, rather than pressured, to engage'. An adaptation for people with psychosis 'reduced the number and duration of sessions, shortened the meditation practices, and provided steady guidance during practices to prevent absorption in psychotic symptoms during stretches of silence'. In four reviews, adverse events in evidence-based MBPs occurred in 0-10.6% of participants and were no more common than in comparison conditions; only 19% of 47 RCTs against active controls reported on adverse events.
claims.finding_zh: 关于正念课程潜在伤害的综述：课程中，老师常提醒学员不要超出安全或可承受的界限，并在困难感觉难以承受时建议如何调整练习；练习的理由应讲清楚，学员应感到是被邀请而不是被迫参与。针对精神病性障碍的改编版「减少了课程次数和时长，缩短冥想练习，并在练习中提供持续的引导，以免在长时间静默中沉浸于精神病性症状」。四篇综述显示，循证正念课程中不良事件发生率为0-10.6%，并不比对照组多；在47项与积极对照比较的随机试验中，只有19%报告了不良事件。
claims.sample: Literature review; summarises 4 reviews of adverse events
claims.limitations: Not a systematic review (the authors judged the literature too small); adverse-event monitoring in trials is sparse, so true rates are uncertain; recommendations are expert-based.
claims.app_implication: Write every practice in invitational language with explicit adapt/stop options. For users who flag vulnerability or high distress (and in sleep mode), default to shorter practices with steady guidance and no long silences.

citation.authors: Baer R, Crane C, Miller E, et al.
citation.title: Doing no harm in mindfulness-based programs: Conceptual issues and empirical findings

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; PubMed abstract (PMID 30638824); PMC open-access full text PMC6575147 (sections 4.1, 5, 6.2.2, recommendations, Table 4)
verification.problems: No discrepancy. All three quotes match the full text verbatim. The numbers are correct: Goyal 2014, 9 of 47 RCTs (19%) reported AEs; Banks 2015, 13/123 (10.6%); overall 0-10.6% of participants 'when reported', at similar rates in MBPs and controls 'when compared'. 'Too small for a systematic review' is also verbatim. Note: the steady-guidance adaptation comes from Chadwick, Taylor & Abba (2005) as summarized by Baer et al., and was developed for psychosis. Extending it to other vulnerable users or sleep mode, as the app implication does, is a reasonable design choice but goes beyond the evidence.

claims.topic: Resonance (HRV-biofeedback) breathing: Lehrer protocol and home-practice dose
claims.finding: Two-centre RCT (n = 68 steroid-naive adults, no inhaled steroids in the past month, with mild-to-moderate persistent asthma; NCT02766374). After one month of asthma education, participants had 3 months (10 weeks of training) of HRV biofeedback (HRVB) or an active comparison: EEG alpha biofeedback, relaxing music and relaxed paced breathing at the person's baseline rate, about 15 breaths/min. HRVB training steps: determine the resonance frequency; train longer exhalation than inhalation, pursed-lips breathing and diaphragmatic paced breathing at the resonance frequency; then practise at home with a portable trainer (StressEraser) 'twice daily for 20 min' (same instruction in both arms). Both conditions produced similar improvements in methacholine challenge, asthma symptoms and quality of life, with no significant between-group differences. The authors note the study 'produced little evidence for a specific HRVB effect on asthma'. The methacholine improvement was about 65% of the effect of a 4-week course of inhaled budesonide, which was given only to a subgroup of 8 HRVB participants (not powered for this comparison). It was also similar in size to enhanced-placebo effects reported elsewhere. Authors conclude HRVB 'should not be considered an alternative to asthma controller medications'.
claims.finding_zh: 双中心随机对照试验（68名近一个月未用吸入激素的轻中度持续性哮喘成人；NCT02766374）：先进行1个月哮喘教育，再进行3个月（10周训练）心率变异性生物反馈，或积极对照（脑电α波反馈、放松音乐、按本人基线呼吸频率〔约每分钟15次〕的放松节律呼吸）。生物反馈的训练步骤：测定共振频率；练习呼气长于吸气、缩唇呼吸和以共振频率进行的腹式节律呼吸；然后用便携训练器（StressEraser）在家「每天两次、每次20分钟」练习（两组的居家要求相同）。两组在乙酰甲胆碱激发试验、哮喘症状和生活质量上的改善相近，组间无显著差异；作者指出，几乎没有证据表明生物反馈对哮喘有特异性作用。激发试验的改善约为4周吸入布地奈德效果的65%（布地奈德只给了8名生物反馈组参与者，研究并未为这一比较设计足够样本量），也与其他研究报告的「增强安慰剂」效应大小相近。作者结论：生物反馈不应被视为哮喘控制药物的替代品。
claims.sample: n = 68 adults with mild-to-moderate asthma (55 completed post-test methacholine challenge)
claims.limitations: Asthma-specific outcomes in mild disease, where the authors suspect a floor effect. The active control also included relaxed paced breathing. The protocol was shortened mid-trial because of participant burden (20 long-protocol, 44 short-protocol participants). Dropout was 19% (55 of 68 reached the post-test methacholine challenge), with a modified intention-to-treat analysis. The budesonide comparison rests on 8 participants. Home-practice minutes were logged but appear only in a figure, so actual adherence to 2 x 20 min/day is not stated in the text.
claims.app_implication: Use 20 min twice daily only as the instructed research dose for resonance breathing (achieved practice was not reported), while offering 5/10/20-min sessions. Describe benefits as similar to other relaxation and paced-breathing methods, and never as a substitute for medical treatment.

citation.authors: Lehrer PM, Irvin CG, Lu SE, et al.
citation.title: Heart Rate Variability Biofeedback Does Not Substitute for Asthma Steroid Controller Medication

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; PubMed abstract (PMID 29124506); PMC author-manuscript full text PMC5871536 (Methods, Table 1, Results, Discussion)
verification.problems: Metadata and all protocol details match the full text: 10 weeks of training, the Table 1 HRVB steps, the StressEraser home trainer, 'twice daily for 20 min' in both arms, control paced breathing at the baseline rate (~15/min), long/short protocols (20/44 participants), and the floor effect. The 65% budesonide figure is shown without the context that changes its meaning. Budesonide was given only to a subgroup of 8 HRVB participants, and the study was not powered for that comparison. The abstract also states that the methacholine effects were similar in size to enhanced-placebo effects reported elsewhere. The authors say the study 'produced little evidence for a specific HRVB effect on asthma'. The limitations leave out the 19% dropout (55/68 reached the post-test methacholine challenge) and the modified ITT analysis. Home-practice minutes appear only in a figure, so the text does not say whether participants met the 2 x 20 min instruction. 'Steroid-naive' here means no inhaled steroids in the past month. The year 2018 is the print issue (epub Nov 2017), which is acceptable.

claims.topic: MBSR canonical structure: body scan, sitting progression, guidance fading, self-care rules
claims.finding: The 2017 UMass Center for Mindfulness MBSR Authorized Curriculum Guide specifies the following. Body scan: introduced in Class 1 (lying down, or sitting in a chair if necessary) and practised at home with the 45-min recording on ≥6 days/week in Weeks 1-2, then alternated every other day with the Lying-down Yoga recording (≥6 days/week, Weeks 3-4). Awareness-of-breathing (AOB) sitting at home: 10-15 min/day in Week 2 with 'No recording' (participants practise on their own), 15-20 min/day in Week 3, and 20 min/day in Week 4 with attention to breathing, other physical sensations and the whole body. The guided Sitting recording is first handed out at Class 5. Class 5: a 45-min sitting that attends to breath, body, sounds, and thoughts and emotions as 'events' in consciousness, then opens to choiceless awareness/open presence and returns to the breath at the end. 'Longer spans of silence' are emphasised, and the new Sitting recording 'has more silence on it'. All-day silent retreat: sitting with 'less guidance, more silence' (30-40 min); slow walking 'with introductory guidance' (15-30 min) and later with 'less guidance' (20 min); loving-kindness with 'minimal talking, emphasis on spaciousness, ending in silence' (25-30 min; classical phrases are not essential, and any resistance is recognised and affirmed). Week before Class 8: 45 min/day of self-chosen practice with no recordings (if this is too difficult, alternate recordings and self-guidance every other day). Daily home practice: 40-45 min of recorded formal practice plus other practice, ≥60 min in total. Self-care: under the physical risks of mindful yoga, if guidance is not appropriate for one's body or condition, or anything causes pain, 'disregard the teacher' and either modify the pose/movement, rest and imagine doing it, or notice the thoughts and emotions that come up from not doing it. In sitting practice with strong pain, shift posture if the pain is posture-related, investigate the sensations, or shift attention to the breath if they are overwhelming; the same approach is offered for difficult emotions. The guide also warns that sadness, anger or fear can seem stronger as practice develops, and that symptoms can sometimes worsen, particularly in the early weeks.
claims.finding_zh: 麻省大学医学院正念中心（CFM）2017年版《MBSR官方授权课程指南》规定：第1课引入引导式身体扫描（躺着做，必要时可坐在椅子上），第1-2周在家跟45分钟录音练习、每周至少6天，第3-4周与卧式瑜伽录音隔天交替；觉察呼吸的静坐：第2周每天10-15分钟，指南明确写明「不用录音、自己练」，第3周每天15-20分钟，第4周每天20分钟（关注呼吸、其他身体感受和整个身体）——静坐引导录音要到第5课才发放；第5课做45分钟静坐，依次觉察呼吸、身体、声音，把想法和情绪当作意识中的「事件」，再到无拣择觉察/开放临在，最后回到呼吸，并强调「更长的静默」，新发的静坐录音「静默更多」；全天静修课中，静坐「更少引导、更多静默」（30-40分钟），慢走先有入门引导（15-30分钟），之后「更少引导」（20分钟），慈心练习「尽量少说话、强调空间感、以静默结束」（25-30分钟；传统祝愿语不是必需的，并认可、接纳可能出现的抗拒）；第8课前一周每天自选练习45分钟、不用录音（如果太难，可录音与自主练习隔天交替）。每日家庭练习为40-45分钟有录音的正式练习加上其他练习，总计至少60分钟。自我照顾：在正念瑜伽的身体风险说明中写道，如果听到的引导不适合自己的身体或状况，或任何动作引起疼痛，应当「不听老师的」，改做这个姿势/动作，或休息并在想象中做，或觉察不做这个动作时出现的想法和情绪；静坐中遇到强烈疼痛时，若与姿势有关就调整姿势，也可以探究这些感受，难以承受时把注意力转回呼吸；对强烈情绪也用同样方法。指南还提醒：随着练习，悲伤、愤怒或恐惧可能显得更强，症状有时会加重，尤其在最初几周。
claims.study_type: program manual (official curriculum guide revised and edited by the programme developers; expert prescription, not an outcome study)
claims.sample: Curriculum document for the 8-week MBSR course: orientation session, Class 1 (3 h), Classes 2-7 (2.5 h each), Class 8 (3-3.5 h) and a 7.5-h all-day silent retreat; not an outcome study
claims.limitations: This is an expert curriculum, not evidence of efficacy. Durations, the progression and the share of silence were never tested separately; MBSR's outcome evidence comes from separate trials of the whole package. Recording-free sitting in Weeks 3-4 is inferred (it is explicit only for Week 2). The 'disregard the teacher' rule is written for yoga and movement. The document is proprietary and states that it 'may not be copied, distributed, or transferred ... without written permission'. It was read via a copy hosted by NHS Scotland whose permission status was not checked, so reuse the structure only, never the script text. A live-teacher group format differs from app delivery.
claims.app_implication: Build a staged path. Early weeks combine one long guided practice with short self-guided breath sits. MBSR uses a 45-min body scan; shorter guided versions are an app adaptation, not MBSR. Lengthen sitting from about 10-15 to about 20 min by week 4, then thin out the guidance (more silence), ending with an optional unguided timer mode. Order open-awareness sessions breath -> body -> sounds -> thoughts/emotions -> open awareness -> breath. Write loving-kindness with minimal talk, optional phrases, room for resistance and a silent ending. Movement scripts include 'modify, rest and imagine, or skip'. Sitting scripts include 'adjust your posture, explore the sensation, or return to the breath if it becomes too much'. Tell users early on that difficult feelings can intensify at first.

citation.authors: Santorelli SF, Meleo-Meyer F, Koerbel L, et al.
citation.title: Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR) Authorized Curriculum Guide
citation.venue: Center for Mindfulness in Medicine, Health Care, and Society, University of Massachusetts Medical School

verification.checked_against: Full 65-page PDF downloaded from the cited NHS Scotland URL; text extracted with macOS PDFKit and read: title page, Orientation logistics and risks, Classes 1-8, All-Day class, Appendix A (risks)
verification.problems: (1) 'Practised WITHOUT a recording' is explicit only for Week 2 ('No recording for home practice. Participants/patients are instructed to practice on their own'). Weeks 3-4 give only durations (15-20 min; 20 min with breathing, other sensations and the whole body). That those weeks have no recording is an inference: the Sitting recording is first handed out at Class 5. (2) The 'disregard the teacher' rule appears under the physical risks of mindful yoga and is about poses and movement. Its options are 'modify the pose/movement, rest and imagine doing the pose/movement, or notice and acknowledge any thoughts or emotions' about not doing it. It is not a general rule for every practice. The Class 4 pain guidance also includes 'shifting posture if pain is posture-related'. (3) Sample: classes are not all 2.5 h. Class 1 is 3 h, Classes 2-7 are 2.5 h, Class 8 is 3-3.5 h, the all-day class is a 7.5-h silent retreat, and there is also an orientation session. (4) The week-7 'no recordings' rule leaves out the guide's fallback: if this is too difficult, alternate recordings and self-guidance every other day. (5) evidence_weight 'moderate' overstates a curriculum manual. It is an expert prescription with no outcome data, and its parameters were never tested separately; changed to 'low'. (6) The app_implication 'short, densely guided practices first' is not what MBSR prescribes. Weeks 1-2 pair a long (45-min) fully guided body-scan recording with short UNGUIDED breath sits, so shorter guided sessions would be an app adaptation. (7) Missing, though not an error: the guide warns that emotions can intensify and symptoms can sometimes worsen in the early weeks. All other durations, quotes and the citation metadata match the document.

claims.topic: Breath counting (数息) protocol and training dose
claims.finding: Four studies (>400 participants in total) validated breath counting as a behavioural measure of mindfulness. Study 1 protocol: after a 6-min resting baseline, count breaths from 1 to 9 repeatedly for 18 min, pressing one key on breaths 1-8 and another on breath 9. On losing count, press a key reserved for self-caught miscounts and begin again at 1 with the next breath. Experience-sampling probes came about every 90 s (60-120 s). In Study 1 the average error rate was 22% of count sets (SD 15%), and 29% of errors were self-caught. Randomized online training study (Study 4; final n = 22 breath counting, 20 n-back, 29 no training; attrition 27%, 33%, 15%): two 25-min sessions every weekday for 4 weeks increased FFMQ (trait) mindfulness relative to both controls (group x time F(2,68) = 4.83, p = .01; contrast F(1,68) = 9.63, p < .01). It also decreased mind wandering during breath counting (F(1,68) = 5.40, p = .02). Counting accuracy improved relative to controls in a planned contrast (F(1,68) = 5.89, p = .02), but the overall group x time interaction for accuracy was only a trend (F(2,68) = 2.97, p = .06).
claims.finding_zh: 四项研究（共400多人）验证了数息可以作为正念的行为测量。研究1的做法：先静息6分钟，然后连续18分钟反复从1数到9，第1-8次呼吸按一个键，第9次按另一个键；数乱了就按专门的「自己发现数错」键，从下一次呼吸起重新数1；约每90秒（60-120秒）一次体验抽样提问。研究1中平均有22%的计数组出错（标准差15%），其中只有29%的错误是自己发现的。随机在线训练研究（研究4；最终数息组22人、n-back组20人、无训练组29人；脱落率27%、33%、15%）：4周内每个工作日练两次、每次25分钟，与两个对照组相比，数息组FFMQ（特质）正念得分上升（组别×时间 F(2,68) = 4.83，p = .01；对比 F(1,68) = 9.63，p < .01），数息时走神减少（F(1,68) = 5.40，p = .02）；计划对比显示计数准确率提高（F(1,68) = 5.89，p = .02），但准确率的整体组别×时间交互作用只是趋势（F(2,68) = 2.97，p = .06）。
claims.study_type: validation studies plus a randomized online training study (3 arms)
claims.sample: 4 studies, >400 participants; training study final n = 22/20/29
claims.limitations: Small training arms with high attrition. Mindfulness was self-reported, and Study 4's FFMQ was modified to ask about the last 2 weeks. Task protocols differed across the four studies; for example, Study 4's outcome task had no self-caught-miscount key. A 2023 mega-analysis of five datasets (Ching & Lim, Mindfulness 14:2097-2110, doi:10.1007/s12671-023-02201-9) found breath-counting accuracy related only to attention-related self-report (FFMQ Acting with Awareness and MAAS), with fairly small correlations. In that analysis, self-caught resets correlated with Acting with Awareness, while uncaught miscounts were unrelated to any mindfulness measure.
claims.app_implication: Offer 数息 with 1-9 counting, an optional tap per breath, and a 'lost count' button that restarts at 1. Frame that button as a noticing moment: losing count is common, at about 1 in 5 count sets in Study 1. Never display counting accuracy as a mindfulness score.

citation.authors: Levinson DB, Stoll EL, Kindy SD, et al.
citation.title: A mind you can count on: validating breath counting as a behavioral measure of mindfulness

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; PubMed abstract (PMID 25386148); PMC full text PMC4208398 (Methods Studies 1-4, Results, Fig. 4); Crossref abstract of Ching & Lim 2023 (doi 10.1007/s12671-023-02201-9)
verification.problems: Every number matches the full text, but there are two precision issues. (1) The protocol described (6-min rest, 18-min task, self-caught-miscount key, probes every ~90 s) is Study 1's, yet it reads as if all four studies used it. Study 2 used a 15-min task without experience sampling. Study 3 used a 30-min task with probes every ~3 min. Study 4's 18-min task had no meta-awareness probes and no self-caught-miscount key. (2) Omitted near-null: the omnibus group x time interaction for counting accuracy was only a trend (F(2,68) = 2.97, p = .06). F(1,68) = 5.89 is a planned contrast. The FFMQ omnibus was F(2,68) = 4.83, p = .01. Minor: Study 4's FFMQ was modified to ask about 'the last 2 weeks'. Study 1's n is reported as 164 usable in Methods but 120 in Results. The Ching & Lim (2023) limitation is accurate.

claims.topic: Mindful walking: session structure and RCT evidence
claims.finding: Open RCT (n = 74 adults aged 18-65 with moderate-to-high perceived stress; 36 intervention, 38 waitlist): 8 group sessions over 4 weeks, each ~60 min: meeting and walking to a park (5 + 5 min), warm-up exercises and short walking instructions (5), walking (10), mindful walking (10; observe bodily sensations while walking, moment to moment, without getting lost in distressing thoughts; if difficult, focus on the breath), feedback round (5), walking (10), exercises (5), walking back (5). Adjusted Perceived Stress Scale change at 4 weeks: -8.8 [95% CI -10.8, -6.8] vs -1.0 [-2.9, 0.9]; p < 0.001. Group differences were smaller but still significant at 12 weeks (PSS, SF-36 mental component); no serious adverse events.
claims.finding_zh: 开放式随机对照试验（74名18-65岁、主观压力中到高的成人；干预组36人，等待组38人）：4周8次小组课，每次约60分钟：集合并走到公园（5+5分钟）、热身操与简短讲解（5分钟）、步行（10分钟）、正念行走（10分钟：边走边觉察身体感受，安住当下，不被痛苦的念头卷走；如有困难就关注呼吸）、分享（5分钟）、步行（10分钟）、体操（5分钟）、走回（5分钟）。4周时校正后知觉压力量表变化：-8.8 [95%CI -10.8, -6.8] 对 -1.0 [-2.9, 0.9]，p < 0.001；12周时组间差异变小但仍显著（压力量表、SF-36心理分）；无严重不良事件。
claims.sample: n = 74 distressed adults (about 90% women)
claims.limitations: Unblinded, waitlist control; cannot separate walking exercise, group contact and expectancy; only 10 min per session was explicitly mindful; single trial.
claims.app_implication: Offer an outdoor format of normal walking with a 10-min mindful-walking segment and 'return to the breath if it is hard'. Describe the evidence as one small trial; keep eyes open and include safety prompts.
