claims.topic: Four-phase cycle of focused-attention (breath) meditation
claims.finding: fMRI study of 14 meditation practitioners (ages 28-66, 3 male; ≥1 year of regular practice; mean 1386 lifetime hours, SD 1368). They meditated for 20 min with attention on the breath at the nostrils and upper lip, pressed a button whenever they realised their mind had wandered, and returned to the breath; on average they pressed once every ~80 s. The authors proposed in advance, from the practice of focused-attention meditation, a four-interval cognitive cycle: mind wandering -> awareness of mind wandering -> shifting of attention -> sustained attention. They modelled it as fixed 3-s windows around each button press. Default-mode regions were more active during mind wandering than during the shifting phase (mind wandering was the analysis baseline). Salience-network regions (anterior insula, dorsal ACC) were active during awareness of mind wandering. Executive-network elements (e.g. right dorsolateral PFC, inferior parietal cortex) were active during shifting and sustained attention. Activations were modulated by lifetime meditation experience; for example, more practice was associated with less activity in ventromedial PFC and other regions during the shifting phase.
claims.finding_zh: 功能磁共振研究：14名冥想练习者（28-66岁，3名男性；规律练习至少1年，终生练习平均1386小时，SD 1368）在扫描中做20分钟专注呼吸冥想（注意鼻孔和上唇处的呼吸感受），每当发现自己走神就按键，并把注意带回呼吸（平均约每80秒按一次）。作者事先根据专注冥想的练习提出四段式循环模型：走神→觉察到走神→转移注意→持续专注，并围绕每次按键设定固定的3秒时间窗来分析。与「转移注意」阶段相比，走神时默认模式网络更活跃（走神阶段是分析的基线）；觉察到走神时突显网络（前脑岛、背侧前扣带回）活跃；转移和持续注意时执行网络的部分区域（如右侧背外侧前额叶、下顶叶）活跃。这些激活受终生冥想经验调节（例如练习时间越长，转移注意阶段腹内侧前额叶等区域的活动越低）。
claims.study_type: mechanistic fMRI study (within-subject, no control group)
claims.sample: n = 14 meditation practitioners (≥1 year of regular practice; mean 1386 lifetime hours, SD 1368; bimodal: 5 with >2000 h, 9 with <1200 h)
claims.limitations: Small sample with widely varying experience and no control group. Phases were fixed 3-s windows around self-reported button presses, a duration the authors call 'somewhat arbitrary'. Mind wandering was the analysis baseline, so its DMN activity is relative to the shifting phase only. The study shows mechanism, not clinical benefit.
claims.app_implication: Teach the cycle explicitly (走神 -> 发现 -> 放下 -> 回到呼吸) and frame the moment of noticing as part of the practice rather than a failure; this framing is a design choice and was not tested in this study. An optional 'tap when you notice' interaction mirrors the research paradigm. Count taps as noticing moments, not errors, and expect frequent wandering: practitioners here reported about one episode every 80 s.

citation.authors: Hasenkamp W, Wilson-Mendenhall CD, Duncan E, et al.
citation.title: Mind wandering and attention during focused meditation: a fine-grained temporal analysis of fluctuating cognitive states

verification.checked_against: Crossref + Europe PMC abstract + author-manuscript full text of the NeuroImage paper (OSF/MindRxiv preprint 4fnt6, 'Hasenkamp_NeuroImage 2012.pdf'): Methods 2.1-2.4, Results 3.1-3.3, Discussion 4.1
verification.problems: These are minor; the metadata and the abstract-level statements are correct. (1) finding_zh says '作者据此提出四段式循环', implying the model came from this experiment. The model was proposed in advance from the practice of focused-attention meditation, and fixed intervals were then built around the button presses. (2) The 'default-mode regions active during mind wandering' result comes only from the MW > SHIFT contrast. MW was the GLM baseline, and MW > AWARE and MW > FOCUS gave no significant clusters. (3) The phases were fixed 3-s windows that the authors call 'somewhat arbitrary'. Participants had at least 1 year of regular practice, with a mean of 1386 lifetime hours (SD 1368) in a bimodal distribution, so 'experienced' covers a wide range. I added these details and a precise reading of the DMN result.

claims.topic: RAIN: evidence status (component of a multi-session programme)
claims.finding: Single-site pilot RCT (n = 88 treatment-seeking nicotine-dependent adults smoking an average of 20 cigarettes/day): 8 group sessions twice weekly over 4 weeks of mindfulness training (MT) vs the American Lung Association's Freedom From Smoking (FFS). MT session 2 introduced RAIN, a technique to 'mindfully' work with cravings: Recognize, Accept, Investigate and Note what cravings feel like as they arise. In the full intention-to-treat sample, MT produced a greater reduction in cigarettes/day that was maintained through follow-up (group x time F = 7.01, p = .008). In the treatment-exposed sample (n = 71: 33 MT, 38 FFS) the same effect was F = 11.11, p = .001. In that treatment-exposed sample, CO-confirmed 7-day point-prevalence abstinence was 36% vs 15% at end of treatment (p = .063, a non-significant trend) and 31% vs 6% at the week-17 follow-up (p = .012).
claims.finding_zh: 单中心试点随机对照试验（88名寻求治疗的尼古丁依赖成人，平均每天吸20支烟）：4周内每周2次、共8次小组正念训练，对照为美国肺脏协会的「摆脱吸烟」（Freedom From Smoking）课程。正念训练第2次课引入RAIN，用来以正念方式应对渴求：在渴求出现时识别（Recognize）、接纳（Accept）、探究（Investigate）并标记（Note）它的感受。按全部随机样本（意向治疗）分析，正念组每日吸烟量下降更多，并在随访期保持（组别×时间 F = 7.01，p = .008）；只分析实际接受治疗的71人（正念组33人、对照组38人）时为 F = 11.11，p = .001。在这71人中，经呼出气一氧化碳确认的7天点戒断率：治疗结束时36%对15%（p = .063，未达统计学显著，仅为趋势），第17周随访时31%对6%（p = .012）。
claims.sample: n = 88 randomized; n = 71 treatment-exposed (33 MT, 38 FFS)
claims.limitations: RAIN was one element of a multi-component programme (with body scan, loving-kindness, breath awareness and walking practice) and was not tested on its own. Single-site pilot with one MT therapist and no formal treatment-integrity check. The F = 11.11 result and the abstinence rates come from the treatment-exposed subsample, not all 88 randomized. The 17-week follow-up is shorter than the standard 6 months. FFS was compressed from 8 to 4 weeks and had lower abstinence than typical self-quitters. Outside this trial, a Europe PMC search (Oct 2026) found no controlled trial of RAIN on its own. The closest is an uncontrolled single-arm proof-of-concept of app-delivered RAIN (Recognize, Allow, Investigate, Non-identify) in 49 emotional eaters (Carriere et al., 2024, mHealth 10:24), which reported pre-post improvements.
claims.app_implication: Present RAIN as an informal skill for urges and difficult emotions, taken from programmes with some RCT support, not as an independently validated technique. For cravings, use Brewer's 'Note' ending.

citation.authors: Brewer JA, Mallik S, Babuscio TA, et al.
citation.title: Mindfulness training for smoking cessation: results from a randomized controlled trial

verification.checked_against: Crossref metadata; PubMed abstract (PMID 21723049); PMC full text PMC3191261 (Methods 2.3.1, Results 3.2, Fig. 3, Strengths and Limitations); Europe PMC search plus PubMed abstracts of later RAIN studies (PMIDs 39114459, 38823419)
verification.problems: Metadata and the numbers match the abstract. However, the finding puts 'n = 88' next to results that come from the treatment-exposed subsample (n = 71: 33 MT, 38 FFS). F = 11.11 (df 1,1082) is the treatment-exposed analysis, and the 36% vs 15% and 31% vs 6% abstinence rates are also computed on n = 71 (Fig. 3). The full intention-to-treat analysis of cigarettes/day gave F = 7.01, p = .008. The end-of-treatment difference (p = .063) was not significant; the authors call it a trend. The authors describe the study as a pilot: single site, one MT therapist, no formal treatment-integrity check, 17-week follow-up. The limitation that other RAIN variants 'lack isolated trials' is inaccurate as worded. An uncontrolled single-arm proof-of-concept study tested app-delivered RAIN (Recognize, Allow, Investigate, Non-identify) on its own in 49 emotional eaters (Carriere et al., 2024, mHealth 10:24, PMID 39114459). No controlled trial of RAIN alone was found.

claims.topic: Loving-kindness protocol: sequence, session length, weekly expansion, dose
claims.finding: Waitlist-controlled field RCT at a US software company (202 employees consented and were randomized, 102 LKM vs 100 waitlist; completer sample n = 139, 67 vs 72). The LKM group attended six 60-min group sessions over 7 weeks (20-30 per group, led by a stress-management specialist experienced in teaching LKM). It was asked to practise at home at least 5 days/week with a CD of three guided meditations of 'increasing scope' (the first 15 min, the final 22 min). Week 1 directed love and compassion toward oneself and Week 2 added loved ones. Later weeks built from self to loved ones, acquaintances, strangers and finally all living beings. The paper's general description of LKM: practitioners first focus on the heart region and contemplate a person for whom they already feel warm and tender feelings, then extend these feelings to themselves and an ever-widening circle of others (the trial's own scripts were available only on request). During the workshop, LKM participants reported about 80 min/week of 'meditation, prayer, or solo spiritual activity' (about 60 min/week after it ended; baseline about 13 min/week). In the completer sample, daily positive emotions rose more over time in the LKM group (condition x time b = 0.041, SE 0.011, p = .0004), but this effect was not significant in the authors' intent-to-treat (p = .17) or per-protocol (p = .11) analyses. Among meditators only (a non-randomized dose analysis), each hour of practice per week was associated with 0.06 higher positive emotion on the 0-4 scale in Week 2 (p = .06), rising to 0.17 in Week 7 (p < .0001). There was no effect on negative emotions (b = -0.011, p = .28) and no significant change in compassion (b = 0.021, SE 0.016, p = .21).
claims.finding_zh: 美国一家软件公司的职场随机对照试验，以等待组为对照（202名员工同意参加并随机分组：慈心组102人、等待组100人；完成者分析139人，67对72）。慈心组在7周内参加6次、每次60分钟的小组课（每组20-30人，由有丰富慈心教学经验的压力管理专家带领），并被要求每周至少5天在家跟一张CD练习；CD含3段「范围逐步扩大」的引导（第一段15分钟，最后一段22分钟）。第1周把爱与慈悲送给自己，第2周加入所爱的人，之后依次扩展为自己→所爱的人→熟人→陌生人→一切众生。论文对慈心冥想的一般描述是：先把注意放在心口，想起一位本来就让你感到温暖、柔软的人，再把这份感受延伸到自己和越来越大的圈子（试验所用的具体引导词未公开，需向作者索取）。课程期间慈心组自报每周约80分钟「冥想、祈祷或独处灵修」（课程结束后约60分钟，基线约13分钟）。在完成者样本中，慈心组的日常积极情绪随时间上升得更多（条件×时间 b = 0.041，SE 0.011，p = .0004）；但在作者做的意向性分析（p = .17）和符合方案分析（p = .11）中，这一效应不显著。只在慈心组内部看（非随机的剂量分析），第2周每周多练1小时，积极情绪（0-4分）平均高0.06（p = .06），到第7周升到0.17（p < .0001），这只是相关关系。对消极情绪没有影响（b = -0.011，p = .28），「慈悲」情绪的变化也不显著（b = 0.021，p = .21）。
claims.sample: 202 employees randomized (102 LKM vs 100 waitlist); 139 completers analysed (67 vs 72); mean age 41, 65.5% female
claims.limitations: The main positive-emotion effect held only in the completer sample, not in intent-to-treat or per-protocol analyses. 63 of 202 were excluded (e.g., <3 of 6 classes, <30 of 61 daily reports, missing Time 2). Waitlist control with no active comparison, so demand and expectancy differ. All outcomes and practice time were self-reported (practice as 'meditation, prayer, or solo spiritual activity'). The dose-response analysis is correlational. One company. Teacher-led groups plus CD, not app-only.
claims.app_implication: Default LKM course: guided sessions of about 15 min growing to about 22 min, at least 5 days/week, widening the circle week by week (self, loved ones, acquaintances, strangers, all beings). Opening with an easy loved one follows the paper's general LKM description. Do not promise less negative emotion. Present the rise in positive emotions as something seen in people who kept practising (not significant in intent-to-treat analysis), not as a guaranteed effect.

citation.authors: Fredrickson BL, Cohn MA, Coffey KA, et al.
citation.title: Open hearts build lives: positive emotions, induced through loving-kindness meditation, build consequential personal resources
citation.venue: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology

verification.checked_against: Crossref and PubMed metadata (JPSP 95(5):1045-1062); NCBI PMC full text PMC3156028: Method (Participants, Procedure, LKM Workshops), Results (compliance, positive and negative emotions, effort models) and the Intent-to-Treat Analyses section; Crossref/PubMed checked for corrections (none found)
verification.problems: Metadata is correct. (1) Omitted null: the condition x time effect on positive emotions (b = 0.041, SE 0.011, p = .0004) was significant only in the completer sample (n = 139). The paper's own intent-to-treat (t(1380) = 1.37, p = .17) and per-protocol (t(1380) = 1.58, p = .11) analyses were not significant, and the authors say conclusions about efficacy may need to be restricted to those who invested adequate effort (~70%). The unqualified 'LKM raised daily positive emotions' therefore overstates. (2) The 0.06 to 0.17 per-hour figures come from a meditators-only, non-randomized model that the paper reports as 'was associated with'; 'gain per hour' and 带来 are causal wording. (3) 'Each sitting starts by focusing on the heart region...' is the Introduction's general description of LKM, not a documented description of this trial's CD scripts, which were available only on request. (4) The analysed n per arm (67 vs 72) was missing. All other numbers match the full text.

claims.topic: Self-Compassion Break: three components, phrases, soothing touch
claims.finding: The official Self-Compassion Break (Self-Compassion Institute, Kristin Neff) starts by calling to mind a difficult situation that is causing stress and seeing whether one can feel the stress and emotional discomfort in the body. One then says to oneself: (1) mindfulness, 'This is a moment of suffering' (alternatives: 'This hurts', 'Ouch', 'This is stress'); (2) common humanity, 'Suffering is a part of life' (alternatives: 'Other people feel this way', 'I'm not alone', 'We all struggle in our lives'). Next, one puts the hands over the heart, feeling their warmth and gentle touch on the chest, or adopts another soothing touch that felt right. Then (3) 'May I be kind to myself' (self-kindness, the third component in Neff's model; the page does not label this step), optionally asking 'What do I need to hear right now to express kindness to myself?' (e.g., 'May I give myself the compassion that I need', 'May I learn to accept myself as I am', 'May I forgive myself', 'May I be strong', 'May I be patient'). The page says it can be used any time of day or night.
claims.finding_zh: 自我关怀研究院（Kristin Neff）官方的「自我关怀小憩」（中文名为本文暂译）：先想起生活中一个让你有压力的困难情境，看看能否在身体里感受到这份压力和情绪上的不适，然后对自己说：(1) 正念——「这是一个受苦的时刻」（也可以说「好痛」「哎哟」「这是压力」）；(2) 共通人性——「受苦是生活的一部分」（也可以说「别人也会有这种感受」「我不孤单」「我们每个人都会挣扎」）；接着把双手放在胸口，感受手的温度和轻柔的触碰，或用你发现适合自己的其他安抚性触碰；(3)「愿我善待自己」（对应Neff模型中的「善待自己」，页面本身未标注这一步），也可以问自己「此刻我需要听到什么，才能善待自己？」（例如「愿我给自己需要的关怀」「愿我接纳自己本来的样子」「愿我原谅自己」「愿我坚强」「愿我有耐心」）。页面说明它可在白天或夜里任何时候使用。
claims.study_type: official web page (practice description by the programme developer)
claims.sample: None (practice description)
claims.limitations: This is a practice description, not evidence of benefit. A randomized test of this exercise on its own (Williamson 2020, Psychological Reports: 129 students, 3 weeks of practice vs a time-management control and a no-induction control) found no significant differences in stress, self-compassion or depressed mood. Other support comes only from multi-component programmes (e.g., the MSC RCT, 25 vs 27 waitlist participants). Phrases must be re-authored in natural Chinese, not translated word for word. Year = page datePublished (2023-11-28); the page was last modified 2025-10-24 and has no individual author byline.
claims.app_implication: Offer a 3-5-min 自我关怀三步 with phrases chosen from a short editable list and an optional, user-chosen soothing touch. Tell users to pick a mild difficulty, not the worst one. Do not claim it reduces stress: a randomized test of the exercise on its own found no effect.

citation.authors: Neff K (Self-Compassion Institute)
citation.title: Exercise 2: Self-Compassion Break

verification.checked_against: Official page fetched from self-compassion.org (the claim's URL redirects to the canonical /exercises/ URL), including JSON-LD datePublished/dateModified; PubMed abstracts of Williamson 2020 (PMID 31564217) and Neff & Germer 2013 (PMID 23070875); Europe PMC search for 'self-compassion break'
verification.problems: The page content matches the finding word for word, and datePublished 2023-11-28 is correct (last modified 2025-10-24). (1) The limitation 'No trial isolates this exercise' is wrong. Williamson (2020, Psychological Reports, PMID 31564217) randomized 129 students to a Self-Compassion Break induction, a time-management control or no induction, with practice over 3 weeks. It found no significant between-group differences in stress, self-compassion or depressed mood, and this null result should be disclosed. (2) The phrase 'self-compassion meta-analyses with high risk of bias' is unsourced and has been removed. (3) The URL redirects to the canonical https://self-compassion.org/exercises/exercise-2-self-compassion-break/. (4) The page labels steps 1 and 2 as mindfulness and common humanity but does not label step 3; 'self-kindness' comes from Neff's model. The MSC RCT numbers (25 vs 27 waitlist) are confirmed.

claims.topic: Speech density and structure of a university centre's guided meditations
claims.finding: UCLA's free English guided meditations were recorded by Diana Winston (UCLA Mindful, formerly the Mindful Awareness Research Center, MARC; transcript PDFs created September 2016). They run from 2:44 to 19:00, and the durations printed on the transcripts match the audio files to within about 1 s. Dividing transcript words (excluding titles, copyright footers and stage directions such as [bell rings]) by duration (our analysis) gives guidance densities of about 79 words/min (Short Body Scan 2:44, 217 words), 80 (Body and Sound 3:06, 249), 59 (Breathing Meditation 5:31, 325), 73 (Working with Difficulties 6:55, 506), 80 (Loving Kindness 9:31, 765), 44 (Breath, Sound, Body 12:00, 533), 76 (Body Scan for Sleep 13:50, 1049) and 49 (Complete Meditation Instructions 19:00, 937). Other counting rules shift these by up to about 3%. A simple loudness-based voice-activity estimate on the official audio (our analysis; pauses up to 1 s counted as speech) found speech in roughly 31-32% of the 12-min Breath, Sound, Body practice, 35-36% of the 19-min Complete Instructions, 39-41% of the 5-min breath practice, 50-54% of the short body scan, 52-54% of loving-kindness, 53-55% of working with difficulties, 56-59% of body and sound, and about 55-63% of the sleep body scan (less certain because that track has a continuous background sound). The voice ran at roughly 120-160 words/min while speaking. The breath-anchored practices gather their silence into long blocks: about 50 s in the 5-min practice, about 4 min in the 12-min practice, and two blocks of about 3 min in the 19-min practice. The body scans and loving-kindness guide almost continuously, with no pause longer than about 12 s. Structure: the breath practice offers abdomen, chest/throat or nostrils as anchors and suggests softly noting 'thinking' or 'wandering'. The 12-min practice keeps the breath as the anchor but lets attention go to sounds or body sensations when they become predominant, then return. The loving-kindness practice moves from a loved one (a pet is allowed) to receiving kindness back, to oneself ('not always easy'), to a chosen person or group, to all directions (including people one has difficulty with). It uses the phrases 'May you be safe and protected from danger / happy and peaceful / healthy and strong / have ease and wellbeing' and says that feeling nothing is not a problem. The sleep body scan runs top-down and says that drifting off is fine.
claims.finding_zh: UCLA的免费英文引导冥想由Diana Winston录制（UCLA Mindful，原名正念觉察研究中心MARC；文字稿PDF制作于2016年9月），时长2分44秒至19分钟；文字稿上标注的时长与音频实际时长相差不超过约1秒。用文字稿词数（不含标题、版权页脚和[铃声]等舞台说明）除以时长（本研究计算），得到引导密度：短身体扫描（2:44，217词）约每分钟79词；身体与声音（3:06，249词）约80；呼吸冥想（5:31，325词）约59；与困难相处（6:55，506词）约73；慈心（9:31，765词）约80；呼吸·声音·身体（12:00，533词）约44；睡前身体扫描（13:50，1049词）约76；完整冥想指导（19:00，937词）约49；换一种计词规则，数值最多相差约3%。用简单的音量阈值法对官方音频做人声检测（本研究计算，1秒以内的停顿算作说话），有人声的时间约占：12分钟「呼吸·声音·身体」31-32%，19分钟「完整冥想指导」35-36%，5分钟呼吸练习39-41%，短身体扫描50-54%，慈心52-54%，与困难相处53-55%，身体与声音56-59%，睡前身体扫描约55-63%（该音轨有持续背景声，估计较不确定）；说话时语速约每分钟120-160词。以呼吸为锚的练习把静默集中成长段（5分钟练习约50秒，12分钟练习约4分钟，19分钟练习两段各约3分钟），而身体扫描和慈心几乎连续引导，最长停顿不超过约12秒。结构上：呼吸练习提供腹部、胸口/喉咙或鼻孔作为锚点，并建议在心里轻轻标记「想」或「走神」；12分钟练习以呼吸为锚，当声音或身体感受变得突出时允许注意力转过去，之后再回到呼吸；慈心练习依次为所爱的人（可以是宠物）→接收对方回送的善意→自己（「并不总是容易」）→选定的人或群体→向四面八方扩展（包括相处困难的人），祝愿语为「愿你平安、免受危险；愿你快乐安宁；愿你健康强壮；愿你自在安好」，并说明没有感觉也没关系。睡前身体扫描从头到脚，并说明睡着也没关系。
claims.study_type: official university web page with audio and transcripts + derived transcript and audio analysis (this review)
claims.sample: 8 English recordings with transcripts (2:44-19:00), one teacher
claims.limitations: These are derived, descriptive metrics from one centre and one teacher, in English; Mandarin pacing and syllable rates differ. They show what UCLA does, not what works best, and there are no outcome data. Word counts depend on counting rules (about ±3%). Speech share comes from a simple loudness-threshold detector, not hand annotation, and it shifts with the threshold and with how long a pause still counts as speech. Counting pauses up to 1.5 s as speech adds about 2-7 points. Counting pauses up to 3 s raises the body scans to about 70-80%, loving-kindness to about 63-65% and the 12-min practice to about 39%. The sleep track's continuous background sound makes its estimate less certain. The page was read on 2026-10-23 and may change. The transcripts linked under 'Mandarin' are files named cantonese-*.pdf (column heading 'Cantonese Text') in simplified characters. The breathing one is standard written Mandarin, but several others mix in Cantonese colloquial words (e.g., 嘅, 唔, 啲, 佢, 係), so they are not a reliable Mandarin script for mainland users.
claims.app_implication: Use UCLA's pacing as one reference point, not a rule. Breath-anchored practices: about 30-40% speech, with the silence gathered into one or two long blocks (about 1 min in a 5-min session, about 3-4 min in 12-19-min sessions). Body scans and loving-kindness: about 50-60% speech, with near-continuous guidance and pauses of no more than about 10-12 s. Measure the final Chinese audio with the same voice-activity method. Do not translate, adapt or reuse UCLA's scripts or audio in a commercial app: they are licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (no commercial use, no derivatives).

verification.checked_against: Official UCLA Health page https://www.uclahealth.org/uclamindful/guided-meditations (fetched 2026-10-23); the text and PDF metadata of all 8 English transcript PDFs linked there; all 8 English MP3s linked there (durations with afinfo, plus our own loudness-based voice-activity and pause analysis); the 6 transcript PDFs linked under 'Mandarin'
verification.problems: Verified: the page and URL exist; it lists exactly 8 English recordings. The transcript PDFs were created 2016-09-21. The durations printed on the transcripts (2:44, 3:06, 5:31, 6:55, 9:31, 12:00, 13:50, 19:00) match the audio files to within about 1 s. All structural details check out against the transcripts: the breath anchors; softly noting 'thinking'/'wandering'; the loving-kindness sequence (pet allowed, receiving kindness back, self 'not always easy', chosen person or group, all directions) and its four phrases; feeling nothing is 'not a problem'; the sleep scan is top-down and drifting off is 'fine'. Problems: (1) The speech-share figures rest on an assumed 100-140 wpm delivery that the audio contradicts. While speaking, the voice runs at roughly 120-160 wpm. A loudness-based voice-activity estimate on the official MP3s (pauses up to 1 s counted as speech) gives about 31-32% for the 12-min practice, 39-41% for the 5-min breath practice, 50-54% for the short body scan, 52-54% for loving-kindness and 55-63% for the sleep scan. These sit at or below the lower ends of the claimed ranges (32-45%, 42-59%, 55-82%). So the upper bounds, and the app target of '55-80%' for body scan and loving-kindness, are overstated; loving-kindness stays at about 63-65% even when pauses up to 3 s count as speech. (2) The 12-min 'Breath, Sound, Body' practice is called 'open-awareness'. In the transcript the breath is the anchor ('the breath is our anchor'), and attention moves to sounds or body sensations only when they become predominant. (3) A reproducible recount of the transcript words (excluding titles, copyright footers and [bell] directions) differs by up to about 2.6%: 217/249/325/506/765/533/1049/937 against the claimed 220/254/328/505/785/541/1069/959. Densities change by 2 wpm or less. (4) The limitation 'Mandarin transcripts are actually written Cantonese' is overstated. The files linked under 'Mandarin' are named cantonese-*.pdf (the column heading reads 'Cantonese Text') and use simplified characters. The breathing transcript is standard written Mandarin; the others mix in varying amounts of Cantonese colloquial words (嘅, 唔, 啲, 佢, 係). (5) Citation: the centre now publishes as 'UCLA Mindful' (the page no longer mentions MARC), and the recordings are credited to Diana Winston. The page licenses the meditations under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (no commercial use, no derivatives), which bears directly on an app and was not mentioned.
